## Decision P4-D352 — a census of marks that is only a pool (stage 3's follow-up B, 2026-09-25)

**Measured at 6a7a7d7**, over 46 seeded one-column shapes whose census of marks is only `(withheld)` -- point and declared decimal comma, negatives, affixed units, a workbook, floors 2, 11 and 31, 150 to 5,000 rows -- at seeds 0 to 4: 0 of 230 twins wrote a mark, no `spelling.thousands_marks` check was filed, and 16,935 real grouped cells wore a mark their twin never wrote. And the pool said too much: 29 of the 46 pooled more cells than six marks hold below the floor, all at seven times one less, which fixes each mark's count below it -- ten rows on 23 shapes, thirty on 4, one row on 2.

**The decision.** (1) The two mixture censuses ask `parsing.census_pools` as every other closed census does: a pool over more cells than all but one convention hold below the floor is counted under the commonest convention the cells wrote, `group_separator` and `negative_form` follow it, and the loader refuses such a pool (TM1, NS2). This is the orchestrator's application of the owner's ruling 6 of 2026-09-17 ("a spelling below the floor counts into the commonest", P4-D222); it is not a new owner ruling. (2) A lone pool of `P` is spent over all seven marks wherever `T` is seven or more, so no real mark is left unshown there; at a floor of 2 a lone pool holds at most six cells and the first `T` marks are written, as they are wherever a small pool or a short twin leaves `T` under seven, so a real mark later in the order can go unshown -- seven marks cannot all stand on fewer than seven cells under any rule. `T` is the groupable cells where they number fewer than `P` and the floor together and `P` otherwise, never past `6(f - 1)`; the runs of one value go whole to the mark holding the fewest cells, none reaching the floor, and an empty mark takes the last cell of the fullest (method G6.1). Whole runs rather than fixed shares, measured on this tree over the 17 shapes that still pool: both leave 0 real grouped cells unshown, and whole runs raise `n_distinct` past the published count on 5 twins by 5 where fixed shares do on 10 by 35. (3) The report names the pool against the groupable cells wherever they differ by less than the floor, and the checker files the pool as one count (C6-89). (4) The P4-D265 recount counts only groupable cells, since a cell under a thousand never shows the mark it is offered.

**Measured after**, the same 230 twins: every twin writes a mark, the 85 twins that still pool write all seven; 201 are HELD and 29 WITHHELD, each of the 29 naming the difference; 0 twins and 0 real files are MISSED; `n_distinct` passes the published count on 5 twins by 5. The cost is (1)'s: on the 29 band shapes the twin writes the commonest mark, and 10,560 real grouped cells wear a mark it never writes. Guarded by `tests/test_pool_alone_marks.py`, the `lone_pool` witness, the frozen case `pool_alone_marks` and `K-S3-16`.

(5) **A trailing minus needs a point** (this decision's second skeptic, 2026-09-26): where the census counts negatives under `trailing_minus`, named or a band counted there by (1), G6.4's values step keeps that many negatives pointed, an exchange gives `decimal` to a negative the ladder made whole, and the trailing minus takes its count before the other notations (method G6.1) -- over five such shapes at seeds 0 to 4 the twins wrote, at e294a82, 0 or 1 of 37 with both notation checks missed, 1 of 20 beside brackets with the census missed, and 34 of 37 on whole values, and every count after, nothing MISSED and nothing else moving over the 28-shape battery; guarded by the gate's trailing nodes, the `trailing` witness and the frozen case `trailing_minus_points`. It is never written `12-`, which reads as text (rewriting a twin that way took 2 missed checks to 16), so where the published forms leave too few pointed negatives -- a band whose ten pointed cells ruling 6 counted into `plain` -- the shortfall stays named and missed.

(6) **Whole negatives nearest zero** (the skeptic of (5), 2026-09-26): beside a trailing minus, G6.4's last walk takes the side that is not negative first and the negatives nearest zero first, and P2-C5-F3's later stratum is later in that order (method G6.4). At 8448e5f, 25 negatives written `12.34-` beside 20 written `-007` and 90 whole positives kept every trailing minus and missed 5 checks on 20 of 20 twins over four such shapes: the whole negatives went to the most negative strata, which no field three figures wide holds. After, 0 missed, and over 41 seeded shapes and the 28-shape battery at seeds 0 to 4 no other verdict moves. Where the side that is not negative carries the point-free count, no negative is made whole and each notation is spread over the band (G-large's 15 minus cells span -10506 to -2203, where they stood between -9599 and -7909; the real ones span -9384 to -1928); which side holds the whole values is published nowhere, and now it is the side that is not negative wherever that side can hold them. **A known limit:** where negatives must still be whole, they are the ones nearest zero, so the notation on them sits nearest zero -- 20 whole negatives spread from -995 to -87 beside 25 `x.yy-` and 60 whole positives come back with their mean at -352 against a real -555 (at 8448e5f, -884 the other way). Where the real whole negatives are the LARGE ones the separation is reversed, not narrowed: 20 written `-NNNN` between -9761 and -1636 beside 25 `x.yy-` between -973.67 and -7.01 and 90 whole positives come back, at five seeds of five with every check passing, with the minus cells' mean at -1157.5 against a real -4890.0 and the trailing ones' at -3550.0 against -439.8 (at 8448e5f, -4995.6 and -445.4); which notation stands on the larger negatives is published nowhere. Guarded by the gate's `named-beside-padded`, the frozen cases `trailing_minus_points` (reworked so its walk reaches the negatives) and `trailing_minus_exchange` (the exchange, which no case reached), the witness `trailing_values` (the walk beside, which no frozen case reached, and the last walk's order with and without a trailing minus), a hand-worked chain whose holder is held to the walk's order, and a test of the note's count and entries per commit.

(7) **The negative walk nearest zero too** (the skeptic of (6), round 3, 2026-09-26): beside a trailing minus, G6.4's walk over the negative strata alone, which a named `decimal_plus` asks for whole negatives, takes them nearest zero first as the last walk does, and a walk's count after a chain move covers only the strata it walks (method G6.4). The two walks over the side that is not negative keep stratum order. Measured at 331ad47 over 277 fuzzed one-column profiles at seed 0: the order on the negative walk moves 10 twins and one verdict, a twin missing five checks that then passes all of them; on every walk it moves 30 with the same one verdict, and 22 of them differ from the first for nothing, so it is taken only where a negative can be reached; the recount alone moves none of them. Guarded by those two shapes, the `trailing_values` rows for the walk beside's demand, the side that is not negative ascending and the negative walk's order with and without a trailing minus, and a hand-worked walk beside held to stratum order. The ledger note names each re-stamped entry's tree and what took it, never its value, and a test holds that. **The recount's reach** (the skeptic of (7), 2026-09-27): a walk's count after a chain covers only the strata it walks on every walk that is not over every stratum, so it repairs the walk for `leading_plus` too, with or without a trailing minus. Measured at 657ee92 against 67e6a93 over 138 twins -- 23 seeded one-column shapes at floors 1, 11 and 31, seeds 0 and 3, profiles byte-identical -- the recount alone moves 11, 9 with no trailing minus: six of 40 `+NN` beside 30 `-NN` and 90 decimals on 1..60 from five or six missed checks to none, two dense ones losing five, and one dense signed decimal on nine whole numbers a side at floor 31, missing five checks either way, gaining `styles.spill` on two cells holding -4 written with a point -- accepted by the orchestrator on 2026-09-27 (not an owner ruling; the owner may reverse it), the shape being short of whole numbers on both trees. Guarded by the gate's `plus-beside-whole-negatives`, which at 67e6a93 wrote 36 pluses of 40 with five checks missed at every seed; a third hand-worked chain row holds the negative walk's holder to the nearest-zero order, which nothing held (asked in stratum order, six twins' bytes moved and no verdict). The walk beside's own count after a chain is held by a hand-worked row too, which nothing held (the second skeptic of (7), 2026-09-28): taken over every stratum on that walk alone, 30 `+N.d` beside 40 `N.d-`, 30 `-N` and 70 whole values on 1..9 wrote 37 trailing minuses of 40 at floor 11, seed 0, and missed `spelling.negative_notations`, while the gate, the witness rows and the frozen cases stood. ## Decision P4-D353 — a withheld tail pair is published where withholding it costs the twin its mean or spread (stage 3's follow-up A, 2026-09-26)

**The owner's answers, verbatim.** 2026-09-25: (1) where the published rungs pin a column's middle, the exact skew and kurtosis rebuild withheld tail values, 65 of 110 on one shape: "Accept it" (`K-S3-17`); (2) may a new check leave a tail's innermost row unprotected: "Yes, leave it" -- recorded as given; it governed the direct witness, which this decision does not build, so it decides nothing here; (3) a pinned tail whose withholding makes the twin miss its mean or spread: "Publish anyway"; (4) where: "Only where it costs" -- a pinned tail's pair is published only where withholding it would make the twin miss its column's mean or spread. 2026-09-26: (5) where such a pair and the column's exact mean and spread give the OTHER tail back by subtraction: "Allow it" (`K-S3-21`); (6) dates and clock times, which publish no mean and no spread, get a cost rule of their own "as a later landing" after 3b's core -- asked for by the owner and not built here; (7) is landing 3b.6's; (8) two rebuild channels the shipped stage 3 already had -- beside a tail that LISTS its values the exact mean and spread give the withheld far tail back (24 values over two seeded Likert columns), and where `n_distinct_values`, the mode's count, the sign counts and the rungs pin the whole column every value comes back (the integers 0 to 1,100: all 1,101): "Accept both" (`K-S3-23`, `K-S3-24`), after the owner asked how much they show about the RELATION of the data and was told: a column's own values and their row counts, "never which row holds them", never another column. That question named no exception: on a table SORTED by that column the description publishes the order (`row_order`), so row k holds the k-th value (`tests/test_stage3_gate.py::test_a_sorted_table_places_every_rebuilt_value_in_its_row`). Told of it on 2026-09-30, the owner answered "Yes, it stands". This amends P4-D349 part 1 and meets `K-S3-15`'s target (P4-D351).

**The decision.** (1) THE COST RULE. Where the back-solve withholds a numeric tail's pair -- pinned, as answers 3 and 4 say, or unsettled inside its budget, which is this plan's a-fortiori reading of them and not the owner's words -- the producer asks the would-be description, per moment, whether the G12.3 window drawn from it contains the published mean and spread (`taxonomy._moments_missed`: the checker's own `taxonomy.moment_windows`, which `validation` now reads, over the loader's `contract.numeric_block_facts`; answers remembered by the whole block, its four cell counts and five settings). Candidates come in the order of what they disclose (this plan's order, not the owner's): the other side's own pair where (2) withheld it; of two withheld sides each alone, unsettled before pinned and low before high, then both; of one, that side with the other's pair. The first that keeps both moments is published, else the first that keeps the most, else nothing more. (2) ONE WITHHELD TAIL WITHHOLDS THE OTHER'S PAIR where the rule publishes nothing and the other side lists no values, because beside that pair the exact mean and spread give it back wherever the rungs pin the interior: of the 72 values the base `e294a82` hands back that way at floor 11, the 12 on the one column whose closure costs nothing stay closed to that subtraction (`K-S3-19`) and the other 60 are what answer (5) allows. A SIDE WITHHELD THIS WAY SAYS SO in a remark (contract NF62, NF63), as one whose back-solve did not finish (NF64, NF65; dates and clocks too) and one binary64 cannot hold (NF66, NF67) do, and the summary and the quality report read it: both had said of every side without a pair that its own two distances give its values back one by one, false on `heap_then_one_far`'s low side at floor 11 and on 1,500 all-different values at 20 (review of 2026-09-26; `K-S3-25`: 0 of 64 sides misstated, where the base misstated 20). CLOSED TO THE SUBTRACTION, NOT TO EVERY READING: with no pair at all, a reader of the whole block -- the exact mean and spread beside the rungs, `n_distinct_values`, the mode's count and the sign counts -- rebuilds `heap_then_one_far`, one of `K-S3-19`'s three closures, whole at floor 11, its one-row maximum 1100 among the values, and the integers 0 to 1,100 at every floor from 11 to 50: answer (8) accepted it (`K-S3-24`, 14,115 values over 15 of 52 column-floors). A LISTED other side keeps its pair: TL5 requires both distances of a list, and a one-value list pins its tail by itself, so withholding them would close nothing. Beside it the subtraction still gives the withheld tail back where the rule publishes nothing -- 12 values on each of two seeded 150-row Likert columns at floor 11, the one-row extreme among them, as on the base; answer (5) does not reach it, and answer (8) accepts it (`K-S3-23`). (3) No direct witness is built: every unsettled side either costs a moment, where (1) offers it, or costs nothing. (4) NO DERIVED END, STAIRCASE ROW, WIDTH-WALK VALUE OR STRATUM READ BETWEEN THE TAILS IS A STAND-IN NUMBER: a derived end on `9999`, `-999` or `-9999` moves one grid step toward its boundary (`contract._off_the_stand_ins`, method G5.3b step 5), a staircase row one grid point outward (`contract._row_off_the_stand_ins`), G6.6's width walk, whose nearest candidate from beyond a width's ceiling is the ceiling itself, refuses the three (`generation._figured_inside`) -- which is where skeptic A2 found them: 145 four-figure numbers beside five of five figures at floor 11 wrote `9999` inside the high tail and missed seven obligations at seeds 0, 4 and 9, three-figure negatives wrote `-999`, 1,500 all-different Pareto readings `9999` inside the ladder, all on the base too -- and a stratum the convex form reads between the two tails takes the neighbouring point of its grid toward nought (`generation._drawn_off_the_stand_ins`, method G5.4's last rule), where skeptic Ad found one: on the 899 whole numbers -1400 to -1000 and -998 to -501 one or two strata read `-999` and every twin wrote it deep in its interior at floors 11, 20, 36 and 50, seeds 0, 4 and 9, nothing missed, on the base `af31c57` too. The oracle carries the end, the rows and the interior step; the one frozen case they move, `tail_pad_partial`, is regenerated, and the interior step moves none. The other value passes of G6 are not held to it, and two are measured to write one: G6.5a's fill of a grid with no spare point and its walk to the published count of different numbers can each put a stratum on a stand-in that is a gap between two values the column holds, where it is no outlier and nothing is missed -- `9999` in the high tail of 9000 to 9998 beside 10000 and 10001, `-999` in the low tail of -998 to 0 beside -1001 and -1003, `-9999` in the low tail of -9998 to -9000 beside -10000 and -10003, and `-999` in the high tail of -1300 to -1000 beside -998 and -997, between -1000 and -998, each in one cell at a floor of eleven and seeds 0, 4 and 9 (`tests/test_p4d353_cost_rule.py::test_the_separation_walk_takes_a_stand_in_only_in_a_gap_of_the_column_s_own`); and on skeptic Ad's column the walk still takes `-999` between -1000 and -998 at seeds 4 and 9, where the draw no longer does (`::test_no_stratum_read_between_the_tails_is_a_stand_in`).

## Decision P4-D354 — every day filled: a tail's tie group gives way (stage 3b landing 3b.0, 2026-09-26)

**Measured at e294a82**, 240 twins of 16 seeded shapes at floors 1, 11 and 36, seeds 0 to 4, 25 of them MISSED both distinct counts at every seed: two years of admission dates at 10,000 rows came back with 730 of 731 days, billing dates with 729 and two more 10,000-row tables filling every day of their span with 730 and 729 at floor 11, and 300 days with 299 at floor 36; the admission days written as midnight moments, and every second of ten minutes, lost a unit the same way and bought the value back as a spelling the real column never wrote (G7.9), so they validated. The cause: a tail's tie group stands on one distance and its gap is that point, so the count pass cannot split it, and where the boundary moved in (P4-D346) the group covers several real days.

**The decision.** Method G7.3b step 9: where the count is still short after the count pass, each tail's group of two ranks or more gives ranks to units no rank holds from one to its reach -- the smaller remove from its own distance first, then the smaller distance, then the low tail -- keeping one rank; G12.14 sums the group as wide as the step can move it wherever the count is reachable, in the validator and the generator's report alike. After: 0 of the 25 miss anything, the two hidden losses write every unit and no bought spelling, and the other 215 twins keep their verdicts. Every clause of the step has its witness in `tests/test_stage3b_gate.py` but two bounds no description found reaches: the reach itself and the width-kind half of the standing clause.

**Not done, measured on the landing's product.** Where a real column's outermost units, one cell each, lie past a tail's derived end, the twin cannot write them and misses both distinct counts, on one side or both at once and by several units a side: 5,000 dates filling a year whose first and last weeks hold about one cell a day come back with 363 of 365 days at floor 11 and 359 at floor 36 at every seed, derived ends of 6 and 7 against real outermost units 8 to 10 out; of 150 small filled tables (18 to 40 days, 100 to 320 rows, floor 11, seeds 0 and 1) 38 of 300 twins miss, each losing only the real first or last day and 4 losing both; 600 rows over 50 days hold 49 of 50. On moments the loss is hidden: every second of fifteen minutes at 8,000 rows and floor 36 holds 898 or 899 of 900 and buys each lost second back as a spelling with a mark the real column never wrote (G7.9), so validation passes. A second cause, with no tie group in it: two drawn ranks whose strata overlap land on one unit and leave the unit between them empty (that column's high tail at seed 7 holds distance 27 twice and 25 not at all). Reaching the count past the end needs as many units beyond it as the real column held there, on either tail or both, which nothing published names -- one day past the end on one side repairs neither the year nor the fifteen minutes -- and risks a unit before the real first, as the billing twin already writes one from its shape's outer strata. Both stand, for the owner or the orchestrator to decide. **A unit past the real column's ends, measured by the landing's second skeptic and its fix pass.** A twin writing a unit before the real first or after the real last is older than this landing and identical per twin at e294a82: of 12 filled-range shapes at floors 1, 11 and 36 and five seeds, 12 of the 36 shape-and-floor cases write one at every seed (60 of 180 twins), and so do 184 of 600 twins of 300 random date and clock columns at two seeds. Its cause is step 3: on every such tail the derived end, rounded, stands past the real outermost unit -- by exactly one on those 12 shapes, which is no property of a filled range (400 days each held, the first and last 21 all but empty, 2,500 dates at floor 36, derive a low end of 25 against a real outermost of 23 and write two days before the real first at seeds 3 and 8, the third skeptic's shape), by one to nine units on the random columns -- and the drawn ranks whose strata reach it write there too. No check misses it, because no end is published; repairing it moves every drawn tail, so it is recorded here and in STATE and not built. Guarded by `tests/test_stage3b_gate.py`, the frozen case `every_day_group` and `K-S3-30`.

**The fix pass: a merged run keeps every rank inside its gap.** Two date-tail misses older than this landing (identical at d93fd43) were measured to one cause: G7.3's count pass merges a run of ranks on one unit onto a unit ranks already hold, and asked the run's FIRST rank alone whether that unit lay inside its gap. A body run shares one gap; a tail rank's gap is its own stratum (G7.3b step 8), so the rest of a tail run went past theirs. 2,469 dates over 392 days, a fifth empty, at floor 36 wrote two low-tail ranks a day outside their strata and MISSED the tail's root-mean-square distance at seeds 3 and 8, 5.063 against a window of 4.747 to 5.057; two 1,000-row session tables missed a tail distance the same way at seed 2 on d93fd43, hidden on this landing by step 9's summed window with the ranks still outside. **The decision.** A run moves whole only onto an instant inside its ROOM, the gap of every rank of it, wherever it is offered one -- a neighbour, the nearest held unit of its standing, a neighbour read again, a trade (method G7.3, `_run_room`, the oracle's `run_room`). **Measured after**, e4a5d34 against the fix: 600 twins of 300 random date and clock columns went from 18 ranks outside their gaps in 9 twins and 2 misses to none, 12 twins of the four session tables from 9 ranks in 7 twins to none; on those batteries no twin gained a miss and none changed its count of different units, and the 420 twins of the two filled-range batteries are unchanged. That was true of those batteries only (the landing's third skeptic): over 1,600 twins of 800 more random and small dense date columns, five twins of three columns gained a miss of both distinct counts that shipped stage 3 and e4a5d34 met with ranks outside their gaps -- 83 dates over 59 days, 37 different, came back holding 41 and 43 at floor 36, seeds 3 and 8; 141 dates holding 37 against 36 at both; 104 dates holding 61 against 60 at floor 50, seed 3 -- each through tail runs whose strata meet on one day, whose room is that day, so that no merge can take them. Nine frozen cases of three vectors files move, each a tail run the pass had merged past a rank's stratum, and the shipped generator writes the rebuilt cells. Guarded by the gapped year of `tests/test_stage3b_gate.py`, the `run` witness of `tests/test_oracle_rule_witnesses.py` with four mutants, the nine cases and `K-S3-39`. **The split** (method G7.3, `_runs_split`, the oracle's `runs_split`): once the merges and both trades leave the count over, in rank order, a run of two or more ranks on one unit, none pinned and alone on it, between two ranks, whose room holds no other unit ranks hold of its standing, gives its unit up rank by rank -- its ranks, in order, onto the instant of the rank just below it while that lies inside each one's own gap, the rest onto the instant of the rank just above it, each of its standing, and only where every rank has one. The room clause is not idle: without it three frozen cases of two files move where trades have reshuffled ranks. **Measured after**, c8de51b against the split, over 2,665 twins of 1,131 seeded date and clock columns (those 1,600, the 600 above rebuilt, 285 of 19 fixed shapes and the 180 of the 12 filled shapes): the five meet both counts, no twin gains a miss, no rank stands outside its gap, 8 twins' bytes move; against e4a5d34, no new miss, 20 misses gone, 342 ranks outside their gaps in 166 twins to none, and one twin missed on both trees, 104 dates at floor 50 and seed 8, holds 63 different days where e4a5d34 held 61 against 60. The 240 twins of the writer's battery keep every count and verdict, and the 12 session twins their verdicts. Three frozen cases of two vectors files move, each a run the split now gives up -- `date_traded_merge` and `date_gap_places` hold one different value fewer (13 against published 3 and 10, counts no twin of theirs reaches) and `date_second_field_class` meets its 18 with eleven cells placed otherwise -- and the shipped generator writes the rebuilt cells. Guarded by the small dense column of `tests/test_stage3b_gate.py`, four more `run` rows with five oracle mutants, the three cases and `K-S3-39`. **The stack** (method G7.3, `_ranks_restacked`, the oracle's `ranks_restacked`; the landing's fourth skeptic): over 2,400 twins of 400 more random and small dense date and clock columns at floors 11, 36 and 50, two twins gained a miss of both distinct counts against e4a5d34 and d93fd43 that the split does not repair -- 123 midnight moments over 111 days, 52 different, holding 54 at floor 50, seeds 3 and 8; 77 month-first dates over 48 days, 33 different, holding 35 at floor 36, seed 3 -- and the 104-date twin holding 63 above was of the same kind: tail ranks in pairs on alternate days whose strata shift by one rank each, each pair's room its own day and its neighbours two days off, which give a day up only as a chain, each pair moving one day onto the next; a placement inside every gap holding the count existed and validated for each. So once a round's merges, both trades and the split move nothing and the count is still over, the ranks are stacked afresh: taken by their gaps' upper ends, then lower ends, then rank, a pinned rank's gap being its own instant, each rank joins the unit last stacked for its standing where that lies inside its gap, else stacks the highest unit of its standing inside it -- the fewest units any placement inside every gap keeping every standing can hold -- sorted within each unpinned run with every rank inside its gap, raised in rank order onto the nearest free unit of its standing until the count is met, and taken only where that meets it. **Measured after**, b9e63c9 against the stack: over those 2,400 twins the five that a placement could meet do (the two above, and 103 dates holding 64 and 65 against 60 at floor 50), no twin gains a miss, no rank stands outside its gap and only those five twins' bytes move; over 1,600 twins of the third skeptic's 800 columns the 104-date twin meets its 60 and nothing else moves; against e4a5d34 and d93fd43, 27 and 55 misses gone on the 2,400 and none new. What stays unmet there no placement inside the gaps reaches -- 127 dates at floor 50 hold 48 against 41 where the fewest any placement holds is 46 -- or is the derived-end limit above. No frozen case reaches the stack (every vectors file rebuilds byte for byte), so it is witnessed by the two columns of `tests/test_stage3b_gate.py`, five `run` rows with nine oracle mutants and `K-S3-39`; the split's two clauses no row had parted (alone on its unit, at most owed) and its standing on each way gain four rows and two mutants there. The raise's own clauses no row parted in either road (the landing's fifth skeptic) -- inside its gap, of its standing, only a rank sharing its unit, a pinned rank passed by -- gain four more rows and four oracle mutants, and the generator's four mutants of them turn the shipped rows red. **The gap rule's cost, and its repair.** "No twin gains a miss" held on the batteries above only (the landing's fifth skeptic). Over 1,860 twins of 310 more random, chain-prone and clock-pool date and clock columns at floors 11, 36 and 50, seeds 3 and 8, five twins of three columns missed both distinct counts that shipped stage 3 and e4a5d34 met and validated: 123 ISO dates over 56 days, 24 different, held 26 at floor 36, seeds 3 and 8; 123 month-first dates over 92 days, 35 different, held 38 the same way; 114 midnight moments over 140 days, 43 different, held 46 at floor 50, seed 8. The earlier trees met them only with 3, 8 and 12 tail ranks a day below their strata, and no placement inside every gap reaches them: the fewest days any holds is 25, 37 and 44. They missed from 604ebbd on, which held 27, 42 or 43, and 55: the cost was the gap rule's, which the split and the stack bring closer and cannot close. **The call** (the orchestrator's call of 2026-09-28, not an owner ruling; the owner may reverse it): where no placement with every rank inside its gap can meet the distinct count, a tail rank may leave its stratum by the least amount that meets it, and only where the tail's published windows and every other published check still hold -- which is what shipped stage 3 did on those twins, and they validated clean. **The decision** (method G7.3, `_count_met_past_the_strata`, the oracle's `count_met_past_the_strata`): where the count passes leave the count over and even the stack holds more units than it, the ranks take the stack and give units up one at a time -- a run of the stack's ranks, none pinned, alone on its unit and between two ranks, splits, its lower ranks onto the instant of the rank just below it and the rest onto the instant of the rank just above it, each of its own standing, where each lands inside its gap or, being an unpinned rank of a tail drawn through its shape, strictly beyond its tail's boundary; of every split on offer the one whose rank farthest outside its gap stands least far outside it, then the fewest ranks outside, then the lower run, then more ranks down -- and take the result only where the count is then met and every such tail's summed distance and summed square lie inside G12.14's window. ## Decision P4-D355 — the weekday census of a column of dates (stage 3b landing 3b.1, 2026-09-26)

**The gap.** A column of dates came back with its days of the week spread evenly: the description carried no fact about them, so a clinic open on weekdays came back with a weekend, and every count per weekday computed on the twin was the twin's own.

**The decision.** A column of whole dates read on the local clock, with both tails and one text per date, publishes `weekday_census`: the cells between its two tail boundaries, both included, counted per group of weekdays. The grouping is chosen by the census line alone from a MENU of three -- each weekday alone; Monday to Friday alone with the weekend together; the weekdays together and the weekend together -- and no other rule chooses one, because a rule merging a SPECIFIC short weekday into its neighbour tells a reader that weekday held fewer than the line together with it, so no day of it could hold the line in any table consistent with the rule. The census is published only where the FULL-FILL CERTIFICATE holds (contract WC8, `calendar_certificate`): every class of a counted weekday -- a boundary or rung day, or the days of one stretch between two of them falling on one weekday, less its HOLES: the days the table's declared missing values name, the days the censuses of written forms leave empty (`calendar_rules.form_holes`) and a placeholder day the block publishes as `read_as_missing` (`calendar_rules.placeholder_holes`) -- has a WITNESS, a table meeting every published fact, what the grouping tells and the body's real count of different days, holding the line on one day of the class; a class with none is withheld where stage 3's facts alone could fill it, and otherwise is RESIDUE, whose every configuration stage 3 allows the census must allow. Every fact is unchanged by exchanging two days of one class, and a hole belongs to no class, so no set of days of any shape is confined inside one to the line less one by the census. The loader asks the same certificate on the reader's own bounds and the form and placeholder holes, and refuses a census that fails it; the producer publishes only what its loader accepts. `weekday_census` is EXACT-OBSERVABLE: the file's own cells between the two published boundaries hold every group's published count exactly, and the validator counts them and never produces a census. The twin meets the census by moving body ranks inside their own gaps (method G7.3f), keeping every tail, rung, width kind and hole, and putting its count of different days back.

**Measured before building** (the design's prototype, `design-v4.md`): the certificate here gives the prototype's verdict on 201 of 201 date columns of its fixture sets and on 449 of 449 tiny bodies, and certifies the monthly visit of the battery in 3,907 network solves where the prototype took 7,814. **After**: the battery's six date columns at 1,000 rows publish all six censuses and every twin at seeds 0 and 4 validates with nothing missed and its weekday statistics inside the gate's scoped bounds; the brute force finds no published census confining a set of days; the oracle mirrors the pass from G7.3f's text and agrees with the generator cell for cell on 54 seeded columns of three shapes and spellings; on the loss battery's admissions the twin's weekend share reads 14.8 per cent against 14.7 real where it read 28.5, and its weekday distance 0.002 where it read 0.139. Step 3's prior was rewritten once: with the calendar a trace beside the drawn ranks, a clinic's few Tuesday cells piled into one gap and 39 of 306 seeded twins missed their count of different days; with the ranks and the calendar weighing the same, 0. **Not in this landing** (design SECTION 9): date columns whose rows cannot put the line on one day, columns of few dates whose squeezed stretches are wide, dense logs the census would narrow, and groupings beyond the menu are withheld and say why; timestamp columns publish `[]` until landing 3b.2. Guarded by `tests/test_stage3b_gate.py`, the loader's WC1 to WC8 mutations, the frozen cases of G14.3 and `K-S3-31` to `K-S3-33`.

**Repaired at review (2026-09-28).** The premise that every published fact is unchanged by exchanging two days of one class was false where a census of written forms names a form that only some days can be written in. WC6 asks every such census to name one form holding every parsed cell, so `date_field_widths {first-field-unpadded}` on `m/d/yyyy` tells a reader that no cell falls on the first to the ninth of a month (such a cell would show a joint word, into which the one-field word folds, or the day's own word), and a month name of length `either` tells a reader that every cell is in May. The certificate had put witnesses on those days. Measured on b994990: 104 visits written `m/d/yyyy`, two a day on every day past the ninth, published `[Mon] 12 [Tue] 14 [Wed] 14 [Thu] 14 [Fri] 12 [Sat-Sun] 16`, and a reader who held the holes and the count of different days put every one of the 41 open days between 1 and 9 rows; 149 dates over three Mays published the seven counts and left all 71 open days between 1 and 10; the verifier passed every witness. `calendar_rules.form_holes` now states those holes once, from the published censuses. The producer asks the certificate and WC7 with them beside the declared days, the loader with them alone, and the verifier derives them in its own code. Both columns are now withheld, `narrowed`, and the census copied onto either description is refused on load (WC8); a column whose dates all fall in October to December of one year, or in one May, has no hole between its boundaries and is unchanged. The same review added a witness to each rule that had none: a MISSED line prints no group count below the line, the reader's fewest days take away every unparsed cell, and a day written with a trailing blank counts as two spellings. `K-S3-31` is a headline in place of `K-2B-22b`, as the design's KPI table set it; the landing had left it off without saying so, and the cap stays 30. A second review (2026-09-28) found two gaps. And a placeholder day `sentinel_verdicts` publishes as `read_as_missing` is a hole the design names and the code did not hold: on a column whose body runs from December 1899 every witness stood on 1900-01-01. `calendar_rules.placeholder_holes` now states that hole once, the producer and the loader read it off the block, and the verifier derives it in its own code; no pin was found, and a column around the day whose Mondays the hole leaves three dates is withheld, `few_dates`, its census refused on load (WC7).

## Decision P4-D356 — a lone pool stands only where no reading the block admits pins it (the reviews of follow-up B, 2026-09-28; its final fix, 2026-09-29)

**The decision.** `parsing.mixture_pool_holds` decides every census that pools because no name reaches the line: the mixture censuses and, through `census_pools`, the forms, the decimals', padded and unpadded widths, the offsets and the day-clock marks. A pool stands only where, over every reading -- each name under the line and its capacity, no more names than the pooled cells' spellings, each placed value on no more names than its own spellings, two values free to share one -- any name could be absent and no count is in every reading; a width only a placed value can stand on is shown by the block. The producer places the mode, a tail's values and each value a body rung reads, with true rows and spellings; the loader (NS2, TM1, P6, P6b, P6c, D3, D12) what the mode, the rungs and a listed tail publish, and admits a walk stopped short. A pool that may not stand, or whose walk stops short, is counted under the commonest name every cell can wear -- a band of forms with the widths of the table written wholly in it, unpadded widths at the commonest every placed value stands at. Where no width holds them all, a band says what the pool says, and the pool stands unless the room alone pins it. The comma warning beside a comma band says NF61 for its either-way count, or NF87 ("some") where the band counts every present cell, so the table writing every counted cell with a comma says the same (P4-D347; the orchestrator's decision (i)).

**Measured.** Every review shape red at its base (`tests/test_lone_pools_every_reader.py`). Over 1,200 seeded pool shapes every description loads; 24 of 38 pools of decimals' widths and 23 of 44 of padded widths name a width. Over 597 seeded whole-number columns 12 of 81 field-width pools name one, none refused, no twin misses more; counted at the commonest width alone 45 did, and 5 twins missed their listed tails at every seed. Over 300 shapes of the review rounds' families one census moves; design B's K1 and S1, and one of 500 near-pool shapes, name the comma where they were silent.

**Costs, the owner's to choose.** Fraction bands make the cost rule list both tails 410841a withheld in 5 of 503 shapes; the twins of `frac-100` and `frac-wide` miss `tails.low.values` at every seed (`frac-wide` also `tails.high.values` at seed 1), 410841a's none, and the loader admits a hand pool of `frac-wide`'s widths. In the twin battery (232 shapes) 9 width bands list tail values the carrier walk rounds away, and 5 columns miss their role. The producer reads a clock's own spellings where many dates bound nothing for a reader.

## Decision P4-D359 — the weekday census's third review, repaired (stage 3b landing 3b.1, 2026-09-28 and 29)

**The rules.** The certificate's stage-3 side holds no census information, a weekday counted empty included. Every withholding the table's own numbers decide is said in one sentence (NF74) and stands only where W0 -- the tables whose weekend, or Monday to Friday, lies in its BAND, always withheld -- is certified as a census is, on classes of one stretch's half of the week (`_pooled`). Any certified W0 will do, so each half's band is searched on its own: from the larger of one and the least that half holds in any table of stage 3's facts, through that and its own rows more, each at most the line plus what its capped stretches take; the pair taken is the certified one of least summed width a walk finds that reads a wider band as never certifying less, fewer Monday-to-Friday rows first on a tie. Where the widest pair does not certify, one width past the capped stretches (82b1f1a's) is asked, and where that does not, the census is withheld whatever it holds; the loader refuses a total at a half's least (WC9), which every band holds. A report prints no count of a census that has one below the line, names no short group where naming pins one, and shows a written-form verdict only where its printed ranges settle it. One rule states a description's holes (`calendar_rules.public_holes`) for the producer, loader, day pass, validator and oracle; a body date on one misses the census. The day pass puts the count of different days back across groups too (G7.3f step 8.3); where no placement the day pass can make keeps both, the count gives way and the report says so, naming the twin's own tails where they fell short. One spelling per day is asked of the cells' own texts; a census beside workbook classes storing two ways is refused (WC6); a refusal the published numbers decide walks no day.

**Measured.** Over 56 date columns 43 censuses publish where 2af1f03 published 44, the one lost being the review's attack. Over 269 schedules, clinics, weekend markets and business logs, 165 publish where 2af1f03 published 166; the band at its widest, the line past the least, published 162, losing markets with 30 to 40 Wednesday rows. All 5,621 W0 tables its certificates lay out pass the verifier, and the brute force finds no withheld set confining a day; describing costs 6 per cent more solves, loading nothing. Of the review's 505 heaped twins, ten lost a day to the census; none does now. Searched a half at a time, over the skeptic's 80 markets, logs and clinics and 120 markets, rebuilt seeded, 2af1f03 publishes 51 and 69, one width 47 and 65, the halves 50 and 69; the one left, a one-weekday clinic, and 22 of 369 Tuesday clinics of 212 rows are withheld by their census's own certificate (`narrowed`) under every option. Over 459 tiny fact sets the brute force finds no unsound outcome (45 published, one width 44); bands at the least taken uncertified give 4. The withholding spends about twice the solves.

**Calls and costs.** The band search is the orchestrator's engineering under the floor rule, reversible, not an owner ruling; the owner was told the per-half search would be built, as it costs no privacy and publishes more. The owner, 2026-09-29, "Keep as built": the certificate keeps its band and its 20,000-arrangement cap, so weekly Wednesday sessions whose residue passes the cap (`_weekly_schedule(60)`) stay withheld whatever they hold, where a cap of 40,000 published them at 82b1f1a in 371,273 solves, 66 s to describe. The owner, 2026-09-30, "Accept as a limit": a withheld census may tell a reader that the weekend, or Monday to Friday, holds 1 to 10 rows -- a range, never a value, a date or a row (`K-S3-34`).

**The cap, measured (2026-09-30).** Told that the cap also withholds Tuesday clinics, the owner answered "Measure, then raise": raise it where it frees them at about a minute a column, and ask again where the time is much larger. It holds 13 of 369 Tuesday clinics of 212 rows, 12 of which 2af1f03 published, and 24 of 489 with the skeptic's 120. Every column it stops, described at each cap, in solves and in seconds at a load of 7 to 11, or 3 to 6.5 where quiet:

| cap | clinics published, of 369 and of 120 | of the 24, held by the cap | freed | weekly sessions |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 20,000 | 243 and 90 | 24 | none | withheld, 71 solves |
| 40,000 | 244 and 92 | 18 | 3, at 140,384 to 220,246 solves, 30 to 48 s quiet | published, 1,393,635 solves, 340 s quiet |
| 80,000 | 245 and 93 | 16 | 5, at up to 620,136 solves, 186 s | published |
| 160,000 | 251 and 94 | 9 | 12, at up to 1,369,300 solves, 440 s | published |

From 40,000 three of the 24 stay withheld past the cap, by a certificate that does not hold, one after 810,065 solves (198 s quiet). The skeptic's 80 markets, logs and clinics and 120 markets publish 50 and 69 at every cap, and every census a raised cap publishes loads back equal, under 20,000 too. The sessions' cost is 67ba1de's: searching a half at a time took them from 371,273 solves to 1,393,635, 3.75 times, about 5.5 to 6 minutes. A cap of 40,000 adds about 6 to 9 minutes to the suite and one of 160,000 about 9.5 to 12, unless the test holding the sessions withheld takes another column. No cap frees them all at about a minute a column: 40,000 frees three so, but spends about 5.5 minutes on the sessions and 3.3 on a clinic it still withholds, and nine stay held at 160,000. ## Decision P4-D362 — every NEW commit message is scanned (2026-09-30)

**The owner's answer, verbatim.** The owner first asked "What is the risk of this?", was told that the words were already public many times over and that rewriting would change about 100 commit ids the ledger cites, and answered "Push now, add a guard" (2026-09-30). The question the owner answered said three matches; the guard's own count of the 134 commits pushed at `82b1f1a` is 14 matches in 13 of them, the same three words, each already public before them (104 matches in 87 of the 646 messages up to `d93fd43`).

**The rule.** `tools/hooks/check_messages.py` applies the attested scanner's own manifest, decoder, tokenizer and n-gram match to commit messages, line by line and value-silent: a message file (the commit-msg hook), a revision range, or every commit the grandfather commit `82b1f1a` does not reach (CI's decontam job and the pre-push hook). A shallow clone, or a history without the grandfather, is refused, never passed. `tools/decontamination/` is not touched: the attestation still verifies.

**Whose call each is.** Keeping the 134 commits pushed at `82b1f1a` unrewritten is the owner's "Push now, add a guard". Not rewriting the 646 older public messages is the orchestrator's call, reversible, and so are these: the file sits outside the attested tree; the grandfather is the tip as pushed; a checkout older than the scanner is told, not stopped.

## Decision P4-D363 — counts worked out within one column, and the owner's principle (2026-09-30 and 2026-10-01)

**"Accept the class" (2026-09-30).** Asked whether to keep closing, one by one, the ways a determined reader combines several published facts WITHIN ONE COLUMN to work out a count below 11 ("exactly 10 rows wrote the comma", "the value 45 is held by 5 rows"), the question adding "It never shows which row, or anything across two columns" -- a table sorted by the column does show the row, through its `row_order` (P4-D353) -- the owner chose "Accept the class (Recommended)", whose text read, verbatim: "Your accepted limit, like 'Accept both': every number the description prints still meets the floor; a count worked out by combining several facts within one column is accepted. The second push goes now (the crash fix, the weekday band, the guard, the record corrections); the fidelity-costly pool fix is set aside." Its "every number the description prints still meets the floor" is false: P4-D332 (the orchestrator, 2026-09-22) keeps the odd-kind, sign and pair `count` leaves of 1 to 10 printed, 65 over the 46-shape battery at floor 11 (`K-S3-12`, OPEN at its ceiling).

**The decision.** Within one column, a count below 11 worked out by combining several published facts is accepted; across columns, nothing is. The pool fix of branch `next-fix-P` (P4-D360) was set aside and never landed.

**The owner's principle (2026-10-01), verbatim.** "Go for the second push. Regarding the choice, it's weird this choice to me. Imagine that you are a researcher that is just needing to use your dataset with AI do develop statistical code! This code should be reliable, with good statistical results for as many as possible statistical tests and this twin needs to be built in an accptable time. The only privacy concern is to not have a hippaa violation. TO not have AI reading a whole picture that would be considered a violation....  We don't need to think that someone will try to discovery the data with the twin, that 's not the case!!!! Let's build with this principle!"

**The orchestrator's call, reversible.** That privacy concern does not lift any rule: HIPAA and the institution's own rules still apply to the real table and to the six files a run leaves. What the principle sets aside is a reader reconstructing the data from its description. In this push the weekday cap stays at 20,000, as nothing untested goes in (P4-D359). The next landing re-weighs every guard that exists only against such a reader, starting with the weekday certificate, for statistics and build time.

## Decision P4-D365 — the weekday guards dropped (stage 3b landing 3b.G, 2026-10-02)

**Why.** Under the owner's principle of 2026-10-01 (P4-D363) and his rule that a guard goes only at a high price, the orchestrator dropped every weekday guard that stood only against a reader combining published facts (the build plan's call (a)). Measured on 7b5f698, they withheld 366 of 1,147 censuses, left the twins' weekday share .123 from the real one against .036 without them, and spent 1,159 s describing against 67 s.

**The decision.** `calendar_certificate.py` is deleted: the full-fill certificate, the withholding's certificate and bands, the 20,000-arrangement cap and the ties refusal, with the loader's WC5, WC7, WC8 and WC9. The loader holds a census to WC1 to WC4 and WC6 through `calendar_rules.shape_breach`. The producer withholds a census where a non-empty group holds fewer than three different real dates, or fewer than seven and a half a group on average over two or more non-empty groups (the orchestrator's B1 set seven, for payroll on the 15th and the last day, 6.9 a group, 53 days for 48; its review found one date a month over 51 to 54 months, 7.00 to 7.43 a group, 53 or 54 days for 52, and raised it). Beside every published hole but a width hole -- May's holes where the month-name census holds every cell to May, placeholder days and declared days -- it withholds too where a non-empty group has no free day while it holds a one-row date (the room rule; every day of three Mays came back 83 for 93). Its review measured no column past the ninth that needed it, so it is not asked beside width holes alone; its second review found a column with a date on every day of 240 but five declared missing (`decl4_240_5_2_r1`) whose twins came back 234 different days for 235 once the rule was left off beside declared days, so the orchestrator asked it there again: a twin must pass its own checks, and the weekday share on columns with declared missing days stays withheld as at 668f276 until D0's shared count steps can keep both the census and the count of different days. NF71 says the counts are of days of the week and never of one date, every group that holds rows on three dates at least; NF73 is retired with the ties refusal; NF74 is kept. The validator counts a moment on its day where the file's own description folded it into the dates (P4-D250), and not where it left it unparsed, so the source meets its own census either way.

**Measured** after the second review, on twenty-one batteries (1,867 date columns, seeds 0 to 4; the second review's holes3 and holes4 added, 150 columns between width holes or beside declared days), 668f276 against this landing: censuses published 983 to 1,390; twins with a MISSED check 111 to 106 of 9,305, none new (the unreviewed landing had 184 new, all one date a month or payroll, and the first repair 12, all beside declared days); weekday-share error 0.096 to 0.044; describe 1,505 s to 200 s on a loaded machine. Its stated cost: 50 columns 668f276 published with every twin meeting are withheld, 18 by the few-dates rule and 32 by the room rule (6 Mays and 26 beside declared days). Neither rule can be asked on load.

**KPIs.** `K-S3-32` is floor-only, `K-S3-33` is retired with the certificate, `K-S3-35` is new, `K-S3-39`'s drawn-hole node asks the count pass on its census emptied and holds the published census to its twins, `K-2B-13` is green again and `K-2B-48`'s counter skips a census group's bin indices.

**Its Codex review, item 1: a missed census is not said to be met.** A description the loader accepts can publish a census its own tail boundaries make impossible -- 400 rows of 1 January to 9 April 2024, four to a date, its census edited to Monday to Saturday nought and Sunday the whole body, between a Thursday and a Saturday boundary. Its twin at seed 0 filed `weekday_census` as a deviation while the sentence on how the column is spread said "the published counts per day of the week are met": `_weekday_spread` said so wherever a census was published. The sentence is now read off the day pass's own measurement (`_spread_remarks` is handed the facts the column's completed pass filed as deviations): a missed census is said to be not met, and the weekday is not called unpublished. No loader rule is restored; no twin byte moves. Pinned by `tests/test_stage3b_weekday_review.py::test_a_census_the_twin_misses_is_not_said_to_be_met`.

**Its Codex review, item 2: the two rules are conservative, and say so.** The contract called what the producer withholds "what no twin can meet", and the few-dates rule's text said the day pass meets such a census "only by splitting a date's rows". Neither holds: 1 to 21 January 2024, a hundred rows a date, is withheld by the few-dates rule, and its census restored is met at seeds 0 to 2 with all 21 dates, no generation deviation and no approximation outside its bound, the weekday groups HELD. The few-dates and room rules are conservative rules set on the cases measured where a twin missed; their price is the 50 columns counted above whose twins all met a census now withheld, and the thresholds (three dates a group, seven and a half on average) stay. The contract, `calendar_rules.few_dates`, `calendar_rules.room_short`, their reasons' comments and `taxonomy.weekday_decision` say so. Pinned by `tests/test_stage3b_weekday_review.py::test_the_few_dates_rule_withholds_a_census_its_twins_meet_and_is_called_conservative`.

## Decision P4-D366 — one weekday pass for every census of bins (stage 3b landing D0, 2026-10-02)

**What it is** (the build plan's lane D0, with PLAN.skeptic M1 and M2 and the 3b.3 skeptic's major 5). Method G7.3f's day pass becomes ONE pass over any census of bins (`generation._bins_settled`), so the hour (T2), the weekday of timestamps (D2), the day of the month (D3) and the heavy dates (D4) build on it rather than writing it again. Its state (`_WeekdayPass`) takes seams: a UNIT of any size in ordinals (a date's day 1, a moment's day 86,400, an hour 3,600, a minute 60) whose candidates are whole units away, so a move keeps a rank's place inside its unit; a WRITTEN UNIT, the count of different values being the count of written units held; a DAY for holes and width kinds; `bin_of` and its period; `keep_of`, what every move keeps besides (the day, for a census of hours); and `pair_of`, a second census's group. The weekday census of dates is the pass with every seam at its old value. Steps 5 and 6 search an index of each gap's units by group and kind, the same candidates in the same order as the walk of 400 units (the 3b.3 skeptic's minor 1, n^1.5 to linear); step 8.3 asks every cycle up to seven groups and cycles of at most three above. Four steps are added: 7b CHAIN (paths of single moves through a third group, at most 256), 8.4 UNITS MERGED (a whole written unit merged at its own clock first, the 3b.2-W skeptic's minor 2), 8.5 LONG PAIRS (3b.6's post-pass) and 8.6 THE TWO-CENSUS EXCHANGE (3b.3's blocker 1 (b)). A count the pass leaves long is named as long (`_WEEKDAY_DAYS_LEFT_LONG`) wherever the twin's recounted values are long too, and the folded count's line beside it names the same cause.

**Proof: at the default floor no twin moves** (M2: "identical wherever the D1 head meets every fact"), measured by the landing's review on 717fabe and again on the repaired head, each table described once and its twins written by both, every twin with its deviations, approximations and remarks set against 110cb46's. On 26 date batteries -- skep-weekday's sources, D1's witnesses, D1's reviewers' monthly3, payroll2 and attack2, 3,000 random columns of 90 to 160 dates, the published fixtures, the stage 3 battery's 46 shapes, the 56 date-question shapes, `kpi_shapes` family B with dotted dates and joined, and the gate battery at 40,000 rows: 4,782 tables -- all 15,152 twins at the floor of 11 are byte-identical, and none of the four steps moves a rank. At a floor of 36, 15,144 are. The other eight -- monthly3's `first_2020_60m` (seeds 0 and 4) and `last_2017_60m` (seed 1), sched120's `sched92` (seeds 0 to 2) and `sched97` (seed 0), sparse80's `sparse62` (seed 2) -- are columns whose count of different values 110cb46 already left LONG, and steps 8.4 and 8.5 bring it nearer the published count, every missed check the same: 63 and 68 different values for 65 and 69 against 60 published, 52 for 53 against 46, 49 for 50 against 48, 44 for 45 against 39. That is M2's rule; the landing's sentences that no column of dates reaches the new steps were not, and are restated. The reports move only where a count is left long: on those eight and 51 more twins at the floor of 36 (none at 11) the lines for the count of different values and its folded count name the day pass's cause where 110cb46 printed the general long sentence, every other line the same. Every committed vectors file rebuilds byte for byte through the changed oracle. Columns reach the steps that rarely, so they are frozen on states of ranks: `tests/reference/generation-branch-vectors-15.json` (the numbering table's file 15) holds 40, the landing's ten, among them the hour-unit case M1 asks for, the review's 24 -- each new step once through `_bins_settled`, and a state for every clause a reviewer's mutant changed while the ten still passed -- and the second review's six, one for each line of the repair whose mutant changed an answer while the 34 still held (step 8.2's round, step 8.5's early stop, the rank its tables list on the unit it joins, its count of a unit's holders and its distance from the gaps' first places, and step 8.3's cycle undone last move first, which that review's random states had not reached) -- each with the answer the oracle (`bins_settled`) computes from the method's text. `tests/test_stage3b_shared_steps.py` holds the product to each, turns each red on its own mutant, the reviewer's by id, and holds `sched92` at the floor of 36, red with step 8.5 withdrawn.

**The declared days stay withheld** (the note of P4-D365). On holes3 and holes4 rebuilt from D1-skeptic2's recipe (114 columns, the witness `decl4_240_5_2_r1` reproduced at 433 rows and 235 present days), with the room rule not asked, every census publishes and 64 of 570 twins (25 columns) miss the count of different values, the witness 234 for 235 at seeds 0, 1 and 4, where with it asked, as at 110cb46, 42 of the same twins miss and no other; this landing's twins give the same verdicts as 110cb46's on all 570. The census stays withheld beside declared days because every one of the 64 is SHORT, each day it leaves empty lying past a tail boundary among the dates the twin writes for its tails, which no step of G7.3f moves, while steps 8.4 and 8.5 merge only a count that is LONG.

**Measured cost.** The stage 3b gate battery at 40,000 rows, generation at seed 0, alternated twice with 110cb46 under the same load (about 47): the pass takes 2.4 to 2.8 s for 3.8 to 4.0 on admissions, 3.2 to 3.5 for 13.0 to 14.8 on heaps and 13.4 to 14.1 for 25.6 to 26.6 on schedules, every twin byte-identical. What is left on schedules is mostly step 8.1's own walk of 64 units (`_weekday_nearest`), untouched here. Step 8.5 as landed built its cells again for every pair, and steps 8.2 and 8.4 counted the column's different values again for every unit (the review, item 6); step 8.5 now tables its cells once and updates the four written units a pair touches, and steps 8.2 and 8.4 keep their count, each answer unchanged (23,000 random states against the landed steps, and steps 8.4 and 8.5 against the oracle). On lone moments 400 too long, two groups and ten cells, step 8.5 takes 0.09 s at 20,000 ranks where it took 16.0, and 5.3 s at 984,379 ranks and the cap of 512 pairs (692 MB at peak); on 199,372 lone moments 20,000 too long steps 8.4 and 8.2 take 2.1 and 5.2 s, where the landed steps had merged 4,262 and 149 units by 100 s. **What step 8.5 costs beyond two groups** (the second review, item 4), for landing D3 to budget: a pair asks every two cells and every two groups, and its early stop holds only where two cells share their gap's first place, as cells of one gap on different days do where a census of hours keeps the day. On 199,685 lone moments 2,000 too long, twenty cells and the cap of 512 pairs take 60.7 s with the 31 days of the month as groups and 3.3 s with the seven weekdays, and 5.8 s at 984,379 ranks; on the hour seam with the day kept, 739 cells, 0.5 to 2.2 s. At 984,379 ranks one pair peaks at 752 MB, 457 MB of it the step's own tables, where the step as landed (717fabe) peaked at 455 MB, 153 MB of it its own. Searching cell B by its gap's first place among the cells that hold both groups, rather than asking every cell, would make a pair's work grow with the cells rather than with their square; it is not built here, and D3, which first asks step 8.5 of 31 groups, decides it on its own battery.

**What the review's repair adds.** Step 8.3's cycle is made whole or not at all (method G7.3f): on a unit of more than one ordinal a cell's end units are its gap's partly, a move could find no place there, and the cycle was left half made -- one rank across groups and none back, the census broken, and the product then skipped step 8.6 where the oracle traded. The repair's own search over random states of every step and seam turned it up; no date's day reaches it, and product and oracle agree on 64,000 such states since. `_weekday_traded` states its early stop (item 5). The suite lock's owner read (item 7) is outside the repository.

**Its Codex review, item 1: step 8.3's gain counts written units.** The take asked whether a whole UNIT of a group stood free, while a move keeps a rank's place inside its unit and the count is of written units, and the oracle asked the same. Forty ranks each at 00:15, 01:15 and 02:30 of one day -- a unit of an hour, minutes written, the day kept, each hour a group -- asked for eighty in hour 1, forty in hour 2 and three values, kept 80 at 01:15 and 40 at 02:30 through `_bins_settled`, two values, while 01:30 and 02:15 stood free. Method G7.3f, the product and the oracle now ask each group's MOVER in a cell (`_weekday_mover`: the rank on the written unit holding the most, the one its move takes) for the places it may take inside its gap at its own place in its unit, a place free where its written unit is (`_weekday_take(state, key, group, rank)`, one argument more); step 7b's link asks the same. That state keeps three values and the census (80 at 01:15, 1 at 02:15, 39 at 02:30) and is frozen in the fifteenth vectors file, now 47 states, with six more: a free second on a held day, each step's mover, a link past its gap, and the two states the landing's reviews froze a cycle undone on, which offer no cycle now that the take asks the mover's own places. A cycle is still undone where a move changes the mover of the group it reaches -- the rank moved stands on that group's most-held written unit, or ties it lower in rank order, and has no place of the next group -- so `a_cycle_undone` and `a_cycle_undone_last_move_first` are restated on two such states (M83 and N14 red on them), and M09 and M10 pin the count of each unit's ranks through its one reader now, the short cause's test of a full body. On a date's day a unit is one written unit and every rank of a cell has the same places, so the take is the day's: the 1,506 tables of the identity batteries (4,782 twins at the floor of 11) generate byte for byte as at 9cb2eb5, every answer of the 40 states stands, and product and oracle agree on 3,000 random states of the whole pass over dates, days of moments and hours and on 60,000 of steps 7b and 8.3. Pinned by `tests/test_stage3b_shared_steps.py::test_step_8_3_counts_the_written_units_its_mover_can_take`, red on 9cb2eb5, with C1a to C1d in its mutant table.

**Its Codex review, item 2: where the day is kept, a search asks that day alone.** A gap of D days kept by the day has D cells, and step 8.3's take built every unit of a group across the whole gap for each cell before its kind refused all but one day's: two ranks a day at 00:01 over D days, one at 01:01 on the first, each hour a group, every rank asked in hour 0 and D + 1 values kept, built 24 D squared entries -- 24,576, 98,304 and 393,216 at 32, 64 and 128 days. The take builds 24 entries a day, 768 at 32 days and 480,000 at 20,000 days (40,000 rows), whose whole pass takes about 3 s, and product and oracle agree on 6,000 more random whole-pass states. Pinned by `test_step_8_3_asks_only_the_retained_day`, red on 9cb2eb5 at 32 days.

**Its Codex review, items 3 to 5: steps 8.4 and 8.5 and the index grow with the rows.** On one rank at every hour's :01 over D days, day zero's 01:01 on 00:01, D asked in each hour and N - 1 values kept, step 8.4's same-clock search walked every day of its gap for each unit and its other-clock places were read again from the column for each group and day -- 28,920, 115,440 and 461,280 reads of a group at 120, 240 and 480 rows -- and step 8.5, finding no pair, asked every two day cells, 36,000, 154,800 and 640,800 reads of its tables. Step 8.5 indexes, before any pair, the cells holding a source of each group (`lone_in`, `shared_in`) and counts the cells holding a source of one group beside a place of another (`lone_with`, `shared_with`), and asks a second cell only where one other than the first can raise the pair already found: 27 reads a row, and 119 a day where days holding 00:01 and 01:01 alone alternate with days holding 01:01 and 02:01 twice each, which the sources' index alone still asked two by two (144, 244 and 444 a day at 40, 80 and 160 days on 9cb2eb5). A gap past the rule is walked, step 6's walk stopping, as the index's search does, at a count-keeping place holding the fewest ranks one may; a gap of up to 801 units is indexed as before. Step 3's prior still counts a gap's units one by one where bins do not follow one another unit by unit, about 4 s for 32 million minutes, for the landing that first writes minutes to budget. No answer moves: product and oracle agree, 40,000 random states -- the whole pass, and steps 8.4 and 8.5 asked one, two and five values long -- answer as at 1098376, and the identity batteries' 4,782 twins at the floors of 11 and 36 are 9cb2eb5's byte for byte. Codex's four growth items are held by their pinning nodes in `tests/test_stage3b_shared_steps.py` -- `test_step_8_3_asks_only_the_retained_day`, `test_step_8_4_asks_the_retained_day_and_builds_its_places_once`, `test_step_8_5_asks_only_the_cells_holding_a_source` and `test_the_index_holds_few_units_for_each_rank`, each counting the work at the review's own size and red on 9cb2eb5 -- and those nodes, which the whole suite runs at every landing, are the regression mechanism: a step that grows with the rows again turns its node red.

## Decision P4-D367 — the weekday census of a column of moments (stage 3b landing D2, 2026-10-06)

**Why** (the build plan's lane D2, the 3b.2-W design and its skeptic). A column of dates and times published `weekday_census: []`, and its twin drew each gap evenly, so clinic visits on weekdays alone came back 24 to 31 per cent on weekends.

**The decision.** WC3 widens to a column of moments read on the local clock, not in the joint member, with both tails: its body is cut BY INSTANT, so a cell on a boundary's day but beyond its instant is a tail cell, and each body cell counts on the weekday of its day, in the menu's groups (WC1 to WC4). WC10, loader and producer: the published `p75` stands at least 28 days after the published `p25`. The producer asks the few-dates rule of the moments' days; the few-units rule beside it (the 3b.2-W skeptic's blocker 1, producer-only): where two or more groups are non-empty, at least eight different written units a non-empty group on average -- instants at the column's precision, days where every value stands at midnight; and, at every floor, on a column whose values do not all stand at midnight the unit-room rule, lane D1b's count-room rule (plan P4-D388) restated in written units: the column's units less the most its twin's tails can hold -- a listed tail's values, the floor's number on a side publishing its two distances -- must reach what the census needs between its pins; on a column every value of which stands at midnight, which the twin counts and moves in days as a column of dates, the count-room and count-reach rules of a column of dates, through the one helper the date path asks (`taxonomy._count_rules_reason`). WC6's storage half is asked, its half on written forms is not (the count of different values counts instants), and the room rule beside the same holes only where every value stands at midnight. Every withholding but one without tails says NF74's sentence; no key and no sentence form is added (minor 4). The generator moves a moment through G7.3f's shared pass over a unit and a day of 86,400 seconds and a written unit of a minute or a second, keeping its clock. Step 7c lets a rank whose clock stands outside its gap on the gap's end day take another clock there, and, where no end day offers a group under its total, shifts it onto one of a group at its total from which step 7b leads on. Step 8.7 puts a count still short back at another clock on each rank's own day. None puts a clock on midnight or takes one off it, and a written clock changes only on the ranks steps 7c, 8.4 at another clock, 8.5 and 8.7 move (minor 2). A count left off is counted in values on moments (minor 1), and the tails' cause is named only on a column counted in days. The validator counts a file of moments by instant (V5-W1). The oracle states the moments pass and steps 7c and 8.7 from the method's text, and `tests/reference/generation-branch-vectors-17.json` freezes them on twelve states of ranks. Minor 3 (step 7b in seconds only) was settled by landing D0, whose fifteenth file freezes 7b on states of every unit.

**Measured, and what the proof found.** The lane's battery: the design's 16 shapes at 1,000 and 10,000 rows, the 3b.2-W skeptic's tie and SK shapes (k7 and ties40 at noon, payroll at 1,000 rows among them), and D1's eleven weekday batteries written at noon and at a seeded clock -- 1,258 tables, 3,752 twins a floor, against 9cb2eb5. At the default floor of 11, 994 censuses publish where 9cb2eb5 published none, no twin misses a check, every source table meets its own description, and the twins' weekend share stands 0.026 from the real column's against 0.160 -- 0.004 on published columns and their bodies exactly, against 0.176 and 0.238; every one of the 8,374 counts printed at the two floors is nought or at the line, in the menu's groupings. At a floor of 36, 862 censuses publish, the twins' weekend share stands 0.040 from the real column's on published columns (0.165 before; their bodies exactly, 0.205 before), and no twin misses a check its base twin met: the 27 that miss at 9cb2eb5 (counts of different values on five clocked columns, widths on two holed ones) miss at the head alike, and every source table meets its own description. The proof's own first runs found three things the design had not: steps 8.1 to 8.6 keep a moment's clock, so on few census days the kept clocks met and 2,400 visits on seven Wednesdays came out 1,882 different minutes for 1,933 (step 8.7); at a floor of 36 four twins of Wednesday schedules missed their census, their ranks in a gap from Tuesday 18:04 to Thursday 11:24 reaching neither end day at their clock, both groups at their totals (the shift); and 132 twins of schedules written at noon held more different values than the column, their tails rebuilt on up to 36 values each (the unit-room rule). ## Decision P4-D368 — the day-of-month census (2026-10-09)

**Why** (the build plan's lane D3, the 3b.3 design and its skeptic). The twin drew each gap evenly and lost every day-of-month heap while every weekday census held: on the lane's battery at 1,000 rows and a floor of 11, billing on the 1st and the 15th came back 0.068 to 0.089 of the cells against a real 0.456, a visit on the 10th 0.080 to 0.154 against 0.915, month ends 0.027 to 0.065 against 0.609 and the 30th 0.018 to 0.030 against 0.341.

**The decision.** A column of whole dates -- or of moments every value of which stands at midnight on the local clock, which the twin counts and moves in days (the skeptic's major 4) -- publishes `day_of_month_census`: its body's cells counted over THIRTY-FOUR BINS on a cycle, the days 1 to 27, the 28th to the 30th where not the month's last, and the month's last day by its month's length of 28 to 31 (minor 2), grouped by stage 3b's one merge rule on the cycle (`calendar_rules.merged_groups`, major 1), a one-group census withheld. It is published beside the weekday census where the day of the month departs from the calendar weighted by the published weekday groups by at least four chi-squared per degree of freedom and by more than the weekday groups holding rows depart from the calendar weighted by the day-of-month groups (both on the published groups, major 2); with no weekday census, where it departs by four from the plain calendar; the calendar is counted in 400-year cycles and whole months, never walked. The weekday census is never withdrawn: CA6 read literally is not built (it lost 7 of 10 weekday censuses and took business weekends from 0 to 0.26), nor CA5's forced remainder or CA7's walk (the owner's principle of 2026-10-01). The producer withholds, in one publication note naming no rule (NF104), where a body day stands on a published hole, the middle half spans fewer than 124 days (DM4), a group holding rows holds them on fewer than four different dates, unless it counts only a month's last day and holds every one its calendar offers (blocker 1 (a); the last day of February holds one date a year; three Mays, the other months empty by their written names, held every bin's three dates and their twins missed the weekday census), or the two censuses leave the body too few days for the count of different values once the twin's rebuilt tails are set aside (P4-D388's count-reach rule, asked of both). Published, it says NF102 or NF103. The loader holds DM1 (the cover on the cycle), DM2 (the line), DM3 (the total), DM4 and DM5, WC3's scope alone (major 3: two widths or a workbook's two storages withhold nothing). The generator meets both censuses by the joint day plan, method G7.3i, in the day pass's own slot: pass A, G7.3f over the bins with the days of empty weekday groups as holes; pass B, G7.3f over the weekday census keeping each rank's day-of-month group, step 8.6 trading across them (blocker 1 (b)); where the two leave the weekday census or the kept count off and the weekday pass alone does not, the column takes the weekday pass's days and the twin names the day of the month given way (step 3, the core holds: found in the repair round, six Mays missed the weekday census at every seed); a column publishing none is moved by the weekday pass exactly as before. The validator counts the file's body per bin (V5-W2): EXACT-OBSERVABLE, the file's own cells between the two published boundaries hold every day-of-month group's published count exactly. The oracle states G7.3i from the method's text, in the commit that adds it to the generator (A-P4-59), and `tests/reference/generation-branch-vectors-18.json` freezes six states of ranks, each red on its own mutant.

**Measured** (22 columns: the gate's heaps, schedules and admissions, the design's month ends and business days, the skeptic's untuned shapes and 97 per cent on the 10th; floors 11 and 36, seeds 0 to 4, against 1c8f328). At 1,000 rows 14 columns publish at 11 and 15 at 36; no twin of 220 and no source misses a check; every heap comes back exactly where its bins stand alone (billing 0.456, the 10th 0.915, month ends 0.609, the 30th 0.341, business billing 0.341 of the cells, real and twin alike), the day-of-month distance at most 0.032 at 11 against 0.149 to 0.853 before; every weekday census is the base's, and all 75 twins of columns publishing none are the base's byte for byte. At 10,000 rows 14 columns publish at 11 and 13 at 36, every twin meeting its census brings each heap back exactly, the distance at most 0.007; every weekday census is the base's, as is every twin of a column publishing none; the count-reach rule withholds the monthly visit at 36, whose body held every one of the 160 days of the 7th to the 13th and whose twins, before the rule, came back 166 days for 168 at every seed; one column misses, below. The oracle moves 14 whole columns as the product does.

**Its price and its limits, stated.** A heap beside a stronger weekday pattern is not published: Monday billing's first business day, first Mondays and last Fridays at 11 (the comparison, major 2), as are tied columns (sessions, forty dates; the few-dates rule). The joint share on business days comes back at 0.76 to 0.89 of the real (billing rolled to the next business day 0.389 to 0.399 of 0.466, the last business day 0.479 to 0.491 of 0.610, the 10th rolled to Monday 0.761 to 0.798 of 0.898; before, 0.07 to 0.25): the censuses fix the margins, not the joint (minor 3). At 36, 97 per cent on the 10th leaves 30 other rows, fewer than the line, so the 10th shares its group, and the last business day's February ends share theirs. ACCEPTED UNTIL LANE D4 (skeptic 1's major 1, choice (a)): at 10,000 rows quarter ends -- half the rows on eight quarter-end dates, the rest any day, every one of 730 days held -- gave their count way, 717 to 726 days for 730 at three seeds of five at both floors, where 1c8f328 held it (publishing no census and losing the heap, 0.483 to 0.034).
