## Decision P4-D369 — the count pass splits the tails first, and dates that stand out (stage 3b lanes D4s and D4, 2026-10-12)

**PART ONE (lane D4s): G7.3's count pass splits the two tails' ranks first, and the day-count items owed to lane D4.** Built as its own landing beside lane D4's heavy dates, from a3c1b33.

**Why.** Where a column's different values are too few, G7.3's count pass splits ranks sharing a unit onto free units inside their gaps. It split nearest first, then the lower rank, so a body rank a day from a free day split before a high tail rank whose free day stood further: on logs just above one row an open day the body passed what the weekday census lets it reach, the high tail kept fewer days than its most, and the day pass took the body's extra days back. P4-D388 ruled that risk to stand and named the fix owed (its second verification: 21 of the near-one logs' censuses and 3 of the fresh logs' missing the count at two to seven seeds of ten); P4-D367 found it on midnight moments, silent on an ISO member.

**The decision.** Too few, the pass offers every rank of the two tails (`generation._tail_ranks`: the low tail's first rows and the high tail's last) its nearest free unit first, then the body's ranks, each nearest first and then the lower rank; a tail rank splits only onto a free unit inside its own stratum and only while the count wants more, so the body splits only once no tail rank sharing a day can split directly -- which is not the most the tails could hold: a chain moving another tail rank onto a free day first could free one more, a move the pass does not make (its Codex review, below). A method change of G7.3 (A-P4-59): the product, the oracle (`tail_ranks`, `distinct_pass`) and the sixteenth vectors file's new case `tails_split_first` (72 dates of a near-one log at seed 422: 64 days under the old order, all 65 now; every other vectors file rebuilds byte for byte). No description changes; a twin changes only where the pass splits and the order moves a rank (`_distinct_reached`'s new `tails` argument, empty for the order before).

## Decision P4-D370 — the reader: Excel's hour and the 12-hour clock, read and written back (landing T1, 2026-10-01)

**What it reads.** One clock reader (`parsing.clock_parts`) for the clock role and the slashed stamps' clock half, split at the first space: `H:MM` or `HH:MM`, an optional `:SS`, and `AM PM am pm A.M. P.M. a.m. p.m.` after one space or none. Unmarked hours are 0 to 23; marked, 1 to 12, 12 AM the first hour and 12 PM noon. Refused, as stated limits: `24:00`, a marked 0 or 13 (`00:30 AM` stays free text), `Am`, a one-letter `8:34a`, a marker after two spaces, a no-break space or U+202F, JavaScript's `4/30/2023, 8:34:52 AM`, and ISO with either. No `DATE_FORMATS` member is added; ISO is unchanged.

**One written clock per column, as values, no column key** (contract C6-10a, D12a). The style -- the hour's width and the face -- is the one most cells wrote, ties to today's `hh`. It is a value of `clock_form` (40 forms) and of a slashed stamp's one `datetime_separators` word (`space h AM-PM`). Cells on another face are unread (NF108); cells of the other width are read and written the column's way (NF109; the T1 skeptic's item 2, ruling 6 of 2026-09-17), a minority at or above the line too. Clock values are ordered by instant, the loader's T1 and T3 too. The twin writes the style through `parsing.written_clock`; validation holds it by fit (V5), so a twin that drew no hour below ten is not accused (item 6: the style check sees the hour width `%H:%M` cannot).

**The questions** (the owner's 2026-10-01 evening ruling). An unmarked clock whose hours all lie in 1 to 12 is asked 24- or 12-hour (item 1, its option (a)): the answer `twelve-hour` is the new settings list `forced_twelve_hour_clocks` (`--twelve-hour`), read on that face -- `12` the first hour, as `%I` reads it -- and written in hours 1 to 12. Its premise was measured false in the design: undeclared, `m/d/yyyy h:mm` on a 12-hour face writes hours 0 to 23 and `%I:%M` refuses about half its twin. A one-figure unmarked clock keeps the colon question it had as free text (item 3). A slashed column no value can settle asks which comes first, the answer `--day-first` (item 4). **The one key T1 adds**, against the plan's "no new key" (PLAN.skeptic M3): an answer is recorded in the settings (A-P4-58 point 4) and no key holds this one. Twenty-four settings keys (C6-20); the migration refusal names fourteen options. The integrator merges T1 after 3b.K's re-record and records the goldens, document vectors and manifest again with it.

**G7.5 step 5, the width census's unnamed remainder** (PLAN.skeptic m5; l.17955's case (a)): the named words keep their counts, the remainder goes on whole days, fewest ranks first, in widths the census does not name, each under the line and the named word. Case (a) validates at seeds 4, 0 and 1 (MISSED before); case (b) stays carried, its census one-field. The reference vectors' `month_first_widths` moves with it, product and oracle alike.

**Measured.** Before (668f276): none of the twenty spellings of `tests/clock_spellings.py` read; one-figure hours 758 of 1,000, AM/PM 0; clock-alone twins parsed 255 and 165 of 1,000 by accident. After: K-S3-52. On the design's 34 shapes at 1,000 rows, seeds 0 to 2, 668f276 against the finished head: 25 read now, each 1,000 of 1,000 with every twin cell parsed by the source's own format (or wearing its dotted marker) where one exists; five controls unchanged; JavaScript's comma, a no-break space, ISO with a one-figure hour and a 12/24 mix stay free text; validate 0 throughout. K-2B-14: questions 2,374 and 2,480, 668f276's. K-S1-06, one repeat each at load 4 to 6: 263.7 against 261.2 µs a cell, ratio 2.63 against 2.64. Describe, interleaved, 668f276 against T1, three repeats at load 8 to 13: `MM/dd/yyyy HH:mm` 10k 5.49, 5.39, 4.01 s against 4.66, 4.31, 3.40; 100k 50.5, 34.1, 36.7 against 45.0, 36.8, 32.3; numbers 10k×4 8.44, 8.31, 6.69 against 8.22, 8.40, 5.97. `_clock_of` and `clock_at_midnight` take the stamp's clock from its canonical text, one reading a cell (item 5). A newly read 100k column, Excel's `m/d/yyyy h:mm`: describe 45 s, generate 16 s, validate 83 s, at load 30.

**Stated limits.** A stamp census below the line pools its word, and that twin writes the 24-hour clock. A column writing two faces each above 1 % stays free text, as before. On a declared 12-hour STAMP the twin's time of day is drawn over the whole day, so an instant after noon is written on the dial and reads twelve hours earlier: measured at 1,000 rows, seeds 0 to 2, every twin cell parses under `%m/%d/%Y %I:%M` and validation MISSES 10, 11 and 5 obligations -- rungs, tail distances and, where two instants of a day fold onto one cell, both distinct counts. The twin report reads its cells on the column's face and names each miss validation names (R9; it read them on the 24-hour face before the finish and said the ladder was met); a strict xfail waits for the fix, which needs the draws confined to the half day. A declared clock column, whose space is the dial's half day, misses none. **Not fixed in the repair round** (skeptic 1, item 2): confining the body's draws to the half day is local, but each tail is drawn through a shape fixed in real minutes, its outermost rank at one distance, and validation's windows are built from that same shape, so a half-day tail is a change to G7.3b, G12.14 and their oracle together -- an hour-aware tail, which is T2's hour census. **The gate's carve-out (the orchestrator's call, option (b) of skeptic 2's item 1).** R9's second half, `test_r9_a_declared_twelve_hour_stamp_validates_clean`, is excepted from T1's gate and owned by landing T2; T2's row of the stage's plan carries one sentence for it: the half-day draw belongs to T2's hour census, which must close it, and R9's strict xfail turns into a passing test there. Until T2 lands this limit stands as written, R9 stays a strict xfail whose reason names T2, and every other clause of T1's gate holds. Not built: the evidence example in the column's style (design 2.3), which would add an argument to every date column's evidence; the summary and the twin report say the style in words. The loader's D12a had no words in its invariants and stopped with an error of its own on a broken description; it has them, with a refusal in the battery and in R8. Vectors file 22: five cases, a mutant each.

**Repair round (skeptic 1).** An interactive `profile` stopped with `KeyError: 'twelve-hour'` on the first column the 12-hour question was offered on, columns the base read without a question among them: the answer has key `6` (and `t`), and a guard reads every `Choice` a column's question can offer and holds each to a key. Two guards near the first round's item 3 had no clause that turned red: the summary's style line for the 24-hour clock in one figure (`h-mm`, `h-mm-ss`) and the width tie when as many hours show one figure as two; each has one now.

**Codex's review (one round, at 110cb46; the owner's rule of 2026-09-28: every item fixed, nothing sent back).** Eleven items; items 4 and 5, the date-code question on T1's new clock forms and the reading it promises, are landing R1's (P4-D381) and fixed in its stream. The other nine, each pinned by a clause of `tests/test_stage3b_reader_review.py` red at 110cb46: (1) a cell of the other hour width rewritten in the column's width could spell a value declared missing -- 180 `1:00` beside a declared `01:00` came back as 191 holes against eleven, on clocks and stamps -- so the width is the one that writes no present cell as a declared absence, and where both would, those cells are counted unread (C6-10a); (2) validation's tail recount read stamps on another face, which the producer counts unread, and the unchanged source missed four checks -- it reads the published face now (V-method, beside the fit rule); (3) the slashed pair's readings were compared before the face dropped cells, so 999 day-first beat 990 month-first, fell to 989 and the column was free text -- each reading is counted by the cells its one written clock keeps, one rule with `_stamp_clocks`; (6) G7.5 step 5's greedy walk missed 6 and 7 under 13 and said no days could hold it -- the days are searched depth first, each into the first word, the next, then left out, the first assignment taken, which is the greedy one wherever the greedy one succeeded, so no frozen vector moves; the oracle states the same search and the report's sentence is true; (7) the loader took a ` twelve-hour` style with no declaration -- S8c refuses it, a battery entry beside it; (8) a scripted run filed the 12-hour question under "might be codes" with `--code`, and a one-figure clock under "described as text" -- clock questions have a block of their own offering what their question offers; **The fix stream's second round** (the first round's commits checked item by item against the review, each pinning test red at 110cb46 and green on the fix; every clause below red at c13edd8, the first round's head). Six things the first round left: (1, 2) where both widths spell a declared absence the cells so written are counted unread, and validation's recount still read them -- three `1:00` beside a declared `01:00` and `2:00` stood below a low tail measured without them, four checks missed on a clock and five on a stamp -- and the census of date widths still counted stamps on another face, one check missed; ## Decision P4-D371 — the hour of the day on moments, counted and met (landing 3b.2-H, 2026-10-06)

**What it is** (the build plan's lane T2, with its design skeptic's B1, B2 and M1 and the 3b.4 skeptic's B1). A column of moments read on its own clock -- not in the joint member, not wholly at midnight, with both tails, its published middle half at least four days long and, in a workbook, stored one way -- publishes how many cells between its two tail boundaries fall on each hour of the written clock, in groups the one merge rule chooses on a line, so no group runs past midnight and every count is nought or at least the census line (contract HC1 to HC6, NF88 to NF92 and NF117). Each group holds at least its sure cells: every published boundary and rung in the hour it is written in, and in hour 0 the count at midnight less the rows of every tail listing only midnight values (rule 4 as the skeptic's M1 amends it, so an epoch sentinel's tail is not charged to the body). A census of one non-empty group is published, as the measurement behind the design asked; one group over the whole day is not. The validator recounts it as V5-H1. `hour_census` is EXACT-OBSERVABLE: the file's own moments between the two published boundaries hold every group's published count exactly. Method G7.3g meets it after G7.3f's shared pass at a unit of an hour with the day kept: SAMEDAY before the escape, which keeps the day standing and never touches a listed date, then SPLIT, RELIEF -- a unit whose only place is in a full hour takes one there once another unit of that hour has left it -- the step off midnight and PUT BACK, the units leaving in proportional order. It is the ONE clock pass for every field of the written clock (the 3b.4 skeptic's M4): each step reads its field from the state -- bins of a unit of seconds, a period of bins to a turn, the turn its parent and each parent's group in the coarser census its kin, which the escape and PUT BACK ask before another day -- so landing 3b.4's minutes and seconds are instances of it rather than copies; made so, the hour answered as before on 3,000 random states and on every twin of the battery. Where no weekday census stands, the escape and PUT BACK each have a LAST RESORT onto a day of another weekday, taken only once every move keeping the weekday is made: the landing's first whole suite found three older columns that needed it -- noon moments at a floor of one, 400 moments on 60 values written at 78, visits a minute either side of midnight at 21 and 22 values for 20 -- and on the lane's battery neither resort fires. The oracle restates every step, and the sixteenth vectors file freezes twenty-two states, each red on its own mutant.

**T1's carve-out, closed** (the orchestrator's note of 2026-10-02 under P4-D370). A stamp declared a 12-hour clock with no marker draws each tail rank on the dial's half day (G7.3b step 10 and G12.14, in the generator, the validator's windows and the oracle alike) and its body inside hours 0 to 11, by its census or the half day's own, and the move onto a midnight (G7.5) spreads the published count over the body alone, so its twin validates clean: R9's strict expected failure is a passing test, and the twin report says where the time of day is drawn. The carve-out closed only with the repair round: a weekday clinic written `h:mm` on the dial, its noon slots reading 12:00 and so counted at midnight, had a tail rank chosen for midnight that step 5 took back onto the half day, and every twin at a floor of 11 wrote one cell fewer at midnight than published.

**A fix the battery asked for.** Where the tails listing only midnight values hold every published midnight, G7.3b step 7 no longer stands the other tail's tie group on one: the 1970 clinic at a floor of 36 wrote 53 cells at midnight against 51 published and missed the count at every seed.

**Not built, as the build plan called it.** No walk or multi-census certificate, no fixed menu, and no certificate, band or cap. `K-S3-41` records the class the orchestrator reads into "Accept the class" (P4-D363), not a new ruling: a group of several hours says one of its hours holds 1 to 10 rows -- a range, never a value, a date or a row.

**Measured** on the lane's battery of 25 columns of moments at 1,000 to 10,000 rows -- the design's, the build plan's lab panel, 10-week clinic, burst, on-the-hour and half-hour grids and 1970 clinic, and R9's stamp -- at floors 11 and 36, seeds 0 to 4: all 250 twins validate with nothing missed and all 220 published censuses hold; the three short spans publish none. With the pass withdrawn the same twins sit at an hour TVD of 0.05 to 0.65 from their real columns; with it, 0.0002 to 0.0020 at 10,000 rows and floor 11 (0.0013 to 0.018 at floor 36) and 0.006 to 0.051 at 1,000 to 2,000 rows (0.020 to 0.195 at floor 36). Lab draws between 06:00 and 08:00 come back at 43.3 per cent of the twin against 43.3 real, where the twin before held 8, and discharges between 10:00 and 14:00 at 62.6 against 62.6. Every twin keeps the weekdays the same seed writes with the pass withdrawn, and its count of different values too, but for R9's stamp, whose pass-withdrawn twin folds one or two values on the dial while its own holds the published 998. On the design skeptic's sixteen shapes the design was not tuned on -- month ends, sentinels of 1900, 1970 and 2099, a fifth of the values at midnight, a legacy era of bare dates, bursts, a campaign, an offset, OR starts and arrivals at 100 to 2,500 rows -- at floor 11, seeds 0 to 2, and floor 36, seed 0, every twin validates with nothing missed, weekdays and counts kept, once RELIEF meets the OR starts' census, which every one of their twins missed before it (at both floors, seeds 0 to 4); at 100 to 300 rows a floor of 36 leaves two or three groups, and those twins stand at the flat twin's TVD or a little above it (0.26 to 0.31), below the 1,000 rows from which the gate asks its CAP. **Cost**, at a load of 10 to 65, against 1e8c91f: the pass takes 0.01 to 0.06 s at 1,000 rows, 0.10 to 1.3 s at 10,000 and 0.4 to 4.9 s at 40,000 (arrivals, a lab panel and a clinic, two seeds each), and 13.0 s of a 180 s generate at 1,000,000 arrivals, described in 95 s, 1.13 GB at peak, where 1e8c91f took 114 s to describe and 170 s to generate, 1.09 GB at peak. A union taken rank by rank had made it 0.86 s at 10,000 arrivals before the landing's own measurement found it. The 40,000-row clinic's 94 to 154 s to generate are the count pass's, 84 to 133 s on 1e8c91f (lane G3's). Those shapes are easy ones (the repair round): a column half of whose draws land in hours the census counts empty sends hundreds of ranks through the shared steps' CHAIN and exchange, which filed every movable rank again each round, so a million moments of daytime visits, 07:00 to 18:59 every day, spent 397 s in the pass and 546 s generating against 210 on 1e8c91f, and 100,000 of them 30 s; and fifteen in a hundred moments at midnight over two years, pinned by step 1, split the body at every day holding one and step 3's shares spent 5.7 s of 10,000 rows' pass. Steps 7b and 8.3 now file their cells once a call and the shares ask each gap once, every answer the same (10,000 random states of hours, dates and days of moments, 4,000 of them of up to 36 gaps): in one window at a load of 10 to 15 the million daytime moments take 18 s in the pass and 130 s to generate, against 126 s on 1e8c91f, their twin byte for byte the one before; 100,000 of them 3.4 s in the pass where the landing's head took 25 (16 s to generate against 37, and 11 on 1e8c91f); and fifteen in a hundred at midnight 0.5 s at 10,000 rows where it took 4.7 (1.5 s to generate against 5.6, and 1.1); `K-S3-38` times the 100,000-row node against a budget of 10 s. Step 6 of G7.3f's own stays linear and is most of what is left: 15 s of the million's 38 under a load near 33. The skeptic's other way, a gap read across the cells at midnight step 1 pins, was measured and dropped: on the gate's 10,000 moments every one on the hour it moved the merged midnight group's split to hour 0, the twin's hour 1 holding 8 to 19 cells of 211 real where it held 52 to 72, and its hour TVD past the gate's cap of 0.02 at seeds 0 to 4.

**The repair round** (skeptic 1, 2026-10-07). Besides the cost and the carve-out above: where the column's count is not one the construction reaches, step 6 still puts back a short count, splitting off their shared written unit the first ranks, in rank order, that share one, each inside its own hour, day and gap (2,000 different moments written with two marks between day and clock came back 1,999 at one seed in three; the leftover round below asks it only where the count drawn is not above the published one); step 3 was cut to one round, on the claim that no move of it gives a group room (the leftover round below restores four); the rules no test turned red each gain a clause or a frozen state red on its mutant, but three the skeptic listed that no input can turn red, each answered again by another: the published holes the pass asks, which on a column of moments are only the days its one width word leaves empty (a declared spelling names no moment's day, and a placeholder day judged empty lies outside the boundaries), so the days of another width kind every move refuses; and the escape's own tests for such a day and for a hole, which those holes and `_clock_free` answer. V5-H1's own test for a stamp on another face, which every recount's cells have passed already, is asked of its reader alone; and **a limit is stated**: a 12-hour stamp whose census is withheld comes back with its dial's late morning heavier than the real one (G7.3g).

**The leftover round** (skeptic 2, 2026-10-08). Step 3 makes up to four rounds again: a unit leaves whole while its group is over, so one of `k` ranks leaving a group over by fewer than `k` leaves that group under its count, and a unit an earlier group could not place takes that room in the next round. On about 1,930 random states of hours one round answered three otherwise, two of them further off the census and none nearer; a state of twelve ranks over two days that one round leaves two cells off is frozen in the sixteenth file, red on the one-round mutant. ## Decision P4-D372 — the minutes and seconds of a timestamp, counted and met with the hour (landing 3b.4, 2026-10-12)

**What it is** (the build plan's lane T3, with its design skeptic's B1, M1 to M3 and m1 to m3). Where a column of moments may publish its hour census (HC3), it publishes, for the minute of the hour and -- written to the second or finer -- for the second of the minute, its HEAPS, the values standing out (at least the census line in rows, at least three times the median of the five values each side on the cycle of sixty, M1) with their counts, and a CENSUS of the cells on no heap in groups the one merge rule chooses on a line: `minute_heaps`, `minute_census`, `second_heaps`, `second_census` (contract 6.6.2, MC1 to MC6, MH1, MH2, SE1 to SE6, SH1, SH2, NF93 to NF101, NF118, NF119). A cell counts at the minute and second it is written at; a sixtieth second in its own minute, at second 59. A field publishes only where its body's different values depart from flat, chi-squared per degree of freedom of 4 or more, and not where they follow the hour of the day (M3), withheld with its own sentence beside a middle half shorter than four hours or four minutes (MC4, SE4) and where no heap and no grouping stand; the reasons every census of the clock shares are said once, in the hour's sentence. `minute_census` and its siblings are EXACT-OBSERVABLE: the file's own moments between the two published boundaries hold every heap's and every group's published count exactly (V5-M1, V5-S1). Method G7.3h meets them: G7.3g's one clock pass once for the minute, the hour its parent and the hour census's groups its kin, and once for the second, the minute its parent; then the exchange off midnight, SUBSTITUTE and SPREAD; the tails keep the count at midnight. G7.3's DRAWING RULE draws the body, and each tail whose published values stand on it, on the lattice the fields pin -- the minute where every second is 0, the hour on the hour, thirty minutes on a half-hour grid -- and the steps at midnight, the count pass and the hour pass step by it.

**What the build measured beyond the design, each the builder's call.**
- *A heap is a value of the clock, not a few events.* It must be written at the line's different values: check-ins in bursts of one to six put 15 cells on minute 23 in three bursts, and the twin split its bursts to hold them.
- *A census of the rest standing on a few different values is left out* (D2's FEW UNITS), its heaps kept: a non-empty group under three different values, or groups under eight on average. Fine groups of a few bursts each cost 1,000 check-ins their count of different values at every seed, 1 to 14 long.
- *The flatness test counts each different value once; M3 divides its statistics by the design effect of the cells written alike and asks a strength too*, Cramer's V of 0.2: counted cell by cell with no such division, 1,000 bursty check-ins scored 3.4 to 4.7 against the hour and were withheld; counted value by value, 40,000 cells written `HH:MM:00`, whose busy hours hold far fewer values on :00 than cells, were withheld too. Night charting on the hour beside day entries scores V 0.98 and is withheld at every size.
- *G7.3f's count steps 8.1 to 8.6 do not run on a field* (`_WeekdayPass.count_steps`): over sixty values they ask cycles among up to sixty-four groups and took 20 of the pass's 24 seconds on 40,000 clinic slots; PUT BACK, SUBSTITUTE and SPREAD put the count back.
- *Four steps after the pass*: the EXCHANGE OFF MIDNIGHT (the shared pass moves ranks onto minute 0 of hour 0, 13 more cells at midnight than 18 published), PUT BACK once more where the exchange left the count long (a tied pair split across a held midnight, at 10,000 rows and floor 36), SUBSTITUTE (a count left long where no unit of the run's own group shares its parent) and SPREAD (10,000 clinic slots came back 250 values short, a minute's bin holding one place); and the tails keep the count at midnight where the census forces a body cell onto one, by the written unit where a tail's stratum is narrower than its drawing unit.
- *KIN SHARES* (the skeptic's B1). G7.3f's moves fill each gap's shares nearest first and whole runs first, so at 10,000 rows the hours holding the most tied units sent the most cells to the heaps: clinic slots came back with 20 per cent of hour 8 on :00 and 47 of hour 10, against 35 in every real hour, and INDEPENDENCE failed 1,482 times over the KPI's twins. Each kin group of a gap now takes its own shares of the gap's, no rank of it leaving a written unit it shares to meet them (held to its own shares, a kin group's few ranks split 1,000 bursty check-ins at floor 36 into 108 values too many), and the clause holds on every twin. The clause leaves out cells at a written midnight and a value an hour group expects fewer than the line's cells of, or fewer than the line's cells off, all of which the real table failed (150 times) or a twin failed by about a cell.
- *Counts the body could be left too few cells off a midnight to hold are withheld* (NF118, NF119): a published count at midnight may stand wholly between the tail boundaries in the twin, its tails drawing where their distances put them, so a field publishes only where its counts away from value 0 fit in the body less that count (less the rows of a tail whose every listed value is at midnight). 989 days at midnight beside 11 cells at 09:30 published a heap of 11 on minute 30, met with 6, and the workbook gate of plan P4-D382 exited 3.
- *The second census's rules are SE1 to SE6*, SC1 to SC3 already naming a count column's spellings; NF101 is the minute's alone. The heaps and the census are each their own check (`minute_heaps.counts`, `minute_census.groups`), so each registry fact is bound.

**Measured** on the lane's battery of sixteen columns -- clinic slots, discharges, vitals, bursts, admissions with bare days at midnight, cells written `HH:MM:00`, every cell on the hour, a flat control, a three-hour session, the skeptic's near-pure columns, an epoch placeholder, night beside day, quarter-hour, five-minute and half-hour grids -- at 1,000 and 10,000 rows, floors 11 and 36, seeds 0 to 4 (320 twins, on 33dd126): nothing missed; every published field and hour census held; and K-S3-42's driver at floor 11 finds no twin failing BOUND, CAP, SHAPE or INDEPENDENCE, nor moving an hour or weekday group. At 10,000 rows and floor 11 the minute TVD stands at 0.0005 to 0.0022 (clinic 0.0076 to 0.0092), clinic slots on :00 or :30 at 70.6 to 70.7 per cent of the twin against 70.8 real, quarter hours 95.2 to 95.3 against 95.5, cells written `HH:MM:00` 100.0 per cent on second 0; at 1,000 rows 0.001 to 0.095, the bursts 0.33 to 0.35 (their rest one group, its census on a few values left out), clinic 69.5 to 69.7 against 70.9; at floor 36 the quarter-hour and half-hour grids keep 99.6 to 100 per cent on their grid, and 40,000 cells written `HH:MM:00` meet every fact with G7.3h taking about 2 seconds. Before, the same twins stood at 3 to 4 per cent on :00 or :30 and a minute TVD of 0.3 to 0.9. The flat control, the short session and night beside day publish nothing, as the rules ask. Base 2341173 against this landing, seeds 0 to 2, floors 11 and 36, the hour gate's tables and this one's: every one of the 84 column twins publishing no minute or second fact is byte-identical.

**Not built.** No joint hour by minute census: where minutes follow the hour so far that one count over every hour would mislead some hour group more than a flat field, the field is withheld and its twin keeps today's minutes (the skeptic's owner option, later). The tails of a column written to the minute stand off their grid where a tail's published values do not stand on it. The walk certificate stays out (CA7, as plan P4-D364 called it): a merged group of minutes or seconds says one of its values holds 1 to 10 rows, a range, the class `K-S3-41` now names.

**The repair round** (skeptic 1, 2026-10-12; every item fixed). A field pass keeping its cells at midnight moves no rank onto one -- a written midnight is a kind of its own -- and hour 0 is not free to take value 0, so its share goes to the hours free to take it; where the hour pass left a rank of hour 0 off value 0, a tail gives its midnight way (200,000 cells written `HH:MM:00`: 602 at midnight against 385, now 385). KIN SHARES carries each kin group's rounding from gap to gap (admissions drawn again failed INDEPENDENCE at 9 of 10 twins; none now). Heaps beside a census withheld for its few values pin no lattice; a column written finer than the second publishes no seconds (SE3); SUBSTITUTE runs again while a round puts a value back; M3 withholds only where one count would mislead some hour group more than a flat field; a second census of a few values says so (NF120). **The second repair round** (skeptic 2, 2026-10-13; every item fixed). Where the count is reachable a field pass moves a shared written unit whole or not at all -- in the leftover past its groups' room once -- and where a field's census stands and the count is left long, the count gives way, named in the twin's report (the plan's RESIDUAL; the orchestrator's D4 precedent of 2026-10-13, its confirmation asked): the skeptic's small bursty tables newly missed the count on 11 of 45 twins at a floor of 36 and 1 at 11, now 7 and none, every one named, 157 values off now 105 over 90 twins. A column written finer than the second publishes its minute's facts only where its body cut to the second keeps its count (fuzz seed 3: 2,960 values came back 2,315). The room step's three rules each have a frozen case red without them.

**The Codex round** (2026-10-13; every item fixed, none back to Codex, as the owner ruled on 2026-09-28). M3 asks both its questions over two tables -- the single values holding a twentieth of the body and the rest, and the field's groups by the one merge rule on the line -- dividing only its chi-squared test by the ties' design effect, its strength Cramer's V less what those ties give a table with no dependence: 30 copies of every stamp had sunk a complete dependence under 0.2 (the twin put 5,192 of 10,800 daytime cells on minute 0 against 180 real; withheld, 195), and minutes each under a twentieth had fallen in one column (1,209 of 1,800 morning cells on minutes 00 to 19 against 600; withheld, 572); the 106 battery and fuzz columns publish as on 707cf99. A shared written unit is judged once a round (400 ranks on one: 5.6 times the lines of 100, now 4.0) and the room step's search starts past the tails taken (800 tails: 13.3 times 200's lines, now 4.0), both answering as before. NF93 and NF94 state the heap's sure-cell remainder. The verifier's four items after it, fixed in the same round: M3's table counts each different value once and also asks each hour group against the rest (one stamp written a hundred times had put 205 of 459 daytime cells on minute 0 against 6, and forty thousand cells over fourteen hour groups 2,282 of 5,400 of one hour's on twenty minutes against 1,800; both now withheld, the 106 battery columns publishing as before); KIN SHARES' REACH gives no kin group a part of a group its ranks never reach (200 and 40 on minute 0 where 120 each stood, now 120 each; file 20's `field_kin_unreachable`), and its CLAIMS keep what a kin group carrying a whole rank of a group can take from the kin groups before it (`field_kin_partial`; without them hour 23 of the fresh sample held 6 of 45 on minute 0 against 16, and K-S3-42's INDEPENDENCE, nought again, read 35); and a tail listing any value written 00:00:00 is charged for it, not the epoch's alone (`tail_end_listed`).

## Decision P4-D373 — clock-only columns keep their time of day: a census, heaps, a step and codes (stage 3b landing 3b.5, lane C1, 2026-10-03)

**Why.** A column of clock times holding few enough different values was a set of labels: its rare times were written blank by the level pass, or as made-up text of the clock's shape (`57:95`), so code reading the times ran on the table and raised on its twin. Read as clock times, its body was spread linearly between its rungs. Measured on 110cb46 at 1,000 rows and a floor of eleven (seeds 0 and 4), the hour of day came back 0.180 (a medication round), 0.315 (a handover) and 0.333 (night observations) off in total variation; every heap smaller than a rung gap was lost -- the handover's eight came back on 186 of their 680 rows; seven columns of shift starts, slots, rounds and coded shifts took `categorical` and wrote 42 to 107 invalid cells each; and a column with no tails was a ramp from 00:00, its hour 1.0 off at 100 rows.

**The decision** (the 3b.5 design with every BLOCKER, MAJOR and minor of its skeptic folded in). The clock reading is asked before the categories rule wherever that rule would claim the column (contract 5.2); `--code` still reads it as labels, and the questions file asks where both readings fit (`few-times-of-day-each-shared-by-many-rows`, answers `keep` and `code`), under the owner's rule of 2026-10-01 that the run asks where the data cannot settle a shape. A clock block publishes, beside its tails and ladder:

- `clock_step`, the seconds every parsed value stands on, the greatest common divisor of the dial and every value (the skeptic's minor 1);
- `clock_heaps`, every step standing out from the five either side by the median rule, over EVERY parsed cell, the tails' too (BLOCKER (a));
- `clock_census`, the body's cells on no heap in ten-minute bins nested in hours, or `[]` beside the heaps where fewer than the line are left (NF106; the fold-back is dropped, BLOCKER (b)); a column with no tails publishes heaps and a census over all its parsed cells;
- `clock_codes`, every unread spelling at least the line's rows wrote, written back exactly (NF107; MAJOR 2).

The loader holds them to CC1 to CC5, CH1 and CH2. The generator lays the column by G7A.4b: heaps on their values in the body and in the tails, each tail's other cells drawn through its shape less its heaps, in steps that skip the heaps' distances; each group's count shared over the runs its heaps cut by their steps, a run holding a boundary taking one cell first (MAJOR 1); the boundaries and every published rung its run holds pinned there (minor 2). The validator counts the file against them, V5-C1 and V5-C2, and a body rank's window is its census group's (G12.10b). A label column's held-back level of a clock's shape is written as a clock time (contract 7.9.1, G8.3; MAJOR 3 for the shapes the reader reads), and the level pass keeps a column of clock times beside a few rare words, or beside levels its clock's form does not read, a column of clock times, counting those missing, so its twin reads back as the same role. Clause H counts listed and heap tail cells as placed and holds the hour within 0.03 at 1,000 rows (MAJOR 4). The keys, helpers and anchors are 3b.K's (MAJOR 5).

**Measured** (the design's eight columns, its skeptic's three, Excel's one-figure hour, the 12-hour clock, three coded shifts and a column 2 % words, seventeen in one table; 110cb46 against this landing; seeds 0 and 4, seed 0 at 10,000 rows):

- at 1,000 rows and floor 11 the hour of day comes back 0.000 to 0.013 off on every clock column, against 0.016 to 0.333; every heap standing out on the real column comes back exactly (the handover's 680 of 680 rows, walk-ins' 29 heaps, Excel's 26, the 12-hour clock's 26); the seven columns the categories rule took and the dominant time are clock times, their 18 to 107 invalid cells each gone;
- at 10,000 rows every column reads as clock times, eleven of them `categorical` before, and the hour comes back 0.000 to 0.001 off, against up to 0.344; 18 to 3,047 invalid cells a column become none;
- at 100 and 300 rows the hour comes back 0.003 to 0.260 off, against 0.027 to 1.000, and every heap is exact; at floor 36, 0.004 to 0.052 against 0.016 to 0.333, the largest the shift starts, whose 30-minute jitter falls in their tails;
- a column of clock times beside 2 % words misses the parse line and stays labels, and its 241 to 2,447 made-up cells that no clock reader takes become valid times;
- the validate exits are 0 for every twin and every real table of that battery, before and after; on 337662c they were not for a column of labels beside clock-shaped codes, whose twin read back as clock times (the repair round below), nor on 060a1b7 for a column of times beside one-off notes past one cell in fifty or beside a minority of another precision or face (the second repair round).

The gate is `tests/test_stage3b_clock.py`: sixteen clauses since the repair round, all but NF106's and the floor half of F each red on its own mutant; vectors file 21 freezes fifteen cases with a mutant each; `K-S3-48` and `K-S3-49` are new.

**Stated limits.** A clock column with codes past 1 % of its cells (2 % `unknown`) misses the parse line and is labels, now with valid stand-ins whose hours are spread over the day, which no published fact of a label column holds: counting those times, such a column's hour comes back 0.363 off at 1,000 rows and 0.160 at 10,000, where its unparseable stand-ins counted for nothing before (0.269 and 0.080). R1's codes question (`dates-or-times-beside-a-few-repeated-codes`) reads such a column as clock times on the answer `missing`, but it is not asked everywhere: an `HH:MM` column with 1.8 % `UNK` is asked about at 300, 1,000 and 3,000 rows at a floor of eleven and at 3,000 rows at a floor of 36, and not at 10,000 rows at either floor nor at 300 and 1,000 rows at a floor of 36; at 10,000 rows it is `categorical`, and the level pass counted 1,073 of its rare times missing, so its twin wrote those cells blank where the table has none, its hour 0.027 off (superseded by P4-D390, which deleted the level pass: route 1 counts nothing missing where the column is not left as clock times; not re-measured here); at a floor of 36 it is free text at 300 rows and a long tail at 1,000, its hour 0.488 and 0.475 off. 110cb46 read those two columns so and asked neither, its hours 0.800 and 0.588 off. R1's codes question follows the classifier on a clock column since lane R2c's Codex fix (P4-D383): on the merged classifier the 10,000-row column with 203 `UNK` is read as clock times under `missing` and asked at floors 11 and 36; at a floor of 36 at 300 and 1,000 rows `UNK` stands on 11 and 25 cells, under the census line its question would print, and it is not put (strict xfail; ACCEPTED by the orchestrator, 2026-10-13). A column of `7:30 AM` beside more than one cell in fifty of rare words stays free text and its twin is made-up text, as before: no form names its cells, since a form holds no space: the spaced meridiem, `9:15 AM`, and `08:15:30.123 AM` with a space before the marker, publishes no forms, measured by lane R2b's Codex fix stream (0 of 969 clock cells in shape where `9:15AM` keeps 969) and held as its strict xfail X4 (P4-D383), owned by lane L2 (the orchestrator, 2026-10-13). ## Decision P4-D374 — the minute of the hour on clock-only columns, counted and met (stage 3b landing 3b.5's second step, lane C2, 2026-10-13)

**What it is** (the build plan's row C2; the design's step 2 and its skeptic's MINOR 3). A column of clock times publishing its step publishes `minute_census`, the moments' key on this role (contract 6.13): how many of its BODY's cells -- between the two boundaries, both included, or every parsed cell with no tails -- the clock heaps' among them, fall on each group of minutes of the hour, by the one merge rule on the census line beside the sure cells (MC1 to MC3, MC5). It publishes where the body's cells on no heap depart from flat over the minutes the step reaches, counted by CELLS -- a time of day repeats across the days a column spans, and counted by different values triage times typed on `:00`/`:30` and walk-ins on a ten-minute grid were flat -- and not where they follow the hour so that one count over every hour misleads (M3). MC4 does not apply: a clock column has no date axis. Nor does the moments' few-values rule: clinic slots of 14 to 35 rows at a floor of 36, withheld by it, came back 51 per cent on `:00`/`:30` against 71; published, 67. No sentence is said. The validator counts the file against it, V5-C2, widened. Method G7A.4c meets it: each census group cut at its pins -- the boundaries and the rungs on a step of their group -- into stretches, the table of stretches by minute groups fitted to both counts and rounded with both kept, completed along shortest paths, and each group's cells sorted onto its ranks; a heap's ranks are then windowed by its group (G12.10b). Vectors file 27 (file 21 stands at the 250,000-byte cap) freezes six cases, each red on its mutant.

**Measured** (the design's battery, `tests/clock_census_shapes.py`'s fourteen columns in one table, 1,000 and 10,000 rows, floors 11 and 36, seeds 0 to 4). Fourteen minute censuses published -- five at 1,000 rows at each floor, ampm, Excel's `h:mm` and walk-ins at 10,000 and floor 11, triage at floor 36 -- every one met, no twin and no real table missing a check, every clock census, heap and hour check the base met still met; the 210 column-twins publishing none are byte for byte 707cf99's. ## Decision P4-D376 — the count pass's paid merge keeps its book between attempts (stage 3b lane G3, 2026-10-02)

**The change, which moves no published fact and no twin byte.** Method G7.3's paid merge (`generation._traded_merges`; P4-D258, and the midnight trade of the second Codex round's dates pass) rebuilt the held units, the runs and their offers from every rank on each attempt, and each offer walked every rank for its payment. It keeps them now in one book per call (`_TradeBook`), brought up to date by the ranks a paid merge moved: the runs beside a moved rank and the runs on a unit whose count of ranks changed are offered afresh, a run that was offered the unit the merge left trades that one offer for its next nearest, and that unit leaves the files of held units the searches walk; where a payment takes the last rank of a unit whose ranks stand on more than one instant, the book is built again whole. The unpinned ranks are filed by their standing in the trade, so a payment is sought among those that can give it, and a payer whose search finds no held unit at all, with no unit set aside, leaves its list until it moves or the book is built again: within one book held units only go and their instants move only with a rebuild, so no later walk could find it one. The offers stand sorted in blocks (`_OfferPool`) cut at 256 offers, halved past 512 and dropped when emptied, never merged, so a block holds 1 to 512 offers and most fewer than 256 (the lane's second skeptic): after each paid merge, 94 % of the blocks on 40,000 midnight slots, 90 % on 160,000 and every one on 40,000 clinic slots. Each block's last offer is filed for a halving search, so an offer put in or taken out moves the offers of one block, where the one sorted list the lane first kept them in (311cf30) moved every offer after it (the lane's repair round). `tests/test_stage3b_count_pass_speed.py` keeps 110cb46's pass as its oracle and finds the same merges, ranks and counts per unit over 3,000 drawn trades, over 3,000 more moved to straddle 1970-01-01 so that the unit numbered -1 is held, and over every call the generator makes on seeded clinic slots and on the same slots with one cell in fifty written at midnight; after each of 2,152 paid merges of 1,800 more drawn trades, with blocks cut at two offers, it finds the kept book equal to one built afresh from that moment's state; drawn puts and takes at four block sizes leave the pool reading as one sorted list; at the shipped size a pool cut from 1,000 offers holds blocks of 256, 256, 256 and 232, a block halves at its 513th offer into 256 and 257, and a take changes no block but its own, dropping it once empty; and each of ten mutants of the book's upkeep turns it red, as does each of fifteen of its blocks, its attempts and its walks' set-aside unit, and each of seven of the blocks' sizes that no other test of the file sees (cut at 128 or 512, built at twice the cut, halved at 512, a shrunken block merged into either neighbour or topped up from the next).

**Measured**, 110cb46 against this, CPU seconds to generate one timestamp column at load averages of 2 to 65, so recorded and never judged (the stage-4 skeptic's clinic and quarter-hour shapes, the 3b.2 hour skeptic's lab panel): at 40,000 rows the clinic column 119.3 → 3.4 (80.1 → 3.9 at a second seed), the quarter-hour grid 126.2 → 4.2 (78.0 → 3.4) and the panel 82.9 → 4.4; at 80,000 rows 298.4 → 9.5, 108.2 → 9.2 and 11.2 → 10.0. On the clinic slots with one cell in fifty at midnight, where the pass makes 293, 698, 1,175 and 5,216 paid merges at 10,000, 20,000, 40,000 and 160,000 rows, 1.0, 2.1, 4.3 and 23.4 s, where 110cb46 took 9.1 and 39.7 s at 10,000 and 20,000, this lane's first book (40f1205), whose walks asked again every payer that had found nowhere to go, 2.3, 8.0 and 35.8 s up to 40,000, and at 160,000 rows the pass alone took 29.8 s on 311cf30 and takes 10.3. Every twin and twin report of those tables is byte-identical to 110cb46's, and so are those of the weekday skeptic's thirteen date batteries and 21 smaller timestamp columns (1,303 columns at a floor of eleven, seeds 0 to 2), of the 3b.2 hour design's 16 timestamp columns and its skeptic's 21, two of them at 40,000 rows, of the stage 3b gate's three date columns at 10,000 rows, and of the lane's first skeptic's thirteen tables; at 80,000 to 320,000 rows of the midnight slots, compared with 311cf30's alone, the same. `K-S3-51` counts it without a clock: on the clinic slots the pass reads 2.1 and 3.5 ranks a rank at 10,000 and 40,000 rows, where 110cb46 read 159 and 1,922; on the midnight slots it makes 5.2 and 6.3 held-unit searches a rank at 10,000 and 20,000 rows, where 110cb46 made 197 at 10,000 and the first book 20.6 and 38.9; and there its pool moves 762 and 1,352 offers a rank at 40,000 and 160,000 rows, where 311cf30's one list moved 57,160 and 391,482.

**The Codex review of the lane (2026-10-07): two items, both fixed, no twin byte moved.** (1) The book's files of ranks -- the payers and the ranks on each unit -- were sorted lists, so each rank a merge moved shifted the tail of four of them, and the unit a merge left was deleted from four files of units the same way: on Codex's eight instants of 1 to 8 March 2024, held 7,024 to 28,096 times between them (`heavy_instants` in the lane file), 5f28017 shifted 32 to 515 million entries, about 4,600 to 18,300 a rank, and one merge of a run of m ranks shifted 3m² even when it was the last merge a call owed, its book dropped next: 0.93 s of CPU at 64,003 ranks where 110cb46 took 0.05. The files of ranks are now cut into blocks (`_RANK_BLOCK`, 256, halved past 512 and dropped when emptied, as the pool's are), a unit a merge left keeps its place in the files of units under a mark both ways that the searches jump (`_jumped`, each walk through marks pointed at where it ended), and the last merge owed goes without upkeep. The files now move 525 to 583 entries a rank on the instants and 72 to 98 on the midnight slots, at most 2,048 a moved rank in one large merge, which takes 0.06 s owed once and 0.32 s owed twice at 64,003 ranks: linear, about 4 µs a moved rank. (2) A map keeps the room it once took when its entries go, and the emptied map of every unit a merge left stayed in the book: on Codex's count-pass state of 803 to 3,203 ranks the maps of the runs offered a unit held 482,544 to 7,460,528 bytes where a fresh book's held 2,264 to 9,304, and on 40,000 midnight slots 1,010 empty maps held 6,563,096 bytes. A map of the runs offered a unit, of the runs on it or of its ranks now goes once empty, on both ways an offer leaves (`_book_aim_dropped`): after every merge no map is empty and the maps of the runs offered take about twice a fresh book's bytes there, the room of their most crowded moment, and 9,304 on the 40,000 slots. The twins of the lane's 1,303 and 40 battery columns (seeds 0 to 2), its fifteen CLI tables, the midnight slots at 10,000 and 20,000 rows (seeds 0 to 2) and Codex's March table at 7,024 to 56,192 rows are byte-identical to 110cb46's and 5f28017's, and so are both count-pass states' answers. The March table generates in 0.8, 1.6, 3.9 and 9.7 s of CPU at 7,024, 14,048, 28,096 and 56,192 rows (0.7, 1.6, 4.1 and 11.3 on 5f28017; 3.0, 11.3, 42.9 and 147.5 on 110cb46), and the clinic, quarter-hour and panel tables at 40,000 and 80,000 rows in 4.1 to 10.1 s, as on 5f28017, each process's peak within 4 MB of 5f28017's, at load averages of 8 to 30. The pass's tracemalloc peak is 18.1 MB at 40,000 clinic slots, 12.3 at 20,000 midnight slots, 100.4 at 160,000 and 12.0 on the March table at 56,192 rows, where 5f28017's was 17.2, 11.9, 108.1 and 11.4: each block is a list of its own, and the emptied maps no longer stay. `K-S3-51` bounds the files' moves on both shapes.

**What is left, stated.** On clinic slots with one cell in fifty written at midnight the pass still grows faster than the rows: 1.1, 3.1, 7.7, 22.1 and 66.8 s of CPU at 40,000, 80,000, 160,000, 320,000 and 640,000 rows, at a load average of 2 to 6, so ×2.5 to ×3.0 a doubling; at that rate about 2.3 minutes at 1,000,000 rows and 7 at 2,000,000, more than stage 4's hour can give one column of a 50-column table. Two causes, both counted. The trade empties nearly every midnight unit it is handed, 400 of 402 at 80,000 rows; every run that was offered a unit it empties is offered its next nearest instead, and the last units stand nearest to more and more runs: 110, 158, 175, 215 and 241 offers traded so a merge at those sizes, about two thirds of the pass's CPU at 160,000 and 320,000 rows. And each payment walk still starts at the front of its list, where the payers alone on their unit, which every walk turns away, gather: 12, 19, 27, 42 and 68 reads of the pins a rank. Not built, and each would answer one: an offer found when the pass reaches it rather than when its unit empties, and a payer alone on its unit filed apart until its unit gains a rank. And on a few instants held thousands of times each the pass still grows with the square of the rows (the Codex review's March table): each paid merge splits the runs beside a moved rank afresh over their whole span and files each of their ranks again, offers afresh the runs on the units it touched, reading every rank of each for a pin, and each payment walk steps past the ranks on the unit the run joins -- 229, 452 and 889 reads of the pins a rank at 7,024, 14,048 and 28,096 rows. That column takes ×2.0 to ×2.5 of CPU a doubling up to 56,192 rows and ×3.4 past it, 41.1 s at 112,384 rows and 94.6 s at 200,184 (the verification of its Codex review), so about 40 minutes at 1,000,000 by the ×3.4 a doubling measured to 200,184 rows. Not built: runs split only where a rank moved, and a run's pins counted once. **Memory.** The book is what the pass allocates: its peak, read by tracemalloc, is 17.5 MB at 40,000 clinic slots and 143.6 MB at 320,000, 12.0 MB at 20,000 midnight slots and 109.1 MB at 160,000, so 0.45 to 0.68 KB a row and about 0.45 to 0.7 GB at 1,000,000 rows, inside the 16 GB this work is designed for; one column's whole process peaked at 1.15 GB at 640,000 rows. **On wide gaps the trade stalls** (the same verification, its note 1; lane G3's own code, which 110cb46 holds in a slower form). Four 10-day clusters a decade apart, to the minute, 5 % at midnight, each stamp held 2 to 8 times, generate in 4.7, 11.1 and 22.6 s at 25,000, 50,000 and 100,000 rows; at 200,000 rows (seed 0) generation had not finished after 20.5 minutes of CPU, and 300,000 stalls the same way, while 150,000 rows and 200,000 at seed 1 finish the trade in about 21 s. The cause is in `_traded_merges`' payment walks: nearly every payer of the target's standing stands on the target unit, so a walk read 9,914 payers on average and turned away 9,909.5, and a payment falling short is put back and the same offer tried again. The verifier's proposed fix, output-identical and not built: the book keeps a count of each standing's payers by unit (`_book_filled` counts them, `_book_settled` and `_book_payers_dropped` keep it current), and the trade skips without walking an offer whose standing's payers off the run's unit and the target unit number fewer than the run's size, pinned by a machine-free count of walks on that state. **And the weekday census's target search on sparse dates** (the same verification, its note 5; not G3's code): over 100 years written M/D/YYYY, 1 to 7 rows a date, `_weekday_single_target` takes 17.3 of 43.2 profiled seconds at 100,000 rows and 103.8 of 163.6 at 200,000 (78,064 calls), the same twins and seconds on 110cb46. **Owners** (the orchestrator, 2026-10-09): lane S4b, stage 4's next million-row costs, owns the trade's growth on clinic slots and on a few heavy instants, the wide-gap stall and the weekday target search.

**The call** (the orchestrator's, PLAN section 2 row G2, from the tails measurement of P4-D375; reversible). The width census counts a width fewer than the line wrote into its commonest (P4-D222), so G5.3b step 4's one-width and padded clamps read it as a ceiling no cell passed. A published tail pair says otherwise wherever its Bhatia-Davis reach, `rms**2 / d1` at a least distance of nought, passes that ceiling. Method G6.6.8 then (1) stands the clamp aside: the end is the first whole number at or past the reach, never further than the fitted end; (2) walks that tail: only its outermost strata that fit the line less one and what the pair's totals `m d1` and `m rms**2` leave after the squares of its rows under the width stay past the width, every other stratum past it -- the end's own among them -- is moved under it before any demand is served, and the cells left there come off the demand the census counted them into; on a side rule 1 moved they stand only where they read the published mean and spread, together, no further off than leaving none there, and on a side it did not move the walk stands only where it serves the census strictly better and leaves neither moment further off; (3) wherever rule 1 moved a derived end, reads the values a second time from the same words with both rules withdrawn -- 110cb46's twin, on its own division, made once with the plan -- and keeps the reading nearer the published mean and spread, together. Measured on the shape: at 100,000 rows the twin writes five far cells at 1155800 to 1155804 (the source's at 1155999 to 1156003), its tail mean distance from the published boundary 1,280.485 (published 1,280.485) and spread 11,102 (11,116), nothing missed, `generate` 22.3 s and 138 MB; at 1,000,000 rows five at 2558000 to 2558004 (2559999 to 2560003), the mean met, the tail's spread at 35,533 against 35,577 and the column's at 288,709.83 against 288,709.86 now inside their windows, `generate` 221 s and 851 MB (895 MB on 50a52d6), `validate` 181 s; six misses become three. **Left, measured:** the column's mean, skew and kurtosis at 1,000,000 rows still miss G12.3's windows, which do not reach the published values there (the mean's 500,051.9 to 500,061.4 around 500,012.3, the twin at 500,013.3; skew 0.0017037 against 0.0017093, kurtosis 1.81200 against 1.81205): G12.3's window on a dense column, not this lane's. Rule 4 is a method change, so it is the oracle's too, in the same commit (A-P4-59): `tail_pair_met` is the oracle's last value pass, written from the method's words, and the one frozen case it moves is `tail_shape_ends` (`generation-branch-vectors-8.json`, rebuilt through `tools/provenance/guard_runner.py`), whose twelve-row high tail on tenths is dense: its far cells 34.3, 63.5 and 196.7 became 131.4 and 131.6 beside the run's 28.7, the other 26 vector files the same bytes. ## Decision P4-D378 — the calendar on each value's own clock: two offsets and the joint member (stage 3b landing 3b.7, 2026-10-13)

**What it is** (design 3b7-shared-clock with its skeptic). The weekday (WC3), day-of-month (DM5) and hour (HC3) censuses stand on a column whose cells wear more than one offset, published on the shared clock, and on a column of the joint member: one predicate states their scope (`calendar_rules.census_scope`), and each cell is RANKED by its instant on the published clock, over the pairs as the offset census speaks of them, and COUNTED at the day and hour its own text is written at, a bare date at its midnight. The generator gives every block of ranks the layout fixes a key in G7.4 step 1a -- its written place in a published group with room, off a withheld midnight (item (a)) -- runs every pass on each rank's own clock and takes the frame back run by run, and writes the published count of bare dates (the form step, residual R-P4-12 closed on clocked columns): `resolution_mix` and `format` are EXACT-OBSERVABLE on the joint member, and the construction keeps an all-different joint column all different where its gaps have free midnight days (item (b)), its count held to G12.5's envelope as before (the repair, item 1). The validator places each cell by its unit and counts it as written. Method G7.3k and G7.4 step 1a; vectors file 24.

**Built against the skeptic.** Blocker 1: on the shared clock the sure cells of HC5 are rule 4's alone (`calendar_clock.own_clock_sure`, producer and loader), and the generator, not the loader, matches pins to keys -- the source's offsets prove a match exists. Major 2: the form step caps each gap at its free midnight days, the credit left at the end given to the first ranks with room. Major 3: the count stays in G12.5's envelope on the shared clock. Minor 4: the form step is step 4's first part. Minor 5: D5 is "withheld for its size", decided from published facts. Minor 7: one ranking a column. **Beyond the design, each measured:** where a census stands on the shared clock G7.4 spreads the keys gap by gap (`few_off` at 10,000 rows missed its hour census at every seed with its 196 `+05:30` cells in one block on the body's first ranks); the passes' gaps run across pinned bare dates (cut at each, 39 of 77 seconds at 100,000 rows went to G7.3f's shares); the cells are ranked over the pairs as the offset census speaks of them (ten folded `2024-01-04` read at `(none)` cost the unchanged source its weekday census); and a joint column's body takes no more bare dates than the hour census counts at hour 0 (100 dates beside 300 noon stamps published 94 there, and the rotation gave the body 96).

**Measured** (the 3b.7 design's battery and its skeptic's, 21 columns, floors 11 and 36, seeds 0 to 4, `K-S3-53`). At 1,000 rows all 170 published weekday and 175 hour censuses met, every offset count exact, the written weekday 0.000 to 0.035 off where the base stood 0.007 to 0.292; at 10,000 rows all 185 and 175 met. Every bare date is written as published (the repair) except where the cap at hour 0 leaves it no place (stated limits). Twenty local column cases are the base's byte for byte. At 1,000,000 rows a two-offset column generates in 98.7 s against 55.1 and a joint one in 142.0 against 142.1, peak 1,122 MB.

**Not built: lane T3 is not merged.** Its merge onto the integration head meets a design question: with lane D2's weekday census beside its minute heaps, G7.3g/h's count steps may not leave a rank's weekday, and the count of different values falls short or stays long (a 10,000-visit clinic 1,621 of 2,175; bursts 298 for 279; about 30 tests of lanes T3, D2 and J). A paid SPREAD brings the clinic to 2,165, the rest is open. The minute and second widening (MC3, SE3) is written against T3's code and waits for that merge.

**The repair** (skeptic 1, six items, 2026-10-13). (1) Validation's second statement of exactness for an all-different joint column is gone: 800 stamps on consecutive minutes beside 200 dates every third day came back 778 to 805 of 1,000, MISSED, where the envelope held them; `contract.datetime_counts_reachable` is the one statement, the count stays in G12.5's envelope, and the twin's report says the shortfall in a remark. (2) A bare date the free midnight days cannot place stays a bare date on its gap's nearest midnight, a day another value holds, never a moment with a real key: on 2,000 dates beside 8,000 stamps at `+01:00` and `+02:00` each offset count, the count at midnight and the forms were MISSED and are held. (4) Each new rule is pinned at its use site, red on its mutant: the spread (`few_off`, 10,000 rows), the cap at hour 0 (100 dates beside noon stamps), the producer's sure cells on the shared clock (`dst_clinic`). (5) The censuses compute one instant key a pair and spell the shared clock's text from it: a describe of `n` pairs computes 2n + 2 keys, as the base's 2n, where it computed 5n. Measured on the repair's head, floors 11 and 36, seeds 0 and 1: the all-different joint columns come back all different at 1,000 and 10,000 rows but the tight one (998 or 999 of 1,000, 9,999 of 10,000 at the floor of 36), and 99,997 to 100,000 of 100,000, every shortfall said; nothing is MISSED on them or on the dense columns of items 1 and 2.

**Stated limits.** The count of different values on the shared clock stays in G12.5's envelope (the twin may hold more than published), and so does an all-different joint column's: moments on consecutive minutes beside bare dates come back 754 to 805 of 1,000 and 8,438 to 8,618 of 10,000 (strict xfail), said. Season and offset are not paired, and G7.4 step 2's spread (beyond the design) made it worse: a twin of a daylight-saving column writes the offset not in force on its date for 50.0 to 51.7 per cent of its rows at 1,000 and 10,000 rows, against 34.4 to 39.2 on the base and 34.3 to 39.3 with the spread off -- the trade is every published census met against season pairing. The follow-up, costed: publish each offset key's first and last day under the tails' floor rule, so G7.4 spends keys by season -- a contract field, its producer, loader and validator check, a G7.4 step and its oracle, one lane. `z_plus` (an instrument writing `Z` beside a ward at `+02:00`) withholds its weekday census at 1,000 rows at both floors and at 10,000 at the floor of 36: its Sunday holds 3 and 23 written cells, `Z` cells from Monday's first two local hours. C1's two columns keep their excess, inside the envelope: c0 115 and 99 different values for 63 at floors 11 and 36, c551 149 and 177 for 83. Heavy dates stay on the local clock. **The cap at hour 0 against the forms** (the repair's second skeptic, item 1): the body never takes more bare dates than the hour census counts at hour 0, so where that group caps the body and the tails' gaps hold fewer midnight days than the source's tails held bare dates, the dates left over are written as moments: `noon_ends`, bare dates on the first and last eighth of a span of noon stamps with every value different, writes 98 of 100 at 400 rows, 248 of 250 at 1,000 and 2,498 of 2,500 at 10,000 (97, 247 and 2,497 at the floor of 36), `resolution_mix` MISSED and named in the twin's report, the hour census held; with the cap off every date is written and the hour census misses instead (hour 0 at 85 for 83, 62 for 59 at the floor of 36). Pinned by a gate case and a strict xfail on `noon_ends` and vectors case `leftover_capped_at_hour_zero`. **Where the bare dates fall** (its item 2): G7.3k spends `resolution_mix` by rank, so where bare dates and stamps share days the twin spreads the bare dates evenly over the span -- the share of each fifth of the sorted column that is bare dates is 11.3, 11.3, 10.2, 10.8 and 56.5 per cent on `isomix_alldiff` at 10,000 rows and 19.9 to 20.2 in every fifth of its twins, 50, 50, 25, 0 and 0 on `noon_dates` at 1,000 rows against 24.5 to 25.5; it follows the source only where a stretch holds dates alone (`dense_local`, 94.5 per cent in the first fifth against 100). No published fact says where in time the bare dates fall: code that splits the real table by period and counts the rows carrying a time of day meets a different answer on the twin. **Owners** (the orchestrator's rulings of 2026-10-15 on the sixth push's critic, the owner may reverse any): the daylight-saving offset is lane D5's (daylight-saving offsets on the shared clock); the consecutive-minute shortfall beside bare dates, `z_plus`'s withheld census, the bare dates written as moments at the cap at hour 0, the even spread of bare dates over the span and the 12-hour dial on the shared clock are lane 3b-REST's (the calendar remainders, beside 3b's schedules).

**Codex's review** (2026-10-13, on e8cde1e: reject, five items, each fixed; nothing sent back). Each was reproduced first on e8cde1e by a column of the gate's S3 battery that misses there at floors 11 and 36, seeds 0 to 2, and meets every check on the fix, each red on its mutant. (4) `K-S3-53`'s nodes now hold every case its rule names: the field, frame, spread, form and form-day vectors, the frame taken back once a rank, the sixtieth second, the shared sure cells and the three columns' mutants. (5) The contract's field rows for the weekday and day-of-month censuses and the hour census's note now state the widened scope of WC3, DM5 and HC3. **At integration (batch 3b part 2d, 2026-10-14).** The minute and second widening waited for lane T3; T3 came in through lane J2 (P4-D391), and the widening (MC3, SE3) was re-applied on J2's code from the 3b.7 builder's bundle, not merged as history.
