## Decision P4-D379 — the weekday and the hour of a moment, met together (stage 3b lane J, 2026-10-12)

**What it is.** Where a column of moments publishes a weekday census (P4-D367) beside an hour census (P4-D371), the hour pass kept each rank's day standing, and a rank the weekday pass left on its gap's end day, at a clock no published hour reaches there, stayed off its hour: batch 2b's integration measured 4, 7, 5 and 10 twins of 10 short on five noon stamps a day, two clocks a day, D2's leap column and T2's review column. Method G7.3g step 3 now runs its rounds once more where a weekday census stands, with THE ESCAPE PAID BACK: a unit with no place on a day of its standing takes SAMEPARENT's on the nearest day of another in its gap, while as many movable ranks of that standing move by whole days onto the nearest day of its standing in their own gaps -- every weekday count and every field of their clocks kept, the payer keeping the count of different values preferred among the first and the 1,024 after it, payers too few given back. Chosen over the two other directions: the escape to another day of the same weekday needs a gap of a week, which an end day's gap rarely is; and the weekday pass placing end-day ranks at clocks the hour census reaches would ask the shared G7.3f pass to read a census it does not own, and a noon rung's own day has no such clock before it.

**Measured.** Seven columns -- OR starts, admissions, the 10,000-row clinic and the integration's four -- at floors 11 and 36, seeds 0 to 9: every twin meets both censuses and misses nothing; every twin with one census alone, and every twin the base already met, is byte for byte the base's. At a million rows the round costs 0.7 s of a 124-second generate on the year's clinic and 26.6 s of 213 on noon stamps over 118 days. **A stated limit, not this lane's alone:** at a million rows a group the census still needs can hold no free written unit on any day of a unit's gap -- the clinic at a million comes back 767 ranks off its hours (2,070 before), and noon stamps over 118 days 2,344, which the same column misses with its weekday census withdrawn too (2,908): G7.3g asks free places only. Owned by lane S4b (the orchestrator, 2026-10-13). **The round given back** (the lane's skeptic, finding 1): ward rounds at 08:00 on weekdays and 10:30 at weekends, a million rows over 150 days, came back with 260 different values of a published 150, SPLIT ranks the round put on days of another standing, whose values stood in another hour group, being values no merge of PUT BACK takes back. Where the round placed a unit and the count stands off after steps 4 to 6, those steps run again on the state it began from, which stands where it comes nearer the count, even where it still misses it (a frozen state holds that reading: the lane's second skeptic). That column at a million rows now misses its hour census alone, as before the lane; the clinic keeps 767, and the noon stamps and a handover column (06:45 to 07:14 and 18:45 to 19:14, a year) are unchanged.

**Also.** The tails recount asks the fold the census recounts ask (D2's verifier, older fault (a)); the leap-second columns' count of different values and count at midnight, still missed with the hour census withdrawn or both withdrawn, are lane T2's family, now owned by lane J2 (the orchestrator, 2026-10-13; T2 has landed). **KPI.** `K-S3-62`.

**Codex's review** (2026-10-13, three items, each fixed). (1) A payer could move a rank of a unit its group had listed and not yet asked, whose whole move then took its other ranks off their weekday: Codex's state of nine ranks, hour 12 alone beside seven single weekdays, came back with Monday 2 and Sunday 5 as 3 and 4 (24 and 60 as 36 and 48 at 108 rows), every hour met, in product and oracle. G7.3g step 3 now asks a unit as it stands -- its ranks still on the written unit it was listed on, whole only where they are every rank there (`generation._clock_unit_standing`) -- a thirtieth frozen state holds it, and every frozen state beside a weekday census is checked to keep its weekday counts. (2) A date the file's own description folded into its moments was read in the tails at midnight UTC, not at the offset its census absorbed it into: nine bare dates among `+05:00` and `+04:00` stamps left a low tail's mean and RMS distances HELD outside their windows, and ten bare `2024-01-04` beside `23:00:00-05:00` stamps had a source's low tail of 12 rows recounted as 22; each folded cell is now read as every other cell (`validation._tail_readings_of`'s `folded`). (3) The payers cost the square of a unit's size (a set copied once a payer) and a walk of every empty day between, once a payer: now the set grows in place and the walk reads the occupied days once a unit -- a unit of 32,000 ranks takes 0.14 CPU seconds where 689d405 took 6.3, and a span of 2,000 empty weeks costs what 1,000 do. The ranks asked and their order are unchanged. Measured against 689d405: the lane's 600 twins of ten columns in three modes and its skeptic's 280 are byte for byte the same with the same verdicts, and its 404 random twins of the drift probe keep every weekday count on both trees. At a million noon stamps over 118 days the twin is byte for byte 689d405's, its payers asking the same 22,271,980 places in 27.0 CPU seconds against 28.1.

**At integration** (2026-10-13, batch 3's first part). The hour pass held no placeholder day of a column of counted dates (lane R4, P4-D384) as a hole, where the weekday pass has since batch 2b's integration and the reference's `hour_settled` always did; the round moves ranks by whole days, so it now holds them too (`generation._hour_settled`'s `counted_holes`). Five SAS seconds at noon on each of 118 days across 1 January 1900 call the round at seeds 1 and 2 and keep the day empty either way; `tests/test_stage3b_counted.py` pins the holes, red on the merge's product.

## Decision P4-D380 — numbers written in full describe, and a column nothing reads is split once (landing R0, 2026-10-01)

**The crash** (the reach audit's N0, with its skeptic's corrections 1 and 2). A number a program computes and writes in full -- hours between two times as seconds over 3,600, a ratio of two counts, a time as a fraction of a day: Python's `repr` and pandas' default -- has a different spelling on almost every row, so its fraction widths can be one pool beside about as many widths as rows. `parsing._fill` called itself once per width, and on 668f276 `synthtwin profile` stopped on a bare `RecursionError` with no file in 14, 7 and 15 of 20 seeds of the three shapes at 1,000 rows, and on every workbook time column holding seconds. The walk carries its own stack: its states, their order and its accounting are the recursion's, on 1,500 seeded shapes at seven budgets.

**Its budget, charged for the work.** Made iterative alone the walk stalled -- 41 s at 3,000 rows, past twelve CPU minutes at 10,000 -- because a reading of the free cells (`_topped_up`) wrote the free conventions one at a time over every count of written conventions, about 1.5 million big-number steps for one 3,000-row reading, and was charged one step. A reading is now the sum it is: the loaded conventions are summed first, the free conventions of one capacity are a pool whose totals are a few runs (`_free_totals`, its closed forms checked against every capacity to fifteen), and the old walk over them is kept only where two capacities share a room too small for both. It answers what the walk answered on 6,000 seeded readings. The walk keeps two counts. Its steps are counted one each, as they always were, and decide where it finishes and what it answers. Its work is the same steps with each one's work besides: a reading one more per 256 words its population spans for each big-number step, and a table over the conventions one per 8 cells -- the conventions by the values, charged before it is built, each value's placements and each state written out -- against a ceiling of four times the budget. Where either runs out, the answer the walk always gave on stopping short takes over: the producer counts the census at one width and the loader admits it. Where the widths-by-values table alone is past the budget, `taxonomy._width_bounds` counts its groups and does not build it (`parsing.pool_table_too_large`).

**A step that still nests too deep** ends `profile`, `generate` or `validate` with `errors.stopped_nested_too_deep` and exit 1, never a stack trace.

**The split, once per text** (the skeptic's correction 3). A column the earlier rules decline was split by `taxonomy.affixed_split` sixteen times a cell -- four readings ask it in each of four passes over the census's reading and the description's -- about 1,700 questions to the number reader a cell. A reading keeps each answer by grammar and text (`_Cells.affixes`), and the kept reading the description takes over shares them.

**The review's correction** (skeptic 1 on f31b3c5). The first draft spent the work against the steps themselves, and one column in 668 measured described otherwise than 668f276 did without crashing: 1,000 whole numbers and quotients written in full (seed 8101) finished its walk in 849,564 steps and published `fraction_widths {"(withheld)": 605}`, and charged it stopped short at 1,525,694 and published `{"16": 605}`, its twin writing 604 decimals at sixteen figures. With the work a second ceiling its five files are 668f276's, pinned by their digests; among 623 walks that finished, the most work against plain steps was 1.84 times. Measured on 45a7ecf: of the review's 280 columns (160 of 1,000 rows, twelve of 10,000, 108 of whole numbers and quotients), 522 calls of the walk answer as under one-a-step accounting, none differing; the 423 files 668f276 wrote for 141 of the 1,000-row columns are the same bytes. Cost against the first draft: 13.9 to 20.1 walk seconds over the 1,000-row columns, 8.3 to about 13 over the 10,000-row ones. The table no longer built takes `_width_bounds` from 10.3 to 0.4 s, and the 100,000-row gate column from 37.2 to 28.1 CPU seconds, the same files.

**The review's second round** (skeptic 2 on ae704e6). The table charged before a step counted every value of two rows or more a reader places, and the walk then drops each that bounds nothing (`parsing._bounds_nothing`) before it builds the table. A column of K values each written once as `i.5` and once as `i.50`, beside one `0.125`, hands in only such values, so its real table is the widths by one, yet it was charged the widths by K and one: from 25,001 rows at the default floor (and from 4,401 at a smallest group of 2,100, 10,001 at 1,000) it published `fraction_widths {"3": N}` where the walk with no charge shows `{"(withheld)": N}`. `taxonomy._width_bounds` now leaves such a value out of the groups it counts and hands on: on a census of widths the walk's question is one look a value -- none of its rows narrower than the narrowest width, and as many spellings as rows or as the room -- because every capacity is the same, a value reaches every width from its least up, and there are always more widths than the room. Pinned by the 25,001-row column. Five guards no test watched are pinned too, each test red on its mutant: the table's charge never taken of the steps, the same charge taken of the work, `_fill` stopping on the work, the census of widths counting only values a reader places, and `mixture_pool_holds`' own check before a step. Measured on the repair: the five such columns publish one pool, in 1.1 to 6.3 CPU seconds; of the review's batteries, 480 of 480 files on the 1,000-row columns, 36 of 36 on the 10,000-row ones and 324 of 324 on the 108 mixed ones are the same bytes as ae704e6 gave, and the 423 files 668f276 wrote for 141 of the 1,000-row columns are still the same bytes; the 100,000-row gate column still builds no table and writes the same five files as ae704e6 and f31b3c5, in 28.3 CPU seconds.

**Measured** (load averages 27 to 51, so no seconds were judged). Against 668f276 run with the recursion limit raised in a 1 GB-stack thread: 369 tables -- the reach skeptic's crash, crash20 and slow batteries, its reach and miss batteries, the stage-3 battery, the shipped fixtures and two 10,000-row columns -- give byte-identical profiles, summaries, questions, twins at seeds 0 and 4 and twin reports, 2,534 files, and the same exit on the seven that refuse; the census tests' 10,735 calls of `mixture_pool_holds`, each answered again by the pre-repair walk, differ nowhere. One of those 10,000-row columns (seed 5002) took 736 CPU seconds there and takes 5.8, the same files; another (seed 5000) never finished there in twelve CPU minutes and takes 5.9. Describing the 367 battery tables took 1,062.9 CPU seconds and takes 235.2: a minute-fraction column 42 to 73 s and now 3 s, the 3,000-row column 40.9 s and now 1.0 s. An unread column of 10,000 Oracle timestamps takes 9.8 CPU seconds where it took 93.9, with the same files. `K-S3-54` and `K-S3-55`.

**Stated limits.** At 100,000 rows the table charge answers before a step is taken, so the census is counted at one width, as a walk stopped short counts it; a pool a walk could have shown standing there is counted so too (none measured since the second round; before it, the five columns above). The charge before a step still counts every value handed to `mixture_pool_holds`, those it then drops among them, because dropping one looks at every convention -- the table's own size: so a caller handing in thousands of values that bound nothing over thousands of conventions is answered as stopped short where 668f276 walked on (3,000 values of two rows over 3,000 widths: True there in 8.6 CPU seconds, stopped short here at once; 900 over 9,000, 80.6 seconds there). The census of widths hands in none of them. The same walk is asked four times a column, and not remembered. A reading's splits are kept for its life: about 236 bytes per different text (170 for short texts with units, by tracemalloc over 20,000), so about 0.24 GB a column of a million different texts, beside the cell records the reading already holds; on the 16 GB machine the owner's tables are designed for, a few such columns described at once.

**The Codex review** (on 110cb46; three items, each fixed and pinned in `tests/test_stage3b_full_precision.py` and `tests/test_kpi_ledger_integrity.py`). 1. A leaf of the walk asks one reading for each count under the line, and both counts were asked only after the whole leaf, its True taken before them: at a floor raised with the rows -- 1,000,001 cells of `i.5` and `i.50` at `--smallest-group 500001` -- a leaf started a reading past 4,000,061 of the work and its time grew with the square of the rows. Both counts are asked after every reading now, so a walk stops short at most one reading past either ceiling; on the same million rows it stops at 62,500 readings in 3.7 CPU s and the census is counted at one width. 2. The first split of each different text asked every substring of a span, each read whole: `+` 800 times and an `x` asked 320,400 in about 11 CPU s. `taxonomy._core_reach` reads the span once from each start and stops at the first character no number holds where it stands -- a second point or exponent, a sign, bracket, space or mark out of its place, a group of thousands of other than three figures, a magnitude past binary64's range with no exponent to follow -- and marks the ends no number can stop at; only the rest are asked, in the old order, so the core is the old one: 600,000 seeded texts under both grammars and 600 texts at the edges of the range split as 110cb46 split them, and sixteen kinds of 800-character run ask at most one question a character (none for the signs). Common cells split about seven times faster. What can still be slow -- a run of figures past binary64's range thousands long -- is bounded: past `taxonomy.SPLIT_SEARCH_CHARACTERS` (twenty million characters read for one cell, about five CPU seconds) the run stops with `errors.cell_too_long_to_search` and writes nothing, never a different answer; a list of 4,000 three-figure readings in one cell, 16,004 characters that read as one grouped number, reads about 4.8 million. A start or an end inside a run of characters a reading drops at either end of what it asks -- spaces of any kind, a declared column's points -- reads as the run's kept neighbour does (`taxonomy._kept_places`), so such a run is read once from where it starts and an end inside it is asked once: read again from every place inside it, `Note:`, 7,000 line feeds and a heading, with no figure in the cell, read twenty million characters and stopped the run; they read 7,005 now, and 150,000 texts holding such runs split as the old search split them under both grammars. 3. `K-S3-55`'s driver wrote `described_unread_10k` only when the unread column failed, under a key its rule did not bound, so a failed run read PASS; the flag is written on both roads and bounded at exactly 1.

**Its verification** (on 6c59700) found that item 1's fix had moved a caller asking False of a walk that, on one kind with no value, had always finished -- the loader's band of a closed census (`contract._census_may_speak`: D12, P6, NS2 and TM1) -- and pointed at two more, the twin's two questions of its own pooled marks (G6.1, `generation._pool_mark_count` and `generation._pool_alone_places`). Under a budget of one step the loader refused a hand pool of 32 grouped numbers the walk lets stand, and at the shipped budget a pool of 400,000 under a line of 300,001, which six marks hold; the twin lowered its marked cells one cell a walk stopped short, so 350,000 groupable cells and a pool of 200,000 under that line would have taken about 50,000 walks of three CPU seconds, where 110cb46 took one walk of 4.8 s. All three ask `parsing.lone_pool_stands` now: first two sums every reading meets -- a reading leaving a name absent holds at most the room of the other names at one less than the line, and one with no name at one less than the line at most the room at two less -- then the walk, True where it stops short, as the loader's other call sites ask it. The sums never refuse a pool a finished walk lets stand, and past a line of three they are the walk's whole answer: 240,445 pools at 40 floors from four to 150, one to seven names and every room to nine, against 110cb46's walk. So the three answer as 110cb46 answered at every floor and in bounded time: the loader's band the same on 22,687 pools at floors 1 to 39; the 350,000 cells marked after one walk of 3.8 s; a pool of 2,100,000 under that line, past what six marks hold, refused at once, where 110cb46 took 31.9 s and the loader asking True with no sums took it; and 2,099,995 groupable cells beside a pool of 1,799,995 lowered to the 1,800,000 seven marks let stand in 6.8 CPU s and one walk, where 110cb46 walked about 31 s for each cell it lowered. The oracle is unchanged: it counts the readings out, so it answers as the walk that always finished, and the twin answers so again. Pinned in `tests/test_lone_pools_every_reader.py` and `tests/test_pool_alone_marks.py`, each test red on its mutant.

## Decision P4-D381 — two date questions: which comes first, the day or the month, and what a column's few codes mean (lane R1, 2026-10-01)

**The ruling.** The owner, 2026-10-01: "we try to replicate the database without the imput of the user, but this does not mean that the user shouldn't be asked!" The date reach audit's Q1 and Q2, under its skeptic's corrections; its Q5 (the century) and Q6 need new keys and wait.

**Day or month first.** Asked where a column read under the month-first member of a slashed pair (slashed, dotted, two-figure year, slashed stamps) has every different spelling read by both members: one question for the file, with each column's calendar evidence where one reading puts every date on one position -- month starts `01/03/2023` read month first all fall in one month of the year. `day-first` is `--day-first`; `month-first` declares nothing, and the file that run writes does not ask it back. Not asked under `--day-first`, nor of a column one of whose cells only one reading parses. Hyphenated day-month dates are not read yet, so they are not asked.

**Codes for a missing date or time.** Asked of a column nobody declared where one to five spellings, each on at least eleven rows (or the run's census floor where higher) and together at most a tenth of its present cells, read as no date member and no clock form, and what is left -- at least three different spellings -- clears the date rule's own line (`taxonomy.reading_of_the_rest`: the classifier's decision over different spellings weighed by their rows, its clock half every form of landing T1 on the face most cells wrote), and the classifier itself, asked with the codes declared missing (`taxonomy.role_read`, `_read_the_column` and `_decision` with `profile_column`'s arguments), reads the column as dates or times; the question says that reading, and as the cells left unread those that run holds and does not read, so a stand-in date it sets aside, which the reading parses, is counted read. A code's rows are every cell its declaration takes in its own column, a spelling under the line it matches counted in, and a declaration that would also take a cell some date member or clock form reads is no code. A spelling declared kept is no code. Such a column is asked that and nothing else: no joined question on `00/00/0000`, no checklist line. `missing` is `--missing-value` naming each code, `real-value` is `--keep-value`; both reach every column, and the question names each other column holding the same spellings, with its rows where `census_nameable` allows and "some rows" where not, or says none does; each count is the present cells the declaration takes in that column under that column's own rule, so `-1,0` in a column declared `--decimal-comma` is counted beside a code `-1`. Answered `real-value`, the column is asked no question of what kind its values are and gets no line calling it codes, but one the answer leaves read as a measurement keeps its checklist line (decision D14). A column whose other cells read both ways is put in the day-or-month question of the same file. A clock is asked only where the answer reads what is left as clock times: the categories line drew that, as rule 8 stands after rule 7, until lane R2c's Codex fix left it to the classifier (P4-D383), and at batch 3's integration lane C1's classifier reads four times, a hundred and 101 beside `99:99` at a thousand rows as clock times once the code is out, so each is asked (integration fix 6, CONFIRMED by the orchestrator on 2026-10-13). A spelling an answer declares is called answered, not typed, and named once on the line that repeats the run, each value quoted for the shell (POSIX; PowerShell on Windows) and one starting with a minus sign joined to its option with `=`; a typed option an answer replaced is named there to take out. Every line a person is told to type -- that one, the options a notice offers, the `synthtwin validate` line -- quotes a word holding `~` on POSIX (bash reads `a=~` as the home folder), a word starting with `-` on PowerShell (Windows PowerShell splits a bare `--missing-value=-1.5` before its point), and a `"` on PowerShell as the C runtime reads it back, with the backslashes ending a value that holds white space doubled -- any character .NET counts as white space, the no-break space among them (Windows PowerShell 5.1 passes the `"` bare and wraps such a value in double quotes; PowerShell 7.3 or later keeps the backslashes, so there the declaration misses and the question is put again), and says which shell it was quoted for wherever it quotes one. The generator's refusal of a column too narrow for its values names the column and then the option, never the name inside the option. The cells that read as neither a code nor the reading are said, by count where the disclosure rule lets it through and "a few" where not.

**The file names no code** (A-P4-58). The question says how many codes there are, how each is written and on how many rows; the run that reads the answer finds them again in the table it opens. An answer whose codes are gone declares nothing and says so; two answers making one spelling both a value and none are refused, as on the command line, and so is one column answered both ways. The codes are found again under the typed `--keep-value` and `--missing-value`, and taken where the question's own words, handed back in the file, describe them -- the run that wrote the file was typed the same way, so a word typed on both runs, which the question never counted, stays as typed; otherwise they are found with each typed word a code of the column would match taken out, and taken where the words describe those or nothing was found before, so the answer, the newer statement, replaces a typed word it was about (`asking.date_codes_answered`). Where neither is described the table or the options changed since the file was written: the typed words stand, and a typed word the answer contradicts is said to be left as typed.

**Measured** on 668f276: the five day-first columns' twins parsed 41 to 74 in 100 cells under the person's own format; seven of the eight with codes parsed 0 to 59, and the eighth, which the date rule read, 99.5, its codes written as made-up text; nothing was asked about dates, and three of the eight were asked whether they were blood pressures. After: `K-S3-56`. A column of dates every cell of which its reading parsed is not walked again. Each question is worked out once a run, the screen's pass reused by the file where nothing moved. Measured at 200,000 rows on the repaired tree: date-times with unread cells 0.81 s of a 32 s describe, one count of their spellings and a parse of each different one; slashed date-times read either way 2.21 s of 91 s, each different spelling parsed both ways; and the other columns are counted for every question in one pass over the table, each different spelling judged once: on thirty DateKey columns at 20,000 rows the codes pass took 0.84 s, the count 0.58 s of it, where a pass per question had taken 16.5 s of a 154 s describe.

**Not built; put to the orchestrator, to rule before 3b.K's key cut.** A default that follows the evidence -- month starts read day first unanswered -- needs a way to answer month first against it, a third state of `day_first`: a new settings key, which this lane does not add. The evidence is said in the question; the standing reading stays month first. Neither question is put at the keyboard: both go to the file and the screen. The codes question's clock half read `HH:MM` and `HH:MM:SS` only until the Codex review below; it reads every form of landing T1 now. **Limit:** typed workbook dates beside a code stored as a text number, answered `missing`, give a twin that fails its own validation (exit 3), as `--missing-value -1` does on 668f276; a strict xfail pins it for the lane that mends how a declared number meets text in a typed column.

**The Codex review** (2026-10-02, one round; every item fixed on 110cb46's tree, nothing sent back). Each reproduced first: a code `$(printf marker)` stood bare after `--missing-value` on the line to type, `NOT RECORDED` became two words; 975 dates beside 20 `UNK` and 5 `unk` were said to hold a code on 20 rows and `missing` took 25, and 900 compact dates beside 80 `20230101` and 20 `20,230,101` a code on 20 rows where `missing` took 100; 475 slashed stamps unmarked beside 475 marked AM, and three spellings of one date, were promised dates and answered as labels or `constant`; `1:00` to `9:59`, marked or not, beside `UNK` were never asked; "every other value is" one of the codes stood beside five cells that were neither; `real-value` answered beside a typed `--missing-value UNK` kept `PENDING` alone; a typed `--keep-value UNK` stayed on the repeat beside `--missing-value UNK`, which exits 2; one column answered both ways was read under `missing` alone; forty columns with a code each read the list of questions 3,162 times for an empty answer; and `K-S3-56`'s driver counted a refused control clean. **Cost:** the classifier reads each asked column once more -- thirty DateKey columns of 20,000 rows, the codes pass 1.29 s of CPU on 110cb46 and 20.96 s here, the whole describe 43.2 s and 66.2 s, every one of the thirty asked; each asked column costs about what describing it as dates costs in the run that reads the answer, most of it the placeholder pass's entry test (`_remainder_reading`), which parses every cell under every member. The orchestrator's call, reversible: a reader of its own was what promised readings the classifier does not give. Measured again on 2026-10-03 at 200,000 rows, one ISO column beside `UNK` on one row in fifty: the classifier's pass a question asks takes 7.0 s of CPU on a loaded machine, 18 of every 30 profiled seconds in `_remainder_reading`, about 35 s a million rows.

**The repair of the repair** (2026-10-03, every item still the Codex review's, nothing sent back). Item 5's first repair found the codes under no typed declaration, so a word typed on both runs, which the question never counted, was taken too: on 622e810 960 dates, 30 `UNK` and 10 `XX` typed missing read as labels once `UNK` was answered `missing`, the answer declaring nothing; `NOTE` typed missing was kept by `real-value` about `UNK`; and `NOTE` typed kept was declared missing by `missing`, as on 110cb46. The question's own words now say which codes it counted. Item 1's first repair left four words a shell reads as something else: `~` after a bash assignment-shaped word, a leading `-` and a `"` on Windows PowerShell, and a column's name inside the generator's `'--identifier NAME'`; and only the repeat line said which shell it was quoted for.

**What the check of the repair left open** (2026-10-03, two items, both fixed, nothing sent back). Item 3's repair (998780b) took the classifier's count of the cells it reads as every cell read, and the classifier holds no stand-in date it sets aside: on 27c604b 950 ISO dates, thirty `1900-01-01` and twenty `UNK` were said to be 950 of 1,000 read as dates with 30 more that "stay unread whatever the answer", where `missing` left none unread and counted the thirty missing by their spelling; beside fifteen cells that read as nothing, 45 were said where 15 stay unread. 110cb46 said 980, which was true, and so does the tree now; the cells said unread are the ones the answer leaves unread. Item 1's repair doubled the backslashes ending a value only beside a space or a tab, while Windows PowerShell 5.1 wraps a value holding any character .NET counts as white space: in a model of its native command binder, as no Windows PowerShell was at hand to run it, `a`, a no-break space, `b` and `\` reached the program as one word holding the option typed after it. Any character Python counts as white space, which takes in every one .NET counts, now doubles them.

## Decision P4-D382 — workbook cells read as what they store: dates beside text, moments, clocks (stage 3b lane R3, 2026-10-01)

**The rule** (contract 4.3b, 5.2 and 6.6.2; method G2.2 steps 0, 0b and 3). A column a workbook stores mostly as dates is read as dates where no format clears the parse line, its other present cells counted unparsed; a word named with `--missing-value` is missing, as before. A date format hiding a time reads every cell of its column as a moment where more than one of its dated cells in a hundred holds a time (the default parse line of 0.99 read as cells, `workbook.DAYS_PER_TIMED_CELL`); where some do but one in a hundred or fewer, each timed cell is read as the day its format shows, and the column stays days with no cell unparsed. A date beside a date with a time is read jointly, and two date, date-and-time or clock codes are read, the twin wearing the commonest; the mixes still refused name their kinds, and both cell-cap refusals name a .csv file as the route past them. A column whose every value cell is a time-format number at a whole second under one day is read as clock times, the stored seconds kept, written back as day fractions, and `categorical` stands aside for it where a level would be held back. A locale tag alone is the format language's own. A date or clock the census stores as text keeps its text.

**Measured** on the reach skeptic's workbook cases and the lane's risk battery, 1,000 made-up cells at floor 11, seed 0 (read share, written-back share, validate exit, before → after): 5 % text dates 0 / 0.05 / 3 → 0.95 / 1.0 / 0; 3 % `UNK` 0 / 0.031 / 3 → 0.969 / 1.0 / 0; both 0.921 / 1.0 / 0; text date-times 0.95 / 1.0 / 0; six moments at midnight under `m/d/yyyy` 0.994 / 0.994 / 3 → 1.0 / 1.0 / 0; the date and date-time mix, and two codes of one kind, refused → read, exit 0; clock columns under `h:mm`, `h:mm:ss`, AM/PM and a locale code continuous → clocks, exit 0, the two storing seconds under `h:mm` and AM/PM from a RecursionError; locale codes worn 0 → 1.0; clock grids of 15 and 60 minutes at 1,000 and 10,000 rows exit 3 → 0; stored dates beside ISO text dates exit 3 → 0. Every case the lane does not reach writes a byte-identical twin. The repair round: 995 weekday dates beside 5 timed cells under `m/d/yyyy` keep their weekday census, twin weekend share 0.003 and midnight share 1.0 where reading the column as moments gave 0.282 and 0.009 (sources 0.0 and 0.995), byte-identical to 668f276; the census reads each column under its storage word and hands its reading over, so `synthtwin profile` CPU on 100,000 typed dates is 8.33 s against 668f276's 8.19 s (12.7 s before the repair), 100,000 date-times 18.0 s against 17.8 s. The second repair round: the line "as many timed cells as whole days" left the timed cells unparsed and wrote them as text, so the twin of 1,000 `m/d/yyyy` days beside 1, 5, 10, 40 or 50 timed cells exited 3 at `validate` and pandas read its column as text where the source's is dates (the first round's report named only the 995 + 5 weekday case); from 11 to 499 the column was read jointly as `iso-mixed`. With the line at one cell in a hundred and the few timed cells read as their days, all 29 of the second skeptic's shapes validate at exit 0 on both the twin and the source and every twin's column reads as dates: at one in a hundred or fewer the column is `iso-date` with a weekday census and a twin at midnight 1.0 against a source's 0.99 to 0.999 (the 995 + 5 weekday twin on a weekend 0.005), and above it the twin is byte-identical to e233f7f's, its midnight share exactly the source's; the 48 `r3probe` and `r3extra` shapes are byte-identical to the first round's. `K-S3-57`.

**Cost, and the call.** One published code per column, no new key: the date and date-time mix wears its code on one kind and the canonical code on the other (written back 0.5), and two codes of one kind come back as the commonest. ## Decision P4-D384 — numbers that are dates: read exactly, described as dates, written back as counts (lane R4, 2026-10-06)

**What it is** (the build plan's lane R4, its design review folded in). A spreadsheet, a statistics package and a database keep a date as a number, and an export writes that number: such a column was described as numbers, its twin kept each spelling and lost the calendar -- weekday TVD 0.13 to 0.16 on date counts at 1,000 rows, a 15-minute clinic grid held on 0.009 of cells -- and NF51 read SAS and Stata counts a decade late. One closed table of twelve counting systems (`date_counts.py`) now reads them: Excel's 1900 system with its day 60 and its 1904 system; days, seconds and milliseconds since 1960; days, seconds, milli-, micro- and nanoseconds since 1970; Epic's days since 1840, whose figures after the point are a contact number; SPSS's seconds since 1582. A count is read exactly, by whole-number arithmetic, and one that is not whole is written as the exporter's binary64. A column named under `settings.forced_date_counts` (`--date-count NAME SYSTEM`, or an answer to question Q3) is settled at the finest unit at least its figures' step, described as dates, and twinned as the same counts spelled as it spells them -- `count_form`: places, trimming, fifteen or seventeen significant figures, R's exponent form, the mark, and on Epic's system the census of contact numbers, spaced evenly over the twin's rows (contract 6.6.2, CD1 to CD5, NF115, NF116; method G7.10 and its oracle mirror, frozen in vectors file 26). `count_form` is EXACT-OBSERVABLE: every count of the checked file is held to the published form, and the census of contact numbers exactly (validation method V5-CF). A column whose figures no such unit keeps is not read as dates and says so (NF115). A count naming no date, 1900-01-01 or 9999-12-31 is no value and written back as written, whatever `--keep-value` names; 0 and -1 are read as the days they name.

**Question Q3, "number or date?"** A column read as numbers is asked where, beside each system's set-aside numbers, the rest are nine tenths of its present cells and at least eleven, text cells stand to the date role's own line, at most one in a hundred (one at least) strays, and one rule holds: one width inside 1990 to 2050, counts of days that are not whole writing four figures or fifteen significant ones and Epic days mostly writing no contact number (`inside-a-band`); whole counts finer than a day at midnight UTC, eleven different, inside 1900 to 2050, mostly a year or more from the epoch and not on a thousand-day step (`at-midnight`); every count beside the set-aside numbers written in figures alone, one width of five figures or more, in a system of days (`fixed-width-days`). Every system of the unit whose years fit, and on a column not all whole whose reading would keep every figure (`date_counts.figures_kept`, the profiler's own decision), is offered after `measurement`, which Enter keeps. NF113 says the question, naming a set-aside number only where the census line of cells holds it (eleven at the default floor, 36 at a floor of 36); NF114 gives each system's years from the outermost published rung that is a date of the column, past every heap NF113's words name in every system offered; NF51 is no longer written.

(ii) A tail of counted dates steps its group off the islands before G7.3b step 10 takes it to the half day, in the generator, the validator and the oracle alike. The weekday pass now holds them on moments too, as the oracle's `weekday_hole_days` already did; methods G7.3f and G7.10 say so. The ledger cap moves to 550,000 for `K-S3-60`.

## Decision P4-D385 — four paths of the largest tables grow with the rows, not their square (stage 4 tier 1, 2026-10-01)

**The change, which moves no published fact and no twin byte.** (1) Each end-carrier search of G9.5 and G9.6 is handed the first pair of each shape in the fixed order, the pairs it asked before and in the same order; the second tier of `_identifier_packings`, which needs every pair, works each out from its step. The order was built as a list of every pair of groups, and an all-different column has a group per row. (2) The form pass, the class pass and the level pass of P4-D231 look the levels the floor holds back up in a mapping, where every cell walked a list of them and the class pass copied its list once per level. (3) `_label_content` grows its column in place, where it copied the column once per level. (4) A tally remembers the verdict `_decide` gave it under each set of arguments (`_decision`), so a column's three or four questions walk the ladder once; the memory goes with the tally, and one kept beside the module was refused because it held about 0.7 GB per all-different column of 2,000,000 rows into the next column.

**Measured** on 668f276 and on this, lane D1's certificate stubbed as the measure-first lane stubbed it, in CPU seconds at a load average near 40. On the made-up 50-column health table of 10,000 rows the six files are byte-identical; describing takes 40.2 s for 96.4 and validating 94.0 for 195.0, and the twin is built in 44.6 s and 114 MB where 668f276 reached 5.8 GB and was stopped (with the first change alone, 43.7 s). When the rows double, the pairs handed, the comparisons and the bytes grow 1.0, 2.0 and 1.97 times where the replaced functions grow 4.01, 4.05 and 3.56, and the ladder is walked once per question where it was walked three times (`K-S4-03`).

**This landing's calls, reversible.** `K-S4-03` is a headline in `K-2B-14`'s place, since stage 4 needs one and the board stands at its cap of 30; the ledger's byte cap moves to 364,000 for it; and the class pass's copying, which the lane did not name, is repaired beside the two lookups it did, being the same quadratic over the same levels.

**Its review (one round, 2026-10-02), every item repaired.** (1) The identifier search of G9.6 built every group's permission for every shape before it knew the shape repeated one already tried: on an identifier of `k + 1` group sizes whose last alone can carry the shortest value, `(k * k + 1)(k + 1)` permissions for `k + 1` questions. `_window_change` knows a repeat from its two carriers, and the windows are worked out three at a time: 8,421 permissions at 461 rows become 441, the twin byte-identical. At `k = 60` the twin is built in 6 s where 110cb46 took 215. What remains on that shape is the allocator's walk on the one question that packs -- the other `k` are answered in milliseconds -- which tries every fill of the cell of ordinary numbers written in figures alone that the smaller groups allow before the one that finishes: 101,994 fills at `k = 60` (3,781 rows, 6 s) and 826,616 at `k = 80` (6,641 rows, 57 s and 1.26 GB). It is the walk 110cb46 ran, fill for fill; this decision does not change it, and it is a defect of the allocator's own that the review did not name. (2) **The compatibility decision.** The loader still accepts a level that holds spellings of its label back by group size, as the producer wrote one before P4-D275 -- though not the description that producer wrote, which lacks three entries the format gained since and is refused whole, so such a level reaches the generator only in a description written or edited by hand -- and one holding back a million of them, each written twice, asked G8.2 for trailing spaces up to a million long, about 496 GB, each search starting again at one space. G8.2's supply is now bounded -- the flips at the counter's 4,096th step, as before, the trailing spaces at 64 -- and its walk resumes where it stopped; a group past both is written in its level's commonest published spelling, the label where none is, which is how the producer has counted a spelling below the floor since P4-D275, and the twin's report names how many groups were and prints the count of different values it falls short of. No description the producer writes today reaches the bound. The oracle mirrors it (A-P4-59), and method G8.2 states it. On a column described by the earlier rule, 4,300 groups of two of a 13-letter label: 158 s and a cell of 217 characters before, 0.72 s and 77 now. On the review's own label, 4,200 groups of two described byte for byte as c5d09d5 describes them but for those three entries: 8,816,640 case flips, 105 s and a cell of 125 characters before, 4,096 flips, 0.4 s and 85 now; and its million spellings, two million rows, in 88 s and 544 MB, no cell more than 64 characters longer than the label. (3) Nine lists grown by copying a comprehension in -- `_groups_of` among them, 1,412,996,166 references recopied on an identifier of 1,998,990 rows -- grow in place, and the static guard reads a comprehension as a list. (4) The pair search is measured by the lines it runs, not the pairs it hands back, and the class pass by the bytes it allocates; each growth test requires the regression the review named -- every pair listed and one kept per shape, and the class's list copied per level -- to grow as the square (`K-S4-03`). (5) The references for `_label_content` and `_read_the_column` are frozen texts in `tests/stage4_as_built.py`, no longer rebuilt from the product's source, and a change of meaning made to either product function is required to break its comparison.

## Decision P4-D386 — the second key cut: three declarations and the form of counted dates, reserved (2026-10-02)

**What it is.** The second key cut, as 3b.K (P4-D364) was the first, so lanes R2a, R2c (P4-D383) and R4 (P4-D384) each fill a key without re-recording the frozen vectors, the goldens or the manifest. The settings block carries `century_windows` (R2a, question Q5), `forced_date_columns` (R2c, question Q6) and `forced_date_counts` (R4, question Q3), each `[]`, and every `datetime` block carries `count_form` (R4), `null`; each is LOADER-ONLY until the landing that fills it, and the loader refuses anything else (R16). Twenty-seven settings keys (C6-20). N6's `subsecond_census` is not reserved: it has no design, and a schema fixed before one would cost a second re-record (the R2 design review, m8).

**The cross-key rule, S8d** (the R4 design review, item 10; S8c is the code the T1 review's repair gives its 12-hour rule). A column named in `forced_date_counts` may not also be named in `forced_date_columns`, `century_windows`, `forced_twelve_hour_clocks`, `forced_codes`, `forced_identifiers` or `forced_measurements`; a decimal comma may stand beside it. The loader reads the three declarations' shapes and holds S8d before it refuses them as not empty, so the rule stands before R4 lands and R4 deletes only the refusal.

**Beside P4-D375's relief** (merged with the G1 review's repair): the four keys join C6-45a's list, so a description written before the cut, which carries none of them, reads each as empty, `count_form` as `null`.

**Anchors.** Every append block gains the lines of 3b-R2a, 3b-R2b and 3b-R2c (P4-D383) and 3b-R4 (P4-D384), after 3b-J. R2b has no key: the clock half reads layouts under T1's `forced_twelve_hour_clocks`. Vectors file and KPI numbers for R2a and R4 stay the integrator's to assign.

**Proof.** On 56 cases (the shipped fixtures, the eight shapes as text and workbook, the stage 3b gate's date columns and 23 date, clock and counted-number spellings; floors 11 and 1, seeds 0 and 7), every exit code of 336 runs and all 560 other files (inputs, twins and reports) are byte-identical to 110cb46's, and the 56 descriptions differ from its by 203 added lines, each one of the four reserved keys; the re-recorded vectors files and both goldens differ from 110cb46's by those keys alone; the document vectors and the numeric vectors are unchanged.

**Its review (one round, 2026-10-05), both items repaired.** (1) The loader looked for a column named twice in `century_windows` or `forced_date_counts` by searching a list of the names read before it, and S8d searched six lists, the windows' columns built again each time, for every counted column: work in the square of the entries before a description this version refuses was refused. At 9cb2eb5 a 100-row table's description holding 80,000 different counted pairs, 4.5 MB, took 17.2 s to reach its refusal, and twice the pairs four times as long. The names read are a set, and S8d gathers each other reading's names into a set once; the entries are taken in the order written and the readings in S8d's own order, so every refusal names the entry it named before, and S8d still stands before the reserved-key refusal. The same description is refused in 0.57 s. `tests/test_stage3b_second_cut_work.py` counts the comparisons and hashes asked of the names at 500 and 1,000 entries over three shapes -- a ratio of 2.0, and 4.0 at 9cb2eb5 -- requires the searches 9cb2eb5 shipped, kept there, to grow as the square under the same count, and pins the entry each refusal names and S8d's place. (2) Section 6.6.2 of the contract still said twenty-seven added keys after the cut made them twenty-eight; it says twenty-eight and names `count_form` among the additions, and `tests/test_p4d26_contract_describes_the_producer.py` holds the stated count to `DATETIME_KEYS`.

**The regression mechanism for its loader item** (the push critic of 2026-10-09, minor 14). No ledger entry counts the loader's work. The nodes of `tests/test_stage3b_second_cut_work.py` -- `test_the_reserved_declarations_are_read_in_step_with_their_entries`, `test_the_first_column_written_twice_is_the_one_named`, `test_s8d_names_the_first_counted_column_under_its_first_other_reading` and `test_s8d_stands_before_the_reserved_key_refusal_however_long_the_lists` -- count the comparisons and hashes at 500 and 1,000 entries and pin the entry each refusal names, and those nodes, which the whole suite runs at every landing, are the regression mechanism: a search that grows as the square again turns them red.

## Decision P4-D387 — mostly whole columns are walked, and large tables read, without the square of their rows (stage 4 tier 2a, 2026-10-05)

**The change, which moves no published fact and no twin byte.** (1) G6.4's walk (`_whole_enough`) worked out every later stratum's share for each stratum it visited and asked candidates out to the column's reach: each share is now worked out once and the strata still to be walked are asked of an index (`_walk_shares`, `_held_after`), `_whole_inside` stops past the half unit, one holder is counted rather than searched for, and the numbers taken follow the strata as they move. (2) G5.2's reach step offers its whole numbers a step at a time (`_free_whole_at`), a window search resumes past its last answer and stops at a window one cell wide, each round reads each share once, and rounds that come back to a division they reached are stepped past a whole number of repeats (`_reach_sizes`). (3) Detection cuts the first megabyte into lines once (`dialect.opening_lines`), the survey's walk and the standard reader's check take each line as it is cut (`dialect.lines_in_turn`), and a column's row order is read until it is settled (`dialect._column_order`). (4) The pandas check reads the file a piece at a time, in the steps pandas' own reader parses it (`_pandas_rows_a_piece`, 16,384 rows at fifty columns), and compares and drops each piece; where a piece differs or pandas fails, the file is read again as one frame and checked as before, so every refusal is the whole frame's, word for word, and a file the two readers agree on is held once. Both readings come from one call and are handed over at one line, the whole frame as one piece of every row, so a warning pandas gives about a file shows once, as when it was read once, save for a file pandas reads in part and then cannot read at all: pandas may warn about the part it read (pandas 3, rows ending in a delimiter their header does not), where 110cb46, failing before it handed anything over, showed nothing; the refusal is the same, word for word. The size is pandas' own because pieces of one row read 37 of 2,500 made-up texts that the whole frame refuses, each with lines ended by carriage returns alone.

**Measured** on 110cb46 and 833526d (CPU seconds at load averages of 9 to 60, so none judged; every pair wrote the same bytes). One column of mostly whole charges is twinned at 1,000, 2,000 and 4,000 rows in 0.2, 0.4 and 1.3 s against 5.2, 18.8 and more than 300; day counts with a visit's fraction on some rows, at 4,000 and 10,000 rows, in 0.6 and 1.3 s against 62.7 and more than 300. Rows doubled, the walk runs 2.03 times the lines where 110cb46 ran 4.19, and with the reach step left out it takes 1.1, 2.6 and 6.0 s over 100,000, 200,000 and 500,000 charges, where 110cb46 passed 300 s at 100,000. The made-up 50-column health table is read at 100,000, 200,000 and 500,000 rows in 17.3, 33.8 and 83.3 s, holding 4.20, 4.61 and 4.32 KB a row above its start at the peak, against 23.2, 45.4 and 113.4 s and 6.71, 6.65 and 5.97 KB (2,914 MB at 500,000, at the edge of the 3 GB a process is given). The readings are the same, and so are the readings and refusals of 2,500 made-up texts and of 80 tables of 9,000 to 20,000 rows and 64 to 160 columns, damaged ones among them; a full run's six files are the same bytes at 10,000 and 100,000 rows and its five before `validate` at 200,000, where describing peaks at 1,035 MB against 1,563; and so is every file, exit and message of 33 table-and-setting runs, workbooks and the shipped fixtures' own tables among them. Reading cuts one list of lines where it cut 31 (the first megabyte 29 times, the whole text twice), and five unsorted columns are read as numbers for 17 to 21 cells where every cell was. The replaced functions are the oracles of `tests/test_stage4_tier2a.py`, sixteen of whose tests each fail on 110cb46 by their own measure. `K-S4-02`.

**Calls, reversible.** `K-S4-02` reads its own table at 200,000 rows and not the design's 500,000, which hold about 2 GB at the reader's peak, more than a process is given beside other work on the shared build machine. Its bound, 5 KB a row, stands above this landing (4.56 and 4.70) and below 110cb46 (5.49 and 5.55), read in turn at a load near 9; under heavier load the system compresses pages and both read lower, so the bound is judged on the quiet machine only.

**The next item of stage 4: G5.2's reach rounds.** They now set the time on these columns wherever the ladder is crowded onto fewer whole numbers than strata: each round asks every stratum, and the rounds run toward their bound, the strata and two. Day counts over 3,650 days take 63 s at 10,000 rows (2,037 rounds) and 222 s at 50,000; charges 77 s at 16,000 (1,593 rounds) and 128 s at 32,000; and 500,000 wide charges, 262,293 strata at about three seconds a round, did not finish `generate` in 900 s of CPU, where 200,000 took 31 s. 833526d keeps these rounds: the same rounds and twins at 10,000 and 16,000 rows. The rounds keep moving rather than repeating, and a faster round keeps the bound, so mending them changes the method and may move twin bytes: a landing of its own, owed before such a column of a million rows can be twinned. The reader's peak is now the survey's own; `validate` still lists the checked file's lines in its form checks.

**The Codex review, one round (2026-10-08): both items mended, and no byte moves.** (1) A ladder read upward can still give shares that step back: G5.3's convex form rounds, so between two rungs a unit in the last place apart (`0.1` and `0.10000000000000002`) one share's end can read the higher and the next the lower, and the walk's index then asked every stratum -- 1,250,748, 5,005,496 and 20,050,986 steps read at 2,000, 4,000 and 8,000 rows of a column the producer reads as continuous. Such shares are now laid over the pieces of the line their ends cut, each run a halving makes keeping the furthest step of a share covering it (`_covering_index`), both ends compared as before: from 2,000 to 64,000 rows the walk reads 15,618 to 700,780 entries of the index, 25 to 35 a question, where the scan read 1,250,748 to 1,283,479,890 on the same questions. (2) Lines were cut at line feeds alone, so a file of carriage-return lines, or a run of them after the last line feed, was cut into one list held while the survey filled its table: 3,644.6 bytes a row at the survey's peak against 3,140.6 with line feeds on 10,000 rows of 50 columns, and 3,514.8 against 3,044.1 on 100,000. Every line ending now ends a block, and a pair across a block's end stays one ending (`_line_end_from`): 3,139.1 to 3,140.5 bytes a row with line feeds, carriage returns, the pair and mixed endings at 10,000 rows, and 3,044.0 to 3,044.1 at 100,000. `K-S4-02` now holds the survey's traced peak with carriage returns alone and with mixed endings under 1.05 times its peak with line feeds, machine-free (1.164 and 1.125 on 9fa2008, 1.0 now). Twins, reports and descriptions of 110cb46, 9fa2008 and this head are the same bytes on 402 columns at seeds 0 to 2 -- Codex's at 2,000 rows, the lane's charges and day counts, 360 small mixed ones -- and so are the readings and refusals of the 2,500 made-up texts, the 80 large tables and 144 files written with every line ending, a byte-order mark and quoted line breaks; four of the five tests added fail on 9fa2008 by their own measure. Measuring past 16,000 rows met G5.5's sign repair (`_sign_repairs`), which builds again the list it reads for every stratum it reads while repairing one: the square of the strata for each stratum repaired, 22 of the 26 s `generate` took under a profiler at 8,000 rows of that column, and owed by a later landing; it was measured here with that list built once, to the same twins.

**G5.5's sign repairs, owed above, are mended (2026-10-08, and for nought 2026-10-09), and no byte moves.** `_sign_repairs` counts the values the other strata hold once, at its first grid step, and keeps the count as it repairs them; and each band's walk (`_grid_step_of_sign`) begins where its last one stopped, and from the first step again wherever a value its steps can read back as stops being held -- nought for both sides, which the first steps of a grid of 324 places or more read back as. d36627f began a walk again only for a value strictly on its side, so two negative strata drawn onto `0.0` at 330 places took `-1.0` and `-1.0` where 564c61a gave `-1.0` and `-0.0`; 11fa2aa mends it. A layout's negative strata stand before its positive ones, so a walk begins again only after the last stratum holding nought lets it go. On the Codex column the lines the repairs run grow 2.02 times from 2,000 rows to 4,000, where 564c61a's grew 4.43, and 2.0 times a doubling up to 1,000,000 rows; on strata a quarter of which walk past every point their band holds they grow 2.00 times, where 564c61a's grew 3.92 (`K-S4-05`). `generate` there takes 1.2, 5.7, 27.6 and 647 s of CPU at 8,000, 32,000, 128,000 and 1,000,000 rows, at most 844 MiB resident, where 564c61a took 21.1 s at 8,000 and had not finished 32,000 at 900. In a run of `generate` alone at 1,000,000 rows, 624 s, the repairs take 0.34 s and `_number_cells` 249: its identity walk starts its leading-zero orders from the first again for every repeated spelling of a value, the square of its spellings, which this column's own text grows with (111 MB at that size), owed by a later landing; the other passes together grew 2.4 times from 128,000 rows to 256,000. Twins and reports are the same bytes on 564c61a and this head: the Codex column at 2,000 to 16,000 rows; 360 random columns on a written grid whose twins take 26,035 grid steps, 30 of them written at 324 to 330 places, where no twin took more than one step and d36627f's rule answered alike; and the 172 descriptions the suite hands a sign repair, at seeds 0 to 2 and the suite's own. 564c61a's two functions are the oracle of `tests/test_stage4_sign_repairs.py`: its three growth tests fail on it by their own measure, and d36627f's rule answers otherwise in 418 of its 4,000 strata sets of 322 to 330 places. The third takes both measures again on values that run a line each time a builtin hashes or compares one, because a builtin runs as one line however many values it reads: a repair that kept the values held in a list, or gathered them again at every repair with `dict.fromkeys`, grew about twice on the Codex column by the lines alone (skeptic 1 of the lane). Those values run a line for an ordering comparison too, since a repair sorting them or taking their `min` or `max` at every repair also grew about twice (skeptic 2). On them the repairs grow 2.02 and 2.00 times, 564c61a's 4.79 and 3.94, and three such repairs built from the shipped grid step (a list searched, a dict built again, a list sorted again) 4.01 and 3.76, 3.27 and 3.16, and 3.27 and 3.11; a repair that only copies the values held is seen by neither measure, the accepted limit only `K-S4-05`'s recorded seconds bound. `K-S4-05` holds both measures.

**Recorded beside it, older than this decision** (lane S2's second skeptic, 2026-10-08; already so on 110cb46). A semicolon table whose rows end in `;` and whose header does not is read as ONE column, named by its whole header line, semicolons and all (four fields beginning `patient_id;age`), holding whole records as free text: profile exits 0, asks no question and describes 400 rows and 1 column, so code written on that twin cannot run on the real table. The same table without the trailing `;` reads as its 4 columns, and its comma form reads right. Owed to delimiter detection; its owner is lane R5, reading (the orchestrator, 2026-10-09).

**Lane R5, reading, mends it, and a reader crash beside it (2026-10-13).** (1) Detection required the table's first record to stand at the reading's width, so under the semicolon a header of four fields over rows of five, the fifth empty, was rejected, no candidate read two fields, and the comma a table no candidate reads falls back to took the file; the same held for a tab and a vertical bar, and for a header ending in the delimiter over rows that do not. `survey` already read both shapes, so detection now accepts exactly those two (`dialect.opening_lines_up`): a first record one field narrower than the width, at least two wide, over records at that width that all end in an empty field; or one field wider whose own last field is empty. That record then counts at the width, so the share is 1.0 and a competitor reading as consistently is still asked about in the questions file. A one-field first record never lines up, so a one-column table whose cells end in `;` stays one column. Shared functions changed: `_width_share` (now over `_width_counts`), `_best_reading`, `_sequence_of`; signatures unchanged. The oracle's `best_reading` mirrors it and the document vectors' `delimiter_reading` reads four `lined_up` files, with a second mutant (A-P4-59); the nine cases beside it rebuilt byte-identical. (2) `_sequence_of` turned a cell into an int, and a cell of 5,001 figures, first or later, raised ValueError past Python's 4,300-figure limit; sequence cells are now compared as text with the figures of the number they must be. **Measured** on a battery of 63 made-up tables (comma, semicolon, tab and bar, with a trailing delimiter on neither side, the records, the header or both; LF and CRLF; a byte-order mark; quoted fields holding the delimiter; headerless; one-column; decimal commas beside semicolons; 5,001-figure cells first and later): the other 39 have byte-identical descriptions, questions and twins; the 20 read as one column or refused are read as their four columns, each twin line ending in the delimiter where the source's did, and both twin and source validate at exit 0; the 4 that crashed are described. Over 20,000 random made-up texts 4,267 readings moved, every one where base fell back to the comma. Describing a semicolon table of 100,000 and 1,000,000 rows without the trailing `;` gives the same bytes on base and head (wall 17.5 and 14.4 s, 142 and 162 s, on a machine at load 3 to 6; peak 299 and 272 MB, 1,952 and 1,919 MB); with it, head reads 4 columns in 15.7 and 164 s at 273 and 1,918 MB, where base refused the 100,000-row table at exit 1 (its decimal commas read as a second comma field). Detection alone reads 0.018 s on both, the records it hands the new rule capped by the sample at 1,000 and 1,000,000 rows (`tests/test_r5_trailing_delimiter_reading.py`, each test red on its mutant). **Left:** a headerless table whose rows end in the delimiter reads an empty last column, written back empty, so its trailing delimiter is kept.

**A class of files goes from described to refused (lane R5's repair, skeptic 1's item 1 and skeptic 2's item 3, 2026-10-13).** Any semicolon, tab or bar table whose rows end in the delimiter (or whose header alone does) and that holds a row the reading cannot read was described at 0ecc82d as ONE column (exit 0); read now under its delimiter, that row cannot be read, and the file is refused at exit 1, the refusal the same file gets without trailing delimiters -- except where a row inside the sample holds a value after the closing delimiter; detection then does not line up and the file is still read as one column at exit 0, as on 0ecc82d (row 51 `...;x`, alone or beside a row 61 of two values; skeptic 2's accepted observation). That covers a row that does not end in the delimiter, one that holds a value after it, one that ends in it under a header that alone does, and any row of too few or too many values (skeptic 2's probes over 120 rows ending in `;`: A, row 51 `P0051;age;arm;`; E, row 51 ending `;;`; F, row 51 unclosed and row 61 of two values -- each exit 0 with one column on 0ecc82d, exit 1 on the repair). Measured on four made-up tables of 120 or 600 rows: rows 4, 14, ... (12 in all) not ending in `;`; row 501, past the 400-record sample, not ending in it; row 501 holding `x` after it; a header and row 51 alone ending in it -- each exit 0 with one column on 0ecc82d, exit 1 on the repair. The ragged-rows sentence these files first got ("The first row names 4 columns, but row 51 has 4", and a value needing quotation marks) was false, so `survey` now counts apart the rows that differ from the reading only by the trailing delimiter and, where every offending row is of that kind and no retry without the trailing guess is owed, refuses with `errors.trailing_delimiter_uneven`, which names each row and the delimiter it lacks or carries and asks that every row end the same way; any other ragged row keeps the ragged-rows sentence. The comma form was refused before as ragged and now gets the same true reason. The detection test also pins that a first record two fields narrower or wider lines up with nothing (skeptic item 2). Shared function changed: `survey` (an added branch before the ragged refusal; name and signature unchanged). Skeptic 2's items 1 and 2: a closing empty field is the delimiter that ends the row, not a value, so a row is filed as lacking the trailing delimiter only where it holds `width` fields and its last holds something or is quoted (`P0051;30;F;""` reads "row 51 does not end in a semicolon", not "has 3"; the verifier's item 2), and the ragged sentence counts each row's own values (A reads "row 51 has 3", E "row 51 has 5"); a row of exactly `width` values is left out of the ragged listing, where it would read "names 4 columns, but row 51 has 4", and still counted in the total (F reads "row 61 has 2 (2 rows in total)"). Pinned by `test_a_row_the_reading_cannot_read_is_named_by_its_own_values`, red on mutants `kind0_no_closed_check`, `kind0_count_only` (probe K, row 51 `P0051;30`: "row 51 has 2", which the count-only mutant filed as unclosed) and `any_uneven_not_every`, and by `test_a_quoted_empty_last_value_is_a_value_not_the_closing_delimiter`, red on `closed_ignores_quote`.

## Decision P4-D388 — a weekday census is withheld where the count of different values leaves its body too little room, either way (stage 3b landing 3b.D1b, 2026-10-05)

**Why.** D0's repair found twins at the floor of 36 that published a weekday census and came back holding more different values than their column (59 over its batteries at seeds 0 to 2); P4-D365's few-dates rule had been measured at the floor of 11 alone. A tail that publishes its two distances is rebuilt with up to the floor's number of different days, the count pass leaves the body what the tails leave of the column's count, and the census then asks the body for a day of each of its groups inside every gap between two pins.

**The decision.** The producer withholds the census -- at every floor since its Codex review, above the floor of 11 alone before it -- where the room the count of different values leaves the body is less than the census needs (`calendar_rules.count_room_short`), said in NF74's one sentence; a room equal to the need publishes it. The room is the column's different days less the most days the twin's two tails keep at all but a tenth of seeds (`tails_kept`, since the ruling on its price below; until it the most they could hold, `tails_most`: a listed tail's values; otherwise the floor's number, no more than the tail's rows and no more than two days past what its own spread allows); the need is every pin day (`body_pins`: the two boundaries and the rungs published between them) and, inside each gap, a day of every group holding rows that has a day strictly inside it and is the group of neither of its pin days, at most one a rank; and the census must need a day past the pins. The few-dates and room rules are unchanged. The landing promised every description at the floor of 11 and below unchanged; its Codex review withdrew that promise (item 1) and added the count's other direction (item 2).

**Measured** on the 26 date batteries of D0's identity run (4,781 tables), seeds 0 to 4, 493f6f8 against this landing, over the twins of every table whose document holds, is offered or changes a census (every other table writes one document both sides). "Long by the census": a twin holding more different values than the column beside a published census whose withheld twin meets the count.

| floor | censuses published | twins | twins with a MISSED check | long by the census | withheld, left long / met |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 11 | 2,379 → 2,379 | 17,950 | 35 → 35 | 0 → 0 | none |
| 20 | 2,135 → 1,946 | 14,860 | 146 → 60 | 86 → 0 | 23 / 166 |
| 36 | 1,208 → 1,124 | 7,735 | 147 → 60 | 87 → 0 | 19 / 65 |
| 50 | 978 → 868 | 6,375 | 253 → 95 | 158 → 0 | 34 / 76 |

No twin misses a check its 493f6f8 twin met, and at the landing no document at the floor of 11 changed; its Codex review changes 18 there (below). At the floor of 12, on the eight batteries the landing's review measured there (4,037 tables), 1,931 censuses become 1,901, and the 5 twins long by their census become none: of the 30 withheld one left its twins long (`_hunt(690)`) and 29 were met. The price is the last column's second figure: censuses withheld whose twins met them.

**What was set aside**, scored on 493f6f8's records (censuses withheld beyond 493f6f8's at 20, 36 and 50): the few-dates thresholds scaled with the census line, 618, 509 and 553, and by its square root 367, 303 and 306 with 1, 5 and 5 columns still long by the census; the floor's number alone as each tail's most, 297, 115 and 141. With the twins' own tail days in place of the most the rule would withhold 23, 19 and 71. Withholding at the need itself too, as the landing first did, withheld 19 more at 20 and one more at 50, every one met by its twins, and no census that left a twin long had a room equal to its need. Asked at the floor of 11 the rule would withhold 15 censuses, every twin meeting them, and none at 5, so it was not asked there until its Codex review. Of the 36,835 tail sides of the batteries' published twins, none held more than one day past its spread bound; two are allowed.

**Its review (one round, 2026-10-05), every item repaired.** (1) A room equal to the need publishes, above, and `_hunt(169)` at the floor of 20 holds it. (2) A gap of one rank and (3) the scope at the floor of 12, `_hunt(690)`, each hold a node, and (4) the rule's pins are held to the body pins the generator lays (`generation._date_layout`), where landing 3b.D4 pins each listed date. (5) The counts at the floor of 11 read 15 of 2,379. Of 43 mutants of the rule, its pins, its tails' most, its scope, its call and the generator's body pins, 41 turn a node of `tests/test_stage3b_count_room.py` red; the other two change no answer.

**Its Codex review (one round, 2026-10-06), its three items repaired.** (1) `_hunt(690)` with one `2024-07-02` cell written `2024-05-16` published its census at the floor of 11 and its twins at seeds 2, 3 and 17 held 25, 27 and 27 values for 24 (24 with the census emptied): the count-room rule is asked at every floor now, withholds it, and withholds 15 more censuses of the batteries at 11, every twin of which met them; the landing's promise of no change at 11 is withdrawn. (2) A rebuilt tail can hold fewer days than the real one, and the census can keep the body off the days that make them up: the review's fortnight at 21 came back with 11 for 12 at seeds 0, 7 and 31. The count-reach rule (`count_reach_short`) withholds where the body's NEED passes what the census lets it REACH -- the distinct pin days and, in each gap, the days the census allows, no more than the gap's ranks, no hole, no more of a group than its count -- and the census narrows that reach. The need reads the count pass that runs before the day pass: the body's ranks drawn independently land on about n(1 - (1 - 1/n)^r) of a gap's n days; where that draw and the tails' most fall short of the count the pass only splits and the rule reads the tails at their most -- which the high tail reaches only where the body's nearer splits run out first, as its second verification found (below) -- and where it merges the body keeps no more than its draw and the tails no fewer than their fewest. The tails' fewest and most are G7.3b's spans, its steps written a second time (`tails_fewest`, `tails_most_rebuilt`) and held to `generation._tail_distance_bounds`. (3) `K-S3-59`'s name, the changelog and the test module's opening lines now claim what was measured; fifteen Mondays at the floor of 36, 33 values for 15 with or without their census, stay a stated limit. On the batteries, 4a4b901 against the repaired code (the landing's records, seeds 0 to 4):

| floor | censuses published, 4a4b901 → now | count-room rule at 11, newly withheld and met | count-reach rule, withheld left short / met | left short by the census, 4a4b901 → now |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 11 | 2,379 → 2,361 | 15 | 3 / 0 | 3 → 0 |
| 20 | 1,946 → 1,944 | -- | 2 / 0 | 2 → 0 |
| 36 | 1,124 → 1,122 | -- | 2 / 0 | 2 → 0 |
| 50 | 868 → 865 | -- | 3 / 0 | 3 → 0 |

None is left long either side, and the twins of all 25 censuses newly withheld meet every check at seeds 0 to 4. Over 2,000 short spans (5,496 offered censuses at 11, 21, 36 and 50) the rule withholds 0, 2, 4 and 2, each short at all five seeds, and leaves none short; over 25 weekday-only logs (83 offered at the four floors, seeds 0 to 2) it withholds 6, one short and five met, and every census it publishes is met; over six business-day logs of one to thirty rows a day (24 offered) it withholds four, the log of about two rows a day over two years at each floor, every twin meeting its census restored. That was the rule's price until the ruling below, and it fell on columns holding a row on every day their census allows, or on all but one to three of them, where the count pass merges: the body can reach its own days and those few and no more, and the rule read every merge the pass may make as taken from the tails, down to their fewest, which asks up to four days past the body's own on the full logs measured. Measured at the review's verification, 4a4b901 against the repaired code, each log described at the floors of 11 and 20: of the 52 censuses 4a4b901 published over 28 Monday-to-Friday logs holding every business day (1.25 to 3 rows a day, 8 to 104 weeks) it withholds 21, all at 1.5 to 2.25 rows a day, 18 met by their twins at seeds 0 to 4 and 3 short (at 11, 11: 10 met and 1 short), and their withheld twins write 22 to 30 per cent of their rows on weekends, where the column holds none; of the 47 over 24 Monday-Wednesday-Friday clinics holding every clinic day (1.25 to 2.5 rows a clinic day, 13 to 104 weeks), 10, all at 1.25 to 1.75, 9 met and 1 short; of the 72 over 36 such business-day logs (1.5 to 2.25 rows a day, 26 to 104 weeks) with the federal holidays closed, 2, none at 11; and of the 51 over 28 Monday-to-Friday logs whose rows a day are Poisson draws, some business days left empty, none. Business days closed at random inside the body's span of Monday-to-Friday logs (1.5 to 2.25 rows a day, 39 and 78 weeks) left it withholding 16 of 32 censuses with none closed, 18 of 48 with one, every one met, 4 of 32 with three and none of 48 with six or twelve; the two-rows log with 4 July 2022 alone closed was withheld at all four floors, and with four days closed published at all four (the second verification, item 1). A node held both sides until the ruling below: the two-rows log with its 21 holidays closed kept its census at every floor, and three clinic days a week were withheld at 11, 20 and 36. Set aside: the tails' fewest whatever the draw, the repair's first reading, withheld one row a business day at every floor, which the gate publishes and its twins meet, and 23 of the weekday logs, and walked the body's span; the fewest wherever the pass merges, 12 of the logs; the tails' most alone left `_hunt(2291)` at 11 and one log short. Of 38 mutants of the two rules, their parts, the copy of G7.3b and the producer's call, 36 turn a node red; the other two -- a shortcut dropped, the weight's tolerance widened -- changed no answer found. At a million rows, one column of dates whose two tails tie 200,000 rows on a day each, the description takes 54.5 s where 4a4b901 took 59.7 s (47.5 and 47.3 s of processor time), its peak 723 MB against 669; the twin rebuilds those tails on 5 days where the real ones hold 22, so the reach rule withholds the census, and restored, the twin at seed 0 holds 524 different values for 541, where withheld it holds 541. An extra review of the lane found two calls of the producer the tests let pass, the two tails' rows handed over the other way round and the column's published count in place of its days; the producer's test now tells both apart, each red on its mutant. Recorded, not built: the draw is read at its expectation, so a twin whose body draws more days can still lose one; a workbook's date system is not asked for the tails' edges. **Recorded for the orchestrator, not built.** (1) Fifteen twins at the floor of 36 and fifty at 50 stay long beside a published census, and the census is not the cause: withheld, their twins are long too, their tails rebuilt with more days than the column holds (fewdates, the hunt batteries and the Tuesday clinics). One row a business day at 20 needs about 324 splits and its body offers about 322, so its high tail ends at its 20 at every seed; a log just above one row an open day offers more, and its body passes what the census lets it reach -- `_every_open_day(1.1, 26, 902, Monday to Friday)` at 36 keeps its low tail at 36 at every seed and its high tail at 29 to 35 of 36, and its body holds 62 to 65 days at the five seeds that come back short, where the census lets it reach 61. THE RULING (the orchestrator's, 2026-10-08, under the owner's principle of 2026-10-01: statistics and an acceptable build time, a HIPAA exposure the only privacy concern): this risk STANDS beside the one-in-ten risk, and the decision code does not change.
