## Decision P4-D389 — the packing walk is offered only what the cells after it can finish (stage 4, lane S3, 2026-10-06)

**The defect** (the wave-1 critic of item 1 of landing S1's review, which P4-D385 recorded). On Codex's declared identifier -- `7` written `2k + 1` times beside `k` values written 2, 4, ... `2k` times -- method G9.5's walk tried every set of the even sizes that fits the cell of ordinary numbers written in figures alone before the lone odd group, the only fill that finishes it, and wrote down each state it failed as three tuples. On 493f6f8 the twin took 2.1 s and 70 MB at `k = 50`, 6.7 s and 147 MB at 60, 21.3 s and 335 MB at 70 and 69.5 s and 925 MB at 80, about 3.3 times for every ten groups; at 100 -- 10,301 rows of 101 people, which the producer and the loader accept -- the machine's watchdog stopped it at 3.4 GB after 539 s, and at 200 it passed 1.8 GB in 276 s. The lane's identity battery found a second shape: a declared identifier of 300 values in four forms, 1 to 300 rows each (45,150 rows), passed 1.6 GB, and with the counts read one at a time, 27 of 60 seeded identifiers of 100 to 160 values in two to five forms took the walk past 100,000 states.

**The change, which moves no answer.** On entering a cell the walk reads five necessary conditions off the counts still owed and the groups still unplaced (`_cell_entry`): the least and the most each cell from this one on may hold, every count's cells held to what it owes together until no end moves (`_bounds_settled`); where each size can still stand, a size only this cell can hold being taken here whole; whether every count still owed can be made; which totals this cell may hold that the cells after it can complete; and what those cells must still find among the groups it leaves, each such reserve read once on entering and again inside `_cell_next` wherever the cell takes a copy of a size it reads, the sizes not yet decided counted at every copy (`_reserves_met`). The cell is offered the old order's fills less those, so the first answer is the old one. A failed state is one number (`_walk_mark`) in a memory bounded at 64 MB (`_WALK_MEMORY`); a state past it is walked again and fails again. Method G9.5 states both. The oracle states the answer and not the walk, so it does not move (A-P4-59).

**Measured** on 782bae7. The twin at `k` = 50, 60, 70, 80, 100 and 200 in 0.4, 0.5, 0.6, 0.8, 1.1 and 3.5 s and at most 56 MB, the walk entering `k + 12` states; at every size 493f6f8 finished, twin and report byte-identical. The identity battery -- the shipped fixtures, the stage-3 battery and the lane's walk cases, seeds 0 and 4 -- byte-identical on all 96 cases 493f6f8 finished; its 300-value identifier builds in 3.3 s. On the 35,827 of 36,000 seeded questions the walk as 493f6f8 shipped it answers within 200,000 states -- frozen as the oracle in `tests/stage4_as_built.py` -- the same answer every time and never more states: 1,522,207 where it entered 19,171,395. `K-S4-04`: the states grow 1.6 and 1.8 times as Codex's groups double, where 493f6f8's grew 21.8 times (the test is red on 493f6f8).

**Sixty more, drawn after the conditions were written** (2026-10-07). Seeds 60 to 119 of the same producer, each twin built with the walk stopped at 100,000 states: 7 take it past them (seeds 72, 73, 76, 103, 108, 111 and 112), where the sixty the conditions were read off left 2. And seed 105 showed what no count of states sees: each reserve filed under only the last size it reads, one cell tried every way of taking the smaller sizes before reading it, past 2,000,000 readings without leaving the 70th state of the twin's second packing question, and the twin was unbuilt after eighteen minutes. Each reserve is now read once on entering the cell and filed under every size it reads (782bae7): the fills offered are the same, so the answers and the states are, and that twin builds in 34 s -- seed 82's, 314 s before, in 0.4. `K-S4-04` holds the readings of seed 105's first two questions at 2,000 at most; they take 282.

**What stays** (`K-S4-04` open; STATE's broken list). Exact packing is the partition question, so no walk is quick on every input. Described at the floor of 11, 2 of the first sixty seeded identifiers and 7 of the sixty drawn after still take the walk past 100,000 states, and seed 37's question is still unanswered after 3,000,000 and ten minutes; described at a floor of 36, 12 of the 120 do (seeds 8, 37 and 48 of the first sixty, and 64, 66, 72, 76, 82, 103, 108, 111 and 112 of the sixty after), and seed 8, whose twin builds in 135 states at 11, is still unanswered in its second question after 1,000,001 states and 351 s -- the memory such a walk holds stays within the bound, and its time does not. The conditions cost more a state than 45f85b0's three, so a question they prune little takes longer: a grid built around an answer from the 38 groups of review item P2-C3-F1 took 8.3 s of CPU at 74,747 states where 45f85b0 took 5.6 s at 142,486, measured side by side. And a twin of an identifier in mixed forms can spend minutes outside the walk, in `_filled_layout`, which is not this lane's: of the 111 seeded twins that build on 782bae7, none spends more than 4.4 s in the walk, and seed 57's takes 208 s.

**Its first review (2026-10-07), four items, each repaired.** (1) No test held that `_reach_bits` adds the whole of a size the cell must take: with that branch never taken the walk answered alike in the same states and fills and read its reserves 8,127 times on a question where it reads 9, which a test now holds. (2) and (4) The seeded identifiers had been counted at the floor of 11 alone, and the walk's comment in `generation.py` still gave the first sixty's 2; both now give the 120 at floors 11 and 36. (3) At a million rows the walk cost more than 493f6f8's: on a declared identifier of 1,414 values held by 1 to 1,414 rows each, written as plain numbers -- 1,000,405 rows, where 493f6f8's walk prunes nothing and both enter 228 states -- it took 47.4 s against 16.4, and the twin 128.7 s of CPU against 98.9 and 511 MB against 437 (skeptic 1, 2026-10-07), nearly all of the walk in reading which totals some copies can make, each reading shifting a number as wide as the total once or more for every size. From 4,096 rows on (`_WIDE_TOTAL`) two readings that need no such number come first -- copies totalling less than the range refuse it, and copies taken from the largest size down find a total in it (`_makes_a_total`); for condition 4 the smallest sizes, each at most one more than those before it total, make every total to their sum and are set at once (`_owed_less`) -- and the halving walk reads only what they leave. Under 4,096 rows it reads everything as before, a reserve stopping at the first size that settles it: read the wide way at every width, the walk took 1.12 to 1.16 times a213d43's CPU on the lane's small seeded questions, and as it stands 0.96 to 0.98. Each reading answers as the halving walk does -- on 30,000 seeded inputs at both widths, against the totals built one copy at a time -- so the states, the fills, the answers and the twins are a213d43's. **Why.** The owner's ruling of 2026-09-17, item 5 counted as missing a label row a reader could recover by subtraction (P4-D231); reviews widened it to the forced band (P4-D239), the pinned pool (P4-D271), the four class totals (P4-D261) and the form census (round 2 of the review, item 3), and loader invariants B4b and B4c refused what it removed. ## Decision P4-D392 — a form holds the one gap before a clock's marker (lane L2, forms that hold a space, 2026-10-14)

**The fault (X4, P4-D383).** `parsing.shape_form` gave no form to a cell holding a space or U+202F (contract C6-31a and C6-97, section 7.9), so a column of `9:15 AM` or `08:15:30.123 AM` -- or with U+202F, as Excel and macOS write it -- beside rare words published no form and its twin wrote 0 of its 969 clock cells in their shape, where `9:15AM` kept 969. **The choice, measured before it was built** (`planning-notes/work-2026-10/wave5/L2/moves.py`, 220 tables: 108 clock columns over three roles -- one rare text in 33, labels, alone -- three clocks, three gaps and four markers, the 46 layout spellings and their partial spellings alone and beside rare words, eight two-word columns and four fixture tables, floor 11, seed 0, on 6a248e7): (a) one space or one U+202F, the cell's only one, between a clock's figures and one of the eight marker words moved 40 of the 72 spaced-meridiem descriptions and none of the 148 others, whose twins kept every byte; (b) one interior space anywhere moved those 40 and 27 more holding no spaced meridiem -- made-up names, `Ward 7`, `Bed 12A`, `120/80 mmHg`, two-word notes, stamps beside rare words, 15 layout spellings beside rare words and one fixture table -- and publishes a name's word lengths, the fact the space was kept out for. **(a) is taken**, the narrowest that fixes X4 and U+202F in every role the clock spelling takes a census in: free text beside rare words (0 to 969 of 969, both gaps), labels and codes (U+202F: 1,622 to 3,000 of 3,000; a fraction of the second after either gap: 1,500 to 3,000), and a U+202F column alone, which no clock reader takes (0 to 1,000 of 1,000); every such twin and table of that battery validates, which kept one rare text in 33 and so never reached the clock line (the repair round, below). The clock half of the layout reader and a `9:15 AM` column read as clock times publish no census and are unmoved. **Not fixed, stated:** a stamp beside rare words, `2024-01-05 9:15 AM`, holds two spaces and keeps no form under (a) or (b), 0 of 969 in shape on the battery, as a stamp without a marker beside rare words does. The gap stands as itself in the form (the owner's ruling of 2026-09-15); its key carries the marker as `@@`, `&&`, `@.@.` or `&.&.` and names no marker word. Built in product (`parsing.shape_form`, `parsing.is_a_written_form`, the new `parsing.meridiem_gap_at`; `generation._clock_shape` reads U+202F and `generation._form_words` counts it), oracle (`written_form`, `clock_shape`, `usable_stand_in`) and vectors file 25 (`labels_clock_narrow_gap`, seed 551, its mutant writing the gap as a plain space; every other file rebuilt byte for byte) in one commit (A-P4-59); contract C6-31a, C6-97 and 7.9.1, method G8.2a, G8.3, G8.3b and G9.5 step 7, and the validation method's recount. No loader refusal is added: a description written before L2 (6a248e7's, frozen) loads, generates its old twin byte for byte and validates -- its labels and codes since Codex's review, below. **Cost** (`scale.sh`, free text of `9:15 AM` beside one rare text in 33, read as a long tail at these sizes, its twin byte-identical before and after): describing 4.14 to 4.72 s at 100,000 rows and 30.8 to 31.3 s at 1,000,000, memory 147 and 751 MB, moved under 2 %; generating 4.57 to 5.98 s and 34.4 to 42.6 s, memory 72 and 272 MB unmoved (base and lane run in turn on one machine) -- the census and its recount now taken on such a column, as on `9:15AM`. **What moved in the suite, as measured:** lane C1's traced face table (`HH:MM` beside 10 % `9:15 AM`, 3,000 rows, floor 36) now publishes `%%:%% @@` (78) and `%:%% @@` (204) beside `%%:%%` (2,718) and its twin misses nothing; three mutant clauses that overpaid `%%:%%` on face tables (lane L1's, the route-2 correction's and landing 3b.5's) left nothing to overpay once the minority had a form, so each now writes that minority with a no-break space U+00A0, which holds no form, as the minority was formless when they were measured; and the 3b.5 mutant withdrawing the spaced clock's key withdraws the gap too. The orchestrator named the lane on 2026-10-13; X4 is a passing test for both gaps. **Repair round (skeptic 1, 2026-10-14).** Past G8.3's clock line a gapped form was filled figure by figure with its marker key filled letter by letter, `0:00 AA`, which wears no form: free text of `h:mm AM` with a plain space at clock shares 0.975 to 0.985 wrote 4 to 29 such cells and 11 of 28 tables validated with exit 3 (`forms.published.%:%% @@` MISSED), where base validated them. `generation._filled_form` (through the new public `parsing.key_gap_at`) and the oracle's `filled_form` now fill only the clock's figures, at half the step, write the form's own gap and the marker word the step's parity names (method G8.3); every such twin validates (lane test G9, both gaps; vectors file 22 gains `labels_clock_spaced_line`, seed 552, whose mutant's `00:00 AA` the oracle refuses). ## Decision P4-D393 — a stamp's form holds the space between its date and its clock (lane L3, stamps beside rare words keep their shape, 2026-10-15)

**The fault (the orchestrator's ruling of 2026-10-14 on lane L2's skeptic 1, item 4; P4-D392's stated limit).** A column of date-and-time stamps beside a few words -- an EHR export's `2024-01-05 9:15 AM` or `2024-01-05 09:15`, about 3 per cent `pending` or `unknown` -- is read as text, and each stamp holds the space between its date and its clock, which no form took; the description published no form and the twin wrote 0 of its 969 stamps in their shape (L2's `battery-a1.json`, free-stamp-*), so code splitting or matching the real column's stamps stopped on the twin. **The choice, measured before it was taken** (`planning-notes/work-2026-10/wave5/L3/`: `battery.py`, 384 stamp columns -- ISO, US two-figure, US one-figure and day-first dates, a space or `T`, `H:MM`/`HH:MM`, seconds and milliseconds, no marker, a marker straight on, after a space and after U+202F -- beside rare words, as labels, as declared codes and alone, at a floor of eleven; and L2's `moves.py`, 220 tables). (a) The year-first hyphen and the year-last slash, the spellings the ruling names, with one plain space or one letter before a clock, then nothing, a marker straight on or L2's gap and a marker word, a stamp running to 32 characters: it moved 15 of the 220, all stamps beside rare words, and left REDCap's `05-01-2024 09:15`, a dotted and a two-figure-year stamp beside rare words formless. (b) Taken: any date of three figure runs parted twice by one hyphen, slash or point, a year of four first or a year of four or two last: it moved 20 of the 220, every one a stamp beside rare words, and none of the 200 others, whose descriptions and twins kept every byte; three runs of any width (one, two or four) in any order moved the same tables. On the 384 the twin now writes every stamp of the 288 not read as dates in its source's shape, `T`, marker word and gap included -- 93,024 of 93,024 beside rare words, 93,024 of 93,024 as codes (0 and 0 before) and 279,264 of 279,264 as labels (138,480 before, the published labels alone) -- no twin writes the other gap, and every twin and table validates with exit 0; the 96 read as dates did not move. The space between the date and the clock is a plain space only; two spaces, U+202F there, a month word, a compact date, an offset and a comma after the date keep the cell formless. The generator's figure fill writes a stamp's letter `T` (`t` in a lower-case key) and its marker key as a word, as L2's gap form does, and the room it advertises counts neither as letters (method G8.3). Built in product (`parsing.shape_form`, `parsing.is_a_written_form`, `parsing.meridiem_gap_at`, `parsing.key_gap_at` and `parsing.level_unshaped_before_gaps` extended, their names and signatures kept; new `parsing.stamp_gap_at`, `parsing.stamp_key_gap_at`, `parsing.stamp_key_parts`, `parsing.STAMP_FORM_LIMIT`; `generation._filled_form`, `generation._form_room` and `generation._form_as_read`), oracle (`written_form`, `form_gap`, `key_gap`, `form_room`, `filled_form`, `unshaped_before_gaps`, `form_as_read`, `usable_stand_in`) and vectors file 22 (`labels_stamp_gaps`, seed 571, its mutant filling the `T` by the step; file 25 had no room; every other file rebuilt byte for byte) in one commit (A-P4-59); contract C6-31a, C6-31d, C6-97, W8 and 7.9.1, method G8.2a, G8.3, G9.5 step 7 and G14.3, the validation method's recount. No loader refusal is added: 7d27335's descriptions of stamps as free text, labels and declared codes, and of stamp labels whose levels hold case variants (written straight on after the space, and of 25 characters, at floors 11 and 36), are frozen (`tests/lane_l3_described_before.py`) and load, generate 7d27335's twin byte for byte and validate, each stamp level carrying 0 read as written before L3. **A zone after the clock** (skeptic 2 of L3, item 2): FHIR's `instant` and `dateTime` and JavaScript's `toISOString` write `2024-01-05T09:15:30Z`, whose trailing letter made the form no stamp's, so the fill stepped both letters (`7040-00-00A06:43:99N`, none of 582 stamps in shape beside rare words or as codes). A year-first date's clock may now end in a zone written straight on, one letter or a sign and an offset of two figures, four, or two, a colon and two (`parsing._stamp_gaps_in` and `_stamp_cell_gaps` extended; new `parsing.stamp_key_zone_at`; oracle `STAMP_CELL`, `STAMP_KEY`, `stamp_gaps`, new `stamp_zone`, `form_room`, `filled_form`); the fill writes its letter `Z` (`z` in a lower-case key), outside the step and the room. Measured (`wave5/L3/leftover/probe-zone.py`; `Z`, `.mmmZ`, `.mmmmmmZ`, `-05:00` and PostgreSQL's `.mmm+00`, free text, labels and codes, floors 11 and 36): every stamp is written in its source's shape (582 of 582; 1,454 of 1,454 as labels at 11) where 7d27335 wrote 0; every description and generation exits 0, and every twin validates with exit 0 but four of free text at a floor of eleven (stated below). **The kinds that move** (skeptic 1 of L3, item 1; skeptic 2, items 1 and 2): a description written before L3 of stamps parted by a letter (`T`, or `t` where every one is lower case) and of 24 characters or fewer, whose form 7d27335 already published, generates another twin, with `T` (or `t`), the marker word and the zone's `Z` where 7d27335 wrote a stepped letter (`7040-00-01T28:35` for `7040-00-06C28:35`), the owner's rule of 2026-09-15 that the twin writes as the source wrote; it still loads and validates with 7d27335's exits (frozen in `MOVED`: free text `2024-mm-ddTHH:MM`, `2024-mm-ddtHH:MM` and `2024-mm-ddTHH:MM:SS[.mmm]Z`, labels `2024-mm-ddTh:mmAM`, the new twin pinned). Measured by skeptic 1 on 72 descriptions 7d27335 wrote: the 12 of short `T` stamps move, the 60 others generate byte for byte. **Cost** (`scale.sh`, `2024-mm-dd h:mm AM` beside one `pending` or `unknown` in 33, a long tail at these sizes, base and lane run in turn on a machine at a load of about 12 on 10 cores): describing 19.3 to 21.3 s at 100,000 rows and 125.7 to 127.1 s at 1,000,000, memory 212 to 227 and 892 to 901 MB; generating 3.7 to 23.5 s and 19.6 to 118.4 s, memory 102 and 378 to 366 MB; validating 7.8 to 18.3 s and 52.3 to 158.1 s, memory 219 to 217 and 901 to 904 MB. Generation and validation now write and recount 969,697 stand-ins in their form where they wrote `group-N`: each stand-in is asked G8.3a's number, date and hole questions, and the twin's stamps are described again as the source's were; the stamp read is at most two per `shape_form`, at most 32 characters each (lane test H7). The head re-measured under heavier load: 22.2, 23.8 and 18.3 s at 100,000 rows. **Stated limits.** The twin's stamps wear the source's shape but are no dates (`7000-00-01 26:23`): G8.3a refuses a text stand-in that reads as a date, so a held-back stamp is never written as one, and code parsing the stamps as dates still stops on the twin; a `T` stamp whose marker alone is lower case (`2024-01-05T9:15 am`) has an upper-case key and is written `AM`; a stamp with a month word, a compact date, an offset after a space, more than 32 characters (`2024-01-05T09:15:30.1234567-05:00`) or a comma after the date (`1/5/2024, 9:15 AM`, the en-US default of JavaScript and Java) keeps no form; a zone after a year-last date keeps no stamp form (spaced, no form at all; parted by a letter and of 24 characters or fewer, the form it had before L3, its letters filled by the step: `1/5/2024T09:15:30Z` is written `5/4/3210A00:19:80P`); a mixed-case zone (`T…z`) is written `Z`; and a free-text column whose stamps all stand at the published longest length beside shorter words can miss `length.mean` at a floor of eleven, one made-up word carrying that longest length (exit 3 on the twin at 7d27335 already for `…Z`, now also for `.mmmmmmZ` and `-05:00`, which gained a form; the form fill keeps every stamp's length, and the cause is G9.5's length pin, which sets a published length end on a made-up word even where a published form already writes that length: no change of L3's; THE ORCHESTRATOR'S RULING OF 2026-10-16: a stated limit, owned by the forms lane FM -- `T` stamps written straight on beside short rare words at floors 2 and 11 miss `length.mean` only). The other limits are the forms lane FM's too (the orchestrator's ruling on push critic 8, 2026-10-16, written at batch 4c's integration).

**Codex's review (REJECT, two items, both fixed with lane tests red on 7ffe47b7; nothing sent back).** (1) Fold partners undid the marker: 194 stamps written `AM` and `am` beside six `pending` and six `unknown` publish 388 cells in the form, 390 values and 196 folded; at a floor of eleven, seed 0, the twin wrote 376 in the form with the gap (`aM`, `Pm`, `pM`; exit 3), and written straight on 199 markers turned in part with every count met -- the plan gave the twelve rare words twelve identities, so 194 slots fell on 184 stamp parents, each of which has one whole turn. A slot asked a marker form now walks its family for a whole turn first, a slot asked none spares the parents wearing one, and groups change places, carrying their asked forms, until each marker form has a parent for each slot and each other planned length of its family one for each of its slots (method G9.3, G9.5 step 7; `generation._form_marker_at`, `_whole_turn_walked`, `_whole_turn_indexed`, `_unmarked_places`, `_marker_slots_fitted`). The ordinary clock written both ways failed so on 7d273351 too and is closed with it (H9's clocks). Measured on 110 case-fold columns (stamps, `T` stamps and clocks; a space, U+202F or no gap; `AM` or `A.M.`; short or stamp-long rare words; floors 2, 11 and 36; and 4,000 and 20,000 rows beside `call back N`): 7ffe47b7 met the published counts on 10, validated 6 and turned 15,304 markers or `T`s in part; now 110, 106 and none -- the four left miss `length.mean` as they did on 7ffe47b7, G9.5's length pin, stated above. The lane's 384 stamp columns and L2's 220 tables keep every description and twin byte for byte; vectors and oracle unchanged (the oracle writes no free-text partner). (2) G9.5 step 7 gave a stamp two words, three with the gap; it has one more than its gaps (`2024-01-05T09:15` one, `2024-01-05T09:15 AM` two), as product and oracle count (H10).

## Decision P4-D395 — stage 5's method: one result per run, its misses ranked once, an entry point that prints nothing, every byte held (lane M5, 2026-10-16)

**Why.** STATE's row 5 reads "Results become data with a rank decided once, before any sentence exists; a callable entry point returns results instead of printing them", and its gate "a caller distinguishes a good run from a bad one without reading prose; reports byte-identical". The owner, 2026-10-15: "we can run the app in the terminal, however the instructions and the way to make the application to run needs to be easy anyway!" The lanes that make the terminal easy -- `TI` (doctor, and the line naming the next command), `TT` (one command, `synthtwin twin`), `TS` (an ending of at most 25 lines), `TW` (plain words) -- and stage 6's validator (`S6v`, a class for every pair) each need to know what a run did without reading what it printed. Today none can: the three commands print as they go (`cli._say` and `cli._warn`, called from 75 places in `_run_profile` alone at 3d893032); the exit status is the only machine channel; a `generate` run that gave a published fact up exits 0 exactly as one that gave nothing up (`cli._run_generate` returns 0 once its files are written, and method G12.1 rule 4 makes an approximation outside its range one of those facts); a profile run that leaves questions open exits 0 as one that leaves none; and `--help` and a word the parser does not know end in `SystemExit`. The data already exists -- `validation.Outcome` (checks, listings, census), `generation.Twin` (deviations, approximations, remarks), the description itself. What is missing is one object a run returns, one place where its misses are put in order, and a way to call a command that prints nothing. This page is written before the code (CLAUDE.md, "Plan first"); lane `S5a` builds it, lane `S5b` fills the profile's half.

**Measured before it was written (Step 0).** On 3d893032, the owner's machine, Python 3.13.14, `nice -n 10`, invented data only: a 300-row table of a record number, a date, a weight and a ward from `random.Random(20261016)`, and scripts of the lane's own outside the repository.
- `tools/provenance/guard_runner.py` cannot run the product as its script: under its hook `import numpy` and `import pandas` both stop on `RuntimeError` (forbidden import: `ctypes`), because numpy imports `ctypes`. The same hook installed AFTER the product's imports, by the runner's own `install_guard()`, let `profile --identifier record_no`, `generate --seed 7` and `validate` run whole through `cli.main`: exits 0, 0 and 0, nothing stopped, 0.44 s of wall time and 95 MB at the peak for the three, imports included.
- Run twice, in two folders, all seven files came back byte for byte (the description 17,680 bytes, the summary 8,438, the questions 3,030, the twin 10,262, the twin's report 23,538, the quality report 58,480), and so did every screen once the folder was replaced by a fixed word: 165 lines on standard output and 5 on the error stream for profile, 405 and 1 for generate (404 in a folder whose path needs no quoting: the probe's held a space, and the screen adds the line quoting it), 868 and 0 for validate; the folder stands on those screens 6, 5 and 2 times.
- That twin gave nothing up (0 deviations; 32 approximations, all inside; 1 remark) and the real table validated 166 HELD and 0 MISSED, so the good runs below are good by measurement. Every refusal and unusable command line of part 5's battery but R6 exits through `cli.main` as its row says, and so do its byte-order mark and swapped columns (3); `--help` and an unknown option end in `SystemExit` (0 and 2). The option's refusal is 2 lines; the help page is argparse's, wrapped at the terminal's width: 332 lines at 80 columns, 219 at 120 and 146 at 200, three different texts.
- Damages to that twin, each miss with its fact, its subcheck in brackets and its index in `Outcome.checks`, the validator's own order: one header name re-cased missed 4 (`document.source.header_source` [`header.presence`] 22, `universal.name` [`header.names`] 23, `document.columns` [`columns.order`] 24, `universal.position` [`position.at`] on `ward` 131); thirty `Cardiology` cells written `CARDIOLOGY` missed `label.n_distinct` [`distinct.n_distinct`] (141) before `label.variants` [`levels.cardiology.variants`] (155), a count before the spelling a program matches on; every weight times 1.1 missed 8, all approximated facts judged against their windows (seven rungs of `numeric.percentiles` from [`ladder.p05`] at 103, and the mean [`moments.mean`] at 114); twelve rows dropped missed 37, `document.n_rows` [`rows.n_rows`] (20) first.
- Measured in review round 1 (the reviewers' scripts in `planning-notes/work-2026-10/wave6/M5-sk1-work/` and `M5-stat-work/`, and the lane's own): one present weight cell blanked missed 8, all counts decided exactly: `universal.n_present` [`presence.n_present`] (83) first, then the missing, numeric and used counts (84, 88, 98) and the column's style and width censuses (121, 122, 126, 127). The validate census -- held, within-bound, authorized-deviation, withheld, missed, not-checkable -- is 149, 17, 0, 0, 0, 62 on the clean twin; one to ten cells of one ward written in lower case, or with a space after them, leave it exactly so, and eleven give 2 misses; every cell of the weight column written as a word gives 121, 2, 0, 37, 6, 62, which is 37 obligations whose outcome the run could not say beside 6 misses. G2's description with the weight column's count of zeros written 12 generates through `cli.main` with exit 0 and three deviations: the ladder's low end moved (`percentiles`, published 31.2, the twin 0), decided exactly, and both distances of the low tail outside their bounds (G12.1 rule 4).
- Measured in review round 2 (the lane's scripts in `planning-notes/work-2026-10/wave6/M5/repair2/`): G2's twin with every date written without its padding (`10/9/2024` for `10/09/2024`) gives the census 147, 17, 0, 0, 2, 62 and misses `datetime.date_field_widths` [`widths.padded`] (72), a floor census whose verdict `validation._written_form_checks` chooses among HELD, WITHIN-BOUND and MISSED, and [`widths.unnamed`] (73), HELD or MISSED; neither carries a citation. Lane TI's doctor (its head d924d526, with `cli._total_memory` replaced and the table Step 0's): this computer's memory read as 16 GiB, `doctor t.csv --out-dir out` makes 6 checks, all passed, exit 0, and its last line is `synthtwin profile t.csv --out-dir out` with the folder the person typed; memory that cannot be read leaves 2 checks not made (the memory and the table's size against it) and 4 passed, exit 0, "Every check that could be made passed."; 100,000 bytes of memory fails the table's check, exit 1, ending `synthtwin doctor t.csv --out-dir out`. Through `cli.main`, `validate t-profile.json --twin missing.csv` exits 1, and on POSIX a link left at an output's name and pointing at an input is refused with exit 1 on each command (the description's name at the table, the twin's at the description, the quality report's at the description), the input untouched and the link kept, while a link at the questions file's name, pointing at the table, leaves the description written, the table untouched and the link kept, with exit 0. Imported after the product, `guard_runner.install_guard()`'s hook refuses `import socket` (not loaded by the product's imports), and where `socket` was loaded first, opening one, both with the guard's own message. `print("m")` makes two writes, `"m"` and the line end; `print("m\n", end="")` makes `"m\n"` and an empty one: the same characters.

**1. One result per run** (`src/synthtwin/results.py`, new: frozen dataclasses and two functions, the standard library only; it imports no module of this package that reads a table, draws a number or reaches the generator, because a validate run imports it -- CLAUDE.md, "Rules of the road").

| field | what it holds |
|---|---|
| `command` | `profile`, `generate`, `validate`, `doctor` (lane TI's), `twin` (lane TT's), or `help`, `version` and `status` for `--help`, `--version` and no words at all |
| `verdict` | `no-miss`, `missed`, `refused` or `unusable`, defined below |
| `misses` | every miss of the run in rank order (part 2), never cut short: one for each MISSED check on validate and for each deviation on generate. Empty on `no-miss` and `unusable`. On a refusal it holds exactly the misses whose report the run had handed to the screen before it stopped -- to `screen`, or, where none is given, nowhere at that same moment -- and none where no report had been: a validate run refused at `writing` keeps the misses its report showed; generate's refusal of a twin its table's encoding has no byte for (`errors.twin_not_writable_in_encoding`, step `content`, made after the deviations exist and before the report is shown) keeps none, and so does a memory stop while a report is composed |
| `unjudged` | validate: one entry per WITHHELD check, with its column, fact and subcheck and the key of the rule that kept its outcome back (one key for each sentence the validator gives for that today; S5a lists them), and no measured value. These are the obligations whose outcome the run could not say, so a miss may stand among them; their count is `tally`'s withheld. Doctor: one entry per check that could not be made (lane TI's `made` false: this computer's memory where it cannot be read, and the table's size weighed against it), keyed by the check that composes it; their count is `tally`'s not made |
| `carried` | what the run holds only approximately or does not carry, each entry with its class and its reason (below) |
| `tally` | the command's own counts as (key, count) pairs in a fixed order: validate the census's six, from which V7.2's summary is made (held, within-bound, authorized-deviation, withheld, missed, not-checkable), its exact facts counted there as HELD; generate its deviations, approximations, approximations inside, remarks and columns made up (it does not count the facts it meets: deferred, below); profile its columns and the questions it put and listed; doctor its checks, those passed, those failed and those not made, from lane TI's `passed` and `made` (a check not made is never counted passed nor failed) |
| `floor` | profile, generate and validate: the description's `small_cell_floor` (profile: the one it writes), and beside it `floor_lowered`, true where that floor lies below `contract.SMALL_GROUP_NOTICE_LINE` -- the test by which the summary, the twin's report and the quality report each state a lowered floor today, whoever chose it (typed, or a description written at the old default of 1) |
| `warnings` | each caution the run gave, in order: a `key`, one per builder that composes one today (`made-up-columns` for `rendering.made_up_warning`, `lowered-floor`, `declared-words`, `small-population`, `counted-in-rows`, `left-behind`, `questions-not-written`, `questions-would-replace` for `errors.questions_would_replace_a_file`, and the rest S5a lists), the column where it names one, and its `words` as printed today. `lowered-floor` stands whenever `floor_lowered` is true, because a file the run writes states it, its `words` the caution's own where the screen prints one today (profile, on a floor typed below the line) and empty elsewhere. A warning never moves the verdict (P4-D2 item 5: "a decline is not a failure, and a warning exit would break every script") |
| `questions` | profile only: one record for each entry `asking.questions_document` puts in the questions file today, in the file's order: its `section` (`about_your_file`, `asked` or the checklist's `columns`) and its `order` within it; its column (empty for a question about the file); its kind (`Question.role` and `.reason`); `saw`, the file's `what_synthtwin_saw` (`Question.shape`: a count, a width or a separator, never a cell, A-P4-58's filter already applied); `read_as_now` (`Question.taken`); the answers it offers, each with its `answer`, `means` and what the description then publishes; and whether it was put at a prompt or only written down. The file's other words are the run's (the table's name and the population notice, from the description) or constants of `asking` |
| `files` | each file the run wrote, in the order written: its kind (`description`, `summary`, `questions`, `twin`, `twin-report`, `quality-report`) and its path as the run resolved it; only files that exist when the run returns |
| `left_behind` | working files a finished run could not clear away (today's `_left_behind_note`) |
| `next_command` | the words a person types next, unquoted and as the person typed each path, from `synthtwin` on, with its purpose, or none: `profile` (a doctor that passed, lane TI's `_teaching_profile`), `doctor` (a doctor that failed, `_doctor_again`), `generate`, `validate`, `answer-questions` and `twin` (lane TT's). The purposes are a closed list that grows as the closed list of reasons does: the landing that makes one adds its key. Quoting the words for a shell is the renderer's (`cli._typed_path`) and is never stored |
| `refusal` | set exactly when the verdict is `refused` or `unusable`: its `step` (`command-line`, `input`, `outputs`, `content`, `questions`, `writing`, `memory`, `nesting` or `environment`), its `key` where the catalog has one today (method G12's four `errors.REFUSAL_*`; empty elsewhere), its `words` as printed, and what it says is on disk |
| `steps` | `twin` only: the result of each step it ran, in order |

The four verdicts. `no-miss`: the run reached its end, wrote every file it names and missed no obligation it could judge. It claims no more: on validate the within-bound, authorized-deviation, withheld and not-checkable counts stand beside it in `tally` and the withheld obligations in `unjudged` (V7.3 item 4: a pass means "no checkable obligation was missed"), and, measured above, ten re-spelled cells leave a twin's census as the clean twin's. A profile with questions open is `no-miss` (they are in `questions`), and so is one whose questions file could not be written, with the warning `questions-not-written`, as it exits 0 today; so are help, version and status, and a doctor of which no check that could be made failed: its checks not made are counted apart in `tally` and listed in `unjudged`, never counted passed, as lane TI exits 0 and says "Every check that could be made passed." `missed`: the run reached its end and wrote its files with at least one miss -- on validate a check MISSED, on generate a deviation. `refused`: it could not finish -- a catalogued refusal, a memory or nesting stop, questions left unfinished at a prompt, a stop the write transaction composed, or for doctor a check made that failed (step `environment`). `unusable`: the command line could not be used.

A miss carries its `tier`, `place` and `arrival` (part 2); its `column` (the description's name, empty for the file as a whole) and `partner` (a pair's second column, from stage 6; empty otherwise); its `fact`, the disposition registry's `group.field` for the fact it concerns -- on validate the key its check carries; on generate the deviation's own key, qualified where the miss is made with the registry group that holds that field for the column's role (`universal` for `n_present` and `n_missing`), and a ladder end that gives way named by the end the generator pins (`numeric.percentiles.min` or `numeric.percentiles.max`); its `subcheck` (validate's identity; empty on generate); `judged`, how the producer decided it, set where the miss is made: `window` exactly where the miss is judged against a bound the method grants -- on generate a deviation `generation._bound_notes` makes from an approximation outside its bound; on validate a check made by `validation._within`, `_within_clock`, `_within_instant` or `_tail_window_check`, whose WITHIN-BOUND carries the envelope's citation, or by a count of different values judged against the window a corner of distinctness authorizes (`_lesser_or_held`, and the compound column's window from `_compound_window` where its two ends differ), whose AUTHORIZED-DEVIATION carries the corner's -- and `exact` for every other miss. Among the exact ones by name: the floor censuses of `_written_form_checks` and `_settled_verdict` (a date's field widths and month-name styles; WITHIN-BOUND there means a floor's worth met, with no envelope and no citation) and the windows a pooled count leaves (from the published count to that count and the pool, met as HELD), which are counts. `published` and `achieved` are the producer's own fields copied (`Check.published` and `.achieved`, `Deviation.published` and `.achieved`), as the report prints them; `shown` is false exactly where the producer's `achieved` is empty because V5 keeps the measured side back; and `note` is the producer's further lines, which say why. A VALIDATE RESULT HOLDS NO STRING READ FROM THE FILE IT MEASURED (validation's guarantee, carried through). A PROFILE RESULT HOLDS NO STRING ITS SCREEN AND ITS FILES DO NOT SHOW TODAY: the table's own column names reach `questions`, `warnings` and a refusal's `words` exactly where they reach the screen now (`errors.unknown_column_named` lists them). NO RESULT HOLDS A CELL OF A TWIN: the twin's rows are written and let go, never kept by the result (lane `SG`'s seam).

What is carried. One entry per subject: its `subject` (no names for the table, one for a column, two in schema order for a pair); its `fact` where it is one fact of a column; its `class` and `reason`; its `words` as printed today; on validate its `verdict`, the census word its check got (HELD, WITHIN-BOUND, AUTHORIZED-DEVIATION, WITHHELD, MISSED or NOT-CHECKABLE) or REPORT-ONLY; and, for an approximate entry, its `measures`, each with `published`, `achieved`, `lowest`, `highest`, `inside` and `covers_published` -- the text the report prints, with the answer beside it, which is `generation.Approximation`'s own rule, so no consumer parses a number back. `inside` is true, false or none, and none wherever V5 keeps the measured side back or the subject cannot be checked, so a result neither shows a withheld outcome nor states one never measured.
- Classes. A pair's `class` is contract 4.6a.3's `pairs[].class` read verbatim -- `exact`, `approximate` or `coefficient`, as lane M6's page, P4-D394, writes them -- and never chosen again here. `not-carried` is the result's own value, never one of `pairs[].class`: it stands for each entry of 4.6a.3's `not_carried` list (two columns; its `reason` read from that list, `floor` or `dropped`) and of its `ineligible` list (one column; its `reason` read from that list). A column's own entries are `approximate` (an APPROXIMATED fact, with its measures) or `not-carried` (reason `made-up`: the description publishes no values for the column; `held-back`: cells whose values the floor keeps back are made up), and the table's one entry of class `not-carried`, reason `not-modeled` (nothing between columns is carried), stands wherever the description's `relationships.statistical` is null: on every description until lane S6c, and after it on every description written before it, which contract 4.6a loads and generates exactly as before. Only where that block is an object do its pair entries stand in that entry's place. Each landing that makes a reason adds its key to the closed list.
- What misses. An exact pair's table misses, at tier `count` (V11.2 as M6's repaired page writes it: HELD or MISSED against its target table, the published one raked where the file's margins differ; the entry carries the rows they differ by and the cells the rake moved, as printed). The measures of an `approximate` or `coefficient` pair, and an exact pair's rank correlation, are REPORT-ONLY (V11.2, G15.15): carried with `inside`, never a miss, and never moving the verdict or the exit status. A column's APPROXIMATED fact outside its bound is a miss as well as an entry (G12.1 rule 4), judged against a window.
- A column's exact facts are counted, not listed: on validate as HELD in `tally`; generate does not count them (deferred, below). Every pair is listed whatever its class (`K-S6-04`: none unnamed). Generate lists every approximation, inside or outside, as its report does. Validate lists the pairs of a description whose statistical block is an object, and on every other description the one `not-modeled` entry its report states (V7.3).

**2. The rank, decided once.** The misses stand in the order `(tier, place, arrival)` and in no other, fixed in the result before any sentence about them is made.
- `tier` orders a miss by what else it brings down -- an order of dependence, not a ranking of the owner's two goals, which STATE records as "neither ranked above the other". (1) `form`: the file as a whole -- every check on no column (the header, the names and their order, the count of columns and of rows, the encoding, line endings and dialect, the workbook block) and each column's name and position; every column is read through it. (2) `writing`: which spellings one column's values may wear and how they are read -- its role and type, date and clock formats and what they are read at, separators and decimal marks, layouts, a label's spelling map and its variants, how its missing values are spelled, and a cell wearing no spelling its value admits (`styles.spelled`); every value of the column is read through it, so code written on the twin can read the real column otherwise. (3) `count`: every other miss decided exactly -- counts, listed values with their counts, census groups, counts of different values, a tail's rows, a ladder end that gives way or a rung with no value at it, how many cells wear each spelling (the style, width and mark censuses, a date's field widths and month-name styles among them, whose WITHIN-BOUND means only a floor's worth met), a window a pooled count leaves, and a pair's published table from stage 6; one statistic moves. (4) `window`: a miss judged against a bound the method grants (`judged` is `window`, part 1); one statistic moves by more than the method's bound.
- `place` is 0 for the file as a whole, otherwise the column's `position` in the description, counted from 1 (a pair's: its first column's). `arrival` is the miss's index in its own module's order: `Outcome.checks` (the document first, then the columns as the description lists them) or `Twin.deviations` (the generator's column order). Both are functions of the description, so the rank is as deterministic as the reports (plan D12, V10), and within one module no two misses share an `arrival`.
- `window` is read off `judged` and nothing else. The tier of a miss decided exactly is read from ONE table in `results.py`, keyed by `group.field` (`group.*` names a whole group) and, where one fact holds subchecks of two tiers, by a subcheck pattern beside it (`numeric.numeric_styles` is `count`; its `styles.spelled`, `writing`). The suite holds the table total over every fact of `tests/dispositions.py`'s registry and every key and subcheck a check or a deviation carries on the suite's batteries, and turns red on a key it lacks, on a miss judged against a window that is not `window`, and on one decided exactly that is. S5a's rank test pins `judged` at each site part 1 names, one miss from each site the batteries reach, and M10's two width misses as `exact`, tier `count`. At run time a key the table lacks is ranked `count`: one stated fallback, met on no battery, so a person's run never stops over a rank.
- A census that drops a spelling to nought ranks `count`, like any other count, and this is accepted: ranking it `writing` would make the order turn on the measured side, which V5 keeps back for these counts (a count of the file), so the order would tell what the report does not.
- On the measured damages: the re-cased header's four misses are all `form`; the re-cased label ranks `label.variants` (`writing`) before `label.n_distinct` (`count`), the reverse of the validator's order; the scaled weights' eight are all `window`; the blanked cell's eight are all `count`, `universal.n_present` first (this page's first draft ranked the style census `writing` and put it first); the unpadded dates' two width misses are both `count`, one damage in one tier (round 1's rule, which read `window` off the verdicts a check could choose, put [`widths.padded`] last as `window` and [`widths.unnamed`] in `count`); and on generate the edited count of zeros ranks the ladder's end (`numeric.percentiles.min`, `count`) before the two tail distances (`window`).
- Every surface that puts misses in order of importance -- TS's ending, TT's summary, TW's words -- reads `misses` as given and sorts by nothing else. Whatever states a verdict also states, from `tally`, the within-bound, authorized-deviation, withheld and not-checkable counts beside it (V7.2; V7.3 item 4), and a lowered floor wherever `floor_lowered` is true. The full reports keep their text and the order they print today -- `arrival`, the description's order in which the validator and the generator make their misses (V7.1) -- rendered from `validation.Outcome` and `generation.Twin` as now; the result's misses are made from the same two lists, one for each MISSED check or deviation, so a report and its result are one list in two orders, and `K-S5-01` (d) and (f) hold them to it. No byte of a report moves (`K-S5-02`); putting a report into rank order changes report text: a landing of its own, its goldens re-recorded under part 5's rule.

**3. A callable entry point that prints nothing: `synthtwin.cli.run(argv, *, screen=None, ask=None) -> results.Result`.**
- `argv` is the words a person types after `synthtwin`, read by the same parser (lane TT may restructure it; `run` keeps its shape).
- `screen`, when given, is called with `(stream, text)` -- `"out"` or `"err"`, and exactly the characters the terminal is to show, the display boundary already applied (`parsing.visible_lines`) -- at the moment and in the order `_say` and `_warn` print them today. So the disclosure still reaches the person before the files exist (P1-D6), a notice still comes before the question it is about, and a run stopped while writing still shows what it shows today.
- `ask`, when given, is called with a prompt -- today's `"    > "`, which `input` writes, so its bytes are `ask`'s own and never the screen's -- and returns the line typed, or none where the person ended input there: end of input, or Ctrl-C at the prompt, which today's `cli._read_one_answer` catches. The question, and the request to type again, reach the person through `screen`; the loop that asks again stays in `cli`. An answer of none ends the questions as today (`errors.the_questions_were_not_finished`): `refused`, step `questions`, exit 1. Without `ask` no question is put and nothing is read, as when `_there_is_somebody_to_ask()` is false today.
- Given neither, nothing reaches `sys.stdout` or `sys.stderr` by any route -- a print, argparse's help or usage text, a library's warning -- nothing is read from `sys.stdin`, `sys.exit` is not called and `SystemExit` is not raised: `--help`, `--version` and no words at all return results whose text goes to `screen` alone (nowhere, when there is none), and a word the parser does not know returns `unusable`. The files are written as the command writes them today. Ctrl-C anywhere but at a prompt still ends the run (`KeyboardInterrupt` passes, as `main`'s docstring says), and an exception no refusal names still surfaces: a defect stays loud.
- `main(argv)` becomes `results.exit_code(run(argv, screen=<the terminal>, ask=<a reader where somebody is there to ask>))`. The terminal's `screen` is the module's one `print`, the rule `tests/test_p1r6f11_display_boundary.py` holds today for `_say` and `_warn`.
- Each command's modules are still imported inside its own branch (P2-D1, P3-D1), so a validate run through `run` reaches no generator; S5a proves it in a fresh interpreter's `sys.modules`, as V10 asks.

**4. Exit codes from the result alone: `results.exit_code(result)`, a function of `command` and `verdict` and of nothing else.** No code path chooses an exit status of its own.

| verdict | exit status |
|---|---|
| `no-miss` | 0 |
| `missed` | 3 on `validate` and `twin`; 0 on `generate`, as today (`cli.main`'s docstring: on generate, 0 means both files were written; a twin that gave a fact up is written, and its report names the fact) |
| `refused` | 1, a doctor check made that failed included, as lane TI ships it (a doctor whose only shortfall is checks it could not make is `no-miss`, 0); a validate run refused at `writing` after its report was shown keeps its misses and exits 1, as today |
| `unusable` | 2 |

A `twin` run takes its verdict, its misses, its `unjudged` and its refusal from ONE of its steps: the step with the most severe verdict, in the order `unusable`, `refused`, `missed`, `no-miss`, and the later of two equally severe; every step's own result stays in `steps`. Two steps' misses are never joined, since each module's `arrival` starts at 0. So a twin whose generate step missed and whose validate step was refused reads `refused`, with validate's refusal, and never `missed`. These are today's codes, case for case; the golden battery records each and `K-S5-02` compares it. Validation method V6.5-A1 states the rule where V6.5 lives.

**5. Every byte held: the golden battery (`K-S5-02`'s design).**
- A case is a command line, the inputs it needs, built at run time by seeded neutral builders as `tests/fixtures.py` builds them (nothing committed as data), and three records: each file in the case's folder after the run, by SHA-256, bytes and lines; the screen as ONE transcript, the characters each stream received in the order made, kept as runs: an empty write dropped and adjacent writes to one stream joined, every change of stream kept (where a write ends is not a byte the person sees: `print("m")` writes `"m"` and then the line end, a route writing both at once shows the same characters, Step 0); and the exit status.
- It is captured through `cli.main(argv)`, the command line as typed, so one harness runs before S5a's change and after it: `sys.stdout` and `sys.stderr` replaced by two writers feeding one transcript; `SystemExit` caught and its code recorded as the exit status (before S5a, `--help` and the parser's own refusals end that way; after it, `main` returns); `os.isatty` answering false, so nobody is asked whatever terminal the suite runs in; the environment fixed for every case, in the harness and in the recorder alike -- `COLUMNS=80`, `NO_COLOR=1`, `PYTHON_COLORS=0`, `FORCE_COLOR` unset -- because argparse wraps its help at the terminal's width (Step 0) and later Pythons may colour it; the case's folder, as given and as resolved, replaced in the transcript by `<FOLDER>`; the installed version replaced by one fixed word in every text output, as `tests/test_twin_golden.py` normalizes the description's.
- Text argparse composes itself -- G10's help page and any usage line it prints -- is also laid out by each Python's own argparse, and CI runs 3.10 to 3.14 where only 3.13 was measured here. Those records are pinned on the recorder's Python minor version, which the module records, and skipped on every other with that reason printed, until a landing measures them equal on every CI Python and lifts the skip.
- The goldens live in `tests/stage5_goldens.py`, a GENERATED Python module like `tests/disposition_seal.py`, so no data-format file enters the tree outside the fixture manifest (CLAUDE.md, "Open-source hygiene"): one line per case and record, then a digest over every record, beside the digests of the battery's table of cases and of the recorder's source. These digests are consistency checks, not proof of how a record was written: the gate test computes the three again and turns red where one differs (the seal's pattern), so a record edited without its digest, a case changed without recording again and a recorder changed without recording again show in the ordinary suite.
- They are written only by `tools/goldens/record_stage5_goldens.py --write` (new), which imports the product, THEN installs `tools/provenance/guard_runner.py`'s own hook (`install_guard()`), then runs the whole battery under it. It cannot run as the runner's script, because the hook refuses `ctypes` before numpy can load (Step 0). Without `--write` it reproduces every record the same way and compares, writing nothing.
- WHAT IS AUTHORITATIVE IS CI'S GUARDED REPRODUCTION. S5a adds a step to `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, in a job that installs the product, on the POSIX cell of the recorder's Python: `python tools/goldens/record_stage5_goldens.py`, without `--write`, red where any reproduced record differs from `tests/stage5_goldens.py`. Before the battery, the recorder makes a negative control under the hook it has just installed: it imports `socket` and, where `socket` is already loaded, opens one; unless that stops on the guard's own message (`guard_runner.GUARD_MESSAGE`; measured, both stop, Step 0), the recorder stops red and records nothing, so a recorder whose hook is missing cannot pass. A record written by any other route is therefore held, on every CI run, to what the guarded recorder makes of the code it sits beside; that a landing names each record it moves stays its review's. This step stands beside the fixture manifest's checker, which cannot hold this module: that checker runs each generator as the runner's script.
- RE-RECORDING (the December plan's red-team item 22): only through that tool, in the same commit as the change that moves the bytes; that commit's message and its landing's plan decision name every case and record that moved, and why. Two kinds of landing may do it: one whose stated purpose changes those bytes (TW's words, TS's ending, a report repaired), and a method landing whose change moves them (the stage-4 lanes; S6a, which puts contract 4.6a's pairs into every description; S6b and S6f, which change the twin and its reports; SG if it moves a byte). Lanes S5a and S5b exist to move no byte: each records the goldens once, in its first commit, on the code as it stands, and never again, and its review reads `git diff <that commit>..HEAD -- tests/stage5_goldens.py`, which is empty. A lane rebased onto a head whose merged lanes moved those bytes -- S5a onto S6a's merge, planned for 10-28, inside S5a's 10-26 to 10-30 -- makes that recording again on the new base, in a commit of its own before any change of its own, naming the merged lanes that moved them, and its review reads the diff from that commit. A golden detects a change and is no oracle: what a report must say stays pinned by the tests that pin it now (the validator's red battery, the twin's recounts); this battery pins that it does not move.
- The battery holds at least these cases (S5a may add one, never remove one). Each class is written when the case is written, from how the case is built, never read off a run. A case that builds on another runs after it, in its folder; every other case has a folder of its own.

| id | command line | built input | class (`K-S5-01`) | exit | pins |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| G1 | `profile t.csv --identifier record_no` | Step 0's 300-row table | no-miss | 0 | a profile's three files and its screen; lane TI's next command |

**The KPIs' measurement text, fixed here** (a page stamps none; lane E0 enters `K-S5-01`'s OPEN baseline, S5a stamps both, S5b, TT, TS and TW re-run them):
- **`K-S5-01`** (headline, new): a caller tells a good run from a bad one from the returned result alone. Over every case of the golden battery that names a class -- its good runs, its refusals, its unusable command lines and every damage -- the class, and for a damage the columns, facts and (on validate) subchecks it breaks, each with its tier, and the tier its first miss must have, for a refusal its step, and for each case its warning keys, its floor, its carried classes and reasons and its next command, are written in the battery's table when the case is written, never read off a run. `cli.run(argv)` is called with no screen and no reader (Q1 alone with its reader; I1 and I2 with the fault their rows inject; DR1 to DR3 with the memory reading their rows fix), and a case is met when: (a) nothing reached standard output or standard error and nothing was read from standard input; (b) the result's verdict is the case's class; (c) `results.exit_code` of the result equals the exit status the battery recorded for that command line through `main` (for Q1, I1, I2 and DR1 to DR3, which the battery does not record, the exit their rows write); (d) every column and fact (and, on validate, subcheck) the damage breaks is among the misses, the misses stand in non-decreasing `(tier, place, arrival)`, there are exactly as many as `Outcome.census.missed` on validate and `len(Twin.deviations)` on generate, one for each MISSED check or deviation, and the first has the tier written for it; (e) a refusal's step is the one written for it; (f) `tally` equals what the producer counted for the same inputs -- validate's six counts `Outcome.census`, with `unjudged` exactly its WITHHELD checks; generate's the deviations, approximations, those inside, remarks and columns made up of `Twin`; doctor's the checks, passed, failed and not made of lane TI's `_doctor_checks`, with `unjudged` exactly its checks not made; (g) the warning keys, in order, `floor` and `floor_lowered`, and `next_command` -- its words as one tuple and its purpose -- equal those written for the case; (h) the classes, reasons and (on validate) verdicts in `carried` equal those written for the case; (i) each miss's `published`, `achieved` and `note` equal its producer's (the MISSED check, the deviation), its `shown` is false exactly where that producer's `achieved` is empty, each carried measure's `published`, `achieved`, `lowest`, `highest`, `inside` and `covers_published` equal its producer's (`generation.Approximation`; on validate the check of that fact, `inside` none where it is WITHHELD), and the rank values are checked one by one against values the test finds without the result's code: `place` against the column's `position` read from the description (0 for the file), `arrival` against the index of the miss's producer in `Outcome.checks` or `Twin.deviations`, and `tier` against the tier the case's row writes for that miss, or, for a miss the row does not name, `window` where its producer's `judged` is and otherwise the rank table's entry for its key and subcheck, looked up by the test. Only the result's fields are read: no text field is parsed or searched. The test also hands its own checker a correct result corrupted one field at a time -- `published` and `achieved` exchanged, `inside` made true on D1's two approximations outside their bounds, `shown` made true on a side V5 keeps back, a `place`, an `arrival` or a `tier` moved, a miss dropped or duplicated, the next command's purpose changed -- and each must leave its case unmet. Value: cases met over cases. Target: every case. Baseline, taken before any result exists: a case is met only where its class follows from the exit status alone and it asks nothing of (d) to (i) -- a generate run that gave a fact up exits 0 as a good one does, and no exit status names a column -- recorded OPEN at that share.
- **`K-S5-02`**: every byte a battery run writes or shows equals the recorded one. Over every case of the golden battery but Q1, I1, I2 and DR1 to DR3: each file the run leaves in its folder, its screen transcript as runs of characters, each with its stream and in its order (an empty write dropped and adjacent writes to one stream joined; the folder and the version replaced, and the environment fixed, as part 5 says), and its exit status, against `tests/stage5_goldens.py`, whose digests over its records, over the table of cases and over the recorder's source must each equal the one computed again (consistency checks), and whose every record must equal the one CI's guarded recorder reproduces on the recorder's Python (part 5). Value: records that differ, and the cases holding them. Target: 0. Files and exit statuses on every CI cell, transcripts on the POSIX cells, text argparse composes on the recorder's Python version. A landing that changes a report, a screen line or an exit status on purpose, or a method landing whose change moves one, records the goldens again in the same commit, only through `tools/goldens/record_stage5_goldens.py --write`, and names each moved record and the reason in its commit message and its plan decision; S5a and S5b record once, in their first commit (again on a new base after a rebase, in a commit of its own), and never again. It is a measure of regression: 0 at that first recording by construction.
