## Decision P4-D397 — install and first run: one install command, `python -m synthtwin`, `synthtwin doctor`, and `profile` teaching `generate` (lane TI of the December plan, 2026-10-15)

**Why.** The owner, 2026-10-15: "we can run the app in the terminal, however the instructions and the way to make the application to run needs to be easy anyway!". Measured before the lane on 3d89303 (the R5 map, section 1.2): a clone, an environment the README left unstated and `pip install -e .`, then three commands and one questions file edited by hand; `python -m synthtwin` stopped with "'synthtwin' is a package and cannot be directly executed"; and `profile` printed no next command although README and the `generate` teaching chain said every command does.

**What is built.** (1) `src/synthtwin/__main__.py` hands `python -m synthtwin` to `cli.main`, the console script's own function. (2) `scripts/install.sh` (macOS and Linux) and `scripts/install.bat` (Windows; a batch file because managed machines refuse PowerShell scripts) find Python 3.10 or later, make `.venv` in the synthtwin folder, install from `requirements-install.lock` with `--require-hashes` -- given a wheel folder, README's two offline commands flag for flag (`--no-index --find-links FOLDER --require-hashes`, then `--no-index --no-deps` for the synthtwin wheel) -- and end by running `synthtwin doctor`, whose exit code they return. (3) `synthtwin doctor [TABLE] [--out-dir FOLDER]` prints one line per check: Python 3.10 or later, numpy and pandas loadable, the output folder taking a file (a test file written and removed), total memory through `os.sysconf` and "could not be read" where it does not exist (Windows), and a named table's size against that memory -- large when ten times the size passes half the memory, ten being `K-S4-02`'s measured nine times a file's size at the reader's peak rounded up. It never opens the table. Exit 0 when every check passed, 1 otherwise, each PROBLEM line saying what to do. (4) `profile` ends with `_teaching_generate`'s two lines on both ways a run that wrote a description ends. No other report text moves; the parser takes one more command word and is not restructured (lane TT does that).

**Principle 3, kept by one admission.** The offline scanner admits `os.sysconf`: it takes a configuration name and returns an integer, opening nothing and running nothing; no subprocess, ctypes or network reaches `src`. The claim inventory counts `doctor` apart from the three commands of a run, with its reason, so "three commands" stays the run's true count.

**Proof.** `tests/test_terminal_install.py`: `python -m synthtwin` dispatch and `--version` in process; each doctor check forced to fail by monkeypatch, and exit codes; doctor passing with every way of opening a file refusing the table (mode 0 besides, on POSIX); profile's last line on both exit paths; the scripts' flags; the README; the CI step. CI runs the install script from a wheel folder on the first shard of every tests cell (Ubuntu and Windows on 3.10 to 3.14, macOS on 3.14), proved on the first push that carries it. KPIs: `K-S8-01` (the terminal's headline, OPEN: 1 install command, 5 run commands, 1 hand-edited file, against the base's 2, 5 and 1 under the repaired measure below; target 1, 1, 0 by lanes TT and TS) and `K-S8-04` (GREEN, its CI count read as configuration until the first push runs it). The headline cap goes from 31 to 32 by the orchestrator's recorded call D15 of the December plan; the owner may veto it.

**Stated limits.** The clone install still fetches pip's build backend unpinned, as `pip install -e .` always did; the offline path does not. Free memory cannot be read without native code, so doctor weighs total memory. The scripts are run on Windows and macOS only by CI. Their owners (the orchestrator's naming of 2026-10-19, written at batch 4d's integration): the unpinned build backend and the scripts run only by CI are lane DEP's, whose offline bundle pins everything and from which CI installs; doctor weighing total memory is the terminal track's lane TT.

**Repair round 1 (skeptic 1 and Codex's review, 2026-10-15), every item pinned by a gate case red on its mutant (30 mutants, 30 red), save five script guards found unpinned by the verifier and pinned in round 2.** Doctor: a refused look at a table or an output folder (mode 0, or a Mac's protected folders) is a PROBLEM line with a next step, not a stack trace; a package whose load raises any exception is a line and the other checks still run; the test file is created exclusively and only where nothing, not even a dangling link, stands at its name, since the validator resolved a link into another folder; a check it could not make is marked `note`, no failure, and the close then reads "Every check that could be made passed."; both closing lines repeat the table and `--out-dir` given; a text table is weighed at ten times its size and said to be a guess from the size alone, a workbook at the reader's measured bound of 632 MB for a million cells whatever its size; a name collision is never called a leftover to delete. `python -m synthtwin` on Python 3.9 says so in words before the command's module, measured on Apple's 3.9.6, where it stopped on a stack trace. The scripts: `venv --clear` every time, after the wheel folder is checked and once a switched-on environment is refused, since pip skips a package whose version is in place without checking its files and a broken or too-old environment was reused; the two offline commands run with `--isolated` and `PIP_CONFIG_FILE` at the null device, since a find-links in `PIP_FIND_LINKS` or a pip.conf was measured to add itself to the folder; every stop says what to do next; the Windows script prints paths through FOR variables, so a folder named with `&` is printed, never run. README teaches switching the environment on, so the plain `synthtwin` line a run prints works as printed, and how to retype a PowerShell-quoted path in Command Prompt. CI installs into a folder whose name holds a space, and the gate asserts the step's condition names a shard of the matrix. The gate's tests read the next-command block as the module prints it, so a temporary folder with a space passes (it failed under the lock runner). `K-S8-01`'s measure counts an environment the install block needs and does not make and what one run takes in a new window (switching on, three commands, the run `--answers` repeats); `K-S8-04`'s CI key is renamed to the systems configured. STATE's KPI row is left to the integrator under the STATE rule; the ledger on the lane's branch then held 215 KPIs, 32 headlines under a cap of 32, 185 green and 14 open (the branch's figures at the time; STATE's KPI row holds the merged count).

**Repair round 2 (the combined verify and the tripwire skeptic, 2026-10-16), every item pinned by a gate case red on its mutant (22 mutants, 22 red; round 1's battery still red but for its two folder-look mutants, whose code this round replaced).** Doctor asks `Path.stat` once for the table and for the output folder: only a missing path is "not there", any other refusal the "not allowed to look at" line, then `os.path.isdir`, which never raises. From Python 3.14 `Path.exists` and `Path.is_dir` answer False where they may not look, which sent a person to make a folder that exists; a gate case gives them the `os.path` forms, so 3.10 to 3.13 prove the 3.14 answer. The gate's passing case reads the memory line as a note where memory cannot be read, as on every Windows cell of CI, where it would have failed, and a sibling case forces that on every system. Both scripts say when they replace an earlier environment and that a package installed into it by hand goes; the Windows script names a window still using it when one cannot be made; the closing lines and README teach switching the environment on in the window that ran the script as well as in new ones. The five unpinned guards are pinned: the Windows switched-on refusal, the Debian advice on Linux alone, the activate line after doctor, doctor's exit code as each script's last command, and exactly one synthtwin wheel. `K-S8-01` and `K-S8-04` are restamped on 5e42f38 with the same values.

**Batch 4b's integration (2026-10-16), the second verifier's item 1, as the orchestrator ruled.** Round 2's 22 mutants left three lines unpinned: a path through a file (`notes.txt/clinic.csv`, `--out-dir notes.txt/out`) is "not there" because `stat` answers NotADirectoryError, and a file named as `--out-dir` is named a file. `tests/test_terminal_install.py::test_doctor_says_a_path_through_a_file_is_not_there` pins all three, under both Path forms, and is red on each mutant (`except FileNotFoundError` alone in `_check_table` and in `_check_output_folder`, and `a_folder = there`), so the lane's tally is 25 mutants, 25 red.

**Lane CF4b: printed commands on Windows are for PowerShell (2026-10-16).** CI's Windows jobs on 68dae22f (run 38916841931) failed on a test that asserted the POSIX line on every platform where the product prints lane R1's PowerShell single quotes, and after Codex's review of a double-quote form meant for the Command Prompt as well (it let one value become extra options in Windows PowerShell 5.1 and let the Command Prompt's `%` and `!` expansion break its quotes) the orchestrator withdrew that form: printed commands on Windows are for PowerShell, byte for byte as 68dae22f prints them, Command Prompt support is a design question for the terminal track (lane TT) with its own Codex round, `tests/test_terminal_install.py` asserts each platform's own form and checks both quoting functions on any platform through `shlex`, PowerShell's single quotes and models of Windows PowerShell 5.1 and of 7.3 (the stated limit stands: 7.3 and later hand over a `"` and the ending backslashes of a value holding white space as written; and a NEW stated limit, found by the push critic of lane CF4b and owned by the terminal track's lane TT, the orchestrator's ruling written at batch 4c's integration: Windows PowerShell 5.1 drops an empty value), and the times-of-day notice's `--twelve-hour` and `--measurement` lines, which printed the column's name bare on every platform, now quote it through `_typed_option` and name their shell, the one change to printed bytes, POSIX ones included, and only where the quoting rule quotes it (the bare line broke for `Visit time` and `Visit & time`: `--twelve-hour Visit time` was two words, and `Visit & time` ended the command at `&`; the rule's plain set is ASCII, so `heure_arrivée`, `Größe` and `Visit#time` are quoted too).

## Decision P4-D398 — the analyst battery: stable statistical results made measurable (lane E0b, 2026-10-16)

**What it is.** The measurement backbone of the owner's direction of 2026-10-16 -- relations between columns that are really broad, regressions, trained models, analyses nobody names in advance, several rows per patient -- built test side only: nothing under `src/` changes, and today's twin is what it measures. Its specification is section 3 of the design study's S2 report (`planning-notes/work-2026-10/bc-design/S2-battery.md`).

**The rule.** For every analysis a researcher might run, the twin's answer should sit about as close to the real table's answer as a second, independent sample of the same size would. An estimate's yardstick is the root mean square of half A's value minus half B's over four half splits of sixteen SplitMix64 groups (by subject where a table has several rows per subject); the twin is inside where it lies within it. Only supported estimates are scored: every defining cell at least 22 rows (11 per half) and, on a two-valued outcome, 22 events and 22 non-events, the analysis running on the real table and all eight halves. Every run carries two controls -- the fresh replicate (the same generator at another seed) and the shuffled twin (every column shuffled on its own) -- every target is stated relative to the replicate (a perfect twin is inside only about 77 % of the time), and a run whose replicate fails its control or whose shuffled twin passes it is void: `controls_hold` false fails the entry. Where a shuffle cannot fail a check its negative control is named: a thin replicate (a tenth of the rows resampled) for twin-seed stability, the structured table ST1 for the null table ST5.

**What was built.** `tests/analyst_kit.py`, a plain-Python fitting kit (least squares, logistic and Poisson regression, Cox with Breslow's ties, a random-intercept mixed model, histogram gradient boosting, AUC, Spearman, restricted cubic splines), building each design a chunk of rows at a time so that memory is the table plus O(p^2), held to closed forms in `tests/test_analyst_kit.py`; `tests/analyst_tables.py`, the six seeded tables ST1 to ST6 with their truth files, built at run time and never committed, held to their truths in `tests/test_analyst_tables.py`; `tests/analyst_battery.py`, the targeted panel (each seeded truth's analysis and the naive models analysts fit), the automatic panel the schema alone gives (capped by ten events a term), both controls and the thirteen KPI computations, every table read with `pandas.read_csv`; `tests/test_analyst_battery.py`, the harness's own guarantees (swapped controls void a run). The fast part runs in the suite (ST1 and ST2 at 5,000 rows, one seed, about 30 s); `tools/measurements/kpi_analyst_battery.py` runs the rest through `kpi_run.py --slow`: all six tables at 20,000 rows, table seeds 1 to 3 and twin seeds 0 to 4 (`--kpi`, about 75 minutes), and 200,000 rows one seed each (`--night`, a child process per table for its own seconds and peak memory, waiting while a named suite lock is held). No dependency is added and no numpy linear algebra is used (the orchestrator's ruling, revisited only if the night measures over budget).

**The KPIs.** K-BC-01 to K-BC-13, all OPEN, their baselines measured on today's twin: K-BC-01 (replication parity, family by family) and K-BC-02 (every seeded truth recovered or named) are headlines, the board's cap rising from 31 to 33 -- the orchestrator's recorded call, which the owner may veto -- and K-S7-01's three-way clause folds into K-BC-02, stage 7b being folded into the broad program. Each must-not-get-worse bound rests on the shuffled twin of the same run (today's twin and a shuffle are both without joint structure, so their difference is noise: 4.5 binomial standard deviations of a difference of two shares, 318/sqrt(n) points) and each target on the replicate. K-BC-11, the twin's report line per analysis family, is recorded as "no line exists": the line is a product change for a later lane.

**Measured at 20,000 rows (three table seeds, five twin seeds, medians).** Today's twin stands where the shuffle stands: K-BC-01, 40.4 % of 2,897 supported estimates inside against the replicate's 78.1 % and the shuffle's 40.9 %, 37.7 points under the replicate (target 10), the trained models its worst family (91.7). K-BC-02, 6 of 96 seeded truths recovered, every one a truth of no effect, against the replicate's 84 and the shuffle's 6: 90 missed and unnamed, 9 of them of three columns. K-BC-03, 18.3 % of 1,272 real-significant estimates kept against the replicate's 91.7 % and the shuffle's 18.2 %; on the null table 5.7 % of pairs called associated (the replicate 4.8 %). K-BC-04, a model trained on today's twin of half the table falls 62 yardsticks under the real half's AUC (the shuffle 56, the replicate 0.55). K-BC-05, today's twin 460 times the replicate's discriminator ratio on its worst table and level with the shuffle on the structured tables (1.06); on the null table 2.26 times the replicate, its own column shapes told apart. K-BC-06, the ICC 0.72 off (the replicate 0.008), all five fixed effects outside their yardsticks, rows per subject 0.88 apart in total variation. K-BC-07 to K-BC-09, time to event 68.9 points under the replicate, missing cells 63.9, curves 60.8. K-BC-10, 15 robust analyses stop on today's twin and none on the replicate: ST2's wide table and subject table (a subject's rows are no longer one subject's) and ST3's three survival analyses (an end date before its entry date). K-BC-12, 85.7 % of estimates stable over twin seeds (the replicate 89.7 %, the thin replicate 20 %). K-BC-13, the harness: the fast part took 23.5 s on a loaded machine (target 60, bound 120), no control failed and the fourteen pinned nodes passed; at 200,000 rows, in a night window holding the shared suite slot on 2026-10-17, all six tables ran, each in a child process of its own, in 245 to 1,263 s (ST2 the fastest, ST1 the slowest: target 1,200, bound 3,600) and peaking at 385 to 1,062 MB (ST1 the largest: target 1,000, bound 2,000), with no control failing; K-BC-01 there reads 42.2 points under the replicate. The night is inside its bounds, so the ruling against numpy linear algebra in the tests stands.

**Choices made here (the orchestrator may revisit any).** (1) The S2 probe's column names and several of its words are in the decontamination manifest, so the tables use other clinical columns -- glucose for the threshold and the U-shaped curve, ventilation for the critical-care flag, urban living for the binary demographic, a language label with two rare levels, procedures for the overdispersed count, a marker for the repeated lab, a dose that is weight times a dose rate for the formula -- with the spec's truths. (2) ST4's three-way parity is not a trained-model outcome: its pair margins are flat, so a greedy tree finds no first split on the real table either (AUC 0.48 trained on half A); the parity is measured by the full logistic model. (3) The restricted spline's straight outer arms bend a parabola's estimate near the outer knots, so the truth tests check each curve by the generator's exact form; no KPI compares a twin with a truth's value, only with the real table's own estimate. (4) K-BC-08 reads the estimates of how missing cells depend on other columns; the pattern and complete-case shares, mostly each column's own missing share, stay in F9 for K-BC-01. (5) The slow tier caps an automatic model at 16 terms and runs the controls' discriminator and trained models at twin seeds 0 and 1 (today's twin at all five). (6) On ST2 the replicate's discriminator ratio is inflated by rows clustered in subjects (the null formula assumes independent rows); the control holds from 5,000 rows.

**Stated limits.** K-BC-12 read at its target on today's twin, as the shuffle did: stability is not fidelity (tightened in the review round below). The fast part, one seed of two tables, guards the harness and catches gross regressions; the judgement is the slow part's. Seconds and peak memory are judged only on the quiet reference machine. `analyst_kit.chi2_sf` stops at 500 terms, 0.7 % off at 69,295 degrees of freedom and p 0.5 (exact to 5e-11 at p 0.05 or less): lane E0L's (the orchestrator's naming, written at batch 4d's integration). K-BC-01 and K-BC-02 are headlines, raising the cap from 33 to 35 (the orchestrator's call D15, set at batch 4d's integration; the owner may veto).

**Review round (two skeptics, 2026-10-18, and the orchestrator's rulings of that day).** Every item is fixed, each pinned by a test red on its mutant (37 mutants, all red on the final head). *Controls.* Each control of K-BC-02 to K-BC-10 is asserted by name on the fast part's own run with either control swapped, and K-BC-12's on a run made to its shape (six could be switched off with every test green). K-BC-01 leaves out the margins a column-wise shuffle keeps exactly -- ST2's rows per subject sat in F7, the shuffle inside on all eight -- and is void (`families_control_void`) where one family's shuffle stands within 25 points of the replicate. *Targets a perfect twin meets.* A fresh draw standing in as the twin missed 15 of 96 truths where K-BC-02 asked none (the statistics skeptic's measurement): K-BC-02 now charges only truths the replicate gets back, and its target is McNemar's z of the truths only the replicate gets against those only the twin gets, at most 2, for all truths and for those of three columns; K-BC-06 counts fixed effects outside against the replicate's; K-BC-05 reads ST2, whose clustered rows put the replicate's own ratio at 2.6 to 15.2, beside its maximum; K-BC-10 charges no twin with an analysis a replicate draw stops on. *The automatic panel.* A heavy-tailed number past the real range made a spline's three terms collinear (z 50,015 on a fresh draw; 4 of 90 stand-in panels and 2 of 90 replicate panels stopped as singular): every automatic predictor is held to the real table's range, and on the three table runs where they stopped none stops now. A logistic model admits an indicator only where it holds 22 events and 22 non-events (5 of 18 table runs lost a rare-outcome model before); the null table tests a label against a number of more than 30 values by Kruskal-Wallis on ranks (the chi-square on its text values saw a fabricated shift on 5 and 7 of 20 seeds, Kruskal-Wallis on 20 of 20); at the slow tier a trained model predicts every two-valued column whose half-A model reaches an AUC of 0.6 (29 at 20,000 rows, where the seeded outcomes alone were). *The kit.* A random intercept with no group of two rows is refused as singular (its likelihood is flat there: ICC 0.003 to 0.98 by seed); separation is named before the steps' failure to settle; Kaplan-Meier's median at exactly a half, Kruskal-Wallis's formula with its ties correction and the booster's own bin for a missing cell are each held to a hand count. *Truth files.* ST4's chapter-B truth is its model's population estimand from the generator's constants, 0.702 (the rare codes in the reference chapters lower it from 1.0), checked at 200,000 rows with 4 SE under 0.3; readmission by ward x diabetes is checked positive and significant at 20,000 rows; and K-BC-02's rule states that at 5,000 rows the diabetes x current smoker cell, about 10 events, is under the floor, so the fast part's three-way clause rests on ventilation x age over 75. *Bounds.* K-BC-07 and K-BC-08 lose their fast shuffle bounds, which could not fail (K-BC-07 to K-BC-09 judge their controls alone at 5,000 rows); the fast part's seconds are bounded at the lane's 60; K-BC-05's rule names the eight and six key columns the tiers run. *K-BC-12* (the orchestrator's ruling): an estimate counts only where it is stable over twin seeds and inside the yardstick on a majority of them, which the shuffle fails. Not taken: the yardstick's fifteen Walsh splits (the skeptic's option), since McNemar's paired comparison absorbs the four-split noise without moving every yardstick. **Restamped at 20,000 rows on fc26d5d4** (load 4.8, no seconds judged): K-BC-01, 40.2 % of 2,930 supported estimates inside against the replicate's 78.2 % and the shuffle's 40.2 %, 38.0 points under; K-BC-02, McNemar's z 8.83 (78 truths only the replicate got back, none only the twin), 2.83 for three columns; K-BC-03, 17.2 % of 1,261 kept against 91.4 % and 16.3 %, the null table 4.8 % (the replicate 3.8 %); K-BC-04, 29 trained models 84.9 yardsticks under the real AUC (the shuffle 77.9, the replicate 1.4); K-BC-05, 464 times the replicate (ST2 beside, 43); K-BC-06, four fixed effects outside past the replicate's one, the ICC 0.72 off; K-BC-07 to K-BC-09, 68.9, 63.9 and 60.8 points under; K-BC-10, 15 analyses stop, none fragile; K-BC-12, 40.5 % stable and inside against the replicate's 79.3 % and the shuffle's 39.8 %. K-BC-13 keeps its night of 2026-10-17 on 2a92bea, where ST1 at 200,000 rows took 1,262.5 s and peaked at 1,062 MB: over its targets of 1,200 s and 1,000 MB, inside its bounds, and the targets stand as set. The review's code (the range clamp, Kruskal-Wallis, more trained models) runs in that night too, so it is measured again in the next night window the orchestrator schedules.

**Second review round (the combined verify and Codex's review, 2026-10-19).** Every item is fixed and pinned by a test red on its mutant (59 mutants on the final code, all red, run with no bytecode written, as the verify asked). *The kit.* Least squares sums its residuals in a pass of their own and the mixed model centres its outcome where the design holds the intercept (an outcome moved by 1e8 had read a residual sum and standard errors of 0, and an ICC of 0.693 for 0.941); Cox's model centres each term, takes every risk against one common bound and keeps a tied time's sums, never its rows (a term moved by 100 had stopped as not converging; a common censoring day had held 6,145 rows at once); a probability at 0 or 1 is separation only where the steps do not settle (a slope of 6 on (-4, 4) settles at 5.58, se 0.30, as R's glm fits it); the Kaplan-Meier median reads a half within R's tolerance (88 subjects whose curve is 44/88 had read 0.5000000000000002 and no median). *Several rows per subject.* The mixed model stops (`singular`, counted in K-BC-10) where fewer than 22 subjects hold two rows, and the ICC's support is those subjects: a twin whose subject numbers collide a few times among unique ones had read an arbitrary ICC scored over a support of thousands. *Scoring.* Every half holds 11 rows a defining cell (a 22-event cell split 21 and 1 in every half had been scored, its yardstick noise), so the supported estimates fall to 2,913 at 20,000 rows and at 5,000 rows no three-way truth is supported: K-BC-02's fast three-way clause, which a twin recovering nothing met, is reported, not judged, and a test holds every McNemar target to one such a twin misses. A rule the real table keeps on every row is read as the share of rows breaking it, with a yardstick of 0: ST3's event date against its status, never scored before, is now in K-BC-08, and the dose truth of K-BC-02 is the formula itself (a dose of 2 x fitted - dose kept the weight's coefficient to the last digit and broke the formula on 2,989 of 3,000 rows). A quarter of an automatic model's terms is kept for pair products, which no automatic model on ST1, ST4 or ST6 had held. K-BC-04 counts a model missing on a side or seed as an infinite gap, its controls void without theirs, and divides by the yardstick as measured (the 0.005 floor had read ten yardsticks as two; one of the 29 yardsticks at 20,000 rows, 0.0041, fell under it, and the replicate's worst stays at 1.4); K-BC-05 never leaves out a discriminator that could not be fitted (a NaN in its maximum had hidden one, or not, by the tables' order). *The slow driver.* Its cache reads every module the panels come from (`kpi_shapes`, `fixtures` and `workbooks` were missing), it runs where `resource` does not exist (Windows), and the 200,000-row chapter-B fit (3.0 s, 85 MB, the generator and one fit) moves to its night, which checks it before any table; the suite holds the estimand to the generator's constants and the generator to them row by row. ST4's effect-bearing codes are rare by weight, not by size: at seed 1, 3 of the 50 hold 11 rows or more at 5,000 rows, 14 at 20,000 and all at 200,000, as `analyst_tables` now states. **Restamped at 20,000 rows on 9109683f** (a loaded machine, no seconds judged): K-BC-01, 40.0 % of 2,913 supported estimates inside against the replicate's 76.5 % and the shuffle's 39.4 %, 36.5 points under; K-BC-02, McNemar's z 8.72 (76 truths only the replicate got back, none only the twin), 2.65 for three columns; K-BC-03, 16.9 % of 1,302 kept against 90.5 % and 16.1 %; K-BC-04, 29 trained models 92.7 yardsticks under the real AUC (the shuffle 79.7, the replicate 1.4), none missing on any side; K-BC-05, 464 times the replicate, no discriminator failed; K-BC-06, the ICC 0.72 off, four fixed effects outside past the replicate's one; K-BC-07 to K-BC-09, 68.9, 66.7 and 60.8 points under; K-BC-10, 15 analyses stop on today's twin, none on the replicate, none fragile; K-BC-12, 40.0 % stable and inside against the replicate's 77.5 % and the shuffle's 39.6 %. K-BC-13 keeps its night of 2a92bea; this round's code runs in the next night window the orchestrator schedules. The verify after this round (2026-10-19) found Codex's seed completeness still open -- a model missing on one or two of five twin seeds read the other seeds' median gap and met K-BC-04's target -- so a model missing on any seed of a side now reads an infinite gap and a rank correlation of -1 for that side, as K-BC-05 reads a discriminator, its count kept in `twin_models_missing` and pinned by a test red on the median's mutant; no value moves, as no model was missing on any side at either tier.

## Decision P4-D399 — the health data zoo: every kind of healthcare data, proven end to end (lane E0a of the December plan, 2026-10-16)

**Why.** The owner, 2026-10-16: "we should be able to ingest all, and when i say all, i really mean all type of data that can come in a healthcare database and reconstruct the twin. We can make question to the user about the data, general question, but we shouldn't assume that the user will know details of the analysis." The December plan tracks it as T3, proven by a catalogue battery re-run at every merge.

**What is built, test-side only.** `tests/health_zoo.py`: thirty-six kinds as seeded generators over twenty-three exports, written at run time and never committed; per export, the general answers a person gives (which column is a record number, which holds codes, that a pressure is two numbers in a cell, how a date orders day and month, which program wrote dates as numbers), offered answers only; the end-to-end run in process (`profile`, the answers, `profile --answers`, `generate` at seed 0, `validate`, its MISSED checks captured by column); and an analyst script per export, written against the column names, run on both files. A kind passes when every step exits 0 or 3, every question its table asks is general (every sentence of the questions file read), validate misses nothing on its columns (a file-level kind takes the file's own obligations), the script holds on the real table, and the twin holds every check: the table's own (codes in their system's pattern, dates in the source's format, units, censored values, '120/80' split, repeated patients) and the generic ones on every column and file (dtypes, missing cells and their spellings, text shapes, the values of a column of few values, rows, byte-order mark, line endings, encoding). Each failure names its owner in `health_zoo.OWNERS`, line by line. Every check carries the spoil of its real table that turns it red, and `tests/test_health_zoo.py` runs all of them. The workbook is read through `tests/crosscheck.py` and left out where openpyxl is absent. `K-HZ-01` to `K-HZ-03` (kpi_rules' id pattern gains the group `HZ`).

**Measured, the baseline (931f0f6).** Every export is described, answered and generated; every one of the 91 questions is about the data; the profiles reach fourteen of the fifteen roles (not `numeric_unrepresentable`, numbers past a float's range, which no healthcare export writes). 17 of 36 kinds pass at 600 rows, 27 at 20,000. The owners: DST (encounters' offsets), LM1 (a joined range's spelling), and, for the orchestrator to name lanes, levels under the floor written as `group-N`, numbers beside a unit read as labels, a decimal-comma weight and a DICOM UID written as made-up characters, DICOM's TM time read as a decimal number, several codes in one cell read as one label, codes made up character by character that their grammar or check figure rejects (TNM, NPI, a partial date), the flowsheet's long form (the between-columns program), notes at small sizes, a missing code inside a score's range, and a mixed result column's mean at 20,000 rows. 36.0 s at 600 rows, 750.1 s and 471.5 MB at 20,000 under load.

**Repair 1 (skeptic 1 and Codex, 2026-10-16), every item pinned by a gate case red on its mutant (30 mutants of the zoo and its driver, 30 red).** The workbook through the cross-check reader, with keys over the delimited exports judged where it is absent and a suite-wide guard against a workbook read around it; the generic checks; the spoils; gate cases for every prerequisite of the pass rule and for a fault of the script on the real table; owners per failure; nine more exports and four more kinds in existing ones (operating-room times and a twelve-hour clock, several codes in a cell, a tumor registry with partial dates, US units, DICOM's DA, TM and UID, a SQL Server export, microbiology, immunizations and providers, risk and comorbidity codes, genomic identifiers, one mixed result column, an empty and a constant column); the hour the clocks skip and the hour they repeat judged by the transition rules, cross-checked against the time-zone database where it is installed; ranges of exactly two bounds; six-figure LOINC codes; the semicolon export answering semicolon; the driver portable to Windows and naming the failing kinds and the prerequisites at 20,000 rows. 12 of 22 and 17 of 22 were the first baseline, on a narrower catalogue and a blinder comparison.

**Repair 2 (the combined verify and the tripwire skeptic, 2026-10-16), every item pinned by a gate case red on its mutant (38 mutants of the zoo and its driver, 38 red; repair 1's 29 still red, three in their rewritten form).** The comparison now sees what repair 1's could not: forms character by character (figures' width, letters' case), so a date or clock written unpadded or in capitals fails where 11 or more twin cells take a form the real never wrote; the spellings of missing counted (none new, none 11 or more real cells write lost, each at its share); the product's `group-N` stand-in on any column; for a column answered `code`, a value the real never writes, ZIP codes aside as HIPAA's Safe Harbor identifiers; values on every column whatever the dtype, so a -99 never written fails; the middle and ends of the numbers past a unit, a decimal comma or a censoring mark; every "present" check with its share, the shares of patients holding two and three rows, and note lengths at three percentiles. Gate cases: a twin that does not read, a miss of the whole file, a command that stops with SystemExit, each aggregate of `zoo_measures`, the driver printing only what it measured (the delimited exports' keys are the judged ones, so a machine without openpyxl measures and judges them). A question about the whole file is now answered by its subject, as the product keys it (before, none was answered). Four kinds no table seeded join, over two exports: two title lines above all-text columns (the product asks which row holds the names, and the person says), day-first dates, two-figure years whose century the person knows, and true/false columns; all four pass. Owners are re-keyed to the zoo-fix track's lanes (UN-1a, UN-1b, CODES-1, CODES-2, CODES-3, GG, TR, LISTS, UN-2, NOTES, KV, beside DST and LM1), and a failure only 'needs owner' covers is counted apart. **Measured on 7bc0b80, every count the same on 3f2b4b5 after the titled report's third ward and last date column took plain names:** 20 of 40 kinds pass at 600 rows and 29 of 40 at 20,000 (25 of the 36 repair 1 had: clinical notes, 17,245 of 20,000 twin notes `group-N`, and the decimal-comma mass index, its middle 48.1 against 25.3, no longer pass); 96 questions, all about the data; 100 analyst checks and 7 obligations fail at 600 rows, every failure owned; at 20,000 rows one failure still needs a lane (the mixed result column's mean, which validate misses). 21.4 s at 600 rows, 520.8 s and 238.4 MB at 20,000 on 3f2b4b5, at a one-minute load under 3.0. **A finding for the orchestrator, not repaired here:** a person who answers the questions file in two rounds loses the first round's answers -- the file the first `--answers` run writes no longer carries them, so an identifier answered in round one is unanswered after round two (`us_vitals`' patient_id becomes `affixed_number` and the twin's share of patients holding two rows or more is 0.98 against the real's 0.84; `diagnoses_procedures` loses its `enc_id` and a SNOMED `code` answer), and the product's own refusal of a file answer beside column answers asks for exactly two rounds; the zoo answers once, as the product's next command invites, and the probe is kept with the lane's notes. **Owners (the orchestrator's rulings of 2026-10-19, written at batch 4c after Codex's merge review and push critic 9):** the one failure at 20,000 rows that needed a lane, the mixed result column's mean, which validate misses, is lane G2T's on the generation side (number tails and spread; it takes it if the cause is in numeric generation, else names its owner) and lane SV's for validate's miss; `health_zoo.OWNERS` still reads 'needs owner' on that line, so `K-HZ-01`'s 20,000-row count of failures needing an owner stays 1 until the lane that takes it writes its name there. The answers lost across two rounds are lane AQ's, the questions file's answers across rounds, built on lane HX's head: an identifier answer lost is a privacy matter under HX's hold rule.

**Stated limits.** Native formats (SAS, Stata, SPSS, Parquet, FHIR) are out, as the owner deferred them (T4). The sizes are 600 rows in the suite and 20,000 through `kpi_run --slow`. ## Decision P4-D400 — `synthtwin profile` reads and describes a large table one group of columns at a time (lane SR of the December plan, 2026-10-18; repairs 1 and 2, 2026-10-19)

**Why.** The owner's big table is 2,000,000 rows by 50 columns, within twelve hours and under the 2.5 GB one process may hold (TRACKED T5). Lane B0 measured the profile process on lane S4d's tree at 476 / 818 / 1,463 MB at 100,000 / 250,000 / 500,000 rows of K-S4-02's mixed table, 4,008 MB projected at 2,000,000 (K-S1-06's Gaussian table at 50 columns: 2,723 MB), the reader alone holding 395 / 758 / 1,308 MB: the file's bytes, its decoded text and a text object a cell of every column, which the census, the description and the questions then held too. (P4-D398, which the December plan reserved for this lane, was taken by lane E0b under its amendment A4.)

**What is built.** (1) Read `in_groups` (`synthtwin profile` passes it), `reading` never holds the file's text whole, only its first MiB and some: it takes the lines as the decoder hands them over, the encoding chosen as `dialect.decoded` chooses it. `dialect.survey` and `settle` take `keep`, the columns a walk holds (every record is still read whole, so every count, refusal and row fact is the same), and `streamed` (`dialect.Streamed`), whose `walks` hand EVERY walk the survey makes the file's lines afresh, so a walk made again -- a guess shown wrong, a reading refused -- reads the file again line by line and never decodes it whole. (2) The walk that holds no column measures what each column's cells cost to hold, each text at its own width as Python 3.10 holds it (`dialect.Survey.cell_bytes`, 9 bytes a cell beside it); groups are cut from those costs under `reading.GROUP_BYTES` (256 MiB) and walks of groups under `reading.WALK_BYTES` (768 MiB), greedily in column order (`reading.runs_under`). Each walk is checked by the standard reader and by pandas and let go before the next is read; what either check would refuse is weighed once every walk is done, so the refusal is the one a reading of every column makes. (3) `reading.column_values(table, place)` is THE GENERIC COLUMN ACCESS for every later lane (stage 6 and the broad between-columns profiler among them): any column, in row order, any number of times; `reading.hold_columns(table, places)` holds any set of columns in one reading; `column_groups` and `column_walks` name the groups and walks. A column outside those held costs one reading of the whole file: `synthtwin profile` reads the file 103 times on either of lane B0's tables at the budgets of 2,000,000 rows (45 and 50 groups, 11 and 10 walks: 3 for the encoding, 12 and 11 walks of the survey, 11 and 10 standard-reader checks, 77 and 79 readings by the access) and pandas reads it once a walk. (4) The description asks each column of it; the population census reads one column at a time (`profile.population_census_of`: the rows holding a value, whether each declared identifier repeats, and the rows each names, `taxonomy.repeats_in`, `people_joined_by`, `people_counted`); the questions of each round are worked out a walk at a time. (5) Every reading is held to the first -- size, modification time, line count and a digest of the lines -- and a file that changed in between, or whose records are no longer where the first reading found them, is refused (`errors.file_changed_while_read`); two versions are never mixed. Nothing is written to disk and no temporary file exists to leave, name or protect. (6) One column's own description: `taxonomy._split_once` remembers at most `parsing.SPELLING_MEMO_TEXTS` texts a grammar, and `taxonomy._tally` holds a label written one way only, otherwise than itself, as that spelling rather than a map of one entry.

**Repair 1 (skeptic 1 and Codex's review of dad8ed3e, 2026-10-19), each item pinned by a gate case red on its mutant (`wave6/SR/repair1/mutants.py`, logs `mutants-1.log` and `mutants-2.log`: 17 mutants, 16 red, the one green named below).** Skeptic 1: (1) the two tests the lane broke follow the new call and the new message; (2) describe's part of K-S4-09 is NOT established and stays open, below; (3) groups and walks are cut by each column's own bytes, so four adjacent note columns are four groups and the walks stay under their budget; (4) a walk made again reads the lines afresh (no whole text, gate case on five shapes); (5) the three unpinned checks are pinned, except the facts pass's own size-and-moment check, dropped: every later reading holds the file to the size and moment taken before it, so it never refused anything; (6) the Gaussian projection of 2ab12d9 rests on a series that falls (168.6 / 520.0 / 220.0 MB) and is NOT a projection: the driver now takes each Gaussian size as the largest of three hash seeds; (7) the access's cost is stated and `hold_columns` takes any places; (8) workbooks at scale are the orchestrator's to own, below. Codex: (1) a reading by the access shares texts by the survey's own rule, so a text repeated late is held once; (2) the census holds one declared column at a time; (3) a refusal kept for a later walk is built again without the frames of the walk that raised it and raised outside the handler that caught the next one, and a walk shown wrong is let go before the next; (4) cells are costed at their own width; (5) a record no longer where it was is refused as a changed file, never an IndexError or a csv error; (6) the driver records no peak where resident memory cannot be read; (7) STATE's KPI row is the batch integrator's, as the repo rule says (STATE's suite row only); (8) `build_document` states that a table read in groups is read again from its file and what that raises. The one green mutant raises a settle-level refusal inside its handler: nothing is walked after that refusal, the reading ends, so it holds nothing longer.

**Repair 2 (the combined verify and the tripwire skeptic of c7ca4aa3, 2026-10-19), each item pinned by a gate case red on its mutant (`wave6/SR/repair2/mutants.py`, `mutants.log`: 5 mutants, all red).** Verify: (1) a line that no longer decodes in a later walk is the file changed -- the facts pass decoded every line under that codec -- and is refused in those words, never a traceback; (2) a gate case swaps two lines with the size and moment kept, so the line digest's order is pinned. Tripwire: (1) the census reads each declared column once, asking whether it repeats and joining its rows in one reading (`taxonomy.people_joined_if_repeating`), as the whole census reads it; (2) every size of the mixed table is the largest of three hash seeds, as the Gaussian's, never PYTHONHASHSEED=0: the night window that re-stamps K-S4-09 and K-S4-11 (`wave6/SR/repair2/night-window.sh`) takes about six hours; (3) `hold_columns` refuses a place that is no column with IndexError before reading, never told to the person as a changed file.

**Proof.** `tests/test_stage4_describe_groups.py` (the gate, named for what it tests since nothing is spilled; 64 cases): fourteen written forms and 400 seeded adversarial files read or refused alike whole and one column a group; `synthtwin profile` of a table raising every kind of question, under four sets of options and two walk budgets, the same bytes and words; what is held, no walk alive when the next is read, and no walk of a group held beside the next; a file changed by a value, a row, its moment, its records, while pandas reads it or while the survey walks it, refused; any column in any order; a run stopped half way leaves no file; the census of several identifiers and of rows naming nobody counted as the whole census counts. Lane S4d's battery of 880 descriptions read one column a group is the base's bytes at repair 1's head (`wave6/SR/battery-fullr1.json` equals `battery-fullbase.json`).

**Measured.** K-S4-09 (OPEN; describe's part RED, not met). On 2ab12d9, by `kpi_run.py --slow` in a night window: describe's peak 220.4 / 376.4 / 701.6 MB at 100,000 / 250,000 / 500,000 rows of the mixed table. Lane B0's least-squares fit read 2,204.5 MB at 2,000,000 only through the curvature the 100,000 point lends it: the last doubling grew x2.09, so linear from 500,000 rows is 2,572 MB and at that doubling's own rate 2,802 MB, both over the watchdog's 2,560 MiB, and this decision's earlier "296 MB under the watchdog" is withdrawn. The Gaussian 168.6 / 520.0 / 220.0 MB falls and is NOT a projection (allocator residue: 183 against 531 MB on one file at hash seeds 2 and 3). The repaired driver measures the mixed table at 1,000,000 rows too and projects from the three largest sizes, takes each size of either table as the largest of three seeds (the mixed table since repair 2), scales the walk budget with the group's, and records no peak where resident memory cannot be read; its re-stamp takes about six hours and is the orchestrator's night window (`wave6/SR/repair2/night-window.sh`). Machine-free at the repair's head d1d6517f: 18.6 (mixed) and 4.2 (Gaussian) traced bytes a cell at 200,000 rows, against 17.7, the bound the watchdog sets once the 78 MB of imports are set aside and the resident peak is taken as 1.4 times the traced one (skeptic 1's measure at 500,000 rows). K-S4-11 (recorded, its value 2ab12d9's): 4,774.3 s (mixed) and 3,127.1 s (Gaussian) projected, against lane B0's 3,451 and 2,731 s, about 38 % more on the mixed table from reading the file again (this decision's earlier "under a tenth of describe's CPU" is withdrawn); inside the owner's twelve hours. Skeptic 1's probe at 10,000 rows, budgets of 2,000,000 rows, at repair 1's head: six adjacent note columns of 60 words 35.0 MB traced read in groups against 60.0 MB whole (47.1 before the repair); one malformed doubled quote, or one doubled space in a comma-space file, read with 0 whole-text decodings (10 before), every file the same bytes as read whole.

**Stated limits.** (a) Describe's part of K-S4-09 is not met: one column's description where every value differs holds 0.8 to 0.9 KB a row at its peak (the mixed table's record numbers and stamps: a `taxonomy._Cell` per cell and per affixed core, the core's exact digits, the folded label), most of the mixed table's peak; its owner is lane H3 (the identity walk's column text; lane SV's describe-once is the first cut; the orchestrator's naming of 2026-10-20, written at batch 4d's integration), and K-S4-09 stays OPEN with describe's part RED. (b) A column whose own cells cost more than a group or a walk is read and described alone: one note column of 60 words (542 bytes a row of file) adds 1,344 traced bytes a row to the profile's peak (15.6 MB at 10,000 rows, 29.1 MB at 20,000), about 2.7 GB at 2,000,000 rows, over the watchdog; owner lane H3 (free text, about 408 s a column at 1,000,000 rows). (c) A workbook is read whole in lane S4d's form, and `workbook.MAXIMUM_CELLS` (1,000,000 cells, on the base) refuses a sheet of 20,001 x 50 or 1,048,576 x 50 before it is described: workbooks at scale are not the owner's native-formats deferral, and are lane XL's (skeptic 1, item 8; the orchestrator's naming, written at batch 4d's integration). (d) Each `column_values` outside the columns held is one reading of the whole file, and stage 6 and the broad between-columns profiler add to this process: they measure their own peak and readings. (e) `validate` reads its file whole (lane SV's); `generate` holds the twin (lane SG's).

## Decision P4-D401 — no real identifier is published while its question is open (lane HX of the December plan, 2026-10-16)

**The finding** (`planning-notes/work-2026-10/wave6/ZOO/CRITIC.md` item 1, on 68dae22f). A long table of 600 rows over 44 patients, `record` written `REC1000xxxx` on each patient's rows, profiled with the person question (P4-D340) put and nobody answering: `record` was read as labels, the description named 26 of the 44 record numbers and the twin wrote them back. Several rows per patient is in scope (TRACKED T2), and under the owner's principle of 2026-10-01 a record number is a direct identifier whatever its count.

**The rule, in the owner's pattern of 2026-09-17 (ruling 8: do not guess, ask), applied literally by the orchestrator's ruling of 2026-10-16.** Where nobody is at the keyboard, a column put a question the ruling names -- the person question, the two-numbers question, or the question answered by a measurement, a code or a record number (padded figures, figures all one width or grouped in threes, and a date count whose values are also one width) -- that nobody answered and nothing declares, whose reading publishes values and is not one of dates or times, is described as record numbers until it is answered: no level name, rung, percentile, mode, tail value, form or prefix. Its block is a declared record number's with no prefix, the evidence NF125 and the census of repetition the counts it publishes imply, layout by layout (C6-80a); its name joins `settings.forced_identifiers`, so the twin writes made-up record numbers, and `person_columns` and the population count do not change. The screen names the columns held; the questions file asks again with `read_as_now: identifier` and says that a blank keeps the column held with the rows counted as rows, while typing `identifier` declares it under the population floor. Any answer gives back its own description byte for byte: a file's `keep` is carried, and a blank under a reading the file named keeps that reading, so a `keep` survives the file it wrote; every declaration (a decimal comma, a clock, dates, a counting system) is an answer; Enter at the keyboard is an answer. Route three of the person rule (a repeating register of e-mail addresses, United States telephone numbers in ten layouts, social security numbers or Medicare beneficiary identifiers) is put beside a declared person column too. A minus sign and one figure, at most a third of the cells, no longer silences the width question of a key. The description is built a second time where a column is held: at 500,000 rows of the record shape, 33.7 s against 22.7 s.

**What holds nothing, and why.** The questions about dates and times (dates written like codes, a date count alone, days of the year, mostly dates, twelve-hour clocks), a column read as dates or times, the point-between-thousands question and the checklist of columns read as numbers: held, every unanswered table of HL7 stamps or clock times would write record numbers where its dates and times stood (98 failures over eleven battery files), and the checklist lists every measurement of every table. Their cells were read as dates, times or plain numbers; a key of figures that only the checklist would list is reached instead by route four of the person rule (repair round 2 below).

**Measured** (`K-S3-64`, new, PRIVACY): over 32 shapes at 600 and 20,000 rows -- record, plan, account and beneficiary numbers in every layout the reviews measured, telephone numbers in six layouts, social security numbers, e-mail addresses, a patient key beside `-1`, ZIP codes, device identifiers, a five-figure subject code, 599 long record numbers beside one short one, and three registers beside a declared person column -- 2,569 real values in what is published, 1,793 fragments and 580,712 real twin cells on 68dae22f, 0 of each now, the question still asked of every one. The zoo's probes on this head: Caboodle `PatientDurableKey` 0 of 60 keys printed (57 on 68dae22f), ZIP codes 0 of 59 (27), device identifiers 0 of 49 (32). Eighteen runs answered or never asked are 68dae22f's bytes (`wave6/HX/repair1/compare_base2.py`), save the questions file of a `+1-` telephone column, which is now asked. No golden moves.

**The price, accepted by the ruling.** Over the suite's description batteries (`wave6/HX/repair1/hold-census-literal.jsonl`), a scripted run holds 158 column readings of 130 names -- 56 the person question reaches (codes, medicines, diagnoses, labels), 23 the two-numbers question (blood pressures among them), 58 of one width (50 of them one 150-column table) and 17 padded -- and up to 28 readings of 19 names of dates written as counts all one width (`sas_days`, `xl_date`), since a ten-figure NPI reads as seconds since 1970 too. The ruling's estimate was 38. Tests about other things whose columns these questions reach press Enter at every question (`tests/keyboard.py`), which keeps 68dae22f's bytes: `test_landing_2b18_forms_and_spellings.py` (six functions), `test_landing_2b16_number_readings.py` (six), `test_joined_pair_round_trip.py` (five), `test_p4d64_judged_stand_ins_written.py`, `test_stage3b_layout.py`, `test_workbook_round_trip.py`, `test_p4d140_number_censuses.py`, `test_stage2_round_trip.py`, `test_extra_round_disclosure.py`, `test_round2_disclosure.py`, `test_stage2_refusals.py` and `test_window_agreement.py` (two each), and `test_ruling_pooled_held_back_levels.py`, `test_ruling_levels_counted_by_subtraction.py`, `test_landing_2b7_mixed_spellings.py`, `test_landing_2b8_labels_text_missing.py`, `test_number_censuses_name_no_row.py`, `test_numbers_beside_labels.py`, `test_numeric_strata_round_trip.py` and `test_p4d382_typed_workbook_cells.py` (one each); `test_p4a60_answers_handed_back.py` now expects its two unanswered columns held; the wide keys of `test_p4d140_number_censuses.py` (two), `test_stage2_round_trip.py` (three) and `test_file_dialect_round_trip.py` (one) are declared measurements.

**Stated limits.** A patient's name, a street address and a full birth date, which no identity question flags, on a long table while the person question is open: 214 real values in the descriptions and 61,559 twin cells over 600 and 20,000 rows (44 of 44 birth dates at 20,000), held at that ceiling by `K-S3-64` and pinned as strict expected failures; owned by lane HX2 (the orchestrator's: while the person question is open, a value is counted in the question's candidate subjects, not rows). A ZIP column answered `code` that prints its common ZIPs is lane CODES-2's (Z1 B's allowlist). A key written beside `-1`, declared or held, gets a twin that misses its published forms (exit 3; on 68dae22f for a declared key alike): the identifier generator's, lane CODES-1 part C's. A held column's census can hold an entry under 11 only where the counts it publishes already imply it.

**Repair round 2 (the combined verify and the tripwire skeptic, 2026-10-17; the orchestrator's addendum 2 chose to close the numeric keys).** ROUTE FOUR of the person rule asks about a column of whole numbers -- plain, written `100001.0`, or grouped in threes by commas, spaces or two points or more -- beside placeholders for nobody (a minus sign and one to three figures, one word), fewer than half the cells, repeating at least twice a value over two values or more, more than half of its values five figures or more; a lone `0` is a whole number counted with the keys, one narrow value among them, so it is not limited to under half the cells (since 4b42d25f; measured: six-figure keys with `0` on 200 of 332 cells are held, the same share of `-99` is not); dates, clock times and joined numbers are not put it. Route three is judged by share (a third of the cells may be something else) and reads an extension after a telephone number, a spaced social security number, sixteen figures in four groups, an internet or web address and an e-mail address after a name. The width question sets aside a lone `0` and nines alone besides `-1`, and only beside cells five figures or more, so a systolic pressure, platelets in thousands or a birth weight beside `-1` or `-9` is described as on 68dae22f. A held census spreads each layout's rows over its share of the values (C6-80a): spread over the whole column, 600 beneficiary identifiers in four layouts left no way to fill a layout of 141 rows and the twin failed its validation; and a layout holds at most the values it can write, the largest remainders closing the shares, since a six-figure key beside a lone `0` on 620 of 20,000 rows gave the `0` two values. Each fix of this round is red on its own mutant (`wave6/HX/repair2/mutants.log`, 18 of 19; the survivor named a lone `0` a placeholder in a branch no cell reached, now removed: a lone `0` is a whole number route four counts with the keys). NF125's contract quote is the product's sentence, pinned. K-S3-64's counter finds a value's longest run of five figures or more printed as a number, and figures alone only with no figure or point against them. PRICE, over the suite's description batteries (`wave6/HX/repair2/hold-census-r2.jsonl`, 97 files): route four holds one column no other question held, two Excel days 45000 and 45001 read as two labels; route three's widening none; the `0` set aside asks ten columns of dates written as counts beside `0` the width question too, so they are held like those all one width; a three-figure reading beside `-1` to `-3` is no longer held; `test_stage3b_counted.py` (one test) now expects its Excel dates beside `0` held. Beyond the batteries the price grows with the table (lane HX's second verify, item 1, measured on 5793f7b0 against 68dae22f): income in whole thousands (15,000 to 180,000, one row a person) is held at 600 rows; daily steps (2,000 to 20,000) and charges in cents are held from 200,000 rows, not at 20,000; any repeating whole-number measurement mostly five figures or more is held at 1,000,000 rows in a scripted run until its question is answered, and `keep` restores 68dae22f's bytes (income at 600 rows: description, summary and twin, the description pinned by a gate case red with route four off); lane HX2 (P4-D406) measures what such a false candidate costs its subject count. Every answered path (`keep` on each new shape, `code` and `measurement` on keys and ZIP codes, `keep` on a record number) and both declared-person tables are 68dae22f's description, summary and twin, byte for byte (`wave6/HX/repair2/compare-r2.log`); a questions file carrying `answered_before` differs. ## Decision P4-D402 — the padded and plus exchanges walk forward: padded code columns generate in linear time (lane H1 of the December plan, 2026-10-16)

**The fault (measured on 68dae22f; `planning-notes/work-2026-10/wave6/H1/`).** `generation._padded_style_swaps`, reached only by numeric columns whose description publishes `pad_widths` (postal codes, MRNs, zero-padded record numbers, numeric procedure and laboratory codes), asked each partner by scanning the column from cell 0: `_first_giver` once per cell of every whole-value trial, `give_up` once per cell-by-cell hand-over, the overflow pass once per cell no width holds, and `_point_free_form_worn` recounting every style handed in for each cell left without a partner. Generate grew x3.0 to x3.4 a doubling on such columns where every other role grew about x2.0; lane B0's window measured the postal-code column at 16.0, 84.4 and 269.3 s of generate at 100,000, 250,000 and 500,000 rows, about 3,630 s projected at 2,000,000 (the owner's T5 in `plan-dec/TRACKED.md`: a really big table in 12 hours, 18 acceptable).

**The walk (the rule unchanged).** Each style taken has a roster of givers for the width, built once in ascending cell order, with a next-alive list (`generation._alive_from`) every partner is retired from; a trial keeps one reach per style and starts again from each roster's first live giver; `give_up` reads the same rosters; the overflow pass keeps one forward cursor per wearing key; and the point-free form is asked once per wearing key for the call, still through its module name, its answer kept for that call only. Within a call a cell only ever stops being a giver, so every partner is the one the scan chose; `_first_giver` is removed. `_plus_style_swaps` is the same family and was measured first, machine-free, on the arguments of a signed column the style walk leaves short by a tenth of its non-negative decimals: 783,131, 3,143,778 and 12,592,672 taker steps at 50,000, 100,000 and 200,000 rows, x4.0 a doubling against the lane's x2.4 bar, so its takers walk forward too, through one next-alive list in their fixed order and one per figure count (through generate, the shapes tried reached it short by 13 or not at all).

**Proof.** `tests/test_stage4_padded_swap_scale.py` holds 68dae22f's two exchanges as oracles: the same answers on 2,000 seeded cases and four of 12,500 to 25,000 cells (and 2,000 signed columns and two of 25,000 cells for the plus exchange), red on six mutants (a reach kept across trials, a giver spoken for not skipped, a cell one style cannot wear retired from every roster, one cursor for every wearing key; a padded giver taking any taker, a taker left free in its figure group); predicate calls x2.0 from 50,000 to 100,000 cells (bound x2.2) where the oracle's grow x3.8; the plus exchange's lines x2.0 where its oracle's grow x3.4; and swapping `_point_free_form_worn` in still changes the twin. Seed-0 twins and reports of lane B0's one-column post_code, visit_id and record_no tables at 50,000, 100,000 and 200,000 rows are byte-identical to 68dae22f's. KPIs: `K-S4-16`, the exchange's predicate calls and its walk's own lines 200,000 over 100,000 postal cells, x2.0 each (bound x2.1; on 68dae22f the same column's calls grew x3.65 from 12,500 to 25,000 cells and its lines x4.0 from 6,000 to 12,500), and the point-free form asked once (at most 8), and `K-S4-17`, one padded code column's generate projected to 2,000,000 rows, 164.3 s (target 400; 68dae22f about 3,630 s), seconds judged only in a quiet window. **The window** (lane H1's, 2026-10-16, the suite slot held, one heavy process, nice 10, at a load average of 5.4 to 8.4, so recorded and not judged): generate CPU of the one-column tables at 100,000, 250,000 and 500,000 rows, by lane B0's runner, post_code 7.2, 17.6 and 35.1 s (B0 on 68dae22f: 16.0, 84.4 and 269.3), visit_id 15.6, 23.4 and 43.3 s (B0: 24.9, 121.8 and 300.9) and record_no 15.8, 24.1 and 46.4 s; `K-S1-06`'s driver, whose Gaussian columns never reach the exchange, read 186.3 s at 100,000 x 20, a ratio of 3.71 and 93.2 microseconds a cell, recorded here and not restamped (its entry is not this lane's).

**What did not move.** No twin byte, golden, vector or METHOD text, and no oracle: `tools/reference` mirrors no padded swap (it mirrors `pad_places` and `pad_need` only), and its `plus_style_exchange` states the plus exchange's rule -- each giver takes the first free partner, a padded one only a partner needing no more figures -- which the forward walk still meets, so it stands as written as the independent witness, and A-P4-59 is not triggered (no method changed). `_served_walk` is untouched and stays a watch item: its lump on visit_id, 0.25, 11.74 and 0.42 s at 50,000, 100,000 and 200,000 rows on the prototype (lane H1's refute), is linear and outside the exchange.

**Repair round 1 (skeptic 1 and Codex, 2026-10-16), each item pinned by a gate case red on its mutant; no product line changed.** Four walks pick every partner the scan picked and ask the predicates no more often, yet are quadratic, and the gate and `K-S4-16` counted only the predicates: the point-free form asked per cell (1,116 asks on 25,000 postal cells against 1; skeptic 1 measured the exchange's CPU x3.6 to x4.1 a doubling under it), a next-alive list that never shortens its links, a trial asking each style from its roster's start, and the overflow cursor put back to cell 0. The gate now counts the walk's own lines under `sys.settrace` on four shapes, at most x2.2 a doubling (the product reads x1.98 to x2.02): those mutants read x3.81 on a distinct-code column of 12,500 cells, x3.96 on Codex's one value taking a partner per cell, and x3.95 on its overflowing cells after a reserved prefix, each answering as the product does, so only the count sees it. The point-free form's asks are bounded by one per wearing key, 8, and the small case asks exactly once (3 under the mutant, which the old bound of under 6 let pass). `K-S4-16` judges the lines and the asks beside the calls and is restamped on bb42a22 (x2.002 calls, x1.996 lines, 1 ask); its evidence cites its own column on 68dae22f (13,473,048 and 49,112,176 calls at 12,500 and 25,000 cells, 1,078 and 1,964 a cell), not the spec's column, whose x4.0 was never measured at 200,000 over 100,000.

## Decision P4-D403 — the packing walk reads the counts of one margin together (lane H2 of the December plan, 2026-10-17)

**The fault** (lane H1's build, 2026-10-16; the owner's T5, big tables generate in time). On a number column of signed changes -- `gauss(0, 40)` written `+3.25`, `+12`, `12`, `-1.50` and `-4` -- `synthtwin generate` never finished at 4,000 or 5,000 rows on 36ad3061 (over 25 minutes in H1's run). `_style_strata` asks method G9.5's packing walk a style question with no answer: `plain` and `leading_plus` owe 1,425 rows together where the strata that may wear a point-free spelling hold 1,416 (1,778 and 1,689 at 5,000 rows). The five conditions `_cell_entry` reads each read one count or one later cell, so the cell answering for `leading_plus` was offered every way of taking its 397 rows from 20 group sizes, up to 7.6e11 partial fills, each refused near its end: 24,244,572 reserve readings in 300 s, unfinished.

**The change, which moves no answer.** Condition 6, `generation._owed_together`: for every non-empty set of the counts one margin still owes (2 to `_TOGETHER_COUNTS` = 8 of them), the rows they owe together must not pass the unplaced rows whose groups can still stand in a cell answering for one of them -- Hall's condition for the margin, read with integer sums and bit masks only. It is a necessary condition, so it passes over only states holding no answer; the walk's order and its first complete filling, or None, are G9.5's as before. So no METHOD text, oracle or vector changes, and `tools/reference`'s `_packed_grid` stays the independent witness. No ceiling, budget or time limit is added (P2-C3-F1): a margin owing more than eight counts is not read, which skips a necessary condition and never changes an answer.

**Measured** on 1df4ca4 against 36ad3061 (`planning-notes/work-2026-10/wave6/H2/build/`). The question is refused on entering its first cell, with no fill and no reserve read, at 4,000 and 5,000 rows (`K-S4-18`), and the twin builds in 0.86 and 0.88 s. Twin and report sha256 are identical on all 26 runs 36ad3061 finished over eight signed and styled number shapes at 1,000 to 50,000 rows (shape b at 2,000 rows took 97.65 s there and 0.27 s here). Shape a at 3,000 to 10,000 rows over column seeds 1 to 5 finishes 30 of 30 in 0.66 to 2.60 s, where 36ad3061 passed 30 s on 21 and wrote the same bytes on the other 9 (`K-S4-19`, recorded; its seconds judged only on the quiet reference machine). Of 8,000 seeded walk questions, 5,000 small and 3,000 large, the 7,998 that finished on both trees under the probe's 200,000-fill limit get the same answer and never more states, fewer on 90; the other two, large nested questions, are not counted as compared: the probe stopped number 1940 (three margins) on both trees, and number 2481 (pairs) on 36ad3061 only, answered here in 38 states; the gate test asks 3,000 nested style questions of `tests/stage4_as_built.py` the same. Gate: `tests/test_stage4_counts_together.py`, red on 36ad3061 (past 20,000 reserve readings) and green here, under pandas 3 and pandas 2. `K-S4-04` re-run, every key as stamped. Its cost, measured by the investigation: 8 % more on a walk of 223,973 states. `tests/test_p2c3f1_published_margins.py`'s no-ceiling witness is now answered in 1,584 states (243,155 before), so it no longer shows a ceiling; a grid from lane H2's search, 223,973 states on both trees with the same answer, takes its place.

**Stated limits.** The general walk is not fixed: a question that holds enough rows but cannot be filled with whole groups still walks exponentially, `K-S4-04`'s family (OPEN, stage 4's allocator walk): 1 of 3,000 large seeded three-margin questions passes 200,000 fills on both trees in this build's draw, and 2 of 3,000 in the investigation's. Every signed-change style question measured has no answer, so the twin keeps the cell walk's styles and the recount names the style miss, as on 36ad3061; that miss is a stated limit owned by the forms lane FM (the orchestrator's ruling of 2026-10-19, written at batch 4c).

**Second repair (Codex's review, 2026-10-18).** The equality above is counted over the 7,998 comparisons that finished, as Codex asked. `K-S4-19`'s driver counted a twin as finished whenever `generate` returned, so with no alarm (no SIGALRM) a 40-second twin counted toward `sweep_finished_within_30_s`; `sweep_tally` now counts only a twin under 30 s and keeps a late one's seconds as the slowest, pinned in the gate file and red on three mutants, and `K-S4-19` is restamped on e170a24 (30 of 30, the slowest 4.35 s on a loaded machine).
