## Decision P4-D404 — layer L0: each eligible column meets its band totals in the generator, and one reservation of records holding nothing (lane BTp of the December plan, 2026-10-18, repaired 2026-10-19; the method written, NOT BUILT)

**Why.** Stage 6, the between-columns design the owner asked to be "really broad" (2026-10-16), meets a family table cell for cell only where each column's own band totals are the table's margins, and today a column meets its rungs inside a window, not its counts between them. Measured on the product's own twins at 36ad3061 (invented data; lane scripts kept outside the repository; method G5.7i): at decile edges every number, date and clock column of an invented ten-column table missed its band totals at every seed, by 4 to 94 rows a column at 5,000 rows and 8 to 262 at 20,000, and an invented cohort's columns by up to 375 at 20,000. A count of few values with one rare high value misses by thousands, on the product's own twins and not on a prototype: 2,959 rows off at 10,000 rows (a fixed case), 5,717 at 20,000 and 29,676 at 100,000, with 30,000 rows on the value 3 where the real column held 12,465 (lane M6 measured the same at 12,471, its P4-D394 not merged), its median 3 against 2 and its mean 2.55 against 1.77 both called inside by its own report. The cause there is G5.2a step 3 dividing the longest run where the tail's rare values outnumber the ladder's runs, and G6.5a's separation lifting every stratum above it by one value; without the lift the same strata miss by 48 and 416 rows. The 200,000-row legs are two night-window scripts named in G5.7i.

**What is written** (`docs/spec/generation-method-v1.md`). G5.7: each L0 edge is a cut beside the two sign cuts; the cuts divide the ranks into pieces, and every clause that keeps a cell, a stratum or a value inside its sign band keeps it inside its piece; the ladder is read through a band map whose knots stand at the cut ranks; the strata are shared over the pieces by the Sainte-Lague rule, each piece held to `hi_p = min(C_p, A_p + F_p)` on a grid, its runs and its free points, and strata no piece can take are not made (the count of different numbers gives way, named); on a grid the strata beyond a piece's runs are made in its widest gap, never by dividing and lifting a run (item 3a); G5.5's sign repair widens into a piece repair; every later value step takes its candidates inside the piece; a last guard. G7.3l (dates): each edge's pin becomes a run from its cut rank to the rung's own rank, and the gap below ends one unit short of the edge. G7A.4d (clocks): edge knots at the cut rank, census groups cut in two (a half's derived count is never printed), the all-different repair piece by piece. G12.15: the rung and moment windows read through the band map at G12.2's half unit, extended only at ranks whose window reaches a cut, to the piece's fallback; a whole unit everywhere, as first written, widened the mean windows of whole-number and gridded columns by 6 to 20 per cent. G4.2a: one reservation of records holding nothing, made at G4 for text files by spelling (the empty text first, then spaces and tabs only) and for workbooks by class (`absent` first, then `blank`, never `empty`, which a reader counts as holding something), so G2.1 step 2's first walk and G2.2 step 6's exchanges do not run beside it, G2.2 step 1 fixes every class that holds nothing before the arrangement, and step 7 writes a reserved blank as a blank cell. G4.2b: `cells_by_band`, the interface G16 calls. G14.3a: thirteen oracle cases, each beside a mutant; case 1 is the count of few values at 10,000 and 20,000 rows, frozen at each value.

**The rules that settle a conflict.** B1: the band totals stand and the other fact gives way, named, because they are the margins of every family table and plan P2-D6's rule 4 already ranks a published count above ladder conformance; B1 is how the generator behaves and excuses nothing in the KPI. B2: the sign counts, the ends, the class counts, whole values and the empty stretches cannot conflict on a description passing G5.7a's five preconditions. B3: where those fail, the column is made without L0, named, and G16.6 meets its families.

**KPIs.** No new KPI and no new published count; no word is drawn; the floor is unchanged. `K-S6-02` is reworded for lane BT to stamp (G5.7h): byte for byte today's twin where `statistical` is null; cells and descriptions identical across the arrangement; every L0 band count exact at 5,000, 20,000 and 200,000 rows; 0 within-column facts held without L0 and missed with it, judged by today's windows extended only beside a cut, every B1 miss counted as a KPI miss against the target 0 and a count above 0 a named residual here, never a pass; and 0 within-band regressions on count columns (the counts at each value and the published rungs, with L0 against without it).

**Whose the rest is.** Lane BT builds the generator, the oracle's cases in the same commit as the method (amendment A-P4-59) and the validation method's mirror of G12.15. G16, G16.5 (G2.1's second walk, the row sequence and the sort) and which rungs form L0 are lane MBC's. Named, not L0's: on columns without an L0 block the division and lift above stand as today, and everywhere G5.3b's high tail piles its rows on its derived end (993 cells on a value the real column never held, at 100,000 rows), with the shape inside a band they cost (`mode_count`, `n_distinct_values`, `field_widths`, the tail distances): lane G2T's, G5's statistics lane. Today's workbook writer writes a record holding nothing as a row with no cells, so formatted blank records read back absent (`validate` exit 3, three `workbook.cell-classes` misses at 120 rows, reported as nothing given up): lane LM2's, the reader and writer remainders, for twins without stage 6.

**Repair round 1** (2026-10-19, both skeptics of 8aa98356): the measurements and their cause corrected; `hi_p`; item 3a; the workbook reservation by class; K-S6-02 (iv) and (v); G12.15's extension beside a cut in place of a whole unit; case 4's eight ranks; the half counts never printed. Each is pinned by `tests/test_l0_method_page.py`, red on the page at 8aa98356 and on its mutant.

**Repair round 2** (2026-10-19, the lane's verify of 0147e236 and the outside review of that head, REJECT). G4.2b hands over four things a cell, a workbook cell's class (with its format kind and date or clock kind) among them, fixed before the arrangement for the cells holding text too, and G2.2 step 7 writes each arranged cell by it, never by classes dealt again in row order. G7A.4d's half count subtracts only the other stretches before the edge, a boundary never on its own (28 and 72, not 27 and 73), and its knots name the index `i_j` and the percent `q_j` apart, both in G7A.4's units. G7.5's absent-spelling step on dates and G7A.4's on clocks without `clock_step` search only the rank's piece, else rule B1. (P3) reads the widest named width's grid and a piece holding no point of the column's grid is read on a finer named width's (the piece grid), so a real column of tenths beside a band of hundredths keeps L0. G4.3 reads `S` without L0, so a lowered or raised `M` moves no later column's words. Item 3a takes the widest ELIGIBLE gap, so no stratum is ever empty. A label column's cells are banded by their level, never their text, and withheld levels' cells lie in `other`. A text file's reserved rows are the first `E_eff` targets. G14.3a gains cases 14 to 16 and parts of 7, 9, 10, 11 and 13; each item is pinned by `tests/test_l0_method_page.py`, red on the page at 0147e236 and on its mutant.

**Repair round 3** (2026-10-19, the lane's verify of 11dd0b6b; the orchestrator chose its fix (B), so every published within-column fact stays held). (P3) holds on every description a producer writes except where a band's or a piece's cells were all written at widths the census counts into its commonest width (each written by fewer than `parsing.census_floor` cells, P4-D221 and P4-D222); such a column can fail (P3), and where it does it is made without L0 under rule B3 and named. **A stated limit, owned by lane BT**, which may lift it later with a measured cost: measured on the profiler at 11dd0b6b, a 400-row column of 20 cells at each of 0.1 to 1.0, 40 cells from 1.01 to 1.09 written ten each at two, three, four and five figures, and 16 at each of 1.1 to 2.0 publishes `fraction_widths` {"1": 400}, p50 1.005 and p60 1.094; every band holds 16 cells or more, and the band between those two holds 40 real cells and no tenth, so the column is made without L0, as today, and its band totals are not met (G14.3a case 17, expected outcome B3). The other fix, extending the piece grid past the named widths, would let `fraction_widths` give way under rule B1 and was not chosen. G5.7d item 3a now says a gap holds at least one free point (case 16 (b): no gap eligible, `M` lowered by one). Both are pinned by `tests/test_l0_method_page.py`, red on the page at 11dd0b6b.

## Decision P4-D405 — a number tail meets its own description on big tables: the shared staircase, rule 4 on a crowded end, and the windows rule 4 draws (stage 4 lane G2T of the December plan, 2026-10-19)

**Why, measured on 36ad3061.** Three within-column misses, one root. (a) Lane B0's 250,000 x 50 table of bells at two places missed every column's published spread by about 12 per cent (`validate` exit 3, 50 obligations); (b) at 1,000,000 rows G2's dense tail missed the column's mean, skew and kurtosis (P4-D377's stated limit), and at 200,000 and 300,000 rows its mean, skew and both tail distances; (c) counts of few values held 194 and 188 of their 200 high-tail rows on the derived end, past the source's largest (lane BTp's point 4). The cause is `contract._tail_steps` (G5.3b's grid staircase): every row of a fitted tail took its own grid point, the next one out where its reading landed on the last, so a tail of `m` rows on a grid stood over at least `m` points -- 100,000 two-place bell readings published a low tail of 1,000 rows at a mean distance of 1.76 and the staircase and the twin stood at 5.03, spread 4.3 per cent high; and every window being drawn through the same staircase, `validate` named nothing below 250,000 rows. On a dense column the staircase crowded its end and `contract._dense_grid` then read no dense side, so rule 4 left it; where rule 4 did place it, G12.3's windows still read the staircase.

**The change** (method G5.3b, G5.1a, G6.6.8 rule 4, G12.3, G12.13; product, oracle and method together, A-P4-59). (1) THE SHARED STAIRCASE: on a column that repeats its numbers (at least two cells a number), on a grid, where the pushed staircase stands more than half a step past the published mean distance, no shared row reaches the one field width the census names (a figure short where a pad is published) and G6.6.8's rule 1 moved no end, each row stands at its own reading, rows on one point sharing it, the outermost on the end and every zero on a nought end (`contract._shared_steps`, `_end_rows`). (2) THE SPREAD FOR THE COUNT: where the ladder's points between the boundaries, estimated rung segment by segment, and the tails' points fall short of `n_distinct_values`, each shared side pushes its fewest outermost rows inside the end one point apart, the shortfall shared in proportion to what each side can gain (`contract._spread_for_the_count`); without it G5.2a divided the longest run and G6.5a's walks moved the body (visits' ones 1,119 against 4,477). (3) RULE 4 ON A CROWDED END: rows held together on the derived end no longer stop a side being dense (`contract._dense_grid`). (4) THE WINDOWS RULE 4 DRAWS: on a dense side the four moments' windows and the tail's root-mean-square window are the hull with those drawn through the ladder rule 4's placement reads (`contract.dense_placed`), in `taxonomy.windows_of`, `validation._tail_window` and the twin's report alike. No description byte moves; the arithmetic rule holds (`+ - * /` and whole-number steps, no new draw).

**Measured** (one process at a time, under `nice -n 10`, at load averages of 7 to 27). (a) Lane B0's 250,000 x 50 table (its `tables.py`, `numeric`), in two daytime windows of the shared slot: `validate` exit 0, nothing MISSED (lane B0 on 3d893032: exit 3, all fifty spreads), every spread WITHIN-BOUND at most 0.18 per cent off the published one (8.4 to 12 per cent there) and every window reaching the published value; `profile` 408 s and 558 MB, `generate` 1,092 s and 1,271 MB, `validate` 1,733 s and 697 MB (lane B0: 385, 789 and 1,500 s; side by side at 100,000 x 10 rows `generate` took 98.8 s on 36ad3061 and 101.2 s here). A two-place bell at 100,000 rows: spread 5.025 against 5.019 (5.235 on 36ad3061), tails 1.83 and 1.78 against 1.76 and 1.73 (5.0 and 5.1). (c) Lane BTp's table at 20,000 rows: one cell on each count's derived end (194, 188 and 158 on 36ad3061), `x10`'s `7` on 41 cells against the source's 56 (none), the counts' spreads within 1.0 per cent (27, 27 and 36), `delta`'s within 0.1 (8.7). A battery of thirteen invented shapes at 2,000 rows (two seeds), 20,000 (two) and 100,000 rows, 65 columns: mean spread error 9.1 per cent on 36ad3061, 0.46 here; columns more than 2 per cent off 33 and 1; tail mean distances more than 10 per cent off 46 and 8, all at 2,000 rows; twin cells past the source's own range 9,849 and 65; no column further off; `validate` named nothing on either tree, every window drawn through the staircase. (b) G2's dense tail: at 200,000 and 300,000 rows four misses on 36ad3061 (the mean, the skew and the tail's two distances), none here, the high tail's root-mean-square at 300,000 rows 19,281 against a published 19,306 (9,592 on 36ad3061); at 1,000,000 rows (`K-S4-21`, in a daytime window of eight minutes) `validate` exits 0 and misses nothing, where 36ad3061 missed the mean, skew and kurtosis (lane S4c's measurement, P4-D377): the twin's mean 3.4 millionths of the spread from the published one, its spread 0.1 millionths, its kurtosis 26 and its skew 3,273 millionths, its high tail's mean distance the published one and its root-mean-square 1,236 millionths off. The oracle reads every tail block of the battery and the fixtures as the product does (75 blocks, 94 shared sides).

**Frozen cases and goldens.** None moves: every reference vector, golden twin and the oracle's 27 vector files are the same bytes (`tests/test_generation_reference.py`, `tests/test_twin_golden.py`, `tests/test_numeric_reference.py`, `check_provenance`); no frozen case has a tail block the shared staircase reads. Tests changed with the method: `tests/test_stage3_tail_rule.py`'s staircase case reads the pushed staircase, which still keeps every row apart, and `tests/test_stage4_million_rows.py`'s dense case now calls a staircase crowding its end dense.

**Validation.** `validate` already flags a twin value past a published end (`ladder.max (heaped end, one-sided)`, MISSED on a probe of 3,000 counts heaped at `100` with one `150`); a derived end is the construction's, not a published fact, so a value past it is K-S4-20's count, not a check. Nothing changed in `validation.py` but the window above.

## Decision P4-D406 — on a table of several rows a person, every published value is counted in persons, but the rungs and tail boundaries of a measurement or code column not attached to its subject, still judged in rows (lane HX2 of the December plan, 2026-10-19)

**Title amended 2026-10-21 (batch 4e's records; push critic 11's MAJOR 4, after Codex's review of the integration, I4e).** It read "every published value is counted in persons". The rungs and tail boundaries of a measurement or code column not attached to its subject are still judged in rows (the orchestrator's ruling of 2026-10-19, item 2; the paragraph on such rungs below): on `K-S3-14`'s repeated-measures table `synthtwin profile` publishes two rungs of a score, each on 11 rows of 10 people. The rule is unchanged.

**The finding** (measured on lane HX's head 5793f7b0; P4-D401's stated limits, the orchestrator's ruling of 2026-10-16 15:20 item 6 (b) and `wave6/HX-tripwire.md` item 3). The floor -- every printed count nought or at least the smallest group size -- counted ROWS, so a value one patient holds on fourteen rows passed it. Beside a declared person column a plan number `XKH#########` and an account number `ACC########` were published (71 of 132 and 72 of 128 values at 600 rows, 139 and 137 of 150 at 20,000; 19,929 and 19,886 real twin cells), and beside a patient key whose person question is open, a name, a street address and a full birth date were. Several rows per patient is in scope (TRACKED T2).

**The rule** (`profile._counted_in_subjects`, `profile._layouts_in_subjects`, `taxonomy.with_census_in_people`, `profile.subjects_holding`). Where the table has a SUBJECT column -- a person column declared or answered (`settings.person_columns`), or every column a question offering `identifier` holds while it is open (the person question's candidates, and a key another identity question holds, such as a patient number padded with zeros that the codes-or-measurements question is put to: skeptic 1's second round, item 1) -- that repeats, each subject cell read with its spellings merged (`profile.subject_keys`: folded, ASCII marks and the zeros opening a run of figures dropped, so `REC-0007`, `rec7` and `Rec 7` are one person; round 2 item 6), each value the description of any other column publishes is counted in DIFFERENT subjects under every subject column at once, read back off the column's own block: level names and spellings, rungs, percentiles and quantile points, mode, tail values, prefixes, examples and the words of its sentences, by text, as a number (an affixed number by its figures) and as the block's date; so is every written form its `shape_forms` names, its present rows as a whole and the remainder of rows that read as no published value (the count the floor merges and prints). A value held by one to ten subjects under any subject column may not be published: in a column ATTACHED to that subject (one value a subject, at most one repeated row in ten differing) or a column of dates or times of day, whatever its rows; in any other where at least the floor's number of rows hold it and it stands off the rungs and the tails' boundaries; the present rows and the remainder wherever the floor's number of rows hold them. Under a subject column of fewer than the floor's number of values every value is held by fewer subjects, so only a column attached to it that tells its subjects apart (`profile._names_its_people`: no one value the first met for more than half of them) is counted there: the names and birth dates of ten or seven patients are held, and a filler code of seven values put the person question blanks no date, label or measurement beside it (the orchestrator's ruling of 2026-10-19 15:42 item 3). A column that would publish one is described as a held record number, the block lane HX gives a column whose identity question is open (no level, rung, mode, tail value or prefix; the census its counts imply; its name in `settings.forced_identifiers`), with its own evidence (contract NF126); a record number's layouts that one to ten subjects wear join the `(withheld)` pool before C6-131b's whole-census rule (`taxonomy.layouts_counted_in_people`), a subject column's own layouts are counted in every OTHER subject column (round 2 item 3: a plan declared beside the patient), and the pool -- every cell no named layout takes, printed or left to subtraction -- is counted in subjects too: while one to ten hold it, the named layout the fewest wear joins it, and a pool still short names no layout at all (round 2 item 4); the twin writes made-up values in its layouts, the screen names the columns, and no answer gives such a value back. A table whose subject columns are each different on every row, or that has none, is described byte for byte as before: the count never runs there (gate case 2), and a library call without `subjects` (the validator's, K-S3-14's) is unchanged.

**Why not each value alone** (measured). Writing a withheld value's cells as blanks and describing the column again kept the rest of its values, but the description then said the real table held blanks it did not, and `synthtwin validate` failed the real table against its own description; and the points along a range of a measurement on a long table of few patients kept landing on values few patients hold (a lab column of 20,000 rows over 44 patients was blanked whole after four rounds). Holding the column keeps the real table meeting its description but for the held census (below), at the cost of every value of a column that would publish one rare value; pooling such a value into the floor's remainder inside each reading, in subject units, is a change to every census of the taxonomy: lane PS (pool in subjects), stacked on this lane's head (the orchestrator's ruling of 2026-10-19 15:42 item 1, which accepted the whole column held for this landing).

**The rungs of a column not attached to its subject (the lane's call, accepted by the orchestrator on 2026-10-19 15:42, item 2, for measurement and code columns only).** The literal rule counts every published point, and the points of a measurement a patient holds on a row or two are values one to ten subjects hold on any long table of few patients: 1,415 such points over K-S3-65's batteries and the zoo, `literal` in K-S3-65, every one also published on a table of one row a person, where the floor publishes rungs whatever their rows (the owner's decision 3 of 2026-09-15, which kept the ladder). So a column not attached to its subject keeps its rungs and tail boundaries as the floor judges them; an attached column (a birth date, a name, a plan number) counts them. No measured leak reopens: K-S3-64's held and counted shapes read 0 and the gate's cases are attached. A column of DATES OR TIMES OF DAY is a Safe Harbor element attached to an individual's rows whatever its rows (a visit, admission, discharge, diagnosis or death date), so it counts every point it publishes as an attached column does (`profile._counted_in_subjects`, `dated`; gate cases in ISO and US spellings).

**The census of the person column** (the BC v2.3 second check; contract 5.3, I2; accepted within one column by P4-D363). COUNTED IN PEOPLE for a DECLARED person column (`taxonomy.with_census_in_people`; restated by the third repair, Codex's items 1 and 6): an entry of at least eleven people is published as it is; the entries of fewer are pooled, the smallest entries kept joining the pool until it holds eleven people or more and can be spread with no entry of fewer than eleven (`taxonomy._floored_spread`: the even spread, or a few people moved a row down or one or two up, a fixed function of the people and rows it spreads), and the pool is spread so. What is published is always a census the twin can deal into the layouts and that prints no real group of one to ten people (`taxonomy._census_safe`), the first of: that spread beside the kept groups where the pooled people can be dealt into the layouts' parts beside the groups kept where they really are (`taxonomy._spread_meets_layouts`, exact for one size or two a row apart, each part's least share possible); each part's pooled people spread over its own pooled rows (`profile._census_parts` reads each part's real census); the census the block's printed counts imply (lane HX's, `taxonomy._even_parts`), floored part by part, or as it is where no entry of it equals a real group; each part's people moved a few rows off the even spread until none does (`taxonomy._safe_by_parts`, the case of a column whose rows past one a value are fewer than eleven, where every census that closes has a small entry); and last, no layout named and every person spread over every row. A census the printed totals force (every value on one row, or all but one) is published as it is. That a census was moved off the even one tells a reader the even one was real: a reader combining the method with printed counts, which the owner's rulings accept. A candidate of an open question, or a subject the count held, keeps the census its printed counts imply that `as_unanswered_identity` gives it (P4-D401), and a person column's own layouts are counted in the OTHER subject columns, not in its own people (stated limits 5 and 6 below). `redcap`'s census {1: 122, 2: 293, 3: 133, 4: 117, 5: 85} is published whole; the real table misses `distinct.n_distinct_by_occurrences` only where a pool is spread.

**Reuse** (lanes MG and GR, item (b) below). `profile.subjects_holding(values, subjects, floor)` counts, for one column's cells and a subject column's cells in row order, each value's rows and at most `floor` different subjects (the subjects read with their spellings merged, `profile.subject_keys`; a blank subject is one subject between its rows), one pass, memory one entry a value (the product counts the values a block publishes through the same core, `profile._holding`); it reads any two lists of text, so it runs on lane SR's `reading.column_values` (P4-D400) unchanged.

**Measured** (the build on adcd58f; its first repair, after skeptic 1's `wave6/HX2-sk1.md`, on 58baa8b, logs in `wave6/HX2/r1/`). Gate `tests/test_stage4_counted_in_persons.py` (39 cases): the seven counted shapes at 600 and 20,000 rows publish 0 real values and 0 fragments, 0 twin cells, every twin validates, and the real table misses only a census spread from a pool; two candidates in either order; a remainder of three patients and a column written for two (held); the written forms of a held name and of two patients' own codes; a census of groups of eleven and more published whole, a pool of three of two sizes and a pool spreading back into its real groups; a size attached and not; visit dates and times of day in ISO and US spellings; a filler code of seven values beside dates and an all but constant region (nothing held); byte identity where no subject column repeats. Twenty-two mutants, each red on the commit its log names (`mutants*.log`): rows for subjects, the first or the last candidate only, a subject counted twice, the remainder or the present rows judged in rows, the narrowing to candidates of eleven values, layouts or forms not counted, the census not counted or its pool under the floor or spread back into real groups, attachment never or at one row in two, dates not read again, prefixes, words of sentences and mapping keys not read, dates and times judged as measurements, and a candidate of few values counting dates or any attached column. `K-S3-64` (restated through its checklist): 0 over 49 held and seven counted shapes at both sizes; the three stated read 214 values and 61,559 twin cells as before. `K-S3-65` (new, exact, PRIVACY): 0 values in scope over 75 tables with the healthcare catalogue on the path (58 on the tree alone); recorded, never failed, the values withheld that the row floor alone publishes -- shapes 667, people 80, catalogue 232 -- and out of scope (`literal`, the points of measurements one to ten patients hold) 829, 282 and 201 after the dates were counted; one catalogue twin misses its forms through the generator's stated limit, counted apart. Description batteries (the suite's 128 files under `wave6/HX2/r1/hx2_census_plugin_r1.py`, which also counts each described table with the counter, `wave6/HX2/r1/census/`): 250 describes with a subject column over 18 files, 0 in scope; 16 descriptions change -- 13 person censuses pooled in people (`test_landing_2b18_identifier_layout.py` 10, `test_p1r7f2_withholding_block.py` 3), `test_cli_profile.py`'s `recorded_on` and `seen_at` (a date and a time beside a declared key, 14 values), `test_p4d341_population_floor.py`'s `site` and `score` (87) and `test_stage3_review_sentences.py`'s `grade` (2) held -- and all 16 twins validate (the build's four form misses are gone). The catalogue at 2,000 rows unanswered and answered the zoo's way (`zoo-cost-2000-final.log`): held `icd10_dotted`, `result_value` and `result`, `weight`, and the date and time columns `collected_at`, `taken_at`, `recorded_at`, `consent_date`, `service_date`, `ts`, `study_date`, `in_room`, `anes_start`, `incision_time`, `case_duration`, `dx_date`, `first_treatment_month`, `created_dttm` and `death_date` (twelve unanswered, fifteen answered: ruling item 2's price); 13 answered person censuses pooled; one new twin miss, the generator's (stated limit 4). False candidates (route four, `false-candidates.log`): income in whole thousands, one row a person, holds the visit dates at 600 rows (10 values; the question about income is open) and changes nothing at 20,000; daily steps at 200,000 rows change no column (61.3 s against 60.4 s). Scale: see the second repair below.

**Second repair (skeptic 1's second round on 815f714a, `wave6/HX2-sk1.md`; 2026-10-20; logs in `wave6/HX2/r2/`).** (1) A key held by another identity question is a subject: the CLI passes every column it holds until answered, not the person question's candidates alone. ## Decision P4-D407 — between columns, the chain's method page: floored family tables drawn with a private key, written before any code (lane MBC of the December plan, 2026-10-19; supersedes P4-D394)

**Why.** The owner, 2026-10-16: "I want the between columns relation to be really broad! ... People will make regressions, people, will train models, people will try to make all type of relation ... and we should be prepared for develop the code and have stable statistical results." The broad between-columns design was chosen over three candidates by two judges, attacked three times and checked three times, and ratified for this page by the orchestrator on 2026-10-19 for the TABLE layer, one row per patient. Its rulings, which this page applies: R1, a count of 1 to `f - 1` (1 to 10 at the default floor) leaks when the whole description fixes it or bounds it inside that range; R3, read possibilistically, over every table some draw with an unknown key could have described the same way; R4, the reader knows which columns hold a value at most once per patient; R5, the draw's temperature 2, provisionally; R6 as amended 2026-10-18, the draw keyed by the installation's key, the table's name and the step, the ledger refusing one table under two names or two keys; R7, the owner's answers to question 12 (change over visits in December; the private report carries both grades and advises which twin to use); R8, the patient layer's open items are lane MG's and the moments' lane MPOL's. The orchestrator's rulings of 2026-10-19 (12:14) on this page's first build: RULE W1 read against the other column's coarsest level, member by member and across the chain, is confirmed; case (ii) of Lemma 3 is confirmed as R1's reading (a count equal in every world to a fact the column publishes about itself adds no exposure, provided W1 fixes no band of any other column for that group); R3 read through a model of the key (keyed BLAKE2b words as independent draws, a reader searching the key space outside the promise) is confirmed; `L0` is aligned to the ladder lane A0a measured. Its addendum of 14:11, on lane MR's price: cite the measurement by a dated sentence, state the price, treat MR's candidate partition as optional, and name scipy as the implementation route.

**What is written (specified, NOT BUILT; no product code changed).** Contract section 4.6b: the ladder (O1), the chain and its complete family tables (O2, O3), slopes (O4), structural words and names (O7, O8), the carried rules' entries (`rules`), the two reports, the content hash, the search's offers (rules W3 and NE), the draw (rule W5) with its stated exponential, the installation's key and ledger, rule words, the rule step and row 9's one test with its computable sufficient form, derived columns as the child of one family, the proofs (Lemmas 1 to 4), `K-S6-08`'s preimage and fixtures, invariants S23 to S28, the dispositions, the promises and stated limits, and the settings. Generation method G16.0 to G16.2, G16.4 to G16.6 and G16.8 to G16.12; G16.3 (lane MPOL) and G16.7 (lane MG) are reserved. Validation V12 for the chain, with six mutants. Invariant S12 stands until stage 6 ships whole. `tests/test_chain_method_page.py` holds what the review round fixed, since no code exists to run.

**P4-D394 is superseded.** M6's page, held at `b762720c` and never merged, published every pair's table; every pair's table forms loops, and loops give away counts of 1 to 10 that every printed cell clears (measured by three candidates independently). Its numbers 4.6a, S15 to S22, G15 and V11 stay unused. Its clauses that hold are restated where used: eligibility with a constant column of variable presence, tabled rows, the coefficient rule (for slopes), the hidden scores, the walk without its rake, cells inside bands, the empty-record reservation (now lane BTp's).

**What the proofs cover, exactly (the design's promises, the floor read as `f`).** For a table with one row per patient: no count of 1 to `f - 1` fixed or bounded by the description's tables, levels, placements, anchors, rule words, structural words and names, for a reader without the key, given one description per table and name on an installation; proven for the published numbers (contract 4.6b.9 (a), a self-contained construction), for the procedure through the draw lemma ((b), under the stated model of keyed BLAKE2b), for each column's own small groups under RULE W1 ((c), case (ii) as ruled), for a carried rule's class over its base (4.6b.7's sufficient form) and, for an order rule carried by a derived difference, over the whole description ((e), Lemma 4), and for the census of records holding nothing beside the tables (RULE WE, the Corollary of (b)); the carried rules' rows 9, 9b, 10 and 14 on one PRECONDITION, open until lane MR's page proves it: MR's inference conditions implied by the base, the class and the antecedent bound, so that every table a carried description allows opens the same rule step (Lemma 2). Checked, not proven, each named in (h): the slopes, the moments, the patient layer, the straddle count, a derived column's pinned order statistics, a carried rule's class beside the chain's families for a source carrier or a formula rule and beside its base columns' finer own facts, several rules sharing a column, and the pseudorandom property. Not promised: a Bayesian reader (on the third attack's B1 table a uniform prior puts 0.891 on the small range, 0.625 from the numbers alone; likelihood ratio up to 324, and at most `m` times `2**30` a step, `m` the step's eligible options); several descriptions of one table (14,532 of 52,373 description pairs leak under two keys in the exact model at f = 11; 136 of 29,018 under one name for two tables; 88 of 7,165 single descriptions with the words known); case (ii)'s reading (stated limit 3: six rows with days 0 shown to have type A or C); the moments and the slopes' values (lane MPOL); the patient layer (lane MG). Statistics (the design's study panel, measured before this page, for the chain together with lane MPOL's polish): 63 per cent of supported estimates inside the yardstick at 20,000 rows under every check (a fresh sample 68); 10 points behind a fresh sample at 50,000 rows under version 2.1's rules, and 21.5 at 100,000; "stops drifting" withdrawn; `K-BC-01` at 200,000 rows failing until lane A0b finds the cause. The chain alone, on lane A0b's 50-column panel without the safety rules: 171 of 273 (63 per cent) at 20,000 rows and 141 of 280 (50) at 50,000. Hours (JUDGEMENT, the design's 7.2 to 10.2 re-priced by this page's statistics review with measured prices: the chain search 177 s at 200,000 x 50 with exponent 1.23, about 30 to 50 minutes at 2,000,000 rows over every tabled row; the polish 19.5 to 28.4 µs a proposal with the second code; the self-test 11.6 minutes a 50,000-row panel): 2,000,000 x 50 in about 7.3 to 10 hours on Python 3.13; the first build's figure for Python 3.10 (about 7.3 to 11.2 hours with the design's two other savings and the self-test sample at 200,000) no longer applies, since lane DEP-1 makes 3.11 the oldest Python synthtwin runs on (the owner, 2026-10-19, 19:00), and 3.11 is not yet measured; less with the 100,000-row sample, which the constant `selftest_sample` now allows; the level variants and RULE W1's full check are not priced.

**Where this page departs from the ratified text, each by measurement or by proof.** (1) RULE W1 is read at the other column's coarsest level, member by member and across the chain (confirmed 12:14; lanes A0b and CHa count its refusals). (2) `L0` is the deciles with `p25` and `p75`, which is lane A0a's measured `dec` ladder (its 10th, 20th, 25th, 30th, 40th, 50th, 60th, 70th, 75th, 80th and 90th percentiles). (3) The walk's latent order carries no cell mean. (4) A derived column's value bands hold at least `max(2 f, f + 4)` rows, so the floor's bound holds at floors below 4. (5) Stray rows holding nothing after the arrangement are given cells only by ineligible columns that no carried rule computes or reads, never by the row sequence, or named. (6) The content hash is unkeyed BLAKE2b over parsed cells keyed by column name, summed over rows. (7) Order rules and formula rules are carried by a drawn step whose "not carried" is always eligible, and row 9's one test reads the rule's BASE, the facts published whether or not it is carried: the design's "description without the rule" holds the computed column's own facts, which a carried rule withholds, so a decision read on them would not be a function of the description it is published in. (8) A derived difference is published only as the child of one family `{D | A}`, `A`'s `missing` band a band of its own, its structural zeros printed as cells, every cell floored, RULE W1 holding and, in a count class, its level cut at 0 floored; a computed column publishes its name, its place and its role only, every other key `null`, `{}` or `[]`, words such as `integer_valued` included. (9) The ledger records a digest of each whole published description (less its run stamps), holds a lock from reading the ledger to writing the description, and refuses a different description of the same table unless the person declares, with `--replace-description`, that the earlier one was never shared; `--new-key` is accepted only where the key file is lost. (10) V12 prints no measured number on any line but a slope's, judges every family against its published table (it computes no moved table), and lets a verdict stand only where every band total of its columns holds and the published table is eligible on the file's own description; a slope's standard error uses the inverse of the parents' cross-product matrix, with its singular cases defined. (11) The weights' raises are read on the score's own scale, `w n`. (12) RULE WE: a root pair is eligible only where the cell bound of the combination blank in every eligible column is at most the rows the census of records holding nothing and the other columns allow. (13) RULE W1 is checked in full at every step. (14) A source carrier and a formula rule take the phrase only, a source carrier only where its difference publishes `n_negative` 0; count classes belong to derived carriers, whose failing rows the generator places. (15) A root "no family" beside a carried rule gives the rules-only description, every eligible column without a parent at `L0`. (16) A family's target in generation reads the twin's counts of its parent cells, not its members' totals alone.

## Decision P4-D408 — the questions file keeps every answer across rounds (lane AQ of the December plan, 2026-10-19)

**The finding** (lane E0a, P4-D399, on 68dae22f; push critic 9's MAJOR M1 (a), owner named by the orchestrator on 2026-10-19). A person who answers the questions file in two rounds lost the first round's answers: the file the first `--answers` run wrote held only the questions still open, so `us_vitals`' patient column, answered as the person in round one, read as an affixed number after round two, and `diagnoses_procedures` lost its encounter key and a SNOMED `code` answer. P4-D401 then kept the answers to questions offering `identifier`, and on its close (fa89ed59) every other answer was still lost: over the zoo's 25 tables and the gate's eight cases (100 answers, four tables answered over rounds), 14 answers lost, 21 files differing between one round and several, one run failing (the build's 20 was read before the gate gained its case of codes in dates) (`titled_report`'s answer about the row of the names lost, so its record-number answer named a column the table read without names did not have); a table raising nine kinds of question lost the order of day and month, a point between thousands, a column of dates and the codes standing for a missing date; and the two runs the refusal of a reading answer beside column answers asks for put the second run's `identifier` on the subject codes, because the second run read the table the old way.

**The rule.** (1) The file every run writes carries, under `answered_before` beside a sentence saying what it is and the column names its answers use (`column_names_these_answers_use`, the names that run read the table with), every answer that run acted on -- from the file, from an earlier run's `answered_before`, from the screen, or typed (`--code`, `--identifier`, `--measurement`, `--decimal-comma`, `--twelve-hour`, `--date-column`, `--date-count`, a `--century` window, the standing window typed as `--century NAME=1969` and kept as `1969-2068`, `--day-first`, `--delimiter`, `--first-row`) -- written from the declarations in force, what a column holds and how its numbers are written each in an entry of its own, the file's own subjects first and then the table's column order, so the same answers given in one round or in several write the same bytes; an answer about codes in a column of dates is kept by the codes' own words, which every round finds alike, and not by its question's counts, which the order of day and month moves. Not written: a blank entry keeping its reading (its question is put again, as P4-D401 puts it), a typed `--metadata-rows` (the file asks to confirm it, and writing it as an answer would confirm it for the person), and `--keep-value` or `--missing-value` (values; the file carries none). A run given no answer writes its file as before. (2) A kept answer stands until a later one replaces it -- another answer written in the kept entry, an answer in the same file about the same column, or a declaration typed on the command line, `--first-row auto` included -- and a later answer replaces a kept one only on a dimension where they really conflict (narrowed in the third round below from any two questions offering a common answer): where the later answer decides the kept answer's family (a typed declaration decides its own family alone; an answer in the file decides every family its question offers an answer of other than `keep`), or where the column cannot hold the two at once (a counted date beside `code`, `identifier`, `measurement` or `twelve-hour`; a comma beside `code` or `identifier`; `twelve-hour` beside `code`). A comma beside a measurement and a comma beside a counted date stand side by side. A kept entry left blank keeps its answer. (3) A kept answer about how the file is read stands for the reading the run that wrote the file took (its `read_as_now`), so handed back as it stands it moves no name: the refusal's two runs now end where the two answers typed at once end. A run that would read the table another way -- the kept entry edited, the question answered again, or `--first-row` or `--delimiter` typed otherwise -- while the file names any column, kept or fresh, refuses and writes nothing; so does a run whose reading gives other names than the file lists (the kept entry deleted, or another table). (4) A run that would drop a kept answer -- one naming a column the table does not hold, or one another answer contradicts -- refuses in plain words before anything is written. P4-D401's hold is unchanged: a kept `identifier` is a declaration, and a kept `keep` releases what `keep` releases.

## Decision P4-D409 — the dependency page: the December library set on Python 3.11 and later, and five zones in which no library float decides a byte of the twin or of anything published (lane MDEP of the December plan, 2026-10-19)

**Why.** The owner, 2026-10-19 about 09:50: "One important thing, we don't need to just use Numpy and Pandas! If the solution goes through other libraries, we can and we must use them. The principle is that it should be offiline withouth AI and in python! Otherwise, we are free!" With the working rule the owner was given that day: any offline Python library is allowed and must be used where it measures better; no AI service; no neural network trained on the real table in December (the generator still reads only the published description; such networks stay allowed elsewhere, as in the test batteries); and synthtwin ships as a fully offline, pinned, hash-checked bundle, the owner's choice. About 19:00 the owner chose Python 3.11 and later, the light native-format conversion as a stretch, and numba "Yes, gated". Five library studies measured the candidates on invented tables of up to 2,000,000 rows on one Mac (`planning-notes/work-2026-10/lib-study/`, summarised in its `LIB-PLAN.md`); every number below is theirs or a probe of this decision's own review, on the same Mac. This decision writes the rules the libraries enter under. It changes no product line, dependency, lock, scanner table or rule file: lane DEP-1 builds the mechanics and lane DEP-2 the bundle (part 7), each citing this decision, and until DEP-1 merges today's scanner (pandas reduced to `read_csv`, numpy to the one seeded draw) binds every lane.

**1. The library set for December.** **Python 3.11 to 3.14**, and 3.15 once CI can run it. Five of the libraries below need 3.11 or later at their current versions and their last 3.10 versions are frozen (numpy 2.2.6, scipy 1.15.3, pandas 2.3.3, pyarrow 25.0.1, scikit-learn 1.7.2); the bundle is 351.7 to 468.3 MB a platform for 3.11-3.14 against 443.8 to 586.4 MB for 3.10-3.14; the test matrix goes from 55 jobs to 45; and the pure-Python parts of the between-columns design ran x1.43 to x1.87 slower on an older Python (3.9 as the stand-in). Who loses: a person whose only Python is 3.10, such as Ubuntu 22.04's default. Shipping an interpreter inside the bundle is lane TT's study, decided at the 2026-11-06 checkpoint. Every pin is exact and is DEP-1's lock; the versions measured were numpy 2.4.6 (3.11) and 2.5.4, pyarrow 26.0.0, scipy 1.18.1, pandas 3.0.6, numba 0.68.0 with llvmlite 0.50.0 (which needs numpy below 2.6), pyreadstat 1.3.6, statsmodels 0.15.0, scikit-learn 1.9.1 and openpyxl 3.1.5.

**Not adopted, with the measured reasons.** polars: errors on a valid `a"b` field, splits a file of lone carriage returns wrongly, and peaked at 1,736 to 1,885 MB at 500,000 rows. duckdb: no better than pyarrow, a quantile rule that differs on one column, and it can install extensions from the internet unless switched off. python-calamine: drops number formats, error cells, the absent, blank and empty classes and the person's spellings (`2.50` read as 2.5, `1E-3` as 0.001), and holds the whole sheet (killed at 1.93 GB at 524,288 rows); it would change the published descriptions of existing workbooks, against the twin writing each spelling as the source wrote it. xlsxwriter: writes `0.1+0.2` as `0.3`, `2**53+1` as `9007199254740992` and a carriage return as `_x000D_`, and was slower than the standard library's streaming writer (3.93 against 2.68 s at 20,000 rows). lifelines: Efron ties only, and it pulls matplotlib, pillow and autograd, one of them source-only. networkx: the chain is a junction tree by construction, and the standard-library check takes 0.046 ms against 5.2 ms, both right. statsmodels in the product: a GLM holds about 13 times its design (1,451 MB at 200,000 x 50; 3,177 to 3,666 MB on the battery's panel), and it fits without a word what the kit correctly refuses (a rank-deficient design, quasi-separation, groups of one row). numba for the generator's draws: under 1 % (0.848 to 0.006 s of a 138 to 189 s column).

**2. The byte-identity zones.** Today generation uses Python integers, + - * / and sqrt on floats and one random stream, the twin is the same bytes on Python 3.10 to 3.14, Windows, macOS and Linux as far as the reference vectors on every CI entry and the minimums job show, and no published statistic comes from a library's float reduction. Today's code also reaches the platform's `pow` through `**` on a float in eight places of zone-G modules (part 3 (a)): three `(spread[first] * spread[second]) ** 0.5` in generation's pair walk, its margin `0.5 * 10.0 ** (-parsing.RANK_AGREEMENT_PLACES)`, the rank agreement's `** 0.5` in `parsing`, and in describe's calendar choices `(1.0 - 1.0 / points) ** parsed` twice (`calendar_clock.lattice_crowded`) and `** 2` (`calendar_rules._per_freedom`). No standard requires `pow` to round correctly (P1-D11), and this Mac's does not: `x ** 0.5` differs from `math.sqrt(x)` on 2,672 of 2,000,000 random doubles, `x ** 2` from `x * x` on 2,609 of 2,000,000, and the calendar's power from the correctly rounded one on 58 of 50,000 pairs, each by one last bit; `10.0 ** -4` and the exact powers of two (`2.0 ** 40` and the like) agree. The vectors have matched on every system so far, which proves the vectors, not the rule; these eight are a stated limit owned by lane DEP-1 (part 3 (f)). The reason is P1's finding at its review round 1 (P1-D2): numpy's reductions made the published mean depend on the order the rows arrived in, and overflowed or underflowed at the ends of the accepted range. A float reduction is not promised to add in the same order across builds, processors or thread counts, so the same table could publish different bytes on two computers, or after a shuffle of its rows. Every product module sits in exactly one zone:

| zone | what it decides | allowed | forbidden | why |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **G**, generation | any byte of the twin | Python integers; numpy arrays of explicit dtype, combined only inside the audited helper of part 3 (c) and (e), whose run-time checks keep every elementwise integer operation equal to Python's (one dtype, never unsigned beside signed; every operand and result proven in Python integers below 2^63 in magnitude (below 2^64 and never negative for the uint64 multiply-high), and below 2^53 wherever an integer meets a float or a true division; a failed check takes the plain-Python path), the exact multiply-high by 32-bit limbs among them (measured byte-identical at 2,000,000 rows), and elementwise float64 + - * / and sqrt in a fixed order; `default_rng(seed).integers` exactly as today (E7, E8); `take` and indexing; Arrow string arrays as storage; a numba kernel of the same operations behind its CI gate (part 4) | an integer operation outside those checks (numpy's int64 wraps without a word; part 3 (e)); float reductions (`sum`, `mean`, `dot`, `@`, `cumsum` on floats), transcendentals and float powers (`exp`, `log`, and `**` or `pow` on a float, whatever the exponent, but an exact power of two; measured above), BLAS and LAPACK, anything from scipy or scikit-learn, `pyarrow.compute` on floats, numpy random distributions other than `integers`, unstable sorts, threaded kernels, numba with fastmath, parallel or cache | the twin must be the same bytes from the same description and seed everywhere; IEEE 754 rounds + - * / and sqrt correctly on every machine, and promises neither a reduction's order nor a transcendental's or a power's last bit |
| **D**, description and shared report | any published byte, and any choice of a published object (the chain search's score, the screen's seeds offered to the chain's draw, the few-rows rule test's verdict) | integer-exact numpy under zone G's checks, inside the same helper: `bincount`, `unique`, elementwise integer operations, int64 `@` with its overflow bound checked first (n x 254^4 is about 8.3e15 at 2,000,000 rows, below 2^63, about 9.2e18); float `bincount` weights only where every weight is a whole number and every partial sum stays below 2^53, so that every sum is exact; float scores that only choose a published object, never a published value, built only from + - * / and sqrt in a fixed order over cells indexed by code, never over rows (a margin over four cells written `a0+a1+a2+a3`), or summed with `math.fsum`; HiGHS only as the search of part 5, its every exhibited arrangement re-checked in Python integers | numpy and BLAS float reductions, scipy statistics, any library float that decides a published byte; any float accumulation over rows; transcendentals and float powers (`log`, `exp`, `lgamma`, `erf`, `**` on a float), numpy's or `math`'s, wherever they decide a published byte or choose a published object: a score that needs one is compared exactly (in integers or `fractions`) or computed with `decimal` in a fixed context, whose `ln` and `exp` are correctly rounded | P1's finding above: a description must not depend on row order or on the computer; `math.log` and numpy's `log` each differ from the correctly rounded logarithm on 4 of 50,000 values here, and another system's library may round other values otherwise |
| **P**, private report, tests, batteries | the custodian's judged grades and advice, the self-test's fits, every test | any adopted library and platform floats (numpy IRLS, scipy Cholesky, HistGradientBoosting), with BLAS and OpenMP held to one thread, as every fit was measured | feeding G or D; byte goldens across platforms on these outputs (tests compare them within tolerances) | nothing generated or published depends on it, the person who runs synthtwin sees everything (the owner, 2026-10-18), and fast fits make the self-check affordable: 75 to 113 minutes of fitting at 2,000,000 rows to under one, projected |
| **R**, reading | how cells are read | pyarrow, and pandas while it is kept, configured by the product's own survey of the file, their cells compared cell for cell or by per-column digest with the standard-library reading, as `reading._check_against_pandas` does today | any library as the authority on the written form; a library's exception text, which is file content, on validate's path, and on the profile path any more of it than today's refusal quotes (`reading._unreadable_in_the_check` prints the library's words under `REFUSALS_MAY_QUOTE` and drops them under `REFUSALS_NAME_POSITIONS`; measured, pyarrow's parse error quotes the whole offending row, where pandas' C parser quotes no cell) | every library tested differs somewhere: Latin-1 and UTF-16, ragged rows, blank lines, a trailing delimiter, duplicate names |
| **W**, writing | the twin file's bytes | the standard library's writers (lane XW's streaming writer reuses today's element functions); zip bytes across zlib builds stay today's stated limit | xlsxwriter (it changes values, measured); a writer that stamps its version or a clock into the file unless that is fixed (Parquet names its writer; SPSS, Stata and XPORT headers carry a write clock, 3, 1 and 12 bytes) | the twin writes each spelling as the source wrote it (the owner, 2026-09-15) |

**pyreadstat is a conversion step outside zone R.** No standard-library reader exists for .sav, .dta, .xpt or .sas7bdat, so pyreadstat could only be the authority on the written form, which zone R forbids. Under the owner's T4-lite (Q2 of 2026-10-19, recorded as "synthtwin converts .sav/.dta/.xpt/.sas7bdat to CSV with value labels applied"), it converts the file once, for .sav, .dta, .xpt or .sas7bdat, with value labels applied, to a CSV, written by the standard library's writer, that the person keeps; that CSV is the source zone R reads and the twin mirrors. Applying labels changes the cells the CSV, and so the twin, carries (a code written as its label); which cells they change is lane NF0's decision, and .sas7bdat is unmeasured in the studies. So the analyst develops on the converted CSV of the real file, and code that reads the .sav directly will not run on the twin. The conversion's bytes depend on the pinned pyreadstat (LIB-PLAN 1.3); lane NF0's decision cites this paragraph.

**P1's "imports numpy nowhere" is reversed for integer-exact use only.** P1-D2 withdrew numpy from the profiler, which "now computes its statistics itself under the rules in P1-D11, using only `math`, and imports numpy nowhere". Describe (zone D) may now import numpy for counting that is exact on integers, as the table states; every published statistic that is not an integer count keeps P1-D11's rules unchanged: nothing accumulated in floating point, exact whole-number sums, each result rounded correctly once at the end, no `**`. A fixed-order float sum is allowed only in a score over a table's cells indexed by code, which chooses a published object and is never published itself, never over rows: 1,000 floats added one by one in file order and again shuffled gave 166554291223.89157 against 166554291223.89148, where `math.fsum` gave 166554291223.89166 both times. P1's finding stands: what is reversed is the blanket ban, not its reason. What is given up: in zone P a judged word near its threshold in the custodian's private report, including the advice on which twin to use, may differ between two computers (D-L1); the size of that difference is unmeasured, every fit was measured on one Mac with one thread, and for a trained model it can be a different split, not a last bit. Nothing in G, D, R or W may change a byte. CI proves G by the reference vectors on every operating system and Python and on the minimums job, and D by the goldens; every new kernel has so far been measured on macOS arm64 alone.

**3. The scanner's zone rule** (lane DEP-1 enforces it in `tools/offline_scan/scan_imports.py`, each rule with a mutation case red in `tests/test_offline_scan.py`, 134 tests today). (a) Zones by module. The twin's writers (`synthtwin.rendering`, `synthtwin.sheetwriting`, `synthtwin.writing`) are zone W and admit no library. The generation path is every other synthtwin module that they, `synthtwin.contract` and `synthtwin.generation` reach by import, walked from the source as `tests/test_contract_loader.py` walks the loader's closure, so a new module joins on the commit that imports it; it is zone G and imports only zone-G APIs, even where describe reaches it too. Reading modules are R and the private-report and self-test modules P, each named in one scanner table entered with its lane's plan decision. `synthtwin.cli` and `synthtwin.__main__` are a dispatcher zone: they may import every zone (`cli` imports 18 synthtwin modules today), compute nothing that is generated or published, and hand zone P's output only to the private report's writer. Any other module is held to zone D. (b) The generation path reaches no zone-R or zone-P module (P2-D1 already keeps the reader out of it), no module of G, D, R or W imports a zone-P module, and a computation that chooses anything published is zone D wherever it is written. (c) Every library name is admitted one at a time with its capability audit (`_ALLOWED_MODULE_ATTRS`, `_KNOWN_MODULE_PATHS`, the result-method tables) and its zone, as `_MODULE_SCOPED_ADMISSIONS` scopes `zipfile` and `expat` today. Where the dtype decides (a reduction is exact on integers and not on floats), the scanner cannot see it, so such names are admitted only inside one audited helper module that checks the dtype and the overflow bound at run time and refuses otherwise; the helper is zone D's, and a zone-G module reaches it only by a plan decision naming it, under which the helper keeps its zone-D admissions, recorded in the scanner's table, rather than becoming zone G by (a). ctypes, cffi, subprocess and multiprocessing stay forbidden in src, and so do joblib, `pyarrow.flight`, `pyarrow.fs` and every entry point that takes a file system or a URI. (d) Argument rules: scikit-learn's `n_jobs` is forbidden (joblib can start process pools); a pyarrow reader is handed only a path that has been through `synthtwin.paths.validate_local_path`, as `pandas.read_csv` is fenced today, and `use_threads=False` (one thread read 500,000 x 20 in 0.27 s); HiGHS (`scipy.optimize.milp`) runs with its output silenced, `mip_rel_gap` 0 and its budget in nodes (`node_limit`), never in seconds (no `time_limit`), so a computer's speed never enters what it answers; HiGHS starts native threads of its own (measured: 1 thread before one `milp` call and 5 after it, with `OMP_NUM_THREADS=1`, and they persist), which zone D accepts because part 5 makes every verdict exact whatever HiGHS answers, and lane DEP-1 records them in SECURITY.md's thread statement and measures their memory; numpy's `sort` and `argsort` in G and D take `kind="stable"`; numba appears only in the one polish-kernel module, only as `njit(fastmath=False, parallel=False, cache=False, error_model="python", boundscheck=True)` with every keyword written (`boundscheck=False` only where lane MPn's decision shows every index proven in range by part 4 (vii)'s check, with the measured cost of the other choice), and no other numba name (no `prange`, `vectorize`, `cfunc`, `objmode`, `config`). (e) Operators. Today's scanner returns the library array for any operator on it (`scan_imports.py`'s operator branch), so `@` and `**` pass unseen: measured on the one draw form in `synthtwin.generation`, `arr @ arr`, `arr ** 0.5` and `arr + arr` give 0 violations each, and `arr.sum()` is refused. The scanner sees no dtype, and numpy's integer operators do not keep Python's integers (measured, numpy 2.5.4): int64 wraps without a word (2^62 x 2 gave -9223372036854775808 against Python's 9223372036854775808, and a sum past 2^63 the same); a uint8 254 squared is stored as 4; uint64 + int64 is computed in float64 (2^53 + 1 plus -1 gave 9007199254740991 against 9007199254740992); `/` on two int64 arrays rounds each operand to float64 first (it differed from Python's correctly rounded `x / y` on 4,961 of 20,000 draws with x from 2^53 to 2^62); `//` by 0 gives 0, and -2^63 // -1 gives -2^63, where Python raises or gives 2^63; and an int64 2^53 + 1 compares equal to the float 2^53. So in G and D every operator with a library operand (+ - * / // %, unary minus, `@`, `**`, the shifts and bitwise operators `<<`, `>>`, `&`, `|`, `^` and `~`, the comparisons and the in-place forms) is written only inside the audited helper of (c) (the polish kernel's compiled code is held instead by part 4 (vii)'s checks), whose run-time checks make it exact or refuse it: all operands of one explicit dtype, int64 or float64, or uint64 for the multiply-high by 32-bit limbs alone, never unsigned beside signed (narrower storage such as 1-byte codes is widened to int64 first); for integers a bound computed in Python integers from each operand's exact minimum and maximum, proving every operand and result below 2^63 in magnitude (for that uint64 kernel, at least 0 and below 2^64), every shift count from 0 to 63, and a left shift's result inside the same bound, and below 2^53 wherever an integer meets a float, a true division or a float comparison, as part 4 (vii) states for numba; no zero divisor; `@` and `**` on integers only (a float `x ** 2` is written `x * x`); a failed check refuses or takes the plain-Python path, with the same bytes. That check costs 1.2 ms beside 1.9 ms for the product itself on two arrays of 2,000,000 int64 (both operands' minimum and maximum; the median of 7 runs). Elsewhere in G and D a library value is used as today, by `int(...)` on each element, which ends its origin. Builtin `sum()` and `functools.reduce` over a library array are refused in G and D (`math.fsum`, exact and order-free, stays allowed). In G and D modules a float literal on either side of `**` (`x ** 0.5`, `10.0 ** k`) is refused, except a base written `2.0` or `2` with an integer-literal exponent, an exact power of two, which a faithfully rounded `pow` (one that returns a neighbour of the exact value) returns exactly, measured exact here for every exponent from -1074 to 1023; no transcendental (`log`, `exp`, `pow`, `lgamma`, `erf`) joins `math`'s enumerated names or numpy's admitted names there; any other `**` on a Python float is the reviewer's check, beside P1-D11's, because the scanner sees no types. Each rule has its mutation case: a float `@` in a G module, `arr ** 0.5` in a D module, `math.log` in a D module, `x ** 0.5` in a G module, an int64 product `arr * arr` written outside the helper in a D module, `arr << k` outside the helper in a G module, and `2.0 ** 52` in a G module admitted. The helper's own tests, required before any lane adopts it, take every boundary above: an int64 product and a sum past 2^63, a uint8 square, uint64 beside int64, an int64 `/` above 2^53, a zero divisor and -2^63 // -1, int64 1 << 63, a shift by 64, and `~` on unsigned storage, each refused or computed with Python's bytes. (f) Today's exceptions. Today's five exact powers of two in zone-G modules (`contract.py`'s `2.0 ** -50` and `2.0 ** 40`, `generation.py`'s `2.0**52` twice and `taxonomy.py`'s `2.0 ** 53`) are admitted by (e) and are not exceptions. **4. Principle 3, restated for one audited kernel.** CLAUDE.md's principle 3 says the product code holds "no native-code calls, no dynamic code loading". Restated (DEP-1 writes it into CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and SECURITY.md): the product code holds no construct that initiates network I/O, no subprocess, no native-code call of its own (no ctypes or cffi) and no dynamic code loading or code generated at run time, except one audited module, the polish kernel, which numba compiles in memory from that module's own source under the gate below; it accepts only local filesystem paths and works fully air-gapped. The libraries' own native code (numpy, scipy, pyarrow, llvmlite) is answered by exact pins and hashes in the bundle, as numpy's and pandas' is today, not by the scanner. The gate: (i) DEP-2's numba vector job runs a whole multi-pass schedule (every pass, every column) of the polish reference table under numba AND under the plain-Python polish on every operating system and Python of the matrix (the studies compared only the first 200,000 to 300,000 proposals of a run), and one differing byte fails the CI gate job, so lane MPn is not adopted while any does; (ii) the plain-Python polish (lane MPg) is the oracle and the fallback, mirrored in `tools/reference` under A-P4-59; (iii) a twin is the same bytes with or without numba installed, which changes the time only; (iv) the kernel is reached by a plain import inside its module, and numba's absence selects the fallback; `cache=False` writes no file, `parallel=False` starts no thread, and `fastmath=False` allows no fused multiply-add (the studies' FMA probe differed by 0.0); (v) Intel Macs, which have no numba wheel, run the fallback and stay supported while CI has an Intel runner (D-L2); (vi) numba's own settings are lane MPn's to close, by `NUMBA_*` environment variable (`NUMBA_BOUNDSCHECK` among them, which overrides the decorator) and by a `.numba_config.yaml` in the working directory, which numba 0.68.0 reads at import (without pyyaml it prints a warning to stderr, which changes what a command prints; with pyyaml every key becomes a setting): when either is present, numba is not imported and the fallback runs, unless MPn's decision admits a variable measured harmless on the reference table. (vii) numba's integers wrap and its indexing is unchecked where Python's are not; measured with this decorator, an integer sum past 2^63 gives -9223372036854775808 against Python's 9223372036854775808, a true division of two integers above 2^53 gives 3002399751580330.5 against 3002399751580331.0, an index past the end returns memory content where Python raises IndexError, and the polish's own formula on integers below 2^40 differed on 0 of 20,000 draws. The studies' equality rested on a bound measured on invented data (code sums far below 2^63, at most 4.3e10 at 2,000,000 rows), not on a check. So before each call the kernel module checks, in Python integers, the bounds lane MPOL's arithmetic note proves: every integer the kernel forms stays below 2^63 in magnitude, and below 2^53 wherever an integer meets a float, a true division or a float comparison; every index is proven in range by that check, or the decorator keeps `boundscheck=True` (part 3 (d)); a failed bound takes the plain-Python fallback. The vector job adds a case past each bound and shows the fallback taken with the same bytes.

**5. The MILP direction rule.** HiGHS searches the integer arrangements of rows the published facts allow, for the between-columns design's two exact tests, whose quantifiers no search may change. Joint-space WIT (BC-ARCH 2.5 (v2.2), inventory row 24): a column's moments are published only if, for every (cell, code) group g of its joint space, some arrangement consistent with every published fact puts at least f rows on g, or else g is in V-, the groups for which none does, and one arrangement puts 0 rows on every group of V- at once; otherwise none of them is published. Row 9's one test (lane MR's price, 1.2): an outcome class K is clean only if one world of K puts 0 rows on every joint cell whose largest value over K is at most 10, and the rule's partition publishes only if every class is clean. Neither test asks whether some arrangement holds a group of 1 to 10 rows, and such an arrangement is no reason to refuse. Codex's instance, from its review of this decision, at f = 11: two joint cells A and B of 100 rows over codes 0, 1 and 2, each with code sum 100, and the column's code counts (50, 100, 50) allow exactly the 51 arrangements A = (t, 100 - 2t, t), B = (50 - t, 2t, 50 - t) for t from 0 to 50; every group reaches at least 50 rows, so WIT publishes, yet t = 5 holds groups of 5 and 10 rows (measured by enumeration; asked for a group of 1 to 10 rows, HiGHS exhibited (10, 80, 10) and (40, 20, 40), which the earlier wording of this part would have refused). Lane MPOL carries it as a required reference case of WIT, published, with that query as its mutant, which refuses it. The study's wording of this risk ("no arrangement with a count of 1 to 10 exists", LIB-PLAN section 5) is read by these quantifiers. The two kinds of claim are not alike. That an arrangement exists (g reaches f; one arrangement zeroes V- or a class's small cells; a class is not empty) is proven by an arrangement, exhibited by HiGHS or by the exact route, that Python re-checks in integers against every published fact (368 of 368 re-checked exactly in the studies). That none exists (no arrangement puts f rows on g; a class is empty) is proven only by the exact route: a closed form evaluated in Python integers, or the exact pure-Python oracle (lane CHo); HiGHS's "infeasible", a reached node budget, an error or a non-integer answer proves nothing. HiGHS is handed integer data with `mip_rel_gap` 0, as lane MR ran it (`milp` exposes no feasibility tolerance, and this rule makes the tolerances irrelevant to what publishes), and a node budget. The verdict is the deterministic exact route's: before any search, a rule in Python integers on the instance's sizes decides whether it lies in the class the exact route always decides within its budget (a closed form's conditions, or a joint space the oracle covers in its integer steps, both stated by lane CHo's decision with their measured time), and an instance outside that class is refused whatever any search finds; inside it the test's value is unique, so HiGHS may only reach it sooner, its re-checked arrangements proving the claims that exist while every absence the verdict rests on is decided by the exact route. So every published verdict is the test's exact value or a refusal fixed before the search, the same on every computer, and with an unbounded budget it is the test's value everywhere. This is the reading this decision takes of the study's "publish on HiGHS's no only where an exact closed form or the oracle confirms it at that size": a confirmation at a size class is evidence about the solver, not a proof about the person's table, and a verdict resting on a tolerance or on a search's luck could differ by platform. (Lane MR's 768 outcome classes at 20,000 and 200,000 rows were decided by worlds HiGHS exhibited and Python re-checked in integers: exact proofs on one Mac, but whether HiGHS finds them within a budget can differ by platform, and a class HiGHS alone called empty was declared clean. MR's model was checked against enumeration on 986 small configurations.) Under this rule MR's 24 published rules at those sizes (row 9's one test on the emergency, lab and stay tables, which the MBC addendum of 2026-10-19 cites) need to lie in the exact route's class or they refuse: they are the first case to re-price, and lane MR measures that price before MBC's ratification cites them. A class that HiGHS alone calls empty never decides which partition publishes. Publishing on arrangements HiGHS exhibits and Python re-checks for an instance outside the exact route's class would be exact and never leak, but HiGHS's search, its floats and its budget would then decide publish against refuse by platform; it is not adopted here and needs the orchestrator's ruling. Its price, an instance outside the exact route's class, is a refusal where the test would publish; lanes MR, CHa, MPOL, MPp and MG measure it in refusals and state it, and nothing else refuses where a test publishes without a decision stating its measured statistical cost. An exact infeasibility certificate re-checked in Python fractions would be a further exact route; it is not adopted here and needs its own decision.
