## Decision P4-D410 — the libraries' mechanics: Python 3.11 and later, four runtime libraries pinned and held to their zones by the scanner (lane DEP-1 of the December plan, 2026-10-19)

**Why.** The owner, 2026-10-19 about 09:50: "If the solution goes through other libraries, we can and we must use them. The principle is that it should be offiline withouth AI and in python!"; about 19:00, "3.11 and later (Recommended)" and, for numba, "Yes, gated (Recommended)". P4-D409 (lane MDEP) writes the library set, the five byte-identity zones and the scanner's zone rule; this decision builds them, as P4-D409 part 7 asks. No product byte moves.

**The change.** `pyproject.toml`: `requires-python = ">=3.11"`; the runtime set numpy, pyarrow, scipy and pandas at the floors the floor Python installs (numpy 2.4.6, pyarrow 26.0.0, scipy 1.17.1, pandas 3.0.6), each with its justification and zones; numba 0.68.0 as the optional `polish` extra, its marker leaving Intel Macs out; one mypy override for the untyped libraries. The three locks are compiled again for 3.11 exactly as before (`uv pip compile --universal --generate-hashes`, the wheel-only line put back): 3.12 and later get numpy 2.5.4 and scipy 1.18.1; the development lock adds statsmodels 0.15.0 and scikit-learn 1.9.1, test-only, and numba; no lifelines. `tests/test_dependencies.py` holds every floor equal across `pyproject.toml` and the three inputs, the extra and its marker, the libraries this landing does not adopt (lifelines, polars, duckdb, calamine, xlsxwriter and networkx, which P4-D409 measured and did not adopt, and pyreadstat, which P4-D409 part 1 adopts for the native-format stretch and which enters only with that stretch's own decision), in no file and each lock's floor Python. The offline scanner admits, one name at a time with its capability audit, `pandas.set_option` (one option, one value), `pyarrow.csv`'s reader and three option classes, `scipy.optimize.milp` with `Bounds` and `LinearConstraint`, `scipy.linalg`'s Cholesky pair and `numba.njit` in `synthtwin.polish_kernel` alone; everything they return answers to nothing until the adopting lane enters a name. The zone rule is P4-D409 part 3: the generation path is computed from every line's imports of the generator, the loader and the three writers; the writers are W, reading and workbook R, the kernel G, nothing yet P, every other module D; a library runs only in its zones, a G or W module may not even import a library its zone does not admit, G and W modules import no R module, and only P imports P. The argument rules: pyarrow's reader takes a validated local path and `ReadOptions(use_threads=False)` written in the call, never a row handler or memory pool; `milp` takes `'disp': False` and a `node_limit`, never a `time_limit`; `njit` is only the decorator `njit(fastmath=False, parallel=False, cache=False)` over a top-level def, and the function it makes is called and nothing else; `n_jobs` is refused on every call, as a keyword and as text; numpy's sorts take `kind='stable'`; llvmlite and joblib join ctypes and cffi as forbidden. `reading.read_table` sets `mode.string_storage` to `python`, the storage it had before pyarrow arrived. `synthtwin doctor` and `python -m synthtwin` ask for 3.11, and doctor names each runtime library's version. The CI tests matrix runs 3.11 to 3.14 (45 jobs where 3.10 made 55) and the minimums job 3.11 with `requirements-min.lock`, its suite reproducing the reference vectors at numpy 2.4.6. The install scripts' floor check asks for 3.11. CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, SECURITY.md and README carry principle 3 restated, the zones and the dependency protocol.

**Measured** (`planning-notes/work-2026-10/wave6/DEP1/`). Byte identity: 29 tables (the health data zoo's 25 and four fixtures) at 2,000 rows profiled, generated with seed 7 and validated in one process each: all 203 files and all 87 command outputs equal on b075342a in today's environment (Python 3.13, numpy 2.5.1, pandas 3.0.5, no pyarrow), on this head there, on the floor environment (3.11, numpy 2.4.6, scipy 1.17.1, pandas 3.0.6, pyarrow 26.0.0) and on the 3.12-and-later pins (numpy 2.5.4, scipy 1.18.1), once the version stamp and the run's folder are set aside; the twin, description and vector goldens (1,744 cases) pass on all three. Reading 500,000 rows by 20 columns with `read_table`, seven interleaved runs each on a loaded machine (load 10 to 19): today 12.66 s median, peak 464 MB (388 MB above the start); this head on the new pins 12.62 s, peak 480 MB (380 above the start: the 16 MB is pandas loading pyarrow at import); without the setting (the mutant) 15.03 s (+19 %) and 507 MB (406 above). The test of the setting is red on that mutant on both venvs, and each of nineteen scanner rules removed in turn turns its cases red. No KPI.

**Stated limits.** The offline bundle, the install scripts' bundle defaults and their "numpy and pandas" messages, the notices and the numba vector job are lane DEP-2's; numba enters the install lock only with lanes MPn and DEP-2. The reading times are from a loaded machine; `read_window.sh` in the notes repeats them in one window on a quiet one (a night script). The development environment `synthtwin/.venv` holds neither pyarrow nor scipy, so doctor's tests fail there until they are installed. `K-P0-09`'s name and rule still read two libraries while its pinned node asserts four, and STATE's CI row still names the 3.10 floor: the integrator's. pandas' option is process-wide, set by the reader, the one module that uses pandas.

**Repair 1 (skeptic 1 and the statistics skeptic, 2026-10-20).** numba's dispatcher carried its compiler settings and its uncompiled body, and `propose.targetoptions['fastmath'] = True` scanned clean and compiled the kernel with fast-math (skeptic 1, numba 0.68.0): the kernel module's decorated top-level functions are now called and nothing else, there and in every module that imports them, and `njit` compiles a top-level def alone. `import pandas`, `scipy.optimize`, `scipy.linalg` and `pyarrow.csv` scanned clean in the twin's writers: a W module now imports only what W admits. `g(**{'n_jobs': 2})` scanned clean: the text `'n_jobs'` is refused wherever it is written. Three cases cover the zone rule's untested parts (an import inside a function, a relative import, a draw in zone D); the comprehension-scope cases name their pandas module `reading.py`, so none is red or clean for the zone's reason (one was red on every venv since part 4); the string-storage test records the storage at every call of pandas' reader, so a setting written after the checking pass is red; CONTRIBUTING asks for 3.11, held by a test of every page's stated floor. Each of thirteen mutants turns its own case red (`repair1/mutants-r1.log`). LIB-PLAN's 1,903 against 1,070 MB is a whole frame turned into lists (its probe calls `.tolist()` on every column, which with pyarrow storage builds a new Python string for every cell): at 100,000 rows of the same table, 494 MB without the setting, 287 with it and 261 today (the statistics skeptic's measurement; pandas 3.0.6 against 3.0.5 is not the cause); `read_table` reads 32,768-row pieces, where the mutant costs 26 MB more growth, and the setting covers the whole-frame fallback too. ## Decision P4-D411 — the workbook twin is written as a stream, byte for byte as before (lane XW of the December plan, 2026-10-19)

**The fault** (the library study, `lib-study/LIB-formats.md` and LIB-PLAN 3.1; a product defect, no library). `sheetwriting._sheet_part` grew the sheet as one text, `text = text + f'<row r="{number}">' + line + "</row>"`, a copy of the whole sheet for every row, and `writing.write_workbook_file` handed every part to `writestr` whole. The study's stand-in was killed by its 1.9 GB guard at 19,999 x 50 after 44 s and at 100,000 x 50 after 51 s; on the real call at 1,000 to 8,000 rows of fifty columns the writer took 0.43, 1.04, 2.87 and 8.38 s at a peak of 106 to 910 MB (`wave6/XW/out-growth-real-call.log`).

**The change, which moves no byte.** `_sheet_pieces` makes the same elements in the same order, a row a piece. `workbook_stream` makes the table's sheet twice: the first pass gives every text its shared-string place (the table is written before the sheet) and counts the sheet's UTF-8 bytes; the second is made as the zip writer takes it, refused if it meets a text without a place. `write_workbook_file` takes (name, size, pieces), tells each member its size before the first piece and writes each piece into `ZipFile.open(entry, "w")`, so zipfile chooses `writestr`'s header (zip64 only past zipfile's `ZIP64_LIMIT`, 2**31 - 1 bytes, over 1.05: about 2.045 billion bytes) and madler's zlib (1.2.12, every Python here) writes the same deflate stream however its input is cut; a part whose pieces are not its size is refused. Forcing zip64, as the study's prototype did, adds 20 bytes to every member's header, so it is not done. `workbook_members` joins the pieces for the method's goldens. The offline scan admits the member writer as its own surface, `write` and `close` only, traced in `writing` only (zipfile itself is admitted to `reading` too). No library (xlsxwriter changes values, measured).

**Measured.** The same bytes on all 31 workbooks `K-S4-22` compares (the five G2.2 goldens, the battery, the zoo's `surveys.xlsx`, a seeded 50-column table) and at 1,000 to 8,000 rows on the real call, where today's takes 0.46 to 4.05 s at 99 to 114 MB. A 100,000 x 50 sheet of 177 MB is written with 0.34 MB traced as held, each pass traced whole; the whole route writes 20,000 and 100,000 x 50 in 12.2 and 63.1 s at a peak of 145 and 357 MB (K-S4-22, 2c031ff; 8bb691c read 13.6 and 68.1 s at 146 and 357 MB), loaded (recorded). Gate: `tests/test_workbook_stream_writer.py`, red on a row copied twice, two rows swapped, a member not told its size, a sheet handed over whole, and `_package` holding the second pass before the zip writer sees a byte (`list(second)`, `("".join(second),)`).

**Stated limits.** The twin's cells and the package's per-cell classes and formats are still one Python tuple a column each, about 2.6 MB a thousand rows of fifty columns: lane SG's (finished columns as Arrow arrays). 1,048,576 x 50 is the night window's (`wave6/XW/night-1m.sh`). The shared strings and the other small parts are still built and held whole, with a UTF-8 copy counted and another written: they grow with the table's distinct text, not with the sheet, so a text-heavy table's peak still holds about twice its distinct text. Zip bytes across zlib builds stay the stated limit of plan P4-D79.

**Repair 1 (skeptic 1, 2026-10-19).** (1) The version guard names the frozen writer's two `exec(compile(...))` routes (`tests/test_version_reach.py`; CI was red on every cell without them). (2) A gate case drives `workbook_stream` and `write_workbook_file` on the wide battery twin: one pass of the sheet made before the zip writer, the second handed on unmade and drawn whole; the two mutants above, made in `_package`, are red. (3) zlib-ng (CPython 3.14 on Windows, a CI cell; distributions shipping zlib-ng-compat) need not write the same deflate stream for a text cut elsewhere, and no Python here links it, so it is not measured: there the gate and `K-S4-22` compare the packages member by member (names in order, every central and local header field but the compressed size and the offsets the zip64 field carries, each text) and assert the bytes only on madler's zlib; the check is red on a moved date, attribute, method, text or order. (4) The member writer is traced in `writing` alone; placed in `reading` it is refused. (5) `K-S4-22` records the memory before and after the parts are made: 135.3 MB before, 357.1 MB once made and at the end of the write at 100,000 x 50, so the write adds nothing (restamped on 8bb691c, loaded).

**Repair 2 (skeptic 2 and Codex's review, 2026-10-20).** (1) Past the zip64 line the zip64 field carries the compressed size (local and central) and the offset (central), which move with the deflate stream: the member comparison keeps the field's id and uncompressed size, drops the rest, and where a field holds the offset alone compares the version numbers as raised to 45; two gate cases (the line lowered with the package deflated at level 1; an offset past the line in one stream only) are red with the field compared raw, and with zlib-ng emulated (only the streamed sheet deflated at level 5) the gate is green, where repair 1's comparison was red on its zip64 case. (2) The memory case starts `tracemalloc` before each pass is called: a pass listing every piece on its first piece (Codex's mutant, green under repair 1's window: 62,504 bytes held against a bound of 85,876) or on the call, or joining them, is red; the clean pass holds 0.34 MB of 177 MB, the zip writer's buffers, the same at 10,000 rows. (3) `K-S4-22`'s driver records null memory where `resource` is missing (Windows), pinned by a gate case red on the unconditional import. (4) The zip64 line is stated as zipfile's `ZIP64_LIMIT` over 1.05, here, in `sheetwriting` and in `writing`. (5) The Measured paragraph gives K-S4-22's stamp.

**The largest size, recorded and never judged (batch 4e's integration, 2026-10-21).** 1,048,576 x 50 ran in the orchestrator's night window of 2026-10-21, 00:25 to 00:30, at load 1.76 to 2.12, on dd9eeb9f, under the guard (`planning-notes/work-2026-10/wave6/XW/out-night-1m.log`). The sheet alone (`--sheet-only`): 1,916,057,234 sheet bytes in a 210,854,746-byte file, the first pass 54.86 s and the write 71.89 s, 1,351.6 MB at its peak (1,088.4 MB before the sheet). The whole route (`--size`: `workbook_stream` and `write_workbook_file` on a real twin) was stopped by the guard at 1.9 GB after 152.8 s (1,856 MB sampled), as the script expected: the package's per-cell classes, formats and cells are one Python tuple a column, lane SG's (finished columns as Arrow arrays). `K-S4-22` keeps its 100,000-row stamp; this size is recorded here only.

## Decision P4-D412 — between columns, the patient page: several rows per patient written before its code, the visit trend and the derived parents first (lane MG of the December plan, 2026-10-20)

**Why.** The owner, 2026-10-16, answering whether several rows per patient comes into scope: "a- Agree to address that"; on 2026-10-18 (ruling R7 of the December plan): change over visits is in December ("Bring into December"); on 2026-10-20 at 08:37: "Let's adopt visit-trend method for december". The broad between-columns design (version 2.3, third repair) was ratified for its TABLE layer on 2026-10-19 (P4-D407); its patient layer was left to this page by ruling R8: the patient-fixed column's row census decided once from the description without it (R8 (1)), and the every-count argument for the patient rows of the inventory (R8 (2)). The orchestrator's ruling of 2026-10-20 on the visit-trend study: method B version 2 adopted; December reads the within-patient correlation at 100,000 rows under `K-BC-06`'s clause (4), 0.07; clause (5)'s two misses are stated and owned by the January stretch item "the ICC inside its yardstick at 100,000 rows"; `Q` is published, never `S` exact; the long-table correlation is this page's to state; lane GR owes a gate case forcing a two-exchange close.

**What is written (specified, NOT BUILT; no product code changed).** Contract section 4.6c, `relationships.grain`: the setting (patients, the patient table and its chain counted in patients, the grain family, types, the band and grid models, the one-world lemma); 4.6c.1, change over visits: the trend `Q_P` behind SWING, with its proof (the slice lemma, the sign-flip chain, the witness worlds keeping each cell's trend, the census tie, every count) and the within-column lemma stated; 4.6c.2, the derived first-date and own-mean parents, their allowed patterns, residual PWIT, the floored split, and the coarser offers that carry the within-patient correlation; 4.6c.3, the gate and the contract text by which `r`'s drawn census replaces the person column's repetition census, every other census of `r` and the unknown person; 4.6c.4, `r`'s census with its open top band, the FLOORED SPLIT at the tight cap (the excess rule for every excess) and the cap lemma; 4.6c.5, patient-fixed columns and R8 (1)'s rule; 4.6c.6, the KEY test and the position list; 4.6c.7, ordered dates by role and computed dates; 4.6c.8, the theorem in patient units (PWIT, `R*` with its tie, a patient union crossed with a type union); 4.6c.9 and 4.6c.10, the wire shape, invariants S29 to S33, the inventory rows 4 (MG's part), 15 to 21 and 35 to 38, `K-S6-08`'s patient cases; 4.6c.11, the promises and the stated limits. Generation method G16.13 to G16.17 (G16.7's reservation filled; the oracle's ten cases after the first repair and sixteen after the second, the two-exchange close among them). Validation V12.7 to V12.9 (seven more mutants after the second repair). Section 4.6b and G16.0 to G16.12 and V12.1 to V12.6 are not edited.

**Where this page departs from the design, each by proof or measurement.** (1) The excess check becomes one exhibited table: the top band's FLOORED SPLIT at the tight cap `ceil(q / m)`, which answers every union of extra values for every excess, and every cap a reader may know (the cap lemma), where the design checked unions only up to an excess of 18 and no cap. (2) The gate also asks for exactly one person column and no tabled row lacking a person value, so that `N` and the unknown person are published facts. (3) While the layer is on, every key of the person column counting rows is read over the patient table, and every repeating multiplicity map is withheld, since each is a census of `r` by another name. (4) R8 (1)'s one test is taken in its computable form: the row census is published only where it is a function of the description without it. (5) The own-mean parent takes the floored split (one exhibited world, patterns allowed for the band) in place of PWIT's round robin, which can deal a patient a pattern its own mean forbids; the first-date parent takes residual PWIT with the parent never pooled. (6) `R*` must tie to every published table holding `r`. (7) The position list ends before a repeated level and holds `null` where a modal value has fewer than `f` patients. (8) A carried rule's `D` is the child of a row family while the layer is on, since `{D | A}` would have a parent counted in rows. (9) The trend's draw rows are numbered 35 to 35d (the study called them 34 to 34d; 4.6b's row 34 is O8). (10) SWING reads a class whose sorted arrangement puts a band of one code with a wider band before it AND after it as reaching only its greedy maximum and its negative: the slice lemma's walk can stop at such a band, so its proof as the study wrote it held only without one (MEASURED, `fix_rigid.py`: no class of the fifteen fixtures has that shape, the fourteenth's one-code band being its lowest, so they read 1,516 passes and 0 leaks under `Q` as before; `ST2`'s two-band row families have none either, so its measured cells stand). (11) `R*` takes no value of `r` above the census's tight cap, so its world is a table under every cap a reader may know.

**What is proven, and what is checked.** Proven, for the reader of section 4.6b's promise and every true cap on `r`: in the band model, the gate (its "off" drawn on every table), the census, every class's own counts by its witness world, the position list with its `null` entries, ordered dates, every union of types under the certificate 4.6c.8 (a) assigns, and a patient union crossed with a type union under each certificate, for the patient chains 4.6c.8 (a) admits (repair 2); in the grid model, as a statement about that model, every union of types under the own-mean floored split and beside a published trend. Checked, not proven (each a `K-S6-08` case lane CHa owes): the within-column lemma for unions of types, the step from the grid model to the column's exact facts for the own-mean split and the trend alike (measured 0 leaks at the level of types over 163,755 SWING passes on all fifteen fixtures), the joint of a FINE or date column's own `L0` totals with its row family's coarser table, and an own mean's pinned order statistics.

**Repair 1 (2026-10-20, the page's first skeptic and its statistics review, `wave6/MG-sk1.md` and `wave6/MG-stat.md`; the orchestrator's rulings of 10:22 and 10:41).** (1) A class read on a threshold stands only beside a world that keeps it: a column the KEY test reads takes the floored split at its `L0` levels with `V` and `V_K` above `T` read from its patterns, or is drawn HELD (the skeptic's 330 leaks refused). (7) G16.14 deals the top band's excess grain cell by grain cell to the row families' totals. (8) The polish keeps every patient in its own-mean band. ## Decision P4-D413 — between columns, the moment page: numbers read finer than the bands, published only where an exact witness holds, by a drawn step whose "publish none" is always open (lane MPOL of the December plan, 2026-10-20)

**Why.** The owner, 2026-10-16: the relations between columns must be broad, "people will make regressions ... and we should be prepared for develop the code and have stable statistical results"; and on question 9, 2026-10-19, asked for the most fidelity possible while "not allowing identification". The chain of plan P4-D407 carries the tables; correlations and least squares among number columns need numbers read inside the bands. Plan P4-D407 reserved them (contract O5 and O6, the word `pinned`, the list `withheld`, inventory rows 22 to 26, generation G16.3) for this page, which the design (BC-ARCH 2.3 r3, ratified for the chain 2026-10-19) asks to prove its items 1 to 7 in writing, each with its remainder named and `K-S6-08`'s enumeration at `f` = 11 as its check.

**What is written (specified, NOT BUILT; no product code changed).** Contract section 4.6d (lane MG's page beside it takes 4.6c, so this one takes 4.6d and invariants S34 to S38): region columns, their linear and second codes and their atoms; the classes `mean`, `spread`, `product` and `correlation`, published as exact whole-number sums; regions as connected subtrees of the chain's tree; one drawn step a region, its option `none` always eligible; the joint-space witness with its quantifiers exact, the exact route, HiGHS as a proposer, the closed form `CF1`; Lemmas 5 and 6 and Theorem 2; the two carriers; the arithmetic; `K-S6-08`'s fixtures; the invariants, dispositions, promises, stated limits and settings. Generation method G17: the polish that G16.3 reserves, its targets in the twin's units and its kernel's operation set. Validation method V13: the moment lines, report-only. `tests/test_moment_method_page.py` computes the page's cases.

**What the proofs cover** (contract 4.6d.5 (h), as repaired). Proven, for one row per patient, a reader without the key, one description per table and name: the drawn step tells nothing the numbers do not, and a refusal is uninformative at every size (Lemma 5); under premises (R) and (S) every witness point of a publishing region extends to a whole table of the preimage and the regions' points combine (Lemma 6); for every union of the full joint table's cells refined by the codes, some table puts at least `f` rows in it or none outside the small own-fact groups it wholly holds or (ruling R11) splits, and where it splits none and those are small atoms the count outside them is 0-able or reaches `f`, which is ruling R9's wording (Theorem 2 (A) and (B)), but for one exception; `CF1`. Premise (S), that every published slope stands in a publishing region and reads only its columns, is a premise on the whole description and, under ruling R10 (strict proof only), an eligibility test, so it holds for every published number; under ruling R12 a slope that stands is published only inside a publishing region, so no published slope stays checked, not proven. Checked, not proven: premise (R), that each witness point is met by readings keeping each column's `mean`, `std`, `skew` and written forms; Theorem 2's exception (i) (two small atoms of one region); the patient-layer combination where lane MG's argument (v) is not proven; the exact route's correctness; the keyed-BLAKE2b model; `B5`'s evidence for the design's witness.

**Where this page departs from the design, each by proof or by condition.** (1) A refusal is DRAWN, not decided by context: `none` is always eligible, so the refusal's preimage is the whole context's (Lemma 5), with ruling R3's residual as its stated limit; `M5`'s 0.95 test reads published sums and its rearrangement bound is left to the witness. (2) Sums are published as exact whole numbers, so the witness and the generator's targets read equations, not rounding intervals. (3) A region holds every node of each of its columns and the path of each correlation, so Lemma 6 needs no condition on how regions sit. (4) While the patient layer is on, no moment reads a repeated column and no correlation pairs a patient-fixed column with a repeated one (refused, not argued); lane MG's exclusive option between its trend and a row-level product moment never binds in December. (5) No moment reads a derived or computed column or a carried rule's column, so Lemma 4 of 4.6b.9 stands.

**The three inputs since the design.** (A) Codex's condition on lane MDEP (P4-D409, part 5; P4-D410): the witness's quantifiers are written exactly; the exact route decides every absence; HiGHS only proposes, with a node budget and never seconds; Codex's two-cell, three-code instance is a required reference case with the old query as its mutant (computed in the test file); no stricter rule is adopted without a decision and a measured cost; the one member of `milp`'s result the build needs is `x`. (B) The arithmetic note (lib-study `LIB-PLAN`, this lane's row): the polish kernel is `int64` sums and binary64 `dJ` in a fixed order with no fused multiply-add, with its bounds checked before each call so lane MPn may compile it; the self-test's fits are zone P (`D-L1`); every profile sum is integer-exact in numpy only inside MDEP's audited helper. (C) Continuous by binary interactions (lane `A0c`): the finer-band carrier publishes only chain families (Theorem 1 of 4.6b.9 covers it); measured once at its own weight of 1/20, where the laboratory value's own triple, ranked first, left it 43.3 SE off as with no seeds (146.5 at a weight of 1.0), and only with the built-in triples forced at 1.0 did blood pressure come to 0.275 of 0.296 (6.6 SE) while the laboratory value went to 93.2; the finer screen's ranking offering age x group x blood pressure (rank 10 of `fseq`) is measured, the chain run offering it is queued. The per-cell slope carrier publishes a parent cell's sums under the witness (Theorem 2; unmeasured: lane `A0c` names it JUDGEMENT). Both gated.

**Points for the orchestrator.** (i) Rulings R9 and R11 (2026-10-20) are applied: the 30-row union is accepted and clause (d) is a named option; a union that SPLITS a small atom's groups (by another region's atoms or a column of no region; skeptic 1's case across two regions, 1 to 3 rows, MEASURED) counts the atom's rows among its own facts, so it is no exception and the GATE no longer waits; option (b) is not adopted; within one column form (A) is the reading (15 rows, `n_zero` 6: 9 rows). R11's first wording, its option (a) read in place of clause (c), is NOT applied, because the verify of 2026-10-20 MEASURED that, inside ONE region, that reading accepts cases `Q` (exactly 3 rows of a cell at one code of a second column) and `S` (a union of 1 to 9 rows), counts of two columns that no column's own facts publish and that R11's basis (counts of one column) does not reach; the witness keeps clause (c), now read over every point, which refuses both and, on the verify's exhaustive search, nothing it held before. This reading was confirmed by the orchestrator as R11 AMENDED (2026-10-20): clause (c) stays, read over every point, and R11's option (a) applies only to unions that split a small own-fact atom. (ii) THE MAIN FIDELITY RISK before the stage-6 gate: as December decides the witness, it publishes almost nothing. A column brings every node holding it, so on lane `A0c`'s 200,000-row chain the means alone make ONE region of all 20 FINE number columns and 38 of 50 families (31 and 47 with the count columns); `CF1` excludes every column a slope reads, and every number column of lane `A0b`'s chain sits in a family with a number child and a number parent; with `witness` `"cf1"` only `none` is eligible there and `correlation` nowhere. Every polished figure was measured without the witness, and 127 (lane `A0b`'s chain without seeds or moments), 188 (that chain polished) and 202 (the seeded chain polished) are REFERENCE MEASUREMENTS, not bounds: the seeded chain without moments, December's chain, was never run (lane MPp measures it, or lane `A0c`'s queue first), and the yield with the witness on is unmeasured and has no stated bound, since a partial polish may lower the estimates it does not target; it rests on lane CHo's oracle class, or a closed form taking slopes and several `L0` bands a cell, deciding those regions; `M-a` carried 68 of the polish's 85 estimates at 20,000 rows and 28 of 35 at 50,000 in lane `A0a`'s ablation. Neither lever the review offered is adopted, each for a reason measured or computed: regions sharing a node cannot be glued without a lemma this page cannot write (three two-way margins with no filling, computed in the test file), and `mean` on interior bands or in one family leaves every number column of that chain under a slope. Lanes MPp and CHa measure the pooled count with the witness on (lane `A0b`'s table, lane `E0b`'s battery) before the gate; if the oracle cannot decide these regions at December's sizes, the loss goes to the owner. (iii) A slope where premise (S) fails is not adopted as a drawn option (the orchestrator's ruling of 2026-10-20, point 2); ruling R12 withholds it (repair round 3, below). (iv) The refinement node for the finer-band carrier is DEFERRED: that carrier delivered nothing at its own weight in its one run, so the amendment of 4.6b.5 and S24 the ruling allows waits for the queued run's gain. (v) Contract 4.6b.14's polish row (lane MBC's clause, not edited here) says `P` = 2 from 1,000,000 rows is lane `A0b`'s measurement; `A0b` measured 172 against 188 at `P` = 2 and 4, and that row leaves the polish's settings to this page, whose G17.1 now reads 4 at every size: the batch's integrator may align the row's words. DONE 2026-10-21 by batch 4e's integration: the row reads `P` = 4 at every size, lane `A0b`'s 172 against 188 recorded and lane MPp measuring 2, 4 and 8 at 1,000,000 rows.

**Settings** (contract 4.6d.10): classes `mean` alone while the witness is `cf1` (`correlation` joins with the first exact class that decides a region holding one; `spread`, `product` and `cell_slopes` off), the second code on skewed columns on the rungs' probability scale (the kit's code), all behind the GATE until `K-S6-08` passes at `f` = 11 and the Codex round accepts the argument; `skew_cut` 1/5, PROVISIONAL (MY ARITHMETIC on log-normal and gamma shapes). The polish's own: four passes at every size, PROVISIONAL (lane `A0b`: two passes 172 of 287 against four's 188 at 200,000 rows; lane MPp measures 2, 4 and 8 at 1,000,000 rows in a night window); its weights PROVISIONAL, the kit's rule for a correlation's (1, 1) sum and `1 / (m v)` elsewhere. No KPI is stamped and no ledger entry changed: the moments are checked by `K-S6-08`'s enumeration and measured by lane E0b's battery (plan P4-D398).

**Repair round 1 (2026-10-20).** On skeptic 1's thirteen items and the statistics review's eight, both of 2026-10-20, each pinned in `tests/test_moment_method_page.py` by a check red on its mutant; no product code, oracle or frozen vector moves, since G17 has no code yet. ## Decision P4-D423 — a column whose values all differ, and free text, described with fewer objects a row (lane H3 of the December plan, 2026-10-21)

**Why.** P4-D400's stated limits (a) and (b): describing one column whose values all differ held 0.8 to 0.9 KB a row at its peak, most of the mixed table's projected 2,694.2 MB at 2,000,000 x 50 (`K-S4-09`, OPEN-WORSE), and one 60-word note column 1,344 traced bytes a row of the profile's peak (the owner's T5 and G4: 2,000,000 x 50 rebuilt in 12 to 18 hours under the 2.5 GB watchdog). The measurement that located the bytes is in P4-D400's dated amendment of this date.

**What is built** (`src/synthtwin/taxonomy.py`, `src/synthtwin/parsing.py`; every description, summary and twin the same bytes). (1) THE RECORD: `_Cell` holds three slots -- the text, the value and one shared entry of `_CELL_FACTS`, the table of every answer the classification gives (what the cell is numerically, its sign, whether it is whole, the two alphabet tests, the declaration), made once when the module loads -- and reads the spelling the number rules read, the exact number and the folded label off them when asked (`_classify`, `_cell_facts`): 64 then 56 bytes a record where it held 112 and the triple 166; `_classify` still classifies each cell once (review item P1-R6-F10's test unchanged). (2) THE TALLY: `_tally` counts its different spellings off its labels and their maps instead of a set of every spelling, and takes the list of texts its records were made from where the caller hands it (`_affixed_verdict`'s cores). (3) EXACT NUMBERS: `_exact_census` and `_exact_count` count them off the sorted values, asking the exact number only where a value repeats; `_distinct_numbers`, `_compound_reading` and `_mode_of` read them so (the zero carrying its last cell's sign as before); `_sentinel_verdicts`, `_cores_judged` and `_read_the_column` ask a cell's exact number only where it holds a candidate's value. (4) WIDTHS: the width censuses keep their counted cells as three lists (`_CountedCells`, `_counted_add`, `_width_add`; `_width_censuses`, `_unpadded_band`, `_width_band`, `_band_width`, `_width_bounds`, `_fraction_widths`), and `_end_pool_band` reads the tally's count of spellings. (5) TAILS: `_numeric_tails_and_causes` counts its different values and heaped ends off the sorted values (`_sorted_runs`, `_end_run`). (6) DATES: `_decide` counts a reading's different texts off the tally where it read every cell (`_different_sources`), `ordered_tails` its grid as runs (`_different_ordinals`), `_census_days` holds one number a day (`_shared_days`), and `ordered_moments` orders moments with no offset by their sorted texts where their instants never fall along them (`_moments_by_text`; otherwise as before). (7) FREE TEXT: the shape of repetition of a free-text, identifier or code block is read off the tally (`_spellings_by_occurrences`; `_text_details`, `_identifier_verdict`, `_decide`), and lengths and word counts share one number a length. (8) THE NUMBER READER: `parsing.classify_number`, `parse_number` and `number_out_of_range` answer a text holding a character no accepted number is written with at once (`_outside_number_alphabet`), the answer their reading always gave, and `splits_into_numbers` cuts a cell by `str.split`. No thread, pool, cache or temporary file; exact integer counting; no float decides a byte.

**Measured** (macOS, the machine at load 30 to 90; traced bytes a row above the column's own cells while `profile_column` describes it, the memos held past their bound as at 2,000,000 rows, on 4682d6ad and on the lane's head, at 20,000 and 40,000 rows): Python 3.11 (floor311), `V` and nine figures 824 and 758 to 418 and 428, eight figures 503 and 434 to 170 and 177, stamps 587 and 526 to 431 and 435, 60-word notes 270 to 142 at 4,000 rows; Python 3.13, 807 to 402 and 412, 502 to 169 and 176, 571 to 414 and 419, notes 290 to 130.5 at 20,000 rows (149 and 141 at 2,000 and 4,000). With the memos at their shipped bound (Python 3.13), at 20,000 and 40,000 rows: 935 and 876 to 554 and 571, 502 and 434 to 177 and 184, 584 and 594 to 423 and 431. CPU untraced (Python 3.13), microseconds a row: 105 to 102, 40.5 to 37.8, 62.5 to 59.1, notes 1,258 to 525. The 2,000,000-row points and `K-S4-09`'s projection are the orchestrator's night window: `planning-notes/work-2026-10/wave6/H3/night-h3.sh <head> kpi|lib|big|shapes`, inside `wave6/H3/window.sh`.

**Proof.** `tests/test_stage4_describe_memory.py`, lane H3's section (16 cases, green with the whole file and review item P1-R6-F10's under Python 3.11 and 3.13): the bounds a row at 20,000 and 40,000 rows (470, 200 and 470) and the notes' at 2,000 and 4,000 (200; traced, free text is described about ten times slower, so 60,000 notes would be five minutes of one test); every field of a record as 4682d6ad's record of ten fields held it, on 3,000 texts under both readings; the exact numbers, the tally's counts, moments, days and the number reader against 4682d6ad's own functions frozen as text (`tests/stage4_as_built.py`: `RECORD_OF_TEN`, `EXACT_MAPS`, `MOMENTS_KEYED`, `DAYS_A_ROW`, `SPLIT_A_CHARACTER_AT_A_TIME`); the description of eleven of the lane's shapes at floors 11 and 1, read whole and one column a group, 4682d6ad's digest. Six mutants, all red (`wave6/H3/mutants.py`, `mutants-1.log`): a copy of each text kept a record, the notes held whole, the zero's sign read off its first cell, repetition counted a label, the alphabet without the group marks, days shared before they are sorted. Byte identity besides: 33 descriptions of `wave6/H3/quick.py`, lane SR's 880-description battery read whole the same bytes as 4682d6ad's, and read one column a group, and the health data zoo at 600 rows (`wave6/H3/bytes/`).

**Stated limits.** (1) The goal of 100 traced bytes a row for a column of record numbers or stamps is NOT met (402 to 435): one record of three slots a cell, 56 bytes, which review item P1-R6-F10 requires; a label written in capitals held folded beside the tally's count of it and its one spelling (about 100 bytes a row); an affixed column's cores and their records (about 120); a stamp's pair (116) and instants (40). Each is held because a rule reads it per label or per cell; a tally holding a column past the categories ceiling by its counts alone is the next cut, owner to be named by the orchestrator. (2) The 2,000,000-row projection is unmeasured here (the night script above). (3) The bounds stand 10 to 13 % above Python 3.11's bytes and 12 to 18 % above 3.13's; Python 3.12 and 3.14, Linux and Windows are unmeasured, CI's first run the first reading of them. (4) The register's peak growing about 245 MB a million rows, and a text met again always more than 8,192 new texts apart answered once a row (P4-D390), named lane H3's at batch 4d, are not re-measured here and stay with the lane's follow-up.
